descriptions.c64:101119: Buy cars and parts from the newspaper classifieds, bolt upgrades into the engine and transmission screw by screw in the garage, then take the hot rod out to race rival drivers.
descriptions.c64:101973: An action adventure in which a journalist roams a sprawling African map in search of the explorer David Livingstone, switching among three weapons and a vaulting pole to get past its dangers.
descriptions.c64:10347: A speeder pilot chases the Alleykat title across eight space stadiums in this vertically scrolling racer with shooting, where events range from demolition derbies to time trials and endurance runs.
descriptions.c64:10353: Thor rolls along on his stone wheel to free Cute Chick from a dinosaur, jumping and ducking past falling rocks, trees, rivers, lava pits, cliff edges and Fat Broad on the way.
descriptions.c64:10354: Fifteen fresh caves for Rockford plus a level editor for designing, saving and playing custom Boulder Dash stages, which can be assembled in sequence on a separate game disk.
descriptions.c64:10355: As Chef Pepper, walk across buns, patties and lettuce to knock them down layer by layer onto the plates below while eggs, sausages and pickles give chase.
descriptions.c64:10357: A wire-frame space flight simulator: pilot a craft above an alien world, searching for evidence of what happened there long ago, with options to switch off either the combat or the exploration.
descriptions.c64:10358: Ride an off-road motorbike against the clock over desert and other terrain, launching off ramps and earning upgrade points for every rider or car overtaken.
descriptions.c64:10359: This follow-up keeps the two-way scrolling jet combat and radar of Falcon Patrol, adds diagonal downward fire and a wider range of foes, and still lets the pilot land on platforms to refuel and rearm.
descriptions.c64:10360: Fly a jet over a wrapping side-scrolling landscape, downing attacking aircraft while watching the radar and touching down on platforms to replenish limited fuel and rockets.
descriptions.c64:10361: Starting as a dull resident of 1980s Liverpool, explore streets and houses, investigate a grisly murder and build up enough personality to finally enter the Pleasuredome.
descriptions.c64:10362: Formula One simulation offering a Ferrari, McLaren or Williams car with different handling, set against rivals who each drive their own way in a World Championship where pit stop planning matters.
descriptions.c64:10363: Baseball for one or two players with a range of pitches from fastballs to curves, base stealing, lineup selection and substitutions during the game.
descriptions.c64:10364: A construction worker races the clock across three girder-site levels of springboards, conveyor belts and elevators, finishing building jobs while dodging enemies.
descriptions.c64:10366: Pilot a ship through nine horizontally scrolling stages of alien attack waves, each ending with a boss that absorbs several hits, with five lives to spend.
descriptions.c64:10367: Chess-like strategy where Light and Dark armies of 18 pieces each meet on a 9x9 board; contested squares turn into real-time arcade duels, and holding all five power points wins outright.
descriptions.c64:10368: Lead a squad of Desert Rangers across a post-nuclear American wasteland, travelling between settlements and slowly uncovering a plot that endangers humanity's survivors.
descriptions.c64:10369: Four colonists compete to get rich on a newly settled planet by producing food, energy, smithore and crystite on their land plots with M.U.L.E. robots and trading goods at auction.
descriptions.c64:10370: Turn-based tactical combat: buy weapons and armour for a squad of soldiers and the odd cyborg, then move them through each mission using action points.
descriptions.c64:10371: A side-scrolling space shooter by Rainbow Arts with weapon power-ups across alien levels, reissued in 1989 under the name Denaris.
descriptions.c64:103745: Play Zamzara, an alien racing through a laboratory to reach its ship before a bomb goes off, blasting monsters along a side-scrolling route under heavy time pressure.
descriptions.c64:104372: Blinky the ghost clears a sideways-scrolling haunted building of traps laid by ghost hunters, gathering the objects needed to cast his spells.
descriptions.c64:104373: The Miner 2049er sequel: as Bounty Bob, walk over every section of framework in 25 mines, working out how to reach each part by jumping, climbing or riding assorted machinery.
descriptions.c64:104374: A three-part Flash Gordon action game: cross a desolate forest shooting minions and avoiding holes, with a map shown beneath the action, then reach the Cave of Barin to confront him.
descriptions.c64:104375: Agent Eliot fights 1930s Chicago gangsters across the docks, the streets and a liquor distillery, jumping and ducking to dodge gunfire and grenades in side-view levels.
descriptions.c64:106310: The fifth Wizardry scenario sends a party of adventurers down through a first-person dungeon to reach the heart of the Maelstrom and stop the sorceress Sorn.
descriptions.c64:107122: Run a private space company in 1996, building orbital stations, conducting research and marketing products, with the focus on the commercial side of spaceflight.
descriptions.c64:107123: Turn-based naval strategy recreating the 1941 hunt for the German battleship Bismarck by the Royal Navy in the North Atlantic.
descriptions.c64:107125: As Sinbad, sail to help the Princess defeat the Black Prince, battling pirates and genies in a Cinemaware tale that leans more on action sequences than most of the studio's games.
descriptions.c64:107127: A first-person Freescape exploration of a cursed pyramid in Cairo: an archaeologist must reach Ra's shrine before the total eclipse of 26 October 1930 sets off the curse.
descriptions.c64:107128: Track V.I.L.E. thieves around the globe as an ACME detective, using geography clues to follow the trail and gathering evidence for a warrant before making the arrest.
descriptions.c64:107129: Switch between the four turtles to fight through New York and rescue April O'Neil from the Shredder.
descriptions.c64:107130: One to nine players act as nobles ruling 18th-century German states, managing land and money turn by turn in a contest to be crowned emperor of the Holy Roman Empire.
descriptions.c64:107131: Investigate an alien ship that has landed beside an American town whose entire population has vanished, after three agents sent in before never came back.
descriptions.c64:108449: Drive a tank through stages set in a forest, at a rocket pad, an airport, a bridge and a refinery, collecting radiation packs and shooting or outmanoeuvring enemies with limited ammunition.
descriptions.c64:108450: Fly a plane over changing terrain, shooting or dodging incoming projectiles, with weapons improving at each new area and three lives available.
descriptions.c64:108451: Space-themed olympiad with five alien events, playable singly or as a tournament, including a 100-metre worm race powered by rhythmic joystick movement that must be paced to conserve slime.
descriptions.c64:108452: Computer version of the board wargame covering conflict in the Persian Gulf region, with full air, land and sea forces for over a dozen nations across up to 25 turns.
descriptions.c64:110205: Three break-dancing games, among them a Simon-style copy-the-moves contest, playable separately or back to back for one or two players, plus a mode for choreographing routines.
descriptions.c64:111209: Police shooting game with three sub-games, including a lone gunfight in a dark Bronx subway station armed with just a six-shot Colt .45.
descriptions.c64:112587: Sequel to Slap-Shot! with one-player games against three computer skill levels or head-to-head matches, featuring passing, checking, penalty shots and shootouts.
descriptions.c64:112589: A goalkeeping game: as the keeper, stop a run of shots from varying angles and distances in matches between 16 selectable teams, with a practice mode.
descriptions.c64:113023: A head-to-head judo contest endorsed by champion Brian Jacks, built around gripping an opponent and timing throws to score.
descriptions.c64:113024: Command an M60A3, M1A1, M3 or M48A5 tank, choosing crew members with individual traits for each mission and switching between the driver, gunner and commander stations.
descriptions.c64:113025: Racing game converted from the Intellivision original with improved graphics and an added track editor, adjustable driving physics and a two-player mode.
descriptions.c64:113026: Up to four players, or one against the computer, claim territories and gather resources on a map, racing to build or capture three cities; adapted from Eon's board game Borderlands.
descriptions.c64:113116: As a foreman, keep water flowing through a pipeline into barrels across 16 levels, patching holes made by drills and blowtorches and fending off pests.
descriptions.c64:113117: Starting in a garden, Monty gathers lumps of coal while timing his dash under crushers and steering clear of hostile boiled sweets in a demanding platform game.
descriptions.c64:113260: A Breakout-style bat-and-ball game: keep the ball in play and knock out every block in each grid, including bricks that take several hits.
descriptions.c64:113261: Swordfighting duels through time based on the film: train against Ramirez, battle Fasil in present-day New York, then face the Kurgan.
descriptions.c64:115694: Fly a rescue ship over the valley of the Leepers on the planet Opthamalia to pick up a stranded crew, avoiding the one-eyed, long-legged creatures that leap up to swallow anything that moves.
descriptions.c64:115700: Cadet MechWarrior Jason Youngblood escapes a Draconis Combine assault on the Citadel of Pacifica and builds a team of BattleMech pilots while following the trail of his father Jeremiah.
descriptions.c64:115763: Isometric adventure aboard the haunted galleon Blackwyche, where Sir Arthur Pendragon fends off skeletons with knives, daggers and an enchanted sword to free the soul of Captain Richard Cavendish.
descriptions.c64:115764: Arcade ice hockey adapted from Konami's coin-op, for one or two players with single games or a tournament, where rough play sometimes erupts into one-on-one fights.
descriptions.c64:115765: Race five rival BMX riders and the clock over six side-view tracks, pulling off stunts and wheelies along the course.
descriptions.c64:116027: Shoot down swooping gargoyles to collect bridge sections, build a span over a lava river, then cross it to face Satan for bonus points and a stronger rocket launcher.
descriptions.c64:11776: Motorbike stunt trials over obstacle-filled courses, ridden against the clock alone or against a friend on a split screen, picking three of eight courses per race.
descriptions.c64:11777: Pickup basketball on four neighborhood courts - schoolyard, alley, parking lot and backyard - each with its own hazards such as oil slicks, with teams picked from local kids.
descriptions.c64:118560: Choose one of four dancers, including the duo Double Trouble, and string together break-dance moves from the moonwalk to harder routines using joystick directions and the fire button, with a warm-up mode for practice.
descriptions.c64:119336: Atoms with one to four bonds drop into a six-slot shaft and must be placed on the board so that every connection is matched, forming stable molecules as the pace rises.
descriptions.c64:119337: Walking home from boxing practice in his underwear, the hero is attacked by everyone in sight - bat-wielding thugs, rampaging gorillas, overly affectionate dogs, karate fighters and crazed bikers - and must punch his way through.
descriptions.c64:11961: Vampire hunter Simon Belmont enters Dracula's castle with his whip, battling skeletons, bats, fishmen and Medusa heads through side-scrolling platform stages.
descriptions.c64:121323: Illustrated adventure in which Sue Ellen summons a detective to South Fork to track down a vastly rich South American oil field described in a letter from Jock Ewing to Miss Ellie.
descriptions.c64:121324: Drive a moon buggy across the lunar surface between stations, jumping craters and rocks and firing both upward and ahead at alien ships, past 25 checkpoints.
descriptions.c64:121416: Mr. Wimpy first crosses a kitchen of shifting manholes to gather ingredients from the larder while Waldo tries to steal them, then assembles burgers in BurgerTime-style platform stages.
descriptions.c64:121907: In 2133, an escaped convict who refused to have his mind reprogrammed battles through six zones of the city on the way to freedom.
descriptions.c64:121964: A street brawler fights through five areas, including city streets and a junkyard, to rescue his girlfriend Maria from the Rogues gang, using fists, kicks and a chain.
descriptions.c64:122060: Two players take turns with artillery pieces in a mountainous landscape, setting barrel angle and powder charge within a time limit to land a hit on the opponent.
descriptions.c64:122061: Link every red cog on the board by placing gears of three sizes on a grid of pegs, which grows sparser on later levels, before time runs out.
descriptions.c64:122062: Guide eight droids through a nuclear power plant wrecked by a deadly explosion to reach the reactor core room, viewing one room at a time in 3D.
descriptions.c64:122063: A knight explores a platform world fighting snakes, dragons, birds and gargoyles and dodging spears and moving pillars, collecting the coins that defeated enemies leave behind.
descriptions.c64:122064: Built on the same engine as Phantasie, this sequel has the party journeying between towns on an overland map, exploring dungeons and fighting monsters, once more opposed by the Dark Lord Nikademus.
descriptions.c64:122081: The trilogy finale: the Dark Lord Nikademus now aims to conquer the whole world, and a party of adventurers sets out to stop him using a system close to the earlier games.
descriptions.c64:122082: Captain a space freighter crewed by quirky aliens, deciding whether to fight or evade pirates and giving quick orders as emergencies pile up during attacks.
descriptions.c64:122083: A fantasy role-playing quest across a tile-based top-down map, where the hero's sprite changes with each mode of travel and the final dungeons switch to a first-person 3D view.
descriptions.c64:122084: Beginning as a poor peasant with a handful of gold, roam the countryside battling monsters to earn wealth, experience and noble rank, following the formula of the first Questron.
descriptions.c64:122085: Isometric racing with 50 included tracks and an editor for laying out curves, crossovers, adjustable jumps and track width, then choosing vehicles and conditions for each race.
descriptions.c64:122086: A troll ventures into cavernous sewers to recover precious relics guarded by cretins, buzzards, skulls and spiders, where one careless jump can end in a fatal fall.
descriptions.c64:122087: The Avatar returns to Britannia, where Lord British has vanished and the usurper Blackthorn enforces twisted versions of the Eight Virtues; set out to find the missing king and restore order.
descriptions.c64:122088: Platform game in the vein of Jumpman: the wizard climbs bricks, ladders and stairs, casting spells at dark creatures or slipping past with levitation, and must find a key to clear each screen.
descriptions.c64:122089: Lord Denethenor, one of four rulers of the realm of Deledain, has turned to dark magic and begun challenging the other lords; adventure across the lands to stop him.
descriptions.c64:122143: Explore an underground catacomb hunting for the five pieces of a broken gemstone while fighting off its guardians and mapping the confusing passages.
descriptions.c64:122144: In this Legacy of the Ancients sequel, Princess Aylea appears in a dream: Baron Taragas has found the powerful artifact Blacksilver in his mines and kidnapped King Durek of Bantross.
descriptions.c64:122274: One or two players tackle a military obstacle course, picking Tommo, the Flame, the Ninja or the Hitman, then vaulting walls and fire pits, crawling through pipes, crossing a rope and shooting targets.
descriptions.c64:122275: Steer a one-man submarine around a single screen to torpedo the four heavy gun emplacements lining the top edge, clearing the way for an invasion force.
descriptions.c64:122286: Lead a series of elite commandos against terrorists, planting charges beside their missiles and getting clear before the blast.
descriptions.c64:122523: Student Arthur Crown, anxious about his Food Economy finals, dreams of ink worms crawling onto the sheet of paper he stands on and must keep them from reaching it.
descriptions.c64:122524: Nemesis battles Torquemada's Terminators across 30 single-screen platform levels, using a sword and a gun with limited ammunition to kill a required number of enemies on each.
descriptions.c64:122525: Illustrated adventure based on the film: as Atreyu, search Fantasia for the one who can rescue it from the all-consuming Nothing.
descriptions.c64:122526: Ed Hick takes his atomic car on a day trip into New York City, battling the traffic, where some vehicles can be safely driven over and others are a real threat.
descriptions.c64:122527: A 3D adventure and role-playing hybrid set on a prison island, where a man teleported there and accused of murder must survive among armed inmates and mutated animals.
descriptions.c64:122533: Golf on the real Royal St George's course in Sandwich, England, aiming for the lowest possible score over a round; released in Europe as Nick Faldo Plays The Open.
descriptions.c64:122534: Based on Clive Barker's film, a side-scrolling action game in which Boone fights through Midian against the Berserkers and the Sons of the Free.
descriptions.c64:122600: Guide a ninja through side-scrolling stages, jumping pits and dodging hazards while enemy ninjas pour out of doorways, never more than four at once.
descriptions.c64:122601: A Gauntlet-style overhead maze game for one or two simultaneous players, collecting treasure and power-ups and defeating enemies across 50 levels with passwords between them.
descriptions.c64:122602: A trainee ninja tackles four tests at the annual games to prove himself, beginning with avoiding arrows that fly in from both sides of the screen.
descriptions.c64:122626: Illustrated three-part text adventure based on Dennis Wheatley's book: Detective Officer Kettering investigates a British financier's apparent suicide on a cruise liner off Miami.
descriptions.c64:122893: Ingrid Bottomlow, a gnome graduate of the Institute of Gnome Economics, is magically exiled to a forest by her family and must get through three tasks in this text adventure.
descriptions.c64:123170: Party-based role-playing with text-adventure elements: form a group of between one and eight characters and take on lengthy scenarios, defeating monsters for power, riches and magic items.
descriptions.c64:123206: A Breakout variant where the goal is carving a gap in the wall wide enough for the paddle to slip through rather than clearing every block, as the bricks creep steadily downward.
descriptions.c64:123431: After a hard day the player dozes off and wakes in the dreamland of Zzzzz, needing to reach its border post to get back to reality; an illustrated text adventure with icon panels beside the picture.
descriptions.c64:124056: The second Questprobe text adventure: Spider-Man takes on Mysterio, whose poison canisters dull his spider-sense, with full-sentence input replacing the two-word parser of The Hulk.
descriptions.c64:124057: Water flowers so they shoot up, shut off the water and harvest them at their tallest for points, while killing worthless weeds and, on later levels, fending off bees.
descriptions.c64:124138: Pilot a remote hover-drone called Monitor through an underground city found on a supposedly lifeless planet, evading its automated defenses in a measured shooter that favors planning over reflexes.
descriptions.c64:124730: Drive a fragile 1920s car across Italy in stages of the historic road race, choosing spare parts before the start and beating the time limit at each checkpoint.
descriptions.c64:124731: Football management: take charge of any club in the top four English divisions, handling the squad, finances and league campaign from an icon-driven menu.
descriptions.c64:124732: One of the earliest 3D pool games, with a fully rotating table and adjustable viewpoint or an optional top-down view, plus precise control over pace, spin and angle for every shot.
descriptions.c64:124733: American football for one or two players mixing play-calling strategy with action, including timeout decisions and choosing which All-Pros or Champs players take the field.
descriptions.c64:124734: Pick an off-road truck by weight and power, stock up on tools and spare parts, then choose a route and drive a punishing cross-country race.
descriptions.c64:124735: Run a 500cc motorcycle racing team on a budget of about four million dollars, handling finances and technical setup, then ride the races on circuits such as Phillip Island.
descriptions.c64:124736: Steer a small ball through parallax-scrolling mazes to find the exit, dodging enemy balls that try to knock it off, trapdoors and killer drones over four levels.
descriptions.c64:124737: A boot camp simulator of five courses, scored for correct actions with penalties for mistakes, and replays for studying attempts; the first is a physical assault course.
descriptions.c64:125073: Leading the Time Warriors, destroy the monster Baal's minions, recover the scattered pieces of a stolen war machine and finally defeat Baal himself.
descriptions.c64:125092: Isometric board game for four human or computer players, similar to Spot: move pieces next to rival colours to convert them, aiming to control the largest share of the board.
descriptions.c64:125122: Post-apocalyptic follow-up to Super Sprint: three armed cars battle over four laps on eight overhead tracks, for one or two players.
descriptions.c64:125192: Score goals by firing small balls from an aiming arrow to knock a larger main ball into the opponent's goal.
descriptions.c64:125201: Infocom mystery text adventure: a disillusioned circus visitor searches the arena, tents and backstage areas for the owner's kidnapped daughter.
descriptions.c64:125219: As a stuntman, ride a motorbike over obstacles and ramps, leap from a speeding car onto a helicopter and race jet skis; too many botched takes cost a life.
descriptions.c64:125220: Mountie Mick runs along nine trains on an auto-scrolling screen to stop bandits from raiding them, reaching the locomotive and swinging onto a handcart to move on.
descriptions.c64:125222: Detective Sir Charles Foxworth and his servant Regis find Raleigh Cartwright III dead aboard the riverboat Delta Princess and have three days to unmask the killer.
descriptions.c64:125230: Golf on a single 18-hole course, picking club, power and direction while accounting for wind, with a close-up window of the green near the hole.
descriptions.c64:125231: Typing tutor built from mini-games where speed matters, such as typing words quickly enough to help a woman outrun a pursuer.
descriptions.c64:125232: Simple bowling: choose a straight, left or right throw and a starting position for each ball, with two players able to take turns.
descriptions.c64:125233: A 1942-style vertical shooter made with the Shoot-'Em-Up Construction Kit, with two-player co-op; an entry in the 2014 SEUCK Compo.
descriptions.c64:125234: A professor uses his time machine to recover a golden key stolen by the Time Warrior, finding coloured keys that unlock destinations such as a caveman era and a deserted space station.
descriptions.c64:125236: A system for designing and saving text adventures, used by many companies to produce commercial games; also released as AdventureWriter.
descriptions.c64:125237: As Dr. Livingstone, explore a national park by the Zambezi; a bad back stops him bending down, so wildlife such as monkeys must be befriended to help.
descriptions.c64:125239: Text-based war game for two to six players based on Alexander's conquests, taking turns to attack neighbouring regions of varying strength to seize the land.
descriptions.c64:125263: Manage a basketball team on a $9,000,000 budget, buying an eight-man roster priced by skill, picking five starters and playing the matches on court.
descriptions.c64:125266: As an agent of the Bureau of Astral Troubleshooters in the 22nd century, take on espionage missions across planets in a first-person adventure set in a criminal underworld.
descriptions.c64:125290: Recover two nuclear weapons stolen by terrorists from opposite ends of a side-view battlefield, switching between a helicopter and a tank.
descriptions.c64:125300: Two-on-two beach volleyball tour that begins in London and moves on to venues across the continents, with the first team to seven points taking each match.
descriptions.c64:125304: Bump into energy stations to link them with beams across 27 levels; each new beam is deadly to touch, so the route has to be planned around it and other obstacles.
descriptions.c64:125313: Strategy game of seizing regions to keep troops supplied, with an emphasis on covert and illicit operations to weaken rival players.
descriptions.c64:125315: Brad Zoom battles the Purple Planet's Brain Eaters in a Galaxians-inspired shooter of 75 passcode-linked levels, moving freely around the lower screen.
descriptions.c64:125319: Sequel to Dark Castle in which Prince Duncan, guided by Merlin, sets out from a fireplace chamber behind the Black Knight's throne to confront him once more.
descriptions.c64:125328: Travel through history in Rufus's phone booth, collecting items to persuade or bribe historical figures into joining Bill and Ted.
descriptions.c64:125334: Fly the Black Hornet stealth fighter against a madman's forces, destroying enemy aircraft, ground installations and buildings.
descriptions.c64:125338: A barbarian fights through monster-filled areas to slay three dragons that plunged the kingdom into darkness, rescuing old men who hand out extra time, vitality or coins.
descriptions.c64:125344: Ikari Warriors-style overhead shooter in which a Rambo-like commando inside a big walking tank cuts down bazooka-carrying soldiers.
descriptions.c64:125350: First-person dungeon role-playing in the land of Trazere, where the renegade mage Zendick has betrayed the Bloodwych order; one or two players set out to stop him on a split screen.
descriptions.c64:125353: A board game modeled on Maxit, played on an 8x8 grid against a series of android opponents over ten stages.
descriptions.c64:125362: Clear each island of bombs by detonating them all, setting off small ones to start chain reactions that ignite larger bombs too powerful to light directly.
descriptions.c64:125364: Mobo and Robo sneak into buildings to collect items planted by a mysterious stranger who is testing his security force, dodging guards along the way.
descriptions.c64:125381: Shoot-'em-up with a learning twist: letters of the alphabet are the targets, meant to help children learn their ABCs.
descriptions.c64:125387: As famed adventurer Trasher, blow up the home of Antrax, the evil ruler who has seized Partomina, a village that was once at peace.
descriptions.c64:125388: After an elephant escapes through an unlatched enclosure into the Amazon jungle, track it down, vaccinate it and return it to the hospital; a 2012 RGCD 16KB cartridge competition entry.
descriptions.c64:125389: Play the shark off Amity Island, devouring swimmers while staying clear of harpoon-wielding hunters.
descriptions.c64:125390: Football management that stresses the psychological side of the job: beyond tactics, pick half-time team talks and public relations moves to shape morale and the club's image.
descriptions.c64:125393: A soldier shoots at four giant heads modeled on the TV series' characters, which fire back and move faster with each new level.
descriptions.c64:125396: Corps-level hex wargame on the Battlefront engine covering the 1944 Normandy campaign, with eight scenarios: Utah, Omaha, Sword, Carentan, Cherbourg, Villers-Bocage, Epsom and Goodwood.
descriptions.c64:125398: A Bomberman clone: clear each of eight boards of hostile creatures with bombs whose blasts reach three squares in every direction.
descriptions.c64:125399: Guide two balls at once across a crater landscape in a one- or two-player contest shown on a panoramic screen.
descriptions.c64:125401: An eagle has carried off the baby from a nursery garden, and the babysitter must search deserts, mountains and forests past dangerous animals to bring it home.
descriptions.c64:125402: One or two players race each other at once as big-nosed boaters who dive beneath the surface to grab treasure, dodging fish and other sea creatures while an air gauge drains for as long as they stay under.
descriptions.c64:125403: A prince transformed into a frog by a wicked wizard must locate each level's key and get to the exit across 50 top-down marsh levels, moving tile by tile past dangers.
descriptions.c64:125405: Text adventure in which a sailor, shipwrecked by a storm on the Pacific island of Atalan, has to explore it and find a way off.
descriptions.c64:125406: Fly an attack helicopter on seek-and-destroy missions against the X-Force terrorists.
descriptions.c64:125407: Mr. Frosty, a young snowman, heads out in the cold to collect presents for Santa in place of an elf who is too drunk to do the job.
descriptions.c64:125408: Aim an anti-aircraft gun to shoot down balloons before they drop dynamite, while birds and helicopters add to the danger.
descriptions.c64:125409: The sheriff of Bandana County gathers enough gold to marry the mayor's daughter, fending off hamburgers, gophers, the Sitting Bull Bikers, giant spiders and other oddities.
descriptions.c64:125410: As sheriff of a Wild West town, guard its bank against the gunslinging Bounty Boys during a string of robberies.
descriptions.c64:125412: Sequel to Bionic Granny: the cantankerous old lady heads into town to collect her pension from the local post office.
descriptions.c64:125413: Smudge collects 20 bombs in each arena while avoiding monsters and moving walls; an enhanced final version of Bomb Chase with an options screen and new music.
descriptions.c64:125414: Rockford digs through caves to gather diamonds and reach the exit before time runs out, avoiding creatures, falling rocks, avalanches and explosions.
descriptions.c64:125415: Hop across jump pads along a galactic route, where each pad colour behaves differently, green ones launching far, and some are traps.
descriptions.c64:125417: Solo contract bridge against a computer that handles both opposing hands. Deals are random, bidding follows ACOL with Stayman and Blackwood, and you can set up specific hands or contracts, replay the play and even look at the opponents' cards.
descriptions.c64:125418: Guide a small green hero through a maze to collect four diamonds worth 750 points each, then escape through an exit that opens in a corner, with arrows showing the way.
descriptions.c64:125419: Football management: pick one of 16 English and Scottish clubs and lead them to the British Super League title in a home-and-away season, with limited tactical options such as formation changes.
descriptions.c64:125420: A version of the 2048 tile puzzle: slide numbered tiles on a 4x4 grid so matching values merge, as a new 2 or 4 appears after every move.
descriptions.c64:125421: Prospector Jake stakes his claim, dodges arrows and tomahawks, and places dynamite in exactly the right spot to strike it rich.
descriptions.c64:125422: A Llamasoft tribute in which a pink camel stranded on a hostile planet tries to escape.
descriptions.c64:125423: Three strategy and trading games: Oil Magnate, Cool Drinks for Sale and Jimmy the Self-made Man.
descriptions.c64:125424: Standing in for Sherlock Holmes, his secretary travels to the island of Nursree, where nursery school children are rioting because the nursery rhymes have been mixed up.
descriptions.c64:125425: Columns-style falling-block puzzle: cycle the order of the three coloured blocks in each falling stone and line up four or more of a colour to clear them.
descriptions.c64:125426: As director of security at a museum under renovation, watch three levels of 81 rooms through office monitors to catch burglars after rare treasures.
descriptions.c64:125427: Inspired by Firebird's 1985 game, Chang must escape the Unknown Island by reaching the harbour, first winning the key to its locked gate.
descriptions.c64:125428: Steer a blue blob around a chasm to reach and kiss the pink blob; touching the walls or the evil wizard sends it back to the start, with no time limit or lives.
descriptions.c64:125429: Grab the key that breaks the princess's cage while steering Bailey clear of the chasm walls and falling stalactites, racing against the clock.
descriptions.c64:125430: Pengo-like game for one or two players: a penguin kicks ice blocks to crush pursuing enemy penguins against other blocks or the screen edge.
descriptions.c64:125432: Uridium-style horizontal shooter set in 2050 among the space stations built by astronaut John Brendan and his crew.
descriptions.c64:125433: Chess against the computer with full rules including castling and en passant, playable as white or black, with a range of extra options.
descriptions.c64:125436: In a near-future Euro-City of 30 million people, tough cops Mike 'Mad Dog' McTavish and Singh 'Big Bang' Kapoor take on the gangs and the crime bosses behind them.
descriptions.c64:125437: With the Alpha Ro sun about to go supernova, help the Atlanteans' Cosmic Ark rescue as many species as possible from the doomed planets.
descriptions.c64:125439: Overhead go-kart racing with a dog theme, against a friend or the computer.
descriptions.c64:125440: Q*bert-style game: hop across a cube grid changing its colours while avoiding Coily the Snake, Boris the Gorilla and cascading balls.
descriptions.c64:125441: Smooth-scrolling Boulder Dash-style digging game with animated graphics and a level generator for building custom stages.
descriptions.c64:125442: A space marine searches the planets Geminus, Sirius and Arius for droids, using up to three weapons against hostile inhabitants and hazards.
descriptions.c64:125443: SEUCK shooter in which Cubotter blasts malfunctioning robots to save the robot race.
descriptions.c64:125444: Remotely fly a Cyberwing Mk. 3 fighter through five alien-ravaged colonies to carry a warning message back to Earth.
descriptions.c64:125449: In 2173, a Dark Force pilot flies against the Cygons, who threaten to fire a giant laser satellite capable of wiping out every planet in the solar system.
descriptions.c64:125452: Send a diver down to gather gold bars and carry them back to the surface while hungry fish prowl the depths.
descriptions.c64:125453: The diver returns to recover jewels spilled from the wreck of the S.S. Richard and haul them up to the surface, now dodging resentful alien fish.
descriptions.c64:125454: Dash around the screen grabbing bombs with the fire button before time expires, avoiding creatures out to capture you.
descriptions.c64:125455: Collect bombs around the screen against the clock while avoiding pursuing creatures, with power-ups that add or remove time and enlarge the monsters.
descriptions.c64:125457: Platform game in which Snuff, an odd little creature, defuses bombs against the clock while elephants try to knock him off the ledges.
descriptions.c64:125458: Top-down single-screen shooter: defend the ten-level Diagon Network guarding the Di-Planium energy source in the Krellis System by destroying every invading alien ship on each level.
descriptions.c64:125459: Begin with a single city and produce armies, ships, fighters and submarines to capture more cities until the whole world is under your control.
descriptions.c64:125466: Vampire-themed text adventure that opens with the narrator waking in icy cold, suddenly far from his uncle's study at Koenigsberg University.
descriptions.c64:125467: A light-hearted two-part text adventure suited to newcomers: find a quiet room where time stands still so adventures can be played without interruption.
descriptions.c64:125468: As the last dodo on 17th-century Mauritius, cross trap-laden areas hunting for hidden eggs while sailors with harpoons and blunderbusses close in, with a map of each area shown first.
descriptions.c64:125470: Catch falling stars in a box whose colour must match each star; letting too many slip past ends the game.
descriptions.c64:125471: Text adventure in which aliens with sinister motives stop your car in a flash of light; thwart them and make it home to Earth.
descriptions.c64:125472: Part of the Extricator trilogy, a text adventure made with The Quill about Professor Roberts, whose secret experiments never fail to bring trouble, picking up after his return from the planet Arg.
descriptions.c64:125473: As the cyborg Voto or Veti, stranded on an alien planet of robot flying objects, blast enemies with a laser and jetpack, collect weapon power-ups and flip switches to open new areas.
descriptions.c64:125474: A single-screen platformer in the Manic Miner tradition in which a small worm-like creature tries to escape from a laundry, its changing height affecting how it moves and jumps. It placed ninth in RGCD's 2012 16KB cartridge competition.
descriptions.c64:125475: Beamed down onto the planet Arg, infiltrate the alien star fleet command base and solve the puzzles of several sectors to free Professor Roberts from the cell block.
descriptions.c64:125477: Football management across the four English divisions of the 1980s: lift a bottom-tier club to the top and win the League and FA Cup double in one season.
descriptions.c64:125478: Score-attack survival: armed only with a pistol, hold back waves of zombies before any reach the camp of a dozen survivors.
descriptions.c64:125479: Pilot a futuristic mini-submarine through a high-tech undersea complex, blasting biological and mechanical horrors in slow-scrolling stages and weaving past obstacles in fast ones.
descriptions.c64:125480: Personality quizzes meant to be played socially, revealing what players are really like and whether friends are bluffing.
descriptions.c64:125482: A police officer whose badge has been stolen blasts through the wall it is hidden behind and then shoots the badge to recover it.
descriptions.c64:125485: A vertically scrolling SEUCK shooter with a tongue-in-cheek backstory about a mad dictator named Stalin, included in the third Shoot 'Em Up Destruction Set.
descriptions.c64:125486: The Bellringer makes his way through castles collecting bags of gold worth 750 points each while avoiding evil knights; a 2013 RGCD cartridge competition entry.
descriptions.c64:125487: Cross-country skiing combined with rifle shooting, raced along a snow trail broken up by shooting rounds.
descriptions.c64:125488: Grab the ring and reach the entrance to the next level before time runs out in this platformer.
descriptions.c64:125489: Locate atoms hidden in an 8x8 grid by firing rays in from the sides and observing whether they are absorbed, deflected or reflected.
descriptions.c64:125490: Amidar-style game: run along the grid to enclose rectangles across the field while avoiding enemies, which can be made to jump out of the way up to three times.
descriptions.c64:125494: Human biology learning game: place bones and organs in their correct positions and study body systems, functions and diseases.
descriptions.c64:125495: Send bombers on precision runs against enemy tanks massing at the border and the factory producing them before they reach your city.
descriptions.c64:125496: Guessing game for one to nine players in which the computer and player take turns working out an object through yes-or-no questions, with the computer learning new objects as it goes.
descriptions.c64:125499: Logic puzzle of grouping identical blocks, sometimes in a required pattern, within the move and time limits shown at the start of each level.
descriptions.c64:125501: In 11th-century China, the dying Duke Zhao of Chongqing banishes his Buddhist priests and lets sorcerers chase immortality, and their rites call forth the demon Narodakini.
descriptions.c64:125505: The bandit roams the screen collecting candy while dodging the sheriff and sour grapes, slipping through gaps in moving walls that hold him fast on contact.
descriptions.c64:125506: Computer version of the children's board game: young players move gingerbread pieces down a rainbow-coloured path through candy lands in search of the missing King Kandy.
descriptions.c64:125507: On Sesame Street, young players assist Big Bird and Little Bird with the mail, sorting it and taking each package to the correct shop to practise object recognition.
descriptions.c64:125519: Solve logic puzzles to reveal pictures of cars as the reward.
descriptions.c64:125526: Bet against the bank on the outcome of single or successive rolls of two dice at a craps table.
descriptions.c64:125527: Playing as Mark or Becky, trapped inside the cave of the Word Wizard, run and jump past hazards to gather enough magic crystals to escape.
descriptions.c64:125529: Following notes left by the aged explorer Jesmon Hys, search the ancient Tombs of Ledromica for a temple of Rah hidden deep inside.
descriptions.c64:125533: Pac-Man clone with four boards per level, each round repeating slightly harder, and the first three boards selectable from the menu.
descriptions.c64:125534: A knight climbs a tower to save a kingdom in this vertically scrolling SEUCK game from the 2010 compo.
descriptions.c64:125535: Educational program for learning computer concepts and BASIC, covering memory, addressing, registers, loops and problem solving.
descriptions.c64:125536: Head-to-head shooter where the player designs the sprites for both their own ship and the enemy, as well as the backgrounds.
descriptions.c64:125537: Steer a ship along the bottom of the screen through oncoming celestial objects of varying speeds, avoiding all contact to reach the next sector.
descriptions.c64:125538: Design simulated fireworks displays and launch them across the night sky in time with music.
descriptions.c64:125543: Fix Rube Goldberg machines with wrong or missing parts by choosing the right replacements, from pulleys upward, to accomplish silly tasks; a forerunner of The Incredible Machine.
descriptions.c64:125545: Choreograph a dancing bear's stage show, design the scenery and compose the music, then save the routines; meant as a gentle introduction to sequential programming.
descriptions.c64:125546: SEUCK shooter set in a department store haunted by monsters, where even the merchandise has come to life.
descriptions.c64:125548: Six mini-games framed as a TV documentary hosted by Salisbury Smythe, following a caveman's daily struggle to survive dinosaurs and wild animals.
descriptions.c64:125550: In Sengoku-era Japan, play Kuruhito, an oni who has rebelled against the Demon Shogun and his invading demon armies; a 2013 RGCD cartridge competition entry.
descriptions.c64:125553: Steer a skier left and right around obstacles, pushing forward to speed up and pulling back to slow down, with harder skill levels earning higher scores.
descriptions.c64:125555: The Duke boys race down the road, jumping every obstacle in their path to get themselves out of trouble.
descriptions.c64:125556: SEUCK shooter in which a pilot breaks through the meteoroids' defences and destroys their army before it can reach Earth.
descriptions.c64:125558: Three frontier simulations about American history - Furs, Voyageur and The Oregon Trail - in which children make decisions, solve problems and navigate as early settlers.
descriptions.c64:125559: Waking in a sealed wing of Dracula's Transylvanian castle, explore its secret passages over several days and learn the Count's nightly habits in order to destroy him.
descriptions.c64:125573: Uncover 20 themed words laid criss-cross over the faces of a 3D cube; vowels score points and grant another turn, blanks end it, and the Wuzzle tracks progress.
descriptions.c64:125646: Gold Box role-playing set in the 25th century: Buck Rogers, revived after centuries of frozen sleep, and a party of New Earth Organization fighters battle RAM's grip on the solar system.
descriptions.c64:125664: Captured by the Treens and held on their research satellite orbiting Venus, Dan Dare breaks free and searches the ship for a way to get an escape shuttle running.
descriptions.c64:125694: Enter the Black Knight's haunted castle to overthrow him, crossing 14 increasingly hard side-view zones of ropes, cages and trapdoors.
descriptions.c64:125712: Side-scrolling space shooter in which a Guardian Warrior can choose to fuse with defeated foes to gain their power or carry on with mortal abilities alone.
descriptions.c64:125713: Stock car racing based on the Tom Cruise film, driving as Cole Trickle through a NASCAR-style season.
descriptions.c64:125715: Second Dragonlance Gold Box adventure: import a Champions of Krynn party to face an undead plague that turns old allies into foes and fills Krynn with rotting monsters.
descriptions.c64:125742: Based on Sam Raimi's film: as Peyton Westlake, back from the dead as Darkman, hunt mobster Robert G. Durant through set pieces such as a helicopter fight, a skyscraper shootout and a dangle above freeway traffic.
descriptions.c64:125847: A one-button game from RGCD's 2014 16KB cartridge competition: a bouncing character has to be kept between the top and bottom edges of the screen, and judges found it fiercely difficult. Artwork is by Saul Cross.
descriptions.c64:125848: Race across a metallic planet surface avoiding obstacles; best with two players, each trying to force the other into collisions without any weapons.
descriptions.c64:125849: A light-handed car race through Tokyo in which the computer handles much of the steering at low speeds, demanding more from the driver the faster you go. Choose 1, 5 or 10 laps, view the whole circuit from above or check the world rankings.
descriptions.c64:125850: Unofficial port of the Spectravideo and ColecoVision game: firefighter Freddy runs along the street dodging falling debris, spraying water at burning windows and rescuing trapped cats.
descriptions.c64:125851: The last part of the Little Sara Sister trilogy, a sideways-scrolling platformer modelled on The Great Giana Sisters, first entered in RGCD's 2012 16KB cartridge competition.
descriptions.c64:125852: Drive a lunar rover across the moonscape, dodging alien blasts and shooting back, with limited shields for emergencies.
descriptions.c64:125853: Four-in-a-row board game for one or two players where completed lines of four vanish from the board, and the goal is to form ten of them horizontally, vertically or diagonally.
descriptions.c64:125855: A programming genius fights off sentient computer viruses that have swarmed his machine and threaten the wider web.
descriptions.c64:125856: Three jungle men, the player plus George and Floyd, race to rescue a girl lost in the jungle past alligators, elephants and birds, scoring points by grabbing birds and pygmies.
descriptions.c64:125857: Fly a paper airplane up and down to keep it from hitting anything, to a remix of the Blue Danube.
descriptions.c64:125858: European Super League edition of Brian Clough's Football Fortunes, rewritten with ESL clubs and player data.
descriptions.c64:125860: Wheel of Fortune-style game: spin the wheel and guess letters in a hidden phrase, revealed by a smurf hostess named Vanna.
descriptions.c64:125861: Early text adventure with a two-word parser set in the land of Hebryptia, notorious for a tough opening.
descriptions.c64:125862: Bounce on a pogo stick up to the twentieth floor, finding the Fraction Elevators by matching fraction pictures to the one shown at the top, with a radar map of the floors.
descriptions.c64:125863: Platform game in which Fröhn sets out to free his Fröhnline, following clues in a joke poem and carrying one item at a time, starting with the Dong.
descriptions.c64:125865: Glob must recover the 16 scattered pieces of the Scroll of Evolution before a candle burns down, dropping between flick-screen rooms with reversed gravity and lifts, then sliding the collected pieces into order in a puzzle mode.
descriptions.c64:125867: Explore the galaxy's 200 billion stars searching for life in a scientifically grounded space exploration and trading game modeled on 1970s Empire-style games.
descriptions.c64:125868: Simple retro shooter: blast aliens swooping onto the screen to music by Rage.
descriptions.c64:125871: Computer version of Awari, a mancala game of sowing stones around pits, won by whoever ends up holding more stones in their kala.
descriptions.c64:125875: Quiz program with four difficulty levels from elementary to graduate school, offering a word-scramble hint when an answer is elusive.
descriptions.c64:125876: Copy the pattern displayed on the right into the left-hand grid using the supplied shapes before an ever-shrinking time limit expires.
descriptions.c64:125878: Sent by the Allfather to execute wicked gods, fly through a sideways-scrolling shooter made with SEUCK for the 2010 Sideways SEUCK Compo.
descriptions.c64:125879: A grammar board game for up to four players who act as budding newspaper reporters, moving around the board and earning money by answering grammar questions. A computer rival named Melvin can join with adjustable intelligence.
descriptions.c64:125880: Children furnish a playhouse with things gathered on visits to a series of magical places.
descriptions.c64:125881: Turn-based wargame covering the opening months of World War I, August to October 1914, in 27 turns of three days each on a map reaching from Paris to Minsk. Command the Western Allies or the Central Powers.
descriptions.c64:125882: Hop Freddie Frog across a busy road with growing traffic, then over a fast river by jumping between logs, to get him and his friends safely home.
descriptions.c64:125884: A puzzle styled like a sprite editor: restore a scrambled pixel pattern to its original image before the time limit runs out.
descriptions.c64:125885: As Ned the Dog, break out of eight single-screen levels of the Traxonians' Grid Zone, seen from above, to rescue his owner Daisy after the Chiggiz walled them in.
descriptions.c64:125886: A reworking of Grid Zone with redesigned levels and new attack formations. Ned the dog gathers gems while dodging lasers, black holes and a lethal orb, and can shield himself a limited number of times.
descriptions.c64:125887: A stylized remake of Flappy Bird: tap to keep a bird aloft and steer it through gaps between obstacles. Published in Commodore Free issue 79.
descriptions.c64:125888: An early build of Heavy Metal Deluxe that blends falling-block puzzling with shooting: match the colours of descending blocks and shoot them back up to score, over 32 levels that gradually speed up.
descriptions.c64:125890: A Pong variant for one or two players in which the ball is struck with your head, made by Oliver Jones with music by Rob Hubbard.
descriptions.c64:125891: A horizontally scrolling space shooter notable for letting two players fight side by side; published in 64'er 1993/11.
descriptions.c64:125893: In an alternate world, the nation of Malexheim fights back against invading legions sent by Hel, the death goddess, then pushes on into Niflheim to strike at the core of her empire.
descriptions.c64:125894: Leaking Delta Radiation has mutated underground creatures that now aim to destroy the research plant and the world; drive a tank into the complex to stop them.
descriptions.c64:125895: A text adventure with simple pictures, set in and around a monastery in the Himalayas.
descriptions.c64:125896: Overhead ice hockey where players skate, score and improve their skills between matches, with multiplayer for friends. From GO64! issue 2003/12.
descriptions.c64:125897: A text adventure about searching for the cup of Christ, written by Andrew Field.
descriptions.c64:125898: A two-part program that helps students understand and solve math word problems.
descriptions.c64:125901: Updated release in which Buzzy, a clumsy worker bee, gathers pollen across 16 levels while dodging natural hazards and wild animals, to lift honey output for the Queen Bee.
descriptions.c64:125903: Science-fiction adventure about a hotel run by a kindly old lady called Grandma, where odd new guests began checking in after a flying saucer was spotted nearby.
descriptions.c64:125904: An adventure in which the hotel caretaker faces the worst winter of his time there, with the building and grounds buried under deep snow.
descriptions.c64:125905: Scrolling platformer in which Howard jumps past moving spikes and bats to gather fragments of his program code, finishing it to impress his girlfriend.
descriptions.c64:125906: Pilot a pulsing light ship through hazardous caverns against a friend or the computer; grazing rocks drains your shields, which recover if you keep clear. Published in GO64! 2003/01.
descriptions.c64:125907: A Defender-style shooter: protect the moons of Mughal, where new defence systems are being trialled, from unknown attackers while managing radar shield, auto-fire and life gauges.
descriptions.c64:125908: An auto-scrolling platformer where a square that can only jump must clear deadly triangles and floors, using black blocks as stepping stones, to cover as much distance as it can.
descriptions.c64:125910: Educational simulation of a car engine: test-run a faulty motor, diagnose the fault and repair it, using a cross-section view where each component can be inspected.
descriptions.c64:125911: A fishing adventure set at the Inner Lakes, where the goal is landing the Irish record tench.
descriptions.c64:125912: Side-on five-a-side football featuring a tournament of eight national teams, two difficulty levels and adjustable match length; each side fields four outfield players and a keeper.
descriptions.c64:125914: Platformer starring Tommy the tomcat, who wanted to be the first to leave the Dream Islands, served a wizard, and now must find his way back home after teleporting away.
descriptions.c64:125916: Horizontally scrolling jet shooter in which you fly as either George W. Bush or Saddam Hussein, dodging bombs, planes, gunfire and ground structures while attacking the other side.
descriptions.c64:125917: A blob locked in a cell in Puzzle Land by a flying monster must solve 32 puzzle levels to escape; a level editor is included. Entered in RGCD's 2013 16KB cartridge competition.
descriptions.c64:125918: As a cowboy, walk along train carriages or across their roofs to stop robbers fleeing by rail, viewed side-on from a raised angle, sometimes choosing between the two routes.
descriptions.c64:125919: Text adventure in which you must keep a frazzled hotelier's business open, and him sane, for a week of 1000 moves while troublesome guests demand service and a health inspector is due.
descriptions.c64:125921: Gather eight music boxes and set them playing at the mansion's way out, fending off four ghosts by throwing heavy objects and working out what the many items in the haunted house are for.
descriptions.c64:125923: Side-scrolling arcade game in which James the fly searches a castle for gold coins and useful items; he has no weapon, and a map of explored areas is drawn below the play screen.
descriptions.c64:125925: Chess tutorial laying out a full system of openings such as the King's Indian Defense and the Najdorf Sicilian, bundled with the Coffeehouse Chess Monster playing program.
descriptions.c64:125926: Computer version of the five-letter word game: pick a secret word from almost 5000 on disk and trade guesses with the Genie, or play a solo version.
descriptions.c64:125927: Return rescued kangaroos to Australia by choosing a route on a world map, then driving through side-scrolling levels.
descriptions.c64:125928: Blackjack simulator built on Ken Uston's methods, recreating the house rules of over 70 US casinos, from deck count and dealer behavior to surrender, splits, doubling and insurance.
descriptions.c64:125930: A port of Kobo Deluxe, the multidirectional space shooter about destroying enemy bases. It placed fourth in RGCD's 2013 16KB cartridge competition and was improved several times afterwards.
descriptions.c64:125932: The King of Alkanien has been poisoned by a stepson too impatient to wait for the throne, and only the Philosopher's Stone, which can also transform metal into gold, can cure him.
descriptions.c64:125933: Walk a man to the top-left corner of the screen to take control of a laser, then shoot only the balls that match. Printed in COMPUTE! 1985/10 among other magazines and collections.
descriptions.c64:125934: Help Perry the Penguin find matching capital and small letters in the letter loft and load them onto trucks bound for an alphabet city.
descriptions.c64:125935: SEUCK-built side-scroller in the vein of Golden Axe: two mercenary heroes, one of them an Amazon, cut down undead hordes that have overrun a peaceful village.
descriptions.c64:125936: Sequel set a thousand years after the vampire tyrant Stryxia fell, when a church built over her resting place to keep her down now stands in a growing town that swallowed Hameria village.
descriptions.c64:125938: After two years in a prison camp hut, put your escape plan into action in this adventure by Paul Eves.
descriptions.c64:125939: Two-player dots and boxes: draw lines, take a box and another turn when you close its fourth side, and win with the most boxes once the grid is filled.
descriptions.c64:125940: A two-level platformer modeled on The Great Giana Sisters, made for the 2004 4K Minigame Competition and serving as the prelude to the Little Sara Sister trilogy.
descriptions.c64:125941: Second Little Sara Sister platformer in the Giana Sisters mould, with nine levels and a reworked soundtrack.
descriptions.c64:125942: Enhanced collection of the three Little Sara Sister games (the original, version 1.5 and the sequel 2), covering around 50 locations from caves and Antarctica to an Egyptian pyramid, each picked from a menu.
descriptions.c64:125943: Introduces programming to ages 9 and up: give a robot commands such as Forward and Repeat to paint polka-dot and checkerboard patterns, then show off the pictures.
descriptions.c64:125944: Sci-fi take on Keystone Kapers: chase an escaping prisoner before he reaches the airlock, with a subgame that awards a jetpack for extra speed. From Commodore Format 38.
descriptions.c64:125945: Pac-Man variant with overhead mazes to clear of pellets while ghosts give chase; some levels let you transform into other forms.
descriptions.c64:125946: Defend Caer Del Taryn by moving a crosshair over the map and zapping invaders; let the city be looted too often and its civilization perishes.
descriptions.c64:125947: The gods of Endoria turned themselves into crystal splinters, and whoever collects them all rules the realm; play one of two rival archmages racing to find them.
descriptions.c64:125948: Crosshair shooter: aim at drifting asteroids and blast them.
descriptions.c64:125949: Business simulation teaching children about production costs, advertising, profit and loss, played competitively by up to six players.
descriptions.c64:125951: General-knowledge quiz for up to six players who must type the correct answer before time runs out.
descriptions.c64:125952: Compact Boulder Dash-style game with design ideas borrowed from Pushcat and Portal, made for RGCD's 2012 16KB cartridge competition.
descriptions.c64:125953: Blast alien invaders by answering arithmetic questions in addition, subtraction, multiplication and division, with adjustable difficulty for ages 4 to 12.
descriptions.c64:125954: As captain of a cargo ship moving Blibbles off their overcrowded planet, round up the creatures that got out of their cell and are wandering into the engine room.
descriptions.c64:125959: Text adventure from the Adventure Master pack in which the goal is to defeat the Black Knight.
descriptions.c64:125960: Partly turned into a bird by the invading Kremins' magic but still in possession of your mind, fly through an arcade platformer to defeat them and free family and friends changed into birds and mice.
descriptions.c64:125961: Minimal action game reinterpreting Super Hexagon, by Paul Koller with a Mikkel Hastrup soundtrack: rotate around the centre to slip through gaps in closing walls. Second place in RGCD's 2013 16KB cartridge competition.
descriptions.c64:125962: Stock market simulation: start with $10,000 and trade shares in companies across sectors such as computers, oil and gas, retail, autos and heavy industry, reading weekly news that moves prices.
descriptions.c64:125966: Three contestants supply questions to the given answers across several categories, gaining money for correct responses and losing it for wrong ones; the richest player wins.
descriptions.c64:125967: A tribute to 1980s LCD handhelds: as a boiler repairman, the player dodges scalding water running through pipes and steam bursting from release valves, grabbing a spanner that appears on the far left and carrying it to the boiler on the right.
descriptions.c64:125970: Defend your home planet against giant alien nuclear missiles in deep space; each hit scores 100 points, while collisions cost one of five shields.
descriptions.c64:125971: Catch falling missiles in the Missile Compaction Container to save your planet from alien attack.
descriptions.c64:125972: Again gather falling missiles into the Compaction Container, now with power-ups and a contamination meter that dooms the planet if it reaches 100%.
descriptions.c64:125973: A tricky isometric maze game built around odd search-and-rescue missions. Released on Commodore Format 16.
descriptions.c64:125974: Property-trading board game modeled on Monopoly, with an optional auction rule.
descriptions.c64:125975: Puzzle Bobble-style shooter where you clear monsters instead of coloured bubbles. Made for RGCD's 2013 16KB cartridge competition.
descriptions.c64:125976: Tetris variant in which the squares left uncleared gradually reveal a cute background picture.
descriptions.c64:125977: Pick or design cartoon characters and combine them into your own animations.
descriptions.c64:125978: Pac-Man-style maze game: eat every dot while four ghosts chase you, using the power dots in the corners to turn the tables briefly; you have three lives.
descriptions.c64:125979: Muppet-themed keyboard and software for children three and up, designed to teach typing and first steps on a computer.
descriptions.c64:125983: Adventure in which you must find and destroy the eggs of giant mutant spiders before they overrun the world, battling natural obstacles along the way.
descriptions.c64:125984: Word game for one to four players against family or the computer, with four levels and thinking time adjustable from 99 seconds down to under 5.
descriptions.c64:125986: Text adventure where the player is carried from the distant past into the far future, inside a vast dome where humanity's last survivors sheltered from a ruined, radioactive Earth.
descriptions.c64:125987: Port of the Soviet clone of Game & Watch Egg: as the wolf from the cartoon Nu, pogodi!, catch eggs rolling down four chutes, scoring a point for each.
descriptions.c64:125988: Snodge the Biblet sets out to free friends held by the evil Biblet Ruler in a guarded hut on a riverbank, fifteen years after the first Nyaaaah! game.
descriptions.c64:125992: Snodge the Biblet tracks down an evil Biblet mafia that captured his friends, in a lick-'em-up adventure.
descriptions.c64:125993: Control a robot sealing radioactive leaks with stones, alone or with a second player as partner or rival; notable for experimenting with subliminal motivational messages.
descriptions.c64:125994: Educational simulation of lake life: as one of several fish species, choose an action at each encounter to find food, avoid predators and survive.
descriptions.c64:125995: Ride a flying horse to rescue a princess kidnapped by a jealous sorcerer who wants her magic powers for himself.
descriptions.c64:125996: As an escaped sheep, munch Farmer Dave's crops to clear each field while avoiding other animals; three bumps end the game.
descriptions.c64:125997: As Shep the border collie, herd a set number of sheep back to their pen in each of 20 levels before shearing time.
descriptions.c64:125998: As a greedy St. Ives seagull, drive off the sheep by bombing them from above so you can claim Farmer Rich's crops, while Shep the sheepdog sometimes interferes.
descriptions.c64:126000: SEUCK lick-'em-up whose shots travel only one square, so you must get right next to enemies to destroy them. From Commodore Zone issue 4.
descriptions.c64:126003: Pac-Man variant where the dots are large turtles that shrink when eaten, so each maze must be cleared twice.
descriptions.c64:126009: Snodge the Biblet faces King Squit, a new ruler crueller than Evil Squatter, who turned Bibletsville's good Biblets evil and captured Snodge's friends.
descriptions.c64:126010: Model car racing head-to-head against a champion computer driver or a second player.
descriptions.c64:126011: Two-part platform arcade adventure about a disastrous episode of interstellar piracy.
descriptions.c64:126012: Guide the explorer Orpheus through the underworld of Hades, gathering all the scattered treasure so he can leave, while avoiding creatures, obstacles and traps.
descriptions.c64:126014: Two submarines face off, firing torpedoes or shooting mines to bounce them into the rival; five hits destroy a sub and give the other a point.
descriptions.c64:126016: Self-paced tutorial for grades 1 to 4 drilling addition that needs carrying and subtraction that may or may not need borrowing, stressing place value.
descriptions.c64:126018: Self-paced tutorial for grades 2 to 8 on multiplication and long division, with practice problems that also call for addition and subtraction.
descriptions.c64:126021: Two-player maze muncher by Richard Bayliss and Paul Kubiszyn, begun in 1995 and shelved after an unfinished demo appeared on a Commodore Format covertape; this deluxe edition came later.
descriptions.c64:126023: Sideways shooter made as a sample for Shoot 'Em Up Destruction Set 2, leading a fleet of ships through deep space, an asteroid belt, an alien world and an alien city.
descriptions.c64:126024: Sequel side-scrolling shooter with parallax scrolling and boss fights, leading a fleet of ships through space, asteroid belts, an alien world and a city.
descriptions.c64:126025: Downhill racing against the clock on eight courses for up to eight players; beat the preview time to qualify for the next World Cup race and earn a life, while crashes or slow runs cost one.
descriptions.c64:126026: After your plane's engine fails on a treasure-hunting shortcut home and you crash-land unhurt in a meadow, find a way to stay alive.
descriptions.c64:126028: Stop aliens from conquering Earth by answering multiplication table questions correctly.
descriptions.c64:126029: Foosball on screen: take joystick control of each row of players to block, pass and shoot, with angled deflections and diving goalkeeper saves.
descriptions.c64:126030: Split-screen race for two or four players driving Moon Patrol buggies, waggling the joystick in Decathlon fashion to build speed; the faster the waggle, the faster the buggy.
descriptions.c64:126031: Single-player Pac-Man clone: clear a maze of dots while dodging four ghosts that emerge from the centre, eating corner power pellets to make them vulnerable for a while.
descriptions.c64:126032: Steer a painter around a house wall to give the whole facade a fresh coat, with three characters per game. Printed in the magazine Computronic in early 1985.
descriptions.c64:126033: Guard a ship launching through a meteor storm with a single shield that can face fore, aft, port or starboard, scoring for each meteor blocked on the way to orbit.
descriptions.c64:126034: Steer a falling plane down winding paths past an ever-growing number of obstacles. Entered in RGCD's 2014 16KB cartridge competition.
descriptions.c64:126035: Falling-block puzzle in the Tetris mould: fit differently shaped parts into a U-shaped pit as compactly as possible. Also released as Brainbox.
descriptions.c64:126036: Chess tutorial devised by Paul Whitehead, who took the Masters Division title at the American Chess Championship as a teenager; it also includes the Coffeehouse Chess Monster playing program.
descriptions.c64:126038: A miniature role-playing game in the spirit of the early Final Fantasy titles, first written in BASIC and later rebuilt for RGCD's 2014 16KB cartridge competition with new tile graphics by fx and music by Twoflower. The hero roams the map and battles monsters.
descriptions.c64:126039: Name a song from up to 25 notes, choosing among four possible answers.
descriptions.c64:126042: One-button skating game: jump over obstacles across the terrain as the pace keeps rising. Entered in RGCD's 2014 16KB cartridge competition.
descriptions.c64:126043: Educational deduction puzzle: fire a laser into a maze from its edge, sized from 3x3 to 13x13, and work out where hidden mirrors, deflectors and absorbers lie from how the beam behaves.
descriptions.c64:126044: Reach the treasure by solving addition, subtraction, multiplication and division problems; a wrong answer brings a step-by-step explanation from the professor.
descriptions.c64:126045: Strategy game in which you run a nationwide campaign for the US presidency.
descriptions.c64:126046: Based on the TV game show: three contestants answer trivia questions to win spins, then use them on the Big Board.
descriptions.c64:126047: Pipe Mania clone: lay pipe pieces outward from a starting station in the bottom right to build a working pipeline. From the September 1993 Magic Disk 64.
descriptions.c64:126049: Frogger variation with music and speech: a frog crosses a road of jousting knights, then a moat of snakes and alligators that may dive under, to reach the princess's castle.
descriptions.c64:126050: Four sub-games by Shaun Southern: a horizontal shooter, a platformer climbed with a yoyo, a scrolling run through a graveyard, and a target shooter borrowing Forbidden Forest's moon and aiming system.
descriptions.c64:126051: Recover the Federation's prized ship Quann Tulla, stolen by its designer Erra Quann to sell its engine secrets to the Evil Empire, and kill the traitor, starting aboard your own damaged, airless ship.
descriptions.c64:126052: Rescue Princess Zota, taken when the sorcerer Balzan's Zeldan guards razed the Boran city in the land of Sark, and save its scattered people.
descriptions.c64:126054: Joust-inspired single-screen game: ride an Osturkey armed with a Laser-Lance, knock foes off their flying mounts by striking from above, then shoot them on the ground.
descriptions.c64:126055: Vertically scrolling helicopter shooter in the style of 1943, unrelated to the Rambo films despite the title.
descriptions.c64:126056: Keystone Kapers-inspired chase: catch the thieves on each level within the time limit. Made for RGCD's 2012 16KB cartridge competition.
descriptions.c64:126057: Floating mutant tomatoes that look edible but are lethal are terrorizing the countryside, towns and cities, swallowing up fleeing people.
descriptions.c64:126059: Based on the TV series Romper Room, teaching children aged 2 to 7 their letters, new words, concentration, cause and effect and word association, guided by the animated character Max.
descriptions.c64:126061: Rotate jumbled numbers back into order at your own pace, with no time limit or lives.
descriptions.c64:126063: Flying platformer: gather items on each single screen to build up enough magic to destroy the Genie, marked by a skull on the map; arrive short of magic and the task is hopeless.
descriptions.c64:126064: Illustrated text adventure: as commander of a salvage ship, recover the Sequerra crystal from a disused convict shuttle left circling asteroid 4-Gamma-7 for 17 years.
descriptions.c64:126065: Lode Runner-like platformer: collect the required items while avoiding roaming enemies, digging holes that drop them to the platform below.
descriptions.c64:126066: SEUCK side-scroller based on H. P. Lovecraft's tale: pilot an old-fashioned submarine against the sea creatures lurking off the coast of Innsmouth.
descriptions.c64:126067: As Bruise Lei, the Shaolin Master's young apprentice, fight evil henchmen, recover forty sacred idols and take revenge for your master to uncover the temple's hidden treasures and scrolls.
descriptions.c64:126068: Sokoban-style puzzle: push coloured crates around a warehouse until all crates of each colour are grouped together; levels arrive in random order.
descriptions.c64:126069: Guess whether the next random ball, numbered 1 to 99, will be higher or lower, in the manner of Play Your Cards Right, with a joker to play.
descriptions.c64:126070: Hungarian SEUCK shooter: travel down a jungle river deep in Africa toward the guarded treasures of a legendary emerald castle.
descriptions.c64:126071: Tron light-cycle style game for up to four players with a 4-player adapter, made for the Vision 2002 party and released in GO64! 2002/10.
descriptions.c64:126074: Light-cycle game: outlast your opponent while weaving around the enclosure without running into a tail.
descriptions.c64:126075: Festive game: fly an airborne sleigh, pick up snowballs from the ground and fire them from a cannon at enemies who shoot back.
descriptions.c64:126076: Run a games company, facing twists drawn from the real experiences of people who worked at Cult Games and D&H.
descriptions.c64:126077: Six short maths tests for children up to age seven, featuring Sooty the magic bear with Sweep and Soo.
descriptions.c64:126078: As Commander Pork, duel the evil Baron von Oinkhofen, whose craft outpaces and outguns yours, relying on LARD missiles and quick reflexes.
descriptions.c64:126079: Hold off swarms of alien breeds threatening your space station with a satellite-mounted cannon that fires in your direction of movement, with only two lives to spare.
descriptions.c64:126080: Search the basement of a magic castle for the stolen Sparkk formula while its monster is away on a picnic; small monsters sap energy, but the clock is the real enemy.
descriptions.c64:126081: Letter-guessing game in three formats: complete nursery rhymes, answer riddles, and fill in famous sayings.
descriptions.c64:126082: Illustrated interactive fiction: type simple commands, solve puzzles and work out which actions lead to the Serpent's Star.
descriptions.c64:126083: Guide Shauny the sheep and Rover the watchdog through the farmyard, rescuing sheep friends and feeding sausages to hungry foxes.
descriptions.c64:126085: SEUCK shooter and winner of the SEUCK 2013 contest: fly a spacecraft in defence of Earth, lasering alien creatures.
descriptions.c64:126086: After nuclear war, supplies in the Silo 64 fallout shelter have run out, so leave with your robot companion to face the devastated world outside.
descriptions.c64:126087: Race down a highway dodging police, roadblocks and potholes, choosing whether to spare or run down jaywalkers and grandmothers to earn angel or devil points.
descriptions.c64:126088: Christmas puzzle: deliver presents to every house, moving only to houses still waiting and crossing forests when needed. From Loadstar 76.
descriptions.c64:126090: One of the earliest text adventures: a knight sets out from a campsite with a mule-like burdenbeast and a dart shooter to recover treasures hidden in the caverns of Spider Mountain. A fantasy rework of Lost Dutchman's Gold with its own odd vocabulary.
descriptions.c64:126091: Time presses so a ball that bounces on its own moves forward over and under an endless line of spikes.
descriptions.c64:126092: Fly a Spitfire across the Channel to destroy grounded flying bombs and enemy planes, and shoot down bombs heading for your base before the fuel runs out.
descriptions.c64:126093: Spy Hunter-style SEUCK shooter fought on land and sea; sixth in SEUCK Compo 2013, then included as a sample with the fourth Shoot 'Em Up Destruction Set.
descriptions.c64:126096: Logic puzzle: slide a square block to the exit within a move limit, knowing it only halts when it hits an obstacle. From Commodore Format 55.
descriptions.c64:126097: Two-player space duel: steer your ship and shoot at your opponent, with ten selectable difficulty levels.
descriptions.c64:126098: One-button game: hold fire to swirl a star around and steer it through rings that pop up at random, without crashing into the walls.
descriptions.c64:126099: Joust-style game in which Sir Lancelot, with a charmed lance, battles beasts terrorizing a mystical land; paired with Robin Hood on a Double-Ender release.
descriptions.c64:126100: Slalom racing: dodge trees and rocks and take the turns tightly for the fastest time.
descriptions.c64:126101: Collect treasure, crosses and jewels in a maze while avoiding skulls; trapdoors and holes drop you to harder levels below, and your map gradually rolls itself up.
descriptions.c64:126102: Slap Fight-inspired vertical space shooter, one of the sample games bundled with SEUCK.
descriptions.c64:126105: Smash TV-style arena shooter: as cartoon hero Squibbly Sqwob, win back the pens stolen by the evil ink blot so cartoons can be drawn again.
descriptions.c64:126107: Hold fire to swing a star in a circle and let go to fling it off in a straight line, collecting the rings that appear around the play area.
descriptions.c64:126109: Golf on Pine View, a southern sandhills course drawn to scale hole by hole with bunkers, water, trees, rough and out-of-bounds areas.
descriptions.c64:126110: Teleport onto starships, find and charge a phaser, shoot the aliens aboard, then reach the console to beam back out.
descriptions.c64:126111: Spelling and vocabulary for ages 6 to 9 with over 4,000 words plus your own lists; in Picture Spell, jump Stickybear around platforms to grab the letters of a pictured word.
descriptions.c64:126112: Creative writing program for grades 4 to 9 with a twist-a-plot feature that pushes young authors to branch their stories.
descriptions.c64:126113: Two players share one control and must cooperate to hit a set number of targets in time, or both die; medals award extra lives.
descriptions.c64:126116: SEUCK shooter where cover and mobility are the keys to gunning down enemies before they get you, with music by Richard Bayliss.
descriptions.c64:126118: Overhead tank game across 8 battle zones, with rotate-and-thrust controls and narrow branching routes whose sturdy walls offer protection.
descriptions.c64:126120: Bounce a ball over squares that vanish beneath it, some needing several bounces, planning a path that always leaves a safe place to land.
descriptions.c64:126123: Bowling viewed from behind the bowler: line up left or right, choose an angle and avoid fouling, with scores kept automatically.
descriptions.c64:126124: Two-player duel between a warrior and an evil doom lord: for five minutes, cast spells that hurl sabres while dodging your rival; the higher score wins.
descriptions.c64:126126: Catch bricks dropping from a rolling bin in a small wheelbarrow; four misses end the game, and difficulty runs from 1 to 15.
descriptions.c64:126127: Beat 'em up: kick and punch through 24 screens to retrieve four mystic scrolls. Issued on cartridge by RGCD as a reward for the C64 in Pixels Kickstarter.
