descriptions.c64:138086: A strategy simulation in which you coach NBA teams from different eras, setting up dream matchups such as the 1985 Celtics of Larry Bird versus the 1972 Lakers.
descriptions.c64:138087: Jeff Minter's package of six mini-games: progress in each earns pieces of completion icons, and the game is won once five icons are assembled before an overall time bar runs out.
descriptions.c64:138088: Real-time tactical simulation of modern armored warfare: command a U.S., Soviet or Chinese battalion as a lieutenant colonel across five scenarios and 40 maps with rivers, hills and minefields.
descriptions.c64:138091: A Space War clone for two players only, included in several Supernova game packs.
descriptions.c64:138093: A brutally hard tank game: break into a heavily fortified enemy city and wreck the nuclear plant that powers it.
descriptions.c64:138156: Two figures at opposite ends of a single screen fight over a bathtub, one player against the computer or two against each other, trying to hold the water at the right level or to fill or drain it so a swan escapes or a fish perishes.
descriptions.c64:138158: A clone of Irem's Moon Patrol arcade game, included in Keypunch's compilation packs Arcade Games and War Games.
descriptions.c64:138163: To power a resource-starved Earth, link the 37 hexagons of the Cosmic Interlace Grid with an unbroken line across from one edge to the opposite edge, freeing hexagons with a trio of ZMX general-purpose robots within one hour of real time.
descriptions.c64:138169: Companion to Kampfgruppe covering platoon-level Western Front combat between 1943 and 1945, with nearly all the ground weapons fielded by Britain, the US and Germany; games end automatically after 30 turns.
descriptions.c64:138171: A commando armed with an M16 and smart grenades recovers the eight pieces of a Bailey bridge to reach a Neutron Beam weapons base and destroy it, fighting through alien troops, tanks and laser emplacements.
descriptions.c64:138172: Grand tactical simulation of the Civil War's bloodiest day around Sharpsburg, Maryland, along Antietam Creek, played in 11 hour-long turns scored on casualties and territorial objectives.
descriptions.c64:138173: Based on the cartoon series: fly a G-Force Phoenix ship to defend the planets Pete, Xenath, Elias, Horaf and Olixal from Zoltar's attacks, destroying enough of his craft at each.
descriptions.c64:138174: Moon Patrol-style action in which 26th-century scientists drive an all-terrain vehicle through the time void, battling across eras with threats ranging from dinosaurs to nuclear hazards.
descriptions.c64:138182: Two players face off in futuristic tanks on a top-down single screen, each needing four hits on the other to win; four arenas with different wall layouts can be chosen.
descriptions.c64:138183: Corps-level World War II command of Axis or Allied forces: give orders to as many as a dozen regiments toward preset objectives and timetables, deciding the role each plays in the battle.
descriptions.c64:138184: A wargame covering four Napoleonic battles, Waterloo, Quatre Bras, Borodino and Auerstadt, playable from either side, plus a construction set for designing maps, troop types, weapon ranges and damage.
descriptions.c64:138198: Follow-up to SSI's Warship covering surface naval battles of World War I between Britain and Germany and of World War II between Germany/Italy and Britain/France, with 79 ship classes.
descriptions.c64:138199: Command RAF Fighter Command in 1940, either for one day of light or heavy raids, or across a 30-day campaign starting on 20 August, on a map of southern Britain.
descriptions.c64:138211: A 100-meter swim for one player, racing for the fastest possible time.
descriptions.c64:138213: A single-screen platform game for one or two players set in the realm of the wizard Aroon, with ten levels plus a bonus stage; collect coins and smash stones with a steel helmet. Published on Golden Disk 64 #12.
descriptions.c64:138214: Hungarian top-down rally racer starring Bburago's miniature toy rally cars. Finishing the original release gave players a code to mail in for a chance at one of fifty real Bburago models; it only came out in Hungary, though crackers later produced an English version.
descriptions.c64:138221: Beach volleyball in which each serve is aimed with the joystick, using an on-screen direction indicator to pick straight, left or right before the server throws.
descriptions.c64:138222: Race a beach buggy through the eight rounds of the Dune Trials, beating each time limit while jumping rocks, shooting down helicopters that would cause crashes, and picking up fuel to keep going.
descriptions.c64:138224: As Beaky, an Andromedan Armed Condor nesting on the hostile planet Crackit, protect your eggs from the native Eggsnatchers who are out to destroy them.
descriptions.c64:138225: Ted the Bear needs batteries for his new Sinclair electric truck, so he climbs a patrolled building site to fetch them, dropping bombs on the guards. A Baby Bear mode allows practice.
descriptions.c64:138226: Steer a black ball to pick up bombs and use them to destroy the other balls. Released on Game On in September 1991.
descriptions.c64:138227: A text adventure made with The Quill and built on Beatles lyrics: in 2953 a keeper of the archives researching ancient Earth comes across 'The Four Kings of EMI'.
descriptions.c64:138228: A text adventure about a simple trip to buy milk that goes wrong at every turn, with obstacles such as obstructive bank staff, transport troubles and a greedy tramp.
descriptions.c64:138263: A vertically scrolling space shooter over 16 short levels: blast swirling alien formations and fixed cannons, grab extras and fight boss ships, alone or with a second player.
descriptions.c64:138264: As bee number 52, gather enough honey from backyard flowers each day to meet your quota, avoiding spiders, grasshoppers, other bugs and lawn sprinklers.
descriptions.c64:138265: Zombies have overrun Burt's beer factory; bounce Burt between platforms through 32 rooms in each of the Shipping, Production and Control departments to wipe them out.
descriptions.c64:138267: Written as a 4KB entry for the 2003 MiniGame Compo: work through four castle sections by lowering the thick brick walls between them, ringing four of eight bells in the correct order.
descriptions.c64:138268: Climb ladders through four castle towers collecting bags of gold worth 750 points each; to move on from each tower, ring five of its eight bells in the right order to raise the final ladder.
descriptions.c64:138269: A box-pushing logic puzzle in the Sokoban mould: a little man must shove crates onto marked spots and can never pull them. Released on Game On in March 1989.
descriptions.c64:138270: As Benji, rescue scientists held by robot drones across the solar system and fly them home to Earth, picking destinations from the engine room and adjusting warp and jump settings.
descriptions.c64:138271: Play a whale dodging fishermen's mines, harpoons and torpedoes while eating plankton and surfacing to breathe; when the plankton runs out, the next tide begins.
descriptions.c64:138272: Two princes of the Empire of Man, trapped with their fleets in the Tyriarus Nebula, must fight off a Berserker wolf pack together, and then whoever survives may turn on the other.
descriptions.c64:138273: Bert the Bug searches a garden for twenty of a wizard's scrolls, shooting at the killer toy mice, kettles, umbrellas and fire extinguishers roaming everywhere.
descriptions.c64:138275: Spelling drills from the Besieged series covering notoriously awkward English words like asthma, ancillary and miscellaneous; correct answers help a crusading knight advance.
descriptions.c64:138276: A chess teaching program that replays Bobby Fischer's games and asks you to guess each move.
descriptions.c64:138278: Based on the Eddie Murphy film: Axel Foley tackles four distinct sub-games, including a Green Beret-style shootout in a warehouse.
descriptions.c64:138279: Steer an orb with the paddles to investigate the fate of Vern Grenington, who vanished along with his whole vehicle service station at Vicinity NAW-911, a region known to hold a black hole.
descriptions.c64:138326: Kicked out by his mother for rudeness, Biff the chimp tries to earn his way back home by doing a series of jobs around the jungle in a flick-screen arcade adventure.
descriptions.c64:138327: Trapped in a space complex by the wizard Jem, Giz must collect 30 gold coins to open the tunnel to Big Ben's bell and ring it to escape, in a multi-directional scrolling platformer.
descriptions.c64:138329: A fishing holiday in the south seas, hunting big game fish while the locals try to make money off you; land enough catches or the vacation ends after a single day.
descriptions.c64:138330: Box your way past eight opponents, including Heap Big Nose and Cheap N' Nasty, to win the title; name your fighter and fight in a side-on view of the whole ring.
descriptions.c64:138331: Mac must deactivate 18 single-screen vaults, climbing ladders and surviving any fall onto smooth ground, while hitting switches in the right order to remove walls, make floors and freeze obstacles.
descriptions.c64:138332: Big Nose the Caveman, whisked through time to modern New York, sets out to free the animals caged in a zoo in a multi-directional scrolling platformer.
descriptions.c64:138333: A comic text adventure spoofing 1930s detective fiction: dim private eye Sam Spillade takes a case to find his client's missing father.
descriptions.c64:138334: Footsy the Bigfoot must fix two breaks in a cable so he can blast open with TNT the cage where a madman holds his girlfriend, travelling through a series of environments.
descriptions.c64:138335: Based on the 1980s film: Jim journeys into the past to warn the World War I pilot Biggles about a devastating German weapon. The game comes in two separate parts.
descriptions.c64:138336: As Barney the clown, perform four increasingly hard circus acts viewed side-on, with options for lives, difficulty and the extra-life score threshold.
descriptions.c64:138359: An educational memory game: ride a bike through the park noticing things like bins, rabbits, frogs, deer and flowers, then recall which items you saw.
descriptions.c64:138360: Pat Splatt, Groove-Town's best poster paster, must fix the posters his rival Nasty Norville has wrecked before time runs out; the starting level can be picked beforehand.
descriptions.c64:138363: Drive a postal land yacht, keeping bird droppings off the shiny paintwork and shooting planes, trains, helicopters and cars that block the way. Also released in Italy as Giacomo Il Postino and Falco.
descriptions.c64:138365: Home-safety quiz on a 5x5 bingo grid: pick a square and answer its multiple-choice question to claim it for a point, or get it wrong and lose that square. Five in a row earns five bonus points and a little dance from Bingo Bugglebee.
descriptions.c64:138366: Computer bingo for up to 99 players: numbers drawn from a bingo machine are checked off on 5x5 cards to complete a pattern, with text or graphics modes and printing of custom-designed cards.
descriptions.c64:138368: A Bionic Granny waits outside the school at 4 o'clock and moves along the bottom of the screen, whacking the departing children with her walking stick.
descriptions.c64:138369: Aliens will overrun Icarus Earth Defense Base within ninety minutes, so an android trained in Eastern martial arts is sent to fight through five levels and destroy them all.
descriptions.c64:138370: A three-part game about raising a family: build a nest and lay three eggs, feed the chicks when they hatch, then help them learn to fly, avoiding obstacles that cost lives.
descriptions.c64:138371: A simple shooter in which a great bird flies over a coral reef, using a short-range blast against other birds, dragons and leaping sea creatures.
descriptions.c64:138372: A one-player version of the pen-and-paper ship-hunting game: you and the computer each hide a submarine, PT boat, battleship, destroyer and carrier on a 10x10 grid. Part of the 30 Games pack.
descriptions.c64:138444: Ghosts have moved into your computer's circuit boards; drive a small vehicle with an anti-ectoplasm beam along the circuits to destroy them and repair damaged chips, with more ghosts on each level.
descriptions.c64:138445: A bundle of three text adventures; in the title story, a student newspaper reporter investigates the Eta Beta Pi sorority, whose members may be behind a friend's disappearance.
descriptions.c64:138446: A single-screen shooter set inside a data bus on the way to the computer's central core: blast the Bits, then the pods they leave behind, across successive waves.
descriptions.c64:138447: Teddy, lost in a forest on the way to the teddy bears' picnic, raids a giant beehive for its honey across 16 single-screen platform levels.
descriptions.c64:138448: A tile-laying board game: players take turns filling squares with tiles in one of three pathway designs, after which a heart-shaped marker travels along the paths until it reaches an empty square.
descriptions.c64:138449: A computer version of Abalone: push black and white marbles around a hexagonal board, aiming to shove six of the opponent's off the edge. Released on Magic Disk 64 in March 1994.
descriptions.c64:138450: A taekwondo sparring simulation built to supplement real training: two-minute bouts against a friend or six increasingly tough computer opponents, scored by landing or blocking blows under the sport's actual rules and penalties, with fighters stepping between three planes of the mat.
descriptions.c64:138451: The wizard Tobias has used the Black Crystal to bring down the kingdom of Beroth after the Brotherhood of Wizards turned him away; travel its realms to recover the seven Rings.
descriptions.c64:138453: Fly the Black Hawk over a chain of island bases, wrecking tanks, missile launchers and planes to raise the enemy's Strategic Loss Factor; both sections scroll vertically, the first guiding a missile camera.
descriptions.c64:138456: Roll a ball across the field's stones to change their colour step by step in a set order of priority until each one vanishes; the goal is to clear them all.
descriptions.c64:138459: The Black Knight has ravaged the valley, killing and capturing its people; gather objects and weapons from the surrounding lands, storm his castle past the guards and slay him.
descriptions.c64:138513: One-on-one martial arts fighting in the style of Way of the Exploding Fist, with moves ranging from basic punches and kicks to rolls, back-flips and roundhouse kicks, performed through eight joystick directions and short or long button presses. Released on Game On in February 1992.
descriptions.c64:138515: A text adventure with small pictures: in 1912 the hunter Forrester Kilbride seeks the fabled Black Pearl and is left alone when his bearers refuse to enter the uncharted Land of the Kalmad.
descriptions.c64:138517: Blackjack for one to five players using Las Vegas, Downtown Vegas, Reno or Atlantic City rules, or custom ones, with adjustable bet limits and deck counts and a hint mode suggesting the best play.
descriptions.c64:138521: Inspired by the film: as a police hunter, track down and eliminate six grades of increasingly intelligent replidroids on Earth, mostly from inside your skimmer.
descriptions.c64:138523: Slippery Sid, spy and son of Blagger, gathers the keys scattered over each level, jumping the robots that guard them before leaving through a doorway.
descriptions.c64:138524: Blagger tours the film sets of director Steven Speilbum, aiming to steal his latest film while dodging characters like Superman, Batman, Tarzan, Jaws, James Bond, Robin Hood and the Hulk.
descriptions.c64:138525: Roll a ball to collect key fragments in numerical order, then find the hidden exit. Released on Game On in October 1989.
descriptions.c64:138528: A duel for two players only: shoot your opponent, and the first to 10 points wins.
descriptions.c64:138531: A space cadet's final test: fly through the heavily defended Blaze Zone of the Andromeda System, moving a ship along the bottom of the screen and shooting aliens and defenses.
descriptions.c64:138532: Hired by the Sahiban to steal the Mazeli superweapon ship Blazer, you fly a vertically scrolling overhead shoot-'em-up armed only with a forward cannon and no power-ups, facing enemies from above and the sides and shooting ground bases.
descriptions.c64:138533: A plane crosses the screen, dropping lower after each pass; bomb the skyscrapers below with the space bar to flatten them before it hits one.
descriptions.c64:138534: A flying saucer low on fuel crosses a city, descending with each pass; bomb all the skyscrapers flat so it can land on level ground.
descriptions.c64:138615: Official sequel to Blitz 2000, a horizontally scrolling shooter against an alien attack on Earth, released with Commodore Zone issue 12.
descriptions.c64:138616: A real-time strategy wargame in which you command German forces trying to conquer Western Europe and England between 1 May and 30 September, against computer-controlled Allies.
descriptions.c64:138617: A text adventure that opens outside a castle in a blizzard: get inside quickly, since every move lowers your body temperature, then defeat an evil wizard.
descriptions.c64:138620: A tough Bubble Bobble-style platformer: collect a set number of items to finish each level unless a key appears to open the exit, while enemies respawn in unexpected places.
descriptions.c64:138624: A Pac-Man clone: steer Blob around his maze home, avoiding the deadly Wibblies, and use four hidden potions to turn the tables for a while. Released with Commodore Format issue 2.
descriptions.c64:138625: Rather than blasting blocks away, shoot pieces into place to destroy the alien buildings that threaten your planet.
descriptions.c64:138626: A reversed space shooter: you are the saucer at the screen's top, firing down on ships and aliens rising toward you.
descriptions.c64:138831: A 3D shooter: escort four merchant freighters carrying vital supplies to Earth through an asteroid belt, dodging rocks, destroying robot mines and alien ships, and managing fuel and shields.
descriptions.c64:138834: Recreates the Gold Run bonus round of the TV quiz Blockbusters on its 5x4 grid of hexagon questions; correct answers claim cells for you, wrong ones turn them black for the opposition.
descriptions.c64:138835: An early Q*bert clone for one or two players.
descriptions.c64:139006: Trap every bubble without ever touching one. Published in 64'er Sonderheft issues 17 and 26 and the 64'er Spielesammlung #3.
descriptions.c64:139007: Sequel to Block'n'Bubble with the same aim of trapping every bubble while never touching one; published in 64'er Sonderheft 30.
descriptions.c64:139010: A version of the Tower of Hanoi puzzle, included in The Big 100 compilation.
descriptions.c64:139011: A 5x7 board starts with one kind of tile per column, then gets shuffled; slide rows and columns with the keyboard to restore the original layout.
descriptions.c64:139012: Early, simple sideways-scrolling shoot-'em-up by Paul Kessels with Maniacs of Noise music that CP Verlag planned to publish around 1991; it never came out, and only this preview build survives.
descriptions.c64:139015: Hark and Kren, whose parents were killed when their village on Sylonia was burned, ride homemade Skywalk jet bikes to the planet Scorpia to wipe out the space convicts known as the Scorpions.
descriptions.c64:139016: A head-to-head shooter for two players only: whoever has the most kills when the timer expires wins.
descriptions.c64:139017: Loosely based on two 1986 fantasy gamebooks: play the Quarry, a barbarian, priest or thief slave released once a year into the valley of Gad to be hunted down by the Archveult, the valley's cruel ruler.
descriptions.c64:139018: An Othello-style thinking game for one or two players, published in 64'er in September 1997.
descriptions.c64:139020: A flight simulator of the F/A-18 built around air shows, recreating the U.S. Navy's Blue Angels demonstration squadron with tight formation flying that requires coordinating with the other jets.
descriptions.c64:139021: As the Blue Baron in 1918, fly 12 bombing missions in a side-scrolling shooter: take off from the airfield, fight past enemy aircraft, bomb the target and return home.
descriptions.c64:139044: Sequel to Blue Max set in 2001: pilot a flying saucer bombing enemy targets while avoiding enemy saucers and ground cannon, with the screen border flashing to warn of low altitude.
descriptions.c64:139045: Pilot an intergalactic spacecraft through five stages on a hostile planet to rescue a stranded sister ship and its crew and bring them back to the Blue Moon; touching creatures or obstacles costs a life.
descriptions.c64:139046: An American Civil War strategy game in semi-real time for one player against the computer or two players, with historical or invented missions from the Confederate or Union side.
descriptions.c64:139047: A side-scrolling shooter tied to the TV series: fly a jetcopter across a sea of islands bristling with defenses to reach and disable the enemy stronghold after an alien assault.
descriptions.c64:139048: Two players take a BMX through six freestyle events, each with a qualifying standard to beat; clearing all six repeats them with tougher targets.
descriptions.c64:139049: Having taken treasure from a hidden jungle valley, flee the angry natives on a BMX bike across flick screens, avoiding obstacles, traps and creatures.
descriptions.c64:139050: An arithmetic game for ages six to ten: ride a BMX around a maze to find and jump over the answer to addition, subtraction or multiplication questions.
descriptions.c64:139051: Ride a BMX up an endless vertically scrolling road for as long as possible, dodging cars, other riders, oil patches and more.
descriptions.c64:139053: Sequel to BMX Simulator with four riders instead of two and two terrains: the familiar Dirt tracks and expert-level Quarry races, where tyre thickness can be chosen.
descriptions.c64:139054: One or two players tackle six BMX challenges: a 200m race, longest wheelie, ramp jump, slalom, bunny hops over bars and a jump over a VW Beetle.
descriptions.c64:139056: As Bob Morane, retake a space station overrun by enemy soldiers, hunting down and destroying every one of them in a multi-directional scrolling shooter played much like Prohibition.
descriptions.c64:139057: Bob Winner seeks a lost desert civilisation and must win three keys by defeating bosses in Paris, then London, then New York, two boxers and a gun-slinging cowboy, using items found on earlier screens.
descriptions.c64:139058: A Bubble Bobble-style platformer with trampolines, spread over 70 to 80 levels and finished off with a proper ending.
descriptions.c64:139059: Apprentice magician Bobix of the island Texul learns that his teacher, the magician Bennof, is an impostor who poisoned the queen. Released on Game On in June 1994.
descriptions.c64:139063: In the 1930s, private eye Sam Harlow escapes two hired killers and searches the town for clues and informants to solve the kidnapping of Rita Sweeney, his former wife.
descriptions.c64:139064: Baseball on a split screen, with a field overview beside a batter view that disappears once the ball is hit; draft your squad by each player's skill ratings before play.
descriptions.c64:139065: As King Kayus of Agamen, ride a dragon out to destroy the tyrant Zambaquous across six levels of horizontally scrolling shooting with some vertical movement.
descriptions.c64:139066: A conversion of the arcade football game with big sprites on a small pitch, where winning possession and dribbling forward matter more than passing.
descriptions.c64:139067: Two-on-two basketball: draft teammates from ten players modelled on pro stars and play with or against the computer or a friend, with practice games such as Horse and Around the World.
descriptions.c64:139086: As Quack Fu master Howard the Duck, punch and kick through maze-like landscapes on Volcano Island to rescue Phil and Beverly from a dark overlord's volcano.
descriptions.c64:139087: Race a high-performance car between U.S. cities, planning your own route through fog, snow, road works and day-night cycles.
descriptions.c64:139088: American football from a first-person view: you see what your player sees, with control passing from quarterback to receiver on a pass or from kicker to returner on kicks.
descriptions.c64:139089: Air racing in 250mph planes through southern USA valleys in the pioneering era, across 16 marked courses.
descriptions.c64:139090: Command the Ocean Ranger, a frigate-sized foilborne missile ship, hunting surface, underwater and airborne targets on missions ranging from the easier Bering Sea to the toughest, the Persian Gulf, via Southeast Asia and Central America.
descriptions.c64:139091: Waking in a hut on a deserted beach with no memory and a pounding head, piece together who you are as words and phrases trigger memories of the past.
descriptions.c64:139092: A techno-scavenger in 2049 explores the Koronis Rift, where the Ancients left ships and artifacts behind; send a droid to retrieve modules and work out what each piece of ancient technology does.
descriptions.c64:139093: Hunt down each level's boss and defeat it to win the key to the exit, using a jet-pack to get around and shooting the planet's inhabitants.
descriptions.c64:139094: Back from a century-long voyage, an astronaut finds Earth deserted and logs into Worldnet, the global database of human activity, to learn what happened, in a computer novel told through its records.
descriptions.c64:139095: In 8878, a Pastfinder explores radioactive planets in a vertically scrolling game, retrieving artifacts and time capsules and delivering them safely to base, choosing destinations from a map.
descriptions.c64:139096: Asteroids-like shooting in a lethal stretch of space filled with killer rocks, rogue satellites and boomerangs, with warp holes on each level.
descriptions.c64:139097: An Infocom text adventure: a postal clerk in the fishing village of Festeron delivers an envelope to Ye Olde Magick Shoppe and finds the town mysteriously transformed.
descriptions.c64:139098: A musical take on evolution in eight levels of three phases each; in the first, freeze organisms into energy clusters by reaching web intersections ahead of them.
descriptions.c64:139099: An illustrated text adventure in which an interplanetary secret agent roams the galaxy in a fuel-hungry ship, with touches of dry humour.
descriptions.c64:139100: Pick a fighter from various alien races, including humans, with their own abilities and styles, buy weapons and gadgets, bet on bouts and fight through opponents to face the Fatman.
descriptions.c64:139101: Gramps has invented a device that makes his dreams real; when the dream creature Franklin Snarl kidnaps him into the bizarre world of Tonetown, you follow to rescue him.
descriptions.c64:139102: Pilot the shuttle Discovery from launch to orbit, open the cargo bay to recover and repair a satellite, then land, while burning as little fuel as you can.
descriptions.c64:139103: Tile-matching solitaire with 144 mahjong tiles stacked in a layout; remove them in matching pairs until the board is clear.
descriptions.c64:139104: Control a defense satellite to stop waves of bombs aimed at the United States, with movement and aiming handled independently.
descriptions.c64:139106: Manage a football club from below the top division toward league and European glory, with a squad of up to 15 renamable players, transfers and bank loans.
descriptions.c64:139107: American football management with 16 teams, players rated for skill, energy and form, and a soccer-style transfer market with mid-season trades for cash.
descriptions.c64:139108: Freddy Hardest, a hard-partying galactic playboy and heir to a fortune, takes his spaceship out while drunk and lands himself in serious trouble in this side-scrolling action game.
descriptions.c64:139110: As the Doctor from Doctor Who, stop the Daleks' invasion of Earth with your companions, starting with a hover-platform ride through London's sewers blasting monsters before later fighting on foot.
descriptions.c64:139111: A real-time illustrated text adventure based on Michael Moorcock's trilogy: British officer Oswald Bastable is in command of HMS Shards, an airship, in a steampunk future.
descriptions.c64:139112: Pinball for up to four players on a single table, with rotatable ABC lights at the top worth 10,000 points and bonus multipliers.
descriptions.c64:139113: Eleven joystick-waggling track and field events, including five running races from 100 meters up to a gruelling 1500 meters.
descriptions.c64:139114: Space thief Philip Sunset, hunted by the Drowhar army after stealing its secret Sprocket System, flies for the Terra-1 forces in this horizontally scrolling shooter, grabbing extra weapons, speed and lives against fast swarms of erratic enemies.
descriptions.c64:139115: Drive Pat's van through a busy working day: collect letters and parcels from Mrs Goggins at the post office, deliver them, and help with chores like herding Peter Fogg's sheep.
descriptions.c64:139116: An illustrated text adventure spoofing Star Trek: as James T. Cake, captain of the starship Paralysed, deliver a Rigellian Slime beast and a Trell to the planet Dandrox for experiments.
descriptions.c64:139117: The first game starring the British children's TV puppets: left in charge of the house by Matthew, Sooty must deal with the old bones Sweep has scattered everywhere in this platformer.
descriptions.c64:139118: After a cheese sandwich supper, Fred Bear dreams of driving through Toyland, steering clear of fluffy snakes, wooden ducks, spacemen, toy trucks and other dangerous toys.
descriptions.c64:139119: A text adventure with occasional pictures spoofing M*A*S*H: newly qualified surgeon Pigseye Peers joins a mobile army hospital in Korea, where the first job is to recover a still.
descriptions.c64:139121: Train two middle-distance runners, one for 400m and one for 800m and 1500m, through local races before earning a place in four major championship finals including Crystal Palace.
descriptions.c64:139122: On war-ravaged Nu-Earth, the lone survivor of the Genetic Infantrymen betrayed in the Quartz Zone Massacre sets out to find the traitor responsible.
descriptions.c64:139123: Fly with the RAF's Red Arrows display team, performing loops, rolls and flypasts at over 300mph a few feet from your teammates, following in-flight height and heading instructions.
descriptions.c64:139124: A rally simulation with educational aims: plan routes on a full map where each road has its own traits, such as higher speeds or a tendency to flood in rain.
descriptions.c64:139168: An Earthman crash-lands into an ancient war and pilots a giant blue battle-robot against the red Zoids, fighting from inside the cockpit.
descriptions.c64:139169: Yogi crosses 198 sideways-scrolling screens of Jellystone Park to rescue the kidnapped Boo-Boo, collecting six toffee apples that form a code for freeing him quietly.
descriptions.c64:139170: An illustrated text adventure starring Ralph, a wizard fond of a drink, whose drunken prank of transforming a man during a night out sets the story in motion.
descriptions.c64:139172: A Popeye-style single-screen platformer: Bongo the rat collects gems while avoiding a pursuer, and can teleport by standing on the letters of his name and pressing fire.
descriptions.c64:139176: Top-down football expanded from Kick Off with full tournament modes, fictional players and four pitch types, including a plastic surface with unpredictable bounce.
descriptions.c64:139178: Escape the house room by room: from a reception hall of ten doors, numbered one to nine plus X, clear each room before room X and the final way out open up.
descriptions.c64:139179: A jump jet simulation written by a real jump jet pilot, with ranks from Flight Lieutenant to Group Captain plus a practice mode, and guided missiles for combat.
descriptions.c64:139202: Play poker against two computer opponents, starting with $100 and betting from $5 up to $25 a hand.
descriptions.c64:139203: Sequel to Space-Pilot, the Time Pilot clone: fly a rotating craft across varied environments, downing planes for points, with some departures from the original's features.
descriptions.c64:139205: Zaxxon-like isometric action underground: fly a helicopter through tunnels to the life-support power plant on Zaga 1 and fix its critical fault.
descriptions.c64:139207: Isometric tennis seen from the sideline, with eight-direction movement and shot power set by angle and fire-button pressure; matches are best of three sets under standard rules.
descriptions.c64:139208: A power-station rod controller's annual assessment on a simulator: on a split screen against the computer, keep two Dynamic Rods level.
descriptions.c64:139209: Formula racing converted from the arcade: start in Brazil among 100 cars needing a top-80 finish to qualify, with the field shrinking across eight races.
descriptions.c64:139210: Follows the second Adrian Mole book through 18 months of Adrian's life, presented as sections of challenges where you pick among three options.
descriptions.c64:139211: Officially licensed by the English FA: guide a club side toward FA Cup glory with up to eight players, choosing formation and an attacking, balanced or defensive strategy.
descriptions.c64:139212: Hostile Hadean craft are using Earth's refinery planet Erebus to brew nerve gas. Fly a scrolling overhead shooter, passing over every section of a level to open its dimension duct, then survive a 30-second bonus wave by dodging up and down.
descriptions.c64:139213: Full-court two-on-two basketball with a horizontally scrolling court, a referee calling rough fouls, and teams that start at a salary level to work up from.
descriptions.c64:139214: Four trucks race over off-road tracks built by mirroring and reversing a core set of layouts; losing to a computer truck costs one of your three credits, while wins bring rewards.
descriptions.c64:139215: One of the last four great sorcerers must rescue the other three from the Necromancer before time runs out, flying across 17 screens of wasteland, river and woods, gathering items and keys and avoiding ghosts and sorcerers.
descriptions.c64:139216: THX2240 flees slave-like labour in an agridustrial compound aboard a stolen Crowd Control vehicle, fighting an escape through all 10 levels.
descriptions.c64:139217: Pop bouncing balloons, which split into smaller ones, with upward-shooting hooks across 50 levels; one or two players share the screen, and a second can join at any time.
descriptions.c64:139219: A bounty hunter roams the desert to find a bank, cemetery, saloon, Indian village, mine and fort, shooting cowboys who get in the way and keeping his limited ammunition topped up.
descriptions.c64:139220: Train in the gym with weights, squats and sit-ups, waggling the joystick to fill a bottle of Lucozade, before Daley Thompson takes on the decathlon events.
descriptions.c64:139221: Based on the film: as Frank Harris, stop Holli Would from crossing into the real world by shooting doodles and gathering coins across four cartoon worlds of four levels each.
descriptions.c64:139222: In 2631, Red Falcon terrorists seize the Galuga archipelago off New Zealand ahead of an alien invasion, and Contra commandos Bill Rizer and Lance Bean are sent to stop them.
descriptions.c64:139223: Keep a bakery's production line running while scaring off raccoons that eat the bread and switch off the machines, so the delivery truck fills up and drives away.
descriptions.c64:139224: A knight races the clock through six dungeons collecting scattered door pieces, then defeats the black wizard to rescue a princess held in the castle.
descriptions.c64:139238: A Bagman-style flick-screen platformer: gather all the gold bags across three mine screens using ladders and lifts while dodging two outlaws.
descriptions.c64:139243: Platformer based on the 1991 film: cat burglar Eddie 'Hudson Hawk' Hawkins, just out after ten years in prison, is dragged back into thieving despite plans to go straight.
descriptions.c64:139245: Based on Spielberg's 1991 film: Peter Pan sets out to save his kids from Captain Hook.
descriptions.c64:139247: Fly a laser-armed helicopter over a sea of small islands, finding stranded people before they starve or drown, dropping a ladder to lift them aboard and ferrying them to a safe platform.
descriptions.c64:139248: Choose Roger Murtaugh or Martin Riggs for each of four missions and a final bonus one, running, jumping, swimming, kicking and shooting to stop crime in Los Angeles.
descriptions.c64:139249: Slide blocks left or right with a cursor so they drop and touch matching blocks, aiming to clear every block on each level.
descriptions.c64:139250: Ryu brawls through Las Vegas, the Grand Canyon, Brooklyn and other American stages in this arcade beat-'em-up, using flying neck throws, back flips and hanging kicks, smashing phone booths and oil drums for power-ups and swords, with two-player co-op.
descriptions.c64:139251: A QIX variant: draw lines with a space scriber to wall off at least 75% of the playfield and trap the ball, losing a life if it touches you or your unfinished trail.
descriptions.c64:139253: Wheelie off ramps to leap between platforms on nine single-screen obstacle courses, collecting flags before the fuel gauge, which doubles as a timer, runs dry.
descriptions.c64:139254: Based on the film: newly self-aware robot Number 5 must escape the laboratory, finding hardware and software upgrades that let him jump and fire a laser while evading security.
descriptions.c64:139255: Jungle man Toki, turned into an ape by the wizard Dr. Stark, battles through jungle, underwater and volcanic stages to reach Stark's palace, rescue Wanda and regain human form.
descriptions.c64:139256: Fly a Tornado at low level over built-up areas in a pseudo-3D top-down view, dropping altitude to shoot out six target discs while avoiding trees and buildings.
descriptions.c64:139284: The alien scientist Erra Quann has hijacked the Federation flagship Quann Tulla and taken it to an Empire outpost to sell its engine secrets, and you are sent to stop him.
descriptions.c64:139285: Count Vladimir has stolen King Arnid's Crown Jewels, scattered them across the island of Ognid and kept a sceptre inside his castle; recover them to restore the land of Ix.
descriptions.c64:139286: An illustrated text adventure in which Bugsy, a giant rabbit, climbs Chicago's criminal ladder through theft, extortion, bribery and worse, aiming to replace Al Capone as Public Enemy No. 1.
descriptions.c64:139287: Delta 4's comic text adventure parody of The Hobbit, in three parts and full of jokes such as an Old Ford location next to a New Ford.
descriptions.c64:139288: A Mandroid agent hunts on the planet Cove 4 for Chris Auker, who has stolen the Mandroid files to pass them to the crime lord Max, exploring on foot or with a remote vehicle.
descriptions.c64:139290: As a novice oceanographer, build a reputation exploring more than 75 lost wrecks, then plan, fund, crew and equip an expedition to find the Titanic, charting courses and diving against the elements.
descriptions.c64:139292: A low-gravity 3D Pong invented by the Galcorp corporation: hit the ball so the other player can't return it, scoring when it reaches their back wall.
descriptions.c64:139293: As Brad or Janet, search the castle for parts of the De-Medusa machine, carrying one piece at a time, to unfreeze your partner and escape before the castle blasts off.
descriptions.c64:139294: Sent by a distrustful command to the heavily defended alien world Loughton 2 instead of a deserted colony, pilot a Plasmatron fighter and blast the oncoming waves.
descriptions.c64:139296: A text adventure: with the Silvian invading Meridan once more, seek the legendary eternal Guardian said to dwell deep inside a mountain.
descriptions.c64:139297: A three-part text adventure about a werewolf's curse, each part seen through a different character, starting with a man who wakes up covered in blood.
descriptions.c64:139300: Fire-breathing dragon DJ Puff collects discs hidden in hard-to-reach spots or dropped by certain monsters, burning enemies and jumping through the levels.
descriptions.c64:139301: Sequel to CJ's Elephant Antics: the young elephant crosses the USA to rescue brothers and sisters trapped by The Hunter, firing peanuts and collected bombs in a platform game.
descriptions.c64:139302: A retired superhero recovers diamonds stolen by insane genius Austen van Flyswatter across 12 platform levels riddled with traps.
descriptions.c64:139351: Four styles of arcade shooting across 32 levels, including a vertically scrolling Salamander-style stage with wall flames and a Centipede-style stage.
descriptions.c64:139352: An overhead Super Sprint-style racer for one or two players, with circuits full of underpasses and tight bends.
descriptions.c64:139528: Seven years after World War III, drive the specially equipped Last V8 out of your shelter across a hostile surface, following the orders of a digitised voice.
descriptions.c64:139535: Following Soldier One, you wake in a strange building with a note telling you to collect the pieces of an exit code; explore its flick screens of platforms to escape.
descriptions.c64:139537: A first-person adventure in and around a dark castle: cross a moat full of sharks and battle evil to free your choice of the Prince or Princess.
descriptions.c64:139538: A role-playing game in the vein of Sword of Fargol, built around the legend of a deformed child of Kraizar abandoned in the woods and taken in by the old wizard Ibonek Nawibo.
descriptions.c64:139540: A branching multiple-choice game adapted from Edward Packard's first Choose Your Own Adventure book, in which a kid wanders into a cave that leads to different times.
descriptions.c64:139544: A Pac-Man-inspired maze game set on Disneyland's Tom Sawyer's Island: gather berries while Aunt Polly, Injun Joe and later a bear give chase, escaping via a water wheel, teeter-totter or raft.
descriptions.c64:139545: Based on the Fighting Fantasy gamebook: infiltrate the Black Tower atop Craggen Rock with spells, sword and wits to defeat the warlock Balthus Dire and save the Vale of Willow.
descriptions.c64:139552: Zen the Mole turns a network of sticks blue by walking over them while yellow, turning red for a few seconds to build bridges out to the network.
descriptions.c64:139562: Tag-team wrestling with four teams, the Mad Soldiers, Orient Express, Great Maskmen and Crush Brothers, each wrestler having special moves such as knee butts, body slams and flying head butts.
descriptions.c64:139603: Use a magic wand to create and destroy blocks, arranging them to reach each level's key and unlock the exit.
descriptions.c64:139631: As Jonny, explore Dr. Zin's complex in a side-on flick-screen adventure to rescue your father, who has been kidnapped and forced to build a world-conquering laser.
descriptions.c64:139643: Six Wild West contests, including arm wrestling timed to your arm's strong phases and shooting beer glass targets faster than a rival.
descriptions.c64:139645: Defend New York from invading aliens on a single screen of skyscrapers with a subway tunnel beneath, launching from pads at either edge; one or two players.
descriptions.c64:139647: A text adventure in one of the valleys around Lake Watersmeet: seek your fortune by finding treasure or robbing locals, whose characters move about in real time.
descriptions.c64:139649: Moe, Larry and Curly scramble to raise $5000 to save an orphanage from an evil banker, through scenes based on their TV and film routines, including dodging flying pies.
descriptions.c64:139756: Based on Bob Monkhouse's TV quiz: up to four players answer general knowledge questions on a bingo-style board, completing lines for prizes and clearing the whole card to win.
descriptions.c64:139757: Steer an Olympic bobsled down a mountain, avoiding boulders and obstacles, and above all the chalet, as speed builds toward the finish.
descriptions.c64:139758: Run a bobsleigh team, handling training, equipment purchases and finances, then race the runs yourself; bankruptcy ends the game.
descriptions.c64:139759: Lawn bowls: roll the jack, then send heavier bowls toward it, scoring for each bowl nearer the jack than the opponent's best.
descriptions.c64:139761: With help from his friend Dr. Who and the TARDIS, Bod the Alien travels to an Egyptian pyramid, a medieval castle and a Victorian haunted house to rescue his kidnapped children in a flick-screen platformer.
descriptions.c64:139763: Educational activities about different parts of the human body, followed by a quiz of more than 200 questions.
descriptions.c64:139764: Arriving late to work, the BOFH finds insane activists have taken the servers and workstations hostage and planted bombs in the network closets, and goes to war to take the building back.
descriptions.c64:139765: Delta 4's parody text adventure of Lord of the Rings: Fordo the Boggit must take the Great Ring to Mount Doom, joined by Spam, Pimply and Murky and meeting Bumbadil, Hashberry, Legoland and Giblet.
descriptions.c64:139771: An illustrated story set in the Zork world: a caravan of adventurers heads into Egreth Castle, once home of King Duncanthrax and now overrun by trolls, hobgoblins and night gaunts under a mad wizard.
descriptions.c64:139772: The second ZorkQuest story: the magician Frobwit, Acia, the merchant Gurthark and the scout Ryker travel together toward Accardi-By-The-Sea.
descriptions.c64:139776: From Cassette 50: choose between Master Logic, a Mastermind clone with nine difficulty levels, and Letter Jumble.
descriptions.c64:139777: The meter has run out and the lights are off, letting Bogymen roam; climb ladders from the meter at the bottom right toward the top of a single-screen platform layout.
descriptions.c64:139781: Bounce around collecting every item in the correct order, or lose a life. Released with Commodore Zone issue 13.
descriptions.c64:139782: Bojo the Clown bounces on circus trampolines to reach balloons; each balloon collected reappears elsewhere, so a different trampoline is needed.
descriptions.c64:139783: A head-to-head shooter for two players only, with each side getting its own half of a split screen. Programmed by Mathew Cox, music from Kent Patfield.
descriptions.c64:139784: A tiny 4K minigame-competition entry where falling bombs have to be caught before they go off.
descriptions.c64:139785: Steer Smudge around enclosed arenas gathering 20 bombs per stage while dodging roaming monsters and shifting walls.
descriptions.c64:139787: Bombs are ticking inside the Sellerscale nuclear plant, and a lone hero must defuse them across a series of single-screen platform levels before the north of the globe is wiped out.
descriptions.c64:139788: A lightly reworked follow-up to Bomb Chase in which Smudge again clears each arena of bombs while avoiding enemies, with a cuter look but the same rough edges.
descriptions.c64:139789: Bomb Jack's caped hero returns in a scrolling platform sequel, grabbing bombs for points and avoiding monsters that pop out of crates.
descriptions.c64:139793: A plain Bomb Jack-style game of leaping between platforms to gather bombs, which cycles back to its first screen after a while. Appeared in Happy Computer and a 64'er game collection.
descriptions.c64:139794: Feuding twin brothers Bang and Boom are thrown into the Bomb Squad Pit to settle their quarrel with dropped bombs over three rounds, in a Bomberman-like duel.
descriptions.c64:139795: Locked in a terrorist hideout, break out of the cell and race into town to stop a bomb set to detonate at 4 p.m. in this text adventure from Mogul's Great Adventure Pack.
descriptions.c64:139799: Fly a bomber leftward over enemy territory, moving only up and down, and land 25 bombs on targets without striking any hospital while flak and fighters attack.
descriptions.c64:139801: A plane sweeps back and forth over a city, dropping bombs to level the buildings so it can land, refuel and start the next mission.
descriptions.c64:139802: Fight across 36 fiery Bomberman-style arenas in a solo campaign, or face two to five friends in deathmatch; passwords unlock cooperative play and computer opponents.
descriptions.c64:139803: Hop from platform to platform collecting the objects scattered over each screen without tumbling off. Also known as Bomb Jack Junior, and issued in Italy under the names Labirinto and Vampir.
descriptions.c64:139804: A Polish Bomberman-style duel for two players or one against the computer, blasting through destructible walls in a half-indestructible maze to eliminate the rival. Part of the Triada pack.
descriptions.c64:139806: Jump around each screen picking up tokens while avoiding moving foes; collecting them in their flashing order earns a bonus, and a falling power-up gives a temporary edge. Three lives are all you get.
descriptions.c64:139808: A Minesweeper clone coded entirely in assembly, with genuine mouse support and a high-score table that can be saved.
descriptions.c64:139809: A multi-screen platformer in a Mario-like vein where the goal is to jump up and grab flowers, with the option of leaving a level and coming back to it later.
descriptions.c64:139810: Bono the dragon makes soap from skeletons, and to restock he digs through 22 scrolling castle levels in this Boulder Dash-style puzzle game.
descriptions.c64:139811: Move a little workman up and down ladders between layered floors; the layout of ladders and boxes is rearranged every game.
descriptions.c64:139812: Kteth, a falcon-headed godling of Egypt, is cast out of the Other World with the rest of Set's kin after Set murders Osiris and is defeated by Horus.
descriptions.c64:139817: Run illegal Scotch down the highways in an armed, armoured car while police try to stop the delivery, in a side-scrolling driving and shooting game.
descriptions.c64:139820: An educational platformer where Boppie, a bouncing ball, gathers letters one at a time in the right order to spell words.
descriptions.c64:139824: An Infocom text adventure set during the Cold War on the border between fictional Frobnia and neutral Litzenburg, around a plot involving the arriving US ambassador, told from several viewpoints.
descriptions.c64:139830: After crash-landing on a swampy planet, Borzak must cross five side-scrolling levels to reach his wrecked ship, jumping the many gaps along the way.
descriptions.c64:139838: Worlie the worm finds a hole into a garden of tasty roses, unaware they belong to the king, in this adventure published in 64'er magazine.
descriptions.c64:139841: Two-on-two ice hockey in which each side fields a skater and a goalkeeper, trying to score the most goals in a two-minute match.
descriptions.c64:139842: A motorcycle drag-racing game: pick a Honda Hurricane, Suzuki Katana, Kawasaki Ninja or Yamaha FZR and race the clock or the championship record.
descriptions.c64:139861: Port of Capcom's horizontally scrolling arcade shooter where Lieutenant Henry, with a second player as Sergeant Sanders, flies against the Bozon invaders threatening Earth.
descriptions.c64:139862: Fantasy football played by monsters on a field of landmines, where brutal tackles are allowed and the aim is still to score touchdowns.
descriptions.c64:139916: Budget conversion of Namco's Bosconian: a top-down space shooter where each wave has enemy space stations to destroy among rocks and alien fighters, with a scanner to locate them.
descriptions.c64:139917: Guide a basketball through screen-sized platform stages to the hoop at the end, avoiding hazards like glass bottles and laser beams before time runs out; extra balls give points and lives.
descriptions.c64:139919: A futuristic one-on-one ball sport for two players or one against the computer, played over two 90-second halves with two different ways to score points.
descriptions.c64:139920: Bounce a head around a top-down floating maze, collecting enough lips to finish each level and avoiding the creatures that roam it.
descriptions.c64:139921: A watermelon farmer with a pitchfork plants melons and protects them from bouncing Kamungas during a thunderstorm, defeating the creatures by standing beneath them.
descriptions.c64:139922: A Norwegian dodging game: keep clear of colourful bouncing enemies to reach the next level, with only three lives to spare.
descriptions.c64:139923: Up to three players jump on one another to drain energy and bounce ever higher, winning a level by knocking all rivals off the screen. Released on a Commodore Zone cover tape.
descriptions.c64:139931: A human races around a spiral building seen from above, climbing ladders between floors to collect every item while faster reptiles hunt him down.
descriptions.c64:139945: A ten-pin bowling simulation for up to three players, released in the Commodore Pro-Pak collection.
descriptions.c64:140013: Graphical updates of three Dunjonquest role-playing games, Temple of Apshai, Upper Reaches of Apshai and Curse of Ra, exploring dungeons room by room with only the nearby area visible.
descriptions.c64:140017: Manage a stable of boxers whose skills grow with training and fight experience.
descriptions.c64:140018: Hired by Mr. Box, head of a firm that makes oversized freight boxes, the player has to tidy away the crates the factory keeps churning out.
descriptions.c64:140021: Pick from dozens of boxers rated in power, defence and punishment and fight a single bout or a whole championship, with large fighter sprites and an announcer introducing each match.
descriptions.c64:140022: Steer young heavyweights toward a world title through a text-based management interface.
descriptions.c64:140023: Help Bozo stagger home from the pub by the left route, the right route or across the park; each safe arrival earns more pints, and walking straight gets harder as he drinks.
descriptions.c64:140024: In 1912 Hamburg, a detective and his partner Wilhelm investigate a mummy's supposed curse, and must present evidence and the right answers when the superintendent arrives a week later.
descriptions.c64:140026: Sequel to Brain Disease by Bela Erdei: instead of pushing blocks together, arrange balls to meet each level's goal and move on.
descriptions.c64:140027: Tiles bearing sixteen different symbols keep appearing around the edge of the board; select one and flick it in a direction, and it slides until it hits a wall, a diamond or another tile. Bring matching symbols together to clear them, using the shifting diamonds as bumpers, before the border fills up as the pace quickens.
descriptions.c64:140028: A take-away numbers duel for one or two players, inspired by Coined: players alternate removing a chosen amount from a shared pot of credits, trying to force the opponent into a losing position.
descriptions.c64:140029: Draw lines inside a field of coloured shapes to deflect a bouncing ball into the red ones, aiming to beat the previous screen's score before the timer hits zero.
descriptions.c64:140030: An overhead racer on a constantly upward-scrolling road: weave left and right past other cars, switching between low and high gear, with points only earned in high gear.
descriptions.c64:140031: Stranded on an alien world after a crash, recover two ship parts from each of four bases in this multi-screen sci-fi platformer, managing scarce ammunition against mutants.
descriptions.c64:140066: An illustrated text adventure in which an African huntress sets out to rid the jungle of savage monsters.
descriptions.c64:140068: Perform breakdance moves on joystick command in front of two judges, after choosing the colours of everyone's outfits.
descriptions.c64:140069: An Arkanoid-style bat-and-ball game where some smashed blocks release capsules granting extra balls, lasers or a bigger or smaller paddle.
descriptions.c64:140070: An interactive fiction story where the hero meets the Breakers, an old race awaiting a messiah, on the very day their prophecy names, and must persuade them that he is the one.
descriptions.c64:140075: An Arkanoid-style brick breaker bundled with an editor for building or altering levels to make new games. Published on Magic Disk 64 and Game On.
descriptions.c64:140076: A first-person, racquetball-like spin on Breakout: from one end of a rectangular room, return the ball with a square paddle so it chips bricks off the far wall.
descriptions.c64:140077: Drive, leap and shoot through five side-scrolling stages, from mountains and a bridge to plains, a city and finally an airfield, to recover a stolen jet fighter.
descriptions.c64:140078: A two-player goalkeeper duel in the style of Pong, where the winner is whoever keeps their own goal area clearest.
descriptions.c64:140079: The aged wizard Mijkar went mad and turned his palace into a network of chambers sealed by locked doors, which must now be explored.
descriptions.c64:140080: An illustrated English text adventure: the king has fallen ill and the chosen hero must find his cure, though a weak parser makes several puzzles very hard.
descriptions.c64:140081: A football management board game where between two and five players each run a club through a season, strengthening the squad against human and computer rivals.
descriptions.c64:140082: Take on judo Olympian Brian Jacks across eight events, among them running, archery, cycling, football and swimming, in a contest modelled on the BBC show Superstars.
descriptions.c64:140086: Play the bride, wandering Castle Frankenstein and its grounds to gather the lungs, hearts, kidneys and brains her monstrous partner needs, finding keys to open locked doors.
descriptions.c64:140087: A contract bridge program that adds the Blackwood convention and lets you enter specific deals or play random ones, bidding and playing with a computer partner against two computer opponents.
descriptions.c64:140088: Text-only contract bridge: you and a computer partner take on two computer opponents, first bidding for the contract and then playing out the hand while the program keeps score and rejects illegal bids or plays. Each deal is generated from a seed number, so a memorable hand can be dealt again later.
descriptions.c64:140089: Single-player contract bridge with cards drawn on screen, bidding based on five-card Stayman and Blackwood, a bidding review, automatic scoring and warnings for illegal moves.
descriptions.c64:140090: Electronic contract bridge against the computer, with 99 levels that steadily increase in difficulty.
descriptions.c64:140093: Two players captain sailing brigs and try to sink each other, firing a broadside cannon that cannot aim over the bow or stern while the wind keeps changing.
descriptions.c64:140094: Seek a fortune on the roulette wheel or by driving an ice cream van around Brighton, steering clear of sunbathers and runaway elephants.
descriptions.c64:140095: A real-time text adventure in which Sir Gawain, trapped in a dream of the underworld Ulro, must learn five magic words to escape; the story is narrated in the third person.
descriptions.c64:140096: Sneak past a guard to grab cash and valuables on the top floor before the alarm sounds, then get back down to the getaway driver; each heist the guard grows sharper. Also published as Joe Fox.
descriptions.c64:140098: Tactical combat between Napoleonic-era sailing ships, playable in a fast arcade mode where you steer and fire directly or a more detailed simulation mode.
descriptions.c64:140100: A multi-event sports contest that swaps the Olympics for the streets of the Bronx.
descriptions.c64:140102: Roll a bubble across a grid over five levels, collecting red stones worth four points and blue stones worth two.
descriptions.c64:140103: An early-learning game for ages 4 to 8 where children help Soapie the Sea Serpent steer soap bubbles to catch Zeboingers, building prediction skills.
descriptions.c64:140104: A ghost blows a fragile bubble through the rooms of a castle; where he puffs on it decides its path, and candles, fans and other hazards can pop it.
descriptions.c64:140105: Collect every disk icon on the level while leaving the skull and crossbones alone, and stun pursuers with bubbles that float them to the top of the screen.
descriptions.c64:140106: A puzzle-minded platformer about a little imp determined to gather every gem in the land.
descriptions.c64:140107: In the city of Irkon, enslaved by the wizard Vadra, a revived blob uses magic corks from Kintor to seal the giant bottles spewing bubbles that spawn mutant guards.
descriptions.c64:140108: Weave through a strange dimension, dodging waves of bubbles heading your way.
descriptions.c64:140131: Lava is flowing toward a village, and only a wizard who can reverse it can help; first the bewitched local witch needs a magic powder to restore her so she can fetch him.
descriptions.c64:140133: Explore a multi-directionally scrolling platform maze across three zones in search of the exit, jumping gaps, riding lifts and climbing ladders while collecting coins.
descriptions.c64:140134: Buffalo Bill hosts six humorous Wild West events, starting with knife throwing at a spinning board with a woman strapped to it; any event can be retried after a failure.
descriptions.c64:140135: Ride a horse around a single screen herding buffalo through a gate, keeping them from escaping through gaps into the desert.
descriptions.c64:140137: A one-player Centipede clone by Eric R. Smith, published in an FHD Software Twin Pack; not the Antony Crowther game of the same year.
descriptions.c64:140147: Man a ground gun and shoot down helicopters, bombers and the paratroopers they drop; let enough soldiers land and they form a tank that destroys the gun.
descriptions.c64:140150: A Defender-style shooter based on the Gobots cartoon: as Leader-1, invade the planet Moebius to stop Dr. Braxis and rescue captured Gobots and their human allies.
descriptions.c64:140154: Guide a squadron of three ships escorting relief convoys between the planets of the Coman system in this sideways-scrolling shooter.
descriptions.c64:140190: Antony Crowther's take on Centipede, shooting a segmented centipede as it zigzags down the screen toward a ship at the bottom.
descriptions.c64:140191: Pilot a ship down dangerous tunnels into caverns beneath a planet to wipe out nests of mutant bugs, then fly back up to the surface.
descriptions.c64:140192: Ram bugs with your ship to destroy them while red saucers attack whenever you leave the blue safe zones; holding fire grants brief invulnerability at the cost of fuel.
descriptions.c64:140193: As a bug, dive repeatedly from the surface to the seabed to fetch eggs, avoiding fish that swim across the screen.
descriptions.c64:140194: A Centipede-like shooter starring Zappo, a garden-spraying gadget that moves along the bottom of the screen to blast a centipede creature.
descriptions.c64:140195: Clear bugs from a computer's maze-like circuits using bombs, mines, blockades and bug-hunting hatchlings, in a Dynablaster-inspired game with several ways to kill enemies.
descriptions.c64:140196: A two-player cooperative shooter in which one player defends the top of the screen against bugs while the other fires at those crawling up from below.
descriptions.c64:140197: Bugs Bunny burrows through an abandoned mine hunting clues and carrots, digging past spiders, birds and other critters.
descriptions.c64:140198: Joey the builder won the lottery and insists on building his dream house himself, in a tile-matching puzzle game made of single-screen levels.
descriptions.c64:140199: Ben has four houses to build: first he scales a brick wall to fetch his three tools from the top, dodging a weight and a bug, then gets on with the construction while avoiding hazards.
descriptions.c64:140201: Fly a small ship up a vertically scrolling course packed with Polon gun emplacements and blocking walls, fighting through to destroy their mother ship.
descriptions.c64:140202: Two snow-clearing bulldozers leave trails Tron-style over six rounds with varied layouts; force the rival into a trail or wall, while a head-on crash counts as a draw.
descriptions.c64:140206: A darts game with seven ways to score, including Golf, Cricket and standard 501, aiming each throw with joystick or keyboard.
descriptions.c64:140233: Two-a-side volleyball on indoor or beach courts, played solo against the computer, head-to-head, or with a friend teaming up against the computer.
descriptions.c64:140234: Drive through all four seasons in a Bump 'n' Jump-style race, earning extra points by shoving other cars off the road and leaping over water once past 100 mph.
descriptions.c64:140236: Run a club in one of the top three German football divisions, with the genuine teams and players of the time, handling transfers, training and finances.
descriptions.c64:140238: Collect cosmic creatures around a single-screen maze while bunnies breed from a warren, holding them off with a bunny-zapping laser.
descriptions.c64:140239: A BurgerTime-inspired platformer where a chef climbs ladders and walks over ingredients to drop them down layer by layer, assembling four burgers over four levels.
descriptions.c64:140240: Deliver as many men as possible through the bush while avoiding obstacles and an alligator that grows more aggressive as play goes on.
descriptions.c64:140241: A collector hunts the eight rarest butterfly species across several levels in the one place they are said to live.
descriptions.c64:140242: Bertie the Bee cannot resist sweet fruit, even when it hangs in a big spider's web; fly him across the screen gathering pieces of it.
descriptions.c64:140243: A boxing game that allows dirty tactics like kicks and low blows if the referee is looking the other way; bouts run 15 rounds, and a knockdown only ends the round.
descriptions.c64:140244: A budget spoof of Sir Clive Sinclair's ill-fated C5 electric car, with Clive driving it through a series of screens alternating between two styles of play.
descriptions.c64:140247: Before the CADCAM unit debuts at a trade show, a failed memory bank deep in its circuitry must be repaired against the clock.
descriptions.c64:140248: Explore a dungeon, battle monsters and save gold to buy better weapons and armour from a trader in this 2D role-playing adventure.
descriptions.c64:140249: Thrown out after smashing crockery chasing mice, Caesar the Cat looks for a new home in a choice-based story game for children aged three to nine.
descriptions.c64:140250: A trench-coated detective must make contact in Cairo, recover a microfilm and bring it back to the Chief, preferably after finding a missing revolver.
descriptions.c64:140259: Play two 18-hole courses with Leader Board-style swing controls, choosing from 14 clubs and accounting for wind, with a 3D view and an overhead map.
descriptions.c64:140260: As Tiny Goodbite, climb and jump through the floors of a cereal factory to free the other California Raisins, grabbing each level's key.
descriptions.c64:140261: Battle droid Psycho must find seven Doomsday Devices before Professor Hans de Jaberwocky turns humanity into gunge unless paid a ransom of money, BMX bikes and shiny pebbles.
descriptions.c64:140262: Calvin clears caverns of green dinosaurs and flying robotic hats, starting defenceless in a basic suit and stepping on pads to change into different suits.
descriptions.c64:140264: Four rally-raid events: drop a package from a plane onto a target, drive a van clear of rocks, refuel it by waggling against the clock, and cross rocky ground without going too fast.
descriptions.c64:140265: Race through an abandoned castle as quickly as possible, avoiding the traps laid in its rooms. Also known as Castelli Magici and Castelli Incantati.
descriptions.c64:140266: A knight travels through Camelot to recover four strange 20th-century objects that have appeared in the medieval world, in a sword-swinging platform game from Opera Soft.
descriptions.c64:140270: Wipe out enemy waves in each zone using cannons positioned along the bottom and left edges, collecting power-ups; playable alone but designed for two players together.
descriptions.c64:140271: A tennis-like duel between two gunners firing a cannonball back and forth; the first to 15 points wins. From the Cassette 50 collection.
descriptions.c64:140272: Paddle a canoe around a course for the best time, using forward, reverse, rotation and a fire-button throttle, while keeping off the banks.
descriptions.c64:140273: Ride a cannonball through a side-view maze, Baron Munchausen style, searching for the way out.
descriptions.c64:140276: Captain America infiltrates Dr. Megalomann's Doom Tube, three nested cylinders of decks and rooms linked by the Orbivator lift, some of them contaminated by a deadly virus.
descriptions.c64:140277: Pilot a helicopter through a horizontally scrolling cave in the style of Scramble, shooting everything and never touching the floor or ceiling.
descriptions.c64:140278: One or two players climb 20 stacked levels of the invaded planet Icarus, unlocking doors and reaching each lift in a Gauntlet-style shooter with a split screen.
descriptions.c64:140279: Space courier Captain Kelly is trapped aboard the Obsidian 2 after its security system ignores the shutdown code.
descriptions.c64:140281: A space shooter based on the 1987 TV series, set in 2147 on a devastated Earth ruled by Lord Dread and his machines.
descriptions.c64:140282: A box-pushing Sokoban variant with 255 levels and a number of extra features.
descriptions.c64:140283: Steer a spaceman through 13 tunnels to reach the green asteroid. Later given an unofficial English translation.
descriptions.c64:140284: Trapped in the Glen of Coloured Corpses, roam an island town searching for colour-coded keys to the locked doors in order to escape.
descriptions.c64:140285: A kidnap victim of Buck and Jack, still held after the $20,000 ransom demand, must find the money and escape in this text adventure.
descriptions.c64:140286: A Check Man-inspired puzzle game where Capt'n Kidd moves around a 15x12 grid seen from above, reaching and defusing bombs before their timers run out.
descriptions.c64:140290: Players take turns capturing pieces until a set limit is reached, and the higher score wins; play against the computer or a second player.
descriptions.c64:140292: Run a haulage firm: choose contracts, trucks and routes for the best profit while handling hazards and avoiding speed traps on the motorway.
descriptions.c64:140294: A card-matching memory game, with a ping pong game included as a bonus. Published on a Commodore Scene disk.
descriptions.c64:140327: Puzzler that Stavros Fasoulas and Simon Nicol reportedly coded in one night: you move around an Amidar-like grid set over a star field, colouring in the map Painter-style, with touches borrowed from Quedex and Delta. Meant for Firebird's budget label, it went unreleased.
descriptions.c64:140328: A top-down racer where all cars share the same speed and only a win unlocks the next of 18 tracks; prize money buys nitro, mines and other upgrades between races.
descriptions.c64:140330: A Dutch-language racer where you weave around other cars while shifting up through the gears for more speed.
descriptions.c64:140331: Command carrier task forces in the Pacific War as either the United States or Japan, across six scenarios including Pearl Harbor, Coral Sea and Midway.
descriptions.c64:140332: Mr Livewire tidies the classrooms of St. Hexidecimals, a school for crazed coders, turning every large X into a tick while dodging people, creatures and objects.
descriptions.c64:140334: Pop groups of two or more same-coloured bubbles, scoring more for bigger groups and earning a 500-point bonus for clearing the board.
descriptions.c64:140339: Includes a slot-machine take on five-card draw poker: start with 20 points and gain or lose according to each final hand, with the payout threshold rising after 15 hands.
descriptions.c64:140344: Sent by Lady Artemis into the magical Castle Blackstar, an adventurer seeks a precious orb in this text adventure, keeping any other treasure found and scoring points along the way.
descriptions.c64:140345: A master's demon-summoning experiment has overrun his castle and he has vanished, leaving his young helper to tackle the platform-filled halls.
descriptions.c64:140349: Slip into a castle and find its treasure while avoiding guards, bats and the Baron himself.
descriptions.c64:140350: Find Count Dracula's castle, search it for useful items and finally drive a stake through the Count, while dealing with ghouls and zombies, one of which steals whatever you carry.
descriptions.c64:140351: Steer a small ghost around a haunted mansion seen from above, gathering treasures and shooting in four directions. Released in Europe as Mystic Mansion.
descriptions.c64:140356: Lead Simon through ten levels of a nightmarish castle, finding each room's key to open the way onward, toward a chest holding a rough diamond and his freedom.
descriptions.c64:140359: Recover Klingsar's casket from his castle before he takes it back, solving six educational mini-games that test logic, perception, letters and numbers to earn keys to blocked passages.
descriptions.c64:140362: An evil wizard has seized Mydor's sacred Crown; descend below the castle dungeons to his cave, defeat him and bring the Crown back to the throne room.
descriptions.c64:140365: Throw rocks down on raiders storming the castle walls, earning a shield per stage, with a princess waiting after the seventh. An early example of speech on the machine.
descriptions.c64:140366: A text adventure about defeating a warlock and escaping his stronghold, hampered by a picky parser and a misspelling in its own instructions.
descriptions.c64:140367: Infiltrate Nazi headquarters in disguise, retrieve a hidden bomb and plant it at Hitler's bunker, relying on stealth and bribes, since open gunfire quickly brings the alarm.
descriptions.c64:140371: Command the only laser outpost defending the lunar city of Erriam from Jovian saucers, holding out as long as possible.
descriptions.c64:140374: Venture into the catacombs under Count Damion's castle in a fantasy role-playing game where hearts, speed, strength and morale must all stay above zero.
descriptions.c64:140375: Fly against the alien CLIO civilisation through five large horizontally scrolling levels, from a moon base and alien forest to dark caves and an ancient city, with mid-level and end bosses.
descriptions.c64:140376: Ferry bricks by helicopter, one per trip, from a barge to an island to raise a hotel as tall as possible over six days.
descriptions.c64:140377: Aliens, planets, spaceships and monoliths rain from the sky at different speeds and angles, and all must be caught; missing three means starting over.
descriptions.c64:140378: A two-player arena duel set in the future: grab flying objects before your opponent does while fending off satellites and enemy fire.
descriptions.c64:140383: Search underground crystal caverns for seven treasures and bring them back up to the surface in this text adventure.
descriptions.c64:140384: Escape caves against the clock in a side-scrolling platformer where jump height and distance depend on how long the fire button is held.
descriptions.c64:140385: An educational adventure set in the New Stone Age: left behind with her pet rabbit when her tribe moves to its summer cave, Clair must survive until they return.
descriptions.c64:140387: In this Dig Dug-like game, tunnel through dirt to reach and eliminate burrowing creatures before they collapse the Earth's crust.
descriptions.c64:140393: Sequel to Cavelon: gather the door pieces in each dungeon against the clock, now also harassed by a Black Wizard who unleashes birds and archers.
descriptions.c64:140395: Guide a balloon through the perilous caves of Morgor.
descriptions.c64:140396: Ug the caveman wants a change from Brontosaurus steaks and travels nine islands to carry three pterodactyl eggs from the mountains home, one at a time, without breaking any.
descriptions.c64:140398: A Scramble-like horizontally scrolling shooter: carrying bombs and anti-aircraft missiles, push deep into enemy territory, causing damage and collecting treasure.
descriptions.c64:140399: Steer a falling craft left and right through a continuously scrolling cavern, avoiding the walls and picking up fuel capsules to stay airborne.
descriptions.c64:140405: Play both sides between the Torms and invading Humans: rescue the farming robots the Torms took and blow up their power plant in the caverns below.
descriptions.c64:140406: Jetpack through six levels collecting treasure, avoiding traps and keeping an eye on the fuel gauge.
descriptions.c64:140407: Fly a craft through the computer's own innards, past BASIC and Kernal ROM, toward the CPU in a horizontally scrolling shooter full of lasers and narrow walls.
descriptions.c64:140408: Pilot a saucer through a vast cave system on Uranus's moon Oberon, uncovering the knowledge left behind by an extinct civilisation.
descriptions.c64:140449: A text adventure that starts at a brush-covered cave entrance where Long John Silver's silver is said to be hidden.
descriptions.c64:140451: A deadly dungeon crawl packed with monsters such as Mind Flayers and Intellect Devourers, with the demon Asmodeus waiting for any survivor.
descriptions.c64:140453: Michael Cranford, creator of The Bard's Tale, designed this sci-fi role-playing game in which a party drawn from six alien races, armed with weapons and psychic powers, explores space.
descriptions.c64:140457: A vertical, two-player Pong-style tennis game using a metal ball that emerges from a planet-like sphere in the middle of the court in a random direction.
descriptions.c64:140458: Exiles from the planet Rydthar, whose Absolute Control Stations have run amok, settle on its third moon Xydrahpur, only to find new trouble in its caverns.
descriptions.c64:140464: A Centipede-style shooter: move a craft along the bottom of the screen, with a little room to advance, and blast the Centropod as it weaves down from the top.
descriptions.c64:140466: The three Centurions suit up in exo-frames to stop Doc Terror's minions from stealing Tyron Dichromate, a fusion chemical, from the Weapons Development Centre.
descriptions.c64:140477: A karate fighting game for one or two players, built around enrolling in a martial arts school to learn self-defence techniques.
descriptions.c64:140490: Richard Bayliss's first machine-code game, written in an Action Replay monitor: jump moving objects with the space bar to rack up points.
descriptions.c64:140494: A strategy game against the computer or a friend: add bombs to squares until they reach critical mass and burst into neighbouring squares, setting off chain reactions to wipe out the opponent's pieces.
descriptions.c64:140496: Holding half of a sacred medallion, travel to the land of the bear to recover the other half and a blue sapphire in this Jack Lockerby text adventure.
descriptions.c64:140500: Alien savages have overrun ten cities on a distant planet; bomb them flat from a spacecraft so they can be cleansed and rebuilt.
descriptions.c64:140509: A deliberately absurd text adventure where every object is useless and any wrong move ends the game, though a solution does exist.
descriptions.c64:140510: Adaptation of the TV game show: match pairs among 30 numbered panels to reveal parts of a hidden rebus picture puzzle and solve it.
