descriptions.c64:140514: Rise from alleyway scraps to title fights, training with a heavy bag, sparring partners and a skipping rope under a manager, with 11 moves including high and low punches and blocks.
descriptions.c64:140515: Snooker with six reds instead of fifteen for up to eight players; the solo mode challenges clearing the table with a shot allowance that shrinks with each miss or foul.
descriptions.c64:140517: Draft a team based on player attributes and play baseball on a split screen that shows the whole field on one side and the batter on the other.
descriptions.c64:140545: Play one-on-one basketball as Julius Erving or Larry Bird at a single hoop, to a target score or time limit, with spin moves, outside shots and slam dunks.
descriptions.c64:140546: Based on Jules Verne's novel: a scientist sets out to prove Arne Saknussemm's scroll is true, mixing exploration with action sequences on the way to the Earth's core.
descriptions.c64:140603: A crosshair shooter in which squadrons of aliens swoop and bounce toward you, starting at 40 enemies to destroy.
descriptions.c64:140614: A spelling tutor that uses the SAM speech synthesizer to say a word, use it in a sentence and repeat it, then read each letter aloud as it is typed.
descriptions.c64:140615: Skate through isometric, constantly scrolling streets completing the Street Hawks gang's tests to win membership as the new kid in town.
descriptions.c64:140619: Checkers in both colour and monochrome versions, with a computer-versus-computer mode for watching and learning strategy.
descriptions.c64:140620: The Jams of planet Xnyl live on air and love, but their air is running out, so Pin and Ball build an atmosphere machine to save them.
descriptions.c64:140621: A Bomberman-style sequel: with their ship repaired, Pin and Ball head home to rescue the Jams of their planet, facing trickier levels.
descriptions.c64:140622: A virtual chemistry lab with 50 experiments and thousands of reactions that can fizz, boil over or blow up unexpectedly.
descriptions.c64:140623: Pick up atoms with a crosshair and arrange them into the molecule shape shown, with passwords to resume at later levels.
descriptions.c64:140625: Run a nuclear power station through menus, readouts and typed commands such as shutting down generators; the Chernobyl name has no effect on the simulation.
descriptions.c64:140626: Dash across a bridge gathering cherries while boulders crash down from above.
descriptions.c64:140630: A chess fan dozes off over his board and finds himself in a nightmare beside an enormous chess board, a jeering crowd on either side and a task to complete on its squares.
descriptions.c64:140631: After General Guemon conquers Guldred and kidnaps Princess Karen, the knight Gazem, left for dead on Chesterfield Island, sets out to rescue her.
descriptions.c64:140632: A Pitfall-like adventure over a larger world, built on precise jumps over cactus plants and ending with a leap into darkness.
descriptions.c64:140633: Race one of two vintage Chevrolets against the clock through four multi-section levels in an Out Run-style view, shifting between two gears to pass traffic.
descriptions.c64:140634: A Pac-Man clone in PETSCII graphics: eat every cross and the dollar sign while avoiding the monster to move on.
descriptions.c64:140635: Two trucks gather steel girders to build up crunch power before smashing head-on in a game of chicken.
descriptions.c64:140639: His car out of fuel, a man walks through a forest, cinema, ghetto and graveyard full of ghouls, zombies, ghosts and bats to reach the haunted mansion where his girlfriend is held.
descriptions.c64:140640: A text adventure about lasting until morning in a haunted house while tracking down a lost amulet.
descriptions.c64:140641: Board an alien ship orbiting Earth, disable its weapons, trigger self-destruct and escape, exploring its empty isometric rooms.
descriptions.c64:140646: Wally knows where the Pong Dynasty's jade mines are; across 30 single-screen platform levels he collects set items and then a key to advance.
descriptions.c64:140652: Program little robots with visual instructions so they navigate environments, teaching the basics of computer programming.
descriptions.c64:140653: Stranded by a time warp in a warehouse of white blocks, Charlie must push the four purple blocks together to escape.
descriptions.c64:140654: Survivors of a nuclear war are sealed under the city of Cholo by a malfunctioning computer, and robot droids must be sent to the surface to deal with it.
descriptions.c64:140655: A goldfish eats smaller sea creatures and then other fish to grow, moving from bowl to aquarium to river while avoiding piranhas and nets.
descriptions.c64:140656: A Pac-Man-style maze game: eat all the dots while avoiding Bullies, using a limited speed burst and four ghost repellents.
descriptions.c64:140658: Fly a helicopter through a constantly scrolling battlefield in three sections, dodging and shooting helicopters and balloons before attacking a base, with six skill levels.
descriptions.c64:140659: The last helicopter pilot of a doomed squad fights the Evil Empire's tanks to liberate three Free Continents in a side-scrolling shooter.
descriptions.c64:140662: A reworking of Buried Bucks: a helicopter bombs holes in the ground to dig out a different treasure each level, such as oil barrels, money bags and nuclear material.
descriptions.c64:140665: A ladder-climbing platform game made with the Shoot 'Em Up Construction Kit, where the heroes collect bonus items while mostly avoiding enemies.
descriptions.c64:140667: Car park attendant Chubby Gristle eats burgers, chocolate and other treats across flick-screen platform levels in this Monty Mole-inspired game.
descriptions.c64:140668: As Chuck Norris, walk the path to a monastery where a leader is held hostage, fighting enemies in close-up martial arts battles along the way.
descriptions.c64:140669: Test-fly 14 aircraft, including the Bell X-1 and SR-71, each with its own handling, using ten camera views and zoom up to 256x.
descriptions.c64:140671: A reworked Frexel: fly through the strange Frexel-Kejland region, shooting aliens, grabbing flashing pods for firepower and jump energy, and destroying laser locks to open each exit.
descriptions.c64:140672: The board game for one to four players: spin for a number from 1 to 6 and race from square 1 to 100, climbing ladders and sliding down chutes.
descriptions.c64:140673: Princess Cecil of the land of Oms falls ill, and Romek sets out to find the magic cure, carrying at most two items at a time and working out where each one is needed.
descriptions.c64:140674: Defend Earth from the lunar surface in a first-person shooter, aiming a gun sight at alien attackers that shoot back across several stages.
descriptions.c64:140675: A ring-shaped world built around a sun by a vanished alien race is falling toward its star, and its leftover technology and creatures stand between you and saving it.
descriptions.c64:140680: Perform five acts of Circus Morelli: trampoline, tightrope, juggling, knife throwing and leaping clowns, practising each before the full evening show.
descriptions.c64:140682: Sid Chip is stuck inside a nightmare dreamed by The Great Allonso, made of 20 scrolling circus rings, and must find each ring's exit across odd-shaped platforms, avoiding the creatures.
descriptions.c64:140747: A text adventure that opens on a hill south of a looming Citadel, with walls to circle, a raised drawbridge and a moat to inspect.
descriptions.c64:140748: Shipwrecked when the island Yah-Mon surfaces beneath your boat, find the island's citadel, defeat the sorcerer inside and get away in this Quill-made text adventure.
descriptions.c64:140749: Slide a cannon left and right to shoot down waves of aliens bombing their way toward London's underground nuclear reactor.
descriptions.c64:140751: A cancelled street-life game where a down-and-out tries to work his way up and make serious money, similar in spirit to Rags to Riches.
descriptions.c64:140752: Defend a major city against three types of alien assault over 14 levels, flying a craft in a side-scrolling shooter.
descriptions.c64:140757: Jimbo the big-eared elephant crosses five scrolling platform levels full of enemies and traps to rescue his kidnapped cousin, using his trunk to help.
descriptions.c64:140759: A version of Crowther and Woods' Colossal Cave Adventure, first released by Abersoft as Adventure 1 before Melbourne House renamed it.
descriptions.c64:140760: More rebus puzzles from the TV game show Concentration, for two players or one against the computer, matching panels to uncover the hidden puzzle.
descriptions.c64:140761: Bet on horse racing over a meeting of 1 to 50 races; one player aims to reach a million pounds, while two players try to outdo each other.
descriptions.c64:140762: Own five racehorses and campaign them through 20-week seasons, starting with £5000 and aiming to win the Derby at each season's end.
descriptions.c64:140767: Cowboy cleaners Otto and Bobban must tidy a new hotel littered with paper by vandals before guests arrive, floor by floor over eight platform levels.
descriptions.c64:140768: Otto and Bobban return to clean the Addle Hotel; alone or with a friend, run through large levels clearing up while avoiding mutant rubbish.
descriptions.c64:140770: A text adventure in which Clemens asks you to kill Salvius, the man who wrecked his shop.
descriptions.c64:140772: Six party-themed activities for young children, such as blowing out cake candles, singing nursery rhymes and drawing, teaching letters and numbers with adjustable difficulty.
descriptions.c64:140773: Six educational games teaching letters and numbers to children from age three, with selectable difficulty.
descriptions.c64:140781: Galactic strategy set in the year 3714, when rival governors fight for sole rule of the clone sector. Build fighters, cruisers, dreadnoughts, freighters and troop ships, set taxes, keep morale and the economy up, raise tech levels and put down guerrillas while defending your resources.
descriptions.c64:140783: Terry travels through 32 top-down kingdoms to recover the crystals Baron von Bansai scattered, collecting keys and hopping over enemy balls and bugs.
descriptions.c64:140785: Bounce clowns on a seesaw up into rows of balloons; each landing flings the other clown skyward, in a Breakout-like twist.
descriptions.c64:140786: Backgammon for two players or against three levels of computer opponent, with a mode for watching the computer play itself.
descriptions.c64:140787: Six table and arcade games for one or two players: foosball, 3-D pinball, Skee-Ball, billiards, crazy pool and a shooting gallery.
descriptions.c64:140789: A walking cyborg must gather eight machine parts in order within 15 minutes, each one unlocking a new teleporter destination.
descriptions.c64:140790: A two-player cooperative platformer set in 1639 around the magic sword Excalibur, with both characters working together to clear each level fast.
descriptions.c64:140795: Fly a helicopter in a side-scrolling shooter, knocking out missile defences so a B2 Stealth Bomber can destroy the invading enemy's bases.
descriptions.c64:140802: Four musical modes, among them fishing notes from a pool to build a melody the band then plays, and racing a clam to catch notes.
descriptions.c64:140803: Two monkeys sit in coconut trees hurling coconuts at each other to knock the rival out, while dodging birds and incoming fruit.
descriptions.c64:140805: Guide an intruder droid through the computer network of an alien battleship, bombing guards on 16 levels to send codes back to Earth.
descriptions.c64:140807: Free a city from evil magic by recolouring its houses, crashing a train of colours and digits so the parts swap until the needed code is formed.
descriptions.c64:140809: Sequel to Codename MAT: Mat pilots Centurion II against the Myons in the war over Vesta, a planet rich in the precious Karillium.
descriptions.c64:140811: Illustrated text adventure set in 2550: aliens have raided the lunar base Lunar IV and stolen documents able to wipe out whole planetary systems. Disguised as one of them, agent 12-34P follows their trail by star cruiser. A two-word parser drives play, with full-screen pictures for many locations.
descriptions.c64:140812: Start as a mail room trainee in your uncle's company, delivering mail around his towers in hopes of promotion to his other buildings.
descriptions.c64:140814: Minesweeper with colourful graphics and a mine count adjustable from 10 to 50.
descriptions.c64:140815: A memory game of uncovering matching picture pairs against a time limit, with a move counter.
descriptions.c64:140837: American football with voice synthesis, on-the-fly receiver switching and blitz plays, presented in the style of ABC's Monday Night broadcasts.
descriptions.c64:140862: An experimental audio-visual piece by Mel Croucher following a life in a future where a central computer gradually takes control of all records and state functions.
descriptions.c64:140875: Baseball mixing management and play: choose from 25 famous teams drawn from World Series and All-Star history and set lineups by batting average, fielding or ERA.
descriptions.c64:140888: One or two players move ships along the bottom of the screen, shooting upward at alien attackers.
descriptions.c64:140916: A mechanoid explores over a hundred castle locations, outside, inside and in the dungeons, to find 13 bottles of ingredients for a magic spice, carrying up to three items.
descriptions.c64:141070: A single-screen shooter where endless enemies drop in from the top; any that reach the fire at the bottom come back enraged, recolored and much faster.
descriptions.c64:141071: A Tron-style lightcycle duel: steer a cycle that leaves a solid trail behind it and avoid crashing into walls or trails.
descriptions.c64:141072: Elite-style space trading with an inheritance to spend: start out from Antares station in a worn all-purpose glider, buying and selling cargo between colonies, carrying passengers met in station bars and upgrading your ship. Space flight is a top-down Asteroids-style view with hyperspace jumps plotted on a star map, and pirates lie in wait.
descriptions.c64:141073: As a service droid on a distant colony, guard the food crops from ants, ladybirds and other pests that chew through the perimeter fence, while planning buildings and resources to maximise output.
descriptions.c64:141083: Grand strategy around 1900: lead Britain, France, Germany, the U.S., Russia or Japan and use diplomacy, espionage, armies and fleets to seize over 120 minor nations and rival empires.
descriptions.c64:141084: Push colored crates together into single-color stacks and move them onto the exit to advance; careless pushes can leave a level unsolvable.
descriptions.c64:141085: A Mastermind-style codebreaker: deduce a hidden combination of five tokens in ten guesses from feedback on correct positions and misplaced pieces.
descriptions.c64:141087: Crack a hidden code by deduction in this computer take on Mastermind, issued with an Italian magazine's games supplement.
descriptions.c64:141096: Level 9's compilation of revised versions of its Middle-earth trilogy text adventures (Colossal Adventure, Adventure Quest, Dungeon Adventure), now with still pictures.
descriptions.c64:141097: A BASIC adaptation of Crowther and Woods' original text adventure: explore the cave and collect treasure to reach the highest score.
descriptions.c64:141098: Single-player contract bridge with the computer handling the other three hands, using Acol bidding with Blackwood, Stayman and Baron conventions; supports hand entry, save/load, replay and card recommendations.
descriptions.c64:141099: A strong chess program with adjustable settings, move history and a display of the computer's look-ahead; it can even deliver the difficult king, bishop and knight mate.
descriptions.c64:141100: Mahjong under official British rules: 144 tiles, 14 dealt to each player, and discards that other players may claim when the tile completes a set.
descriptions.c64:141101: A Terry Pratchett Discworld text adventure, illustrated in places, on the flat world carried by four elephants standing on the turtle Great A'Tuin, where the usual compass directions do not apply.
descriptions.c64:141102: Spot where the block shown at the bottom left fits within the main grid, then move the white marker there and press fire; each round asks for ten matches.
descriptions.c64:141104: A Western shoot-out: advance up the main street gunning down desperadoes.
descriptions.c64:141105: Dodge head-seeking missiles drawn to your engine energy; cut the engines without crashing and trick the missiles into colliding with each other.
descriptions.c64:141107: As the last soldier standing, fight through a tropical rainforest, an underground labyrinth and Warbringer's fortress to kill the enemy leader.
descriptions.c64:141109: Fly a Lynx helicopter in a behind-view battle game, protecting allied bases from air and ground attack and ferrying soldiers between them, armed with mines and heat-seeking missiles and helped by a map of enemy forces.
descriptions.c64:141119: Clear the field of colorful moving pieces by pushing matching stones together so they vanish.
descriptions.c64:141120: Command customizable armored war machines in futuristic combat, with around 300 weapon combinations plus adjustable size, armor and placement of control centers.
descriptions.c64:141122: Halley's Comet is carrying bacteria that threaten all life on Earth; pilot a spaceship to intercept it and wipe out the organisms.
descriptions.c64:141123: A single-screen platformer starring Donald Duck, also released in the Netherlands as The Duck Game.
descriptions.c64:141125: An official computer-only sequel to Commando that plays more like Gauntlet than the arcade original.
descriptions.c64:141128: Run a large company as its chief executive, choosing which projects to pursue and growing the business.
descriptions.c64:141129: Match pairs of tiles; removing or shifting tiles makes those above fall, so plan moves to clear every one.
descriptions.c64:141132: A logic puzzle: reproduce the number pattern on the right by clicking squares on the left; each click places a 1 and raises neighboring numbers by one.
descriptions.c64:141133: Sequel with new levels: recreate the target number grid by placing ones that also increment adjacent numbers, best tackling the large values first.
descriptions.c64:141135: From the Gamma Strike light gun pack, mostly a scoreboard that records hits made on the external target.
descriptions.c64:141139: Solitaire card patience drawn entirely in PETSCII characters.
descriptions.c64:141142: Squad-level World War II tactics in France: as a sergeant, command ten American or German infantrymen, each with a name, dossier and individual combat skill ratings.
descriptions.c64:141146: Adaptation of Avalon Hill's Statis Pro Baseball board game: manage a team, set lineups and call plays based on season statistics of major league players.
descriptions.c64:141149: Word searches on a 22 by 20 letter grid in normal or Wordsnake form, with themed or mixed lists of 6 to 24 words, solved against a timer.
descriptions.c64:141150: Crossword puzzles on screen, solvable alone or by groups of up to four players.
descriptions.c64:141155: Corps-level wargame of Germany's 1940 invasion of France for one or two players, commanding Axis or Allied land forces against a human or computer opponent.
descriptions.c64:141156: As Conan, storm a castle to defeat Volta, carrying ten boomerang swords and crossing seven levels of lava pits, geysers and spikes with help from gems, keys and a bird ally.
descriptions.c64:141157: First-person maze action in smoothly scrolling pseudo-3D: thirty timed labyrinths each set a task, such as finding a key past a walrus, chasing roaming musical notes or rounding up a zoo's animals, before you head for the exit. A plasma gun, power-up question marks, one-way passages, teleporters, an overview map and level codes complete it.
descriptions.c64:141160: Guide Freezy from his North Pole ice cream stand through the water to the ice cream islands to fill customers' cone orders, in an educational action game from the Early Learning Friends pack.
descriptions.c64:141161: Two-player modern war game mixing military forces such as armies, warships and missiles with finance including the stock market, oil and piracy.
descriptions.c64:141162: Strategic space warfare in the year 2500: drive off an invading fleet of planet pulverizers ravaging your sector of the galaxy.
descriptions.c64:141163: Third in MicroProse's Command series, recreating five Vietnam battles starting with the French defeat in 1954, using an accelerated real-time system.
descriptions.c64:141164: Episodic mini-games with Creatures-like characters: bomb giant monsters from a balloon, then dodge traps and gather potions to fire a cannon.
descriptions.c64:141167: Slide fuse tiles around a single gap so a traveling spark reaches and detonates every bomb on the level.
descriptions.c64:141170: A magazine type-in of Connect Four: drop discs to line up four in any direction.
descriptions.c64:141173: Join the two blue stones while gravity pulls pieces down, aided by green stones and helpful bubbles.
descriptions.c64:141174: Lead an expedition of climbers, sherpas and porters, moving supplies and equipment from Camp 0 up to Camp 6 over a number of days before a final attempt on the summit of Everest.
descriptions.c64:141177: Turn-based conquest for up to eight players: build a continent of at least ten hexagonal provinces, then recruit soldiers at a gold piece each, raise towers and new villages for taxes, and invade rivals. The old king's troops can be set as allies or enemies, and his crusading brother may return to aid them.
descriptions.c64:141187: Captain a battleship patrolling an inland sea in wartime, tracking aircraft, ships and submarines on three radars and destroying them, along with missiles, in action mini-games.
descriptions.c64:141188: A three-way dueling game included as a bonus on the original disk of The Galleon.
descriptions.c64:141190: A Pac-Man-style maze chase published in a 64'er special issue.
descriptions.c64:141192: Christmas in snowed-in Euro-City: with most police off duty, bank robbers, neo-Nazis, fanatics and terrorists run riot, and a pair of officers must restore order.
descriptions.c64:141195: Play a robber raiding the Acme Diamond Co. and an old mine for jewels, hauling them back to the getaway vehicle while evading clever cops, low-flying choppers and deadly ghosts.
descriptions.c64:141200: As detective Basil Byron, look into the odd behavior of Lord Munroe, an adventurer who withdrew from public life after bringing crates and chests home from an Egyptian expedition two years earlier.
descriptions.c64:141280: A platformer inside a deadly nightmare: survive until the alarm rings at 8:12, with each room entered advancing the clock six minutes, while also raising your dream state.
descriptions.c64:141390: Play one of six giant monsters, among them Godzilla, a tarantula and a robot, rampaging through cities such as New York, London, Moscow, Paris or San Francisco in scenarios like escaping, rescuing or flattening a landmark, while humans resist with tanks and jets.
descriptions.c64:141409: Simulates flying the Piper Archer II (PA-28-181) light aircraft, modeling the variables of real flight including the avionics.
descriptions.c64:141791: Drive-and-shoot action: as British agents chasing terrorists who stole a stockpile from a U.N. camp, race a red sports car down a narrow road blasting other cars.
descriptions.c64:141830: One- or two-player soccer played on city streets rather than a stadium, with preset teams or squads assembled from a cast of characters.
descriptions.c64:141877: Stuntman Dennis must recover the pieces of his Oscar, stolen by his cousin and hidden around a film studio's storerooms. Using only accelerate, brake and jump, he rides a motorbike over hazards, collects the parcels holding the pieces and can draw on porridge power for brief invincibility.
descriptions.c64:141878: A Gauntlet-like dungeon crawl: as Sheba or Thor, alone or with two players at once, explore 15 top-down dungeons gathering all the treasure.
descriptions.c64:141997: Inspired by Q*Bert: bounce a spring from block to block to turn every block the target color, while magnets, clouds, raindrops and monsters drift around the screen.
descriptions.c64:142723: As the dragon-like Frognum, use fire breath and magical artifacts found along the way to battle through a dark world and destroy the Tyrant Beast.
descriptions.c64:142732: In 2096, fly an AGX Hypersonic Fighter in a constantly scrolling vertical shooter, bombing flak batteries and defenses to reach and destroy the rogue CPU known as Computer Control.
descriptions.c64:142738: As Slimey the frog, stranded in an asteroid field, find mine entrances and explore the caverns inside to recover the scattered parts of your ship, seen from above.
descriptions.c64:142869: The Avatar, who once restored Lord British to Britannia's throne, is seized by demon-like creatures in the role-playing finale of the Age of Enlightenment trilogy.
descriptions.c64:143900: Side-scrolling platformer with the sixth Doctor, sent to the second moon of Rijar where the Master has seized a heatonite mining base to build a Time Instant Reply Unit.
descriptions.c64:143951: Puzzle platformer: archaeologist Joe Gunn explores a newly found Egyptian pyramid, possibly the Crocodile King's tomb, solving its secrets screen by screen and trying to escape alive.
descriptions.c64:143969: Warehouse puzzle: shove crates one at a time onto marked squares; two crates in a row cannot be moved, and the level ends when every crate is in place.
descriptions.c64:144001: Federation agent Andrew Angello investigates alien attacks on colonised asteroids, starting with EROC 1, where a faint signal is still transmitting.
descriptions.c64:144008: Jumpman-inspired single-screen platformer: cat burglar Corman uses his long-jumping power to grab every diamond across ten screens linked by ladders and lifts.
descriptions.c64:144010: Detective adventure on the Cornish coast: uncover Aylesbury's secret, find a way home and, if possible, recover the lost goblet.
descriptions.c64:144011: As the knight Corom, travel to Peloria to rescue Princess Diana from the sorcerer Targoth, whose freed powers could banish him for good, while facing monsters that come in two strengths.
descriptions.c64:144013: A top-down Zodiac clone in the vein of Shamus and Berzerk: shooting only works while moving, and touching walls or demons is fatal.
descriptions.c64:144014: Magnetic Scrolls text adventure: a fast-rising stockbroker survives attempts on his life amid talk of insider dealing and must clear his name of a crime he did not commit.
descriptions.c64:144016: Two-player Tron-style race with cars instead of cycles: each vehicle leaves a lethal trail, and the winner is whoever boxes in the other.
descriptions.c64:144017: Text-only adventure: the warrior-sage Corya sets out to destroy the dragon that razed the village of Ermahal.
descriptions.c64:144018: Design starships within limited equipment space, trading off weapons, shields and propulsion, then send them into combat against the computer.
descriptions.c64:144020: Pilot the Plasmobile defending an energy source from the Doovries with a plasma cannon whose indestructible ball keeps destroying everything until you catch it again.
descriptions.c64:144021: Flick-screen maze game: pick the Knight, Queen or King fairy, each with different abilities, and rescue four forest princesses from the Underground-dwelling Dark Wizard.
descriptions.c64:144022: A simple take on Moon Patrol.
descriptions.c64:144025: Text adventure starting in an English village with no stated goal; explore with computer companion Bugsy, discover spacecraft and eventually travel into space.
descriptions.c64:144069: Top-view single-screen shooter: a shuttle pilot takes on the demon wizard Shroud and his army, hidden in the tail of Halley's Comet to invade Earth.
descriptions.c64:144073: Steer a crosshair over an elevated single-screen view, shooting aliens that emerge from the back and wander down; hit enough to advance, as escapees reappear at the top.
descriptions.c64:144074: Fly an outdated Cosmic Cruiser to rescue the hostage crew of an Earth space station seized by the invading Rallom Empire.
descriptions.c64:144077: Timed Sokoban-style puzzles aboard a crashed spacecraft: collect all vials of an Earth-saving substance in each cabin and push spare wires into place to fix the electrics and open the next door.
descriptions.c64:144078: One or two players compete in real time on Conway's Game of Life, flying ships that seed digi-bugs which breed by Life rules, while storms briefly freeze the ships.
descriptions.c64:144079: Multi-directional shooter: as a criminal working for the pirate organization The Council, take on increasingly dangerous missions to hijack space trucks.
descriptions.c64:144082: Choose an adventurer from one of five nations (the U.S., England, France, Germany or Japan) to track down Professor Renegade, who foresaw a catastrophic asteroid heading for Earth, in a multi-level action adventure.
descriptions.c64:144085: Across six levels in each of four oceans, eat a quota of fish while dodging eels, sharks, piranhas and falling anchors, with a supply of ink for defense.
descriptions.c64:144087: Light gun shooter from the Magnum Light Phaser pack: defend the planet from aliens sweeping in sine-wave patterns, with accuracy graded as you play.
descriptions.c64:144088: On the planet Cybor two giant robots fight; as the worker droid Cosmonut, roam inside the head of your side's sabotaged robot hunting enemy infiltrators.
descriptions.c64:144126: Hop between towers Q*Bert-style, stamping them down; four towers of equal height forming a square sink into the ground.
descriptions.c64:144128: Platformer with adventure elements based on the cartoon: Count Duckula, Igor and Nanny move their castle to ancient Egypt in search of the Sax, a magical ancient saxophone.
descriptions.c64:144129: Stranded on Planet Cute, Count Duckula must get back to Transylvania, dodging teddies and fluffy bunnies with a ketchup gun of limited ammo as he crosses each screen from left to right.
descriptions.c64:144130: Recreates the Channel 4 words-and-numbers quiz in its original format of six letters games, two numbers games and a conundrum; with no computer opponent, two players are required.
descriptions.c64:144141: A Connect 4-style game for two: take turns dropping counters into seven columns of an upright grid, with an option to set how many in a line are needed.
descriptions.c64:144143: Guide an airship through a treacherous cave system, with beginner, normal and suicidal difficulty levels.
descriptions.c64:144145: Counting practice for ages 3 to 6: pick the requested number of jungle and circus animals from a field of creatures and watch them parade across the screen.
descriptions.c64:144148: Climb from humble beginnings in a rural town to become the star programmer at a Sydney software company.
descriptions.c64:144149: On a week's holiday in a Herefordshire farm cottage, sightsee and chat with locals while hunting for the fortune the late previous owner is said to have buried around the area.
descriptions.c64:144151: Run an English county cricket team for several seasons, chasing the title and cups in limited-overs matches set between 40 and 60 overs.
descriptions.c64:144157: Poker for up to three people facing one of eight opponents shown in digitized photographs.
descriptions.c64:144168: Single-screen platformer: guide a hungry pig across platforms catching the food that scrolls past, since failing to eat enough means starving.
descriptions.c64:144169: A cowboy dueling shooter where aim matters more than a quick draw.
descriptions.c64:144170: Western quick-draw duel in the spirit of Midway's Gun Fight: two gunslingers face off across the screen, or one player takes on Bad Bob, a sharp-shooting computer opponent. It offers tournament play, many settings, varied arenas including a nod to the Atari VCS, and hats that fly off when hit.
descriptions.c64:144171: New edition of Cowboy Duel that keeps the original showdown and adds three gentler versions of the computer gunslinger Bad Bob, giving less practised players a real chance of winning a gunfight.
descriptions.c64:144173: Fend off aliens by hurling cowpats at them.
descriptions.c64:144185: Ben and Andy, top special forces officers, infiltrate Atlantis, an industrial city seized by the mad scientist Mr. K and his army of artificial soldiers, to stop his bid for world conquest.
descriptions.c64:144186: The Mastermind codebreaking board game on screen, from a German disk magazine.
descriptions.c64:144187: Alone or cooperatively with a friend, collect all the crack rocks scattered across the floor in a Pac-Man-like game.
descriptions.c64:144188: Text adventure as Sam Gamgee, starting outside the gates of Cirith Ungol and crossing the ash wastes of Gorgoroth beneath the smoke of Mount Doom.
descriptions.c64:144189: Illustrated text adventure following the first volume of The Lord of the Rings, as hobbits Frodo, Pippin and Sam carry the Ring toward Mount Doom; the game comes in two parts.
descriptions.c64:144190: Illustrated text adventure following The Two Towers as either Frodo or Sam, closely tracking the book's plot.
descriptions.c64:144201: To destroy the Dark Lord, gather items including the True Ring and cast them into the Crack of Fire in the heights of the Mountains of Moldak, aided by your companion Garston.
descriptions.c64:144203: Breakout clone: bounce the ball off your bat to clear every brick, with falling icons that help or hinder, such as a level skip, ball catch and double balls.
descriptions.c64:144208: Short of money in a small-town hotel opposite the Cranmore building, plot to steal the famous Cranmore Diamond on exhibit there.
descriptions.c64:144215: A Head On-style driving game: speed around collecting dots while avoiding collisions.
descriptions.c64:144216: Futuristic top-down racer on a straight track that narrows and widens, with potholes, gaps and islands to swerve around or jump, and rival cars that try to ram you off; adapted from Burnin' Rubber but never published.
descriptions.c64:144254: Horizontally scrolling space shooter mixing traditional aliens with oddball foes like strawberries and floppy disks.
descriptions.c64:144255: Steer a balloon toward the way out of a cave without touching the spiked walls and ceiling.
descriptions.c64:144256: As balloon pilot Nathan Wigglesworth with co-pilot T.C. Barton, float through 26 side-view single-screen levels to the exit without touching walls or objects that would burst the balloon.
descriptions.c64:144264: As a clown, stop a mad bomber from blowing up a fairground rollercoaster, running along its top in flick-screen side view with a scanner showing you, the bomber and the bomb.
descriptions.c64:144265: Mad Planets-inspired single-screen shooter: from a ship seen from behind, blast celestial bodies hurtling on erratic paths across successive levels to restore order to the universe.
descriptions.c64:144266: Drive a turbocharged Ferrari F40 capable of over 300 mph across America to expose corrupt police running a stolen car racket, choosing routes at forks in the road.
descriptions.c64:144294: Platform shooter: collect every box on the level while avoiding the alien, with limited ammo that the boxes can replenish.
descriptions.c64:144300: Jog along a beach, jumping and ducking past wildlife to reach the distance marker at each level's end, with bonus stages between levels.
descriptions.c64:144417: As Howard the Robot, fix the mess left by Zigmund across four scrolling maze levels, laying paving stones where needed and dodging creatures.
descriptions.c64:144419: Platformer: collect all the hearts on each screen to move on, past roaming monsters and falling hazards.
descriptions.c64:144420: Unarmed Sue, lost in a magical, dark forest, searches for the way out while evading its cunning inhabitants.
descriptions.c64:144421: Updated version of the scrolling platformer in which weaponless Sue seeks the exit of a dark, magical forest full of hostile creatures.
descriptions.c64:144935: Command an interceptor-class ship sent to the Caldorre system, whose three planets' merchants are being raided by agile space marauders that giant battleships could not catch.
descriptions.c64:144937: Educational program: build creatures from heads, bodies, arms and legs, learn programming basics by making them dance, and practice pattern matching, including duets with a computer-made twin.
descriptions.c64:144939: Made with the TSB bank: as Cred, rescue Interrestials from prisons across four single-screen top-view maze levels.
descriptions.c64:144945: A demanding Space Invaders clone with a title intro and music, included in several Keypunch compilations.
descriptions.c64:144947: Fly a space shuttle over an alien planet while the computer steers; release bombs to destroy the enemy cities on your route.
descriptions.c64:144964: Limited-overs cricket pitting England against the West Indies, with editable player names and a choice of who bats first, viewed from above at an angle.
descriptions.c64:144968: Sixty-over cricket against the computer or a friend, using a custom side or one of the two preset teams, England and a World XI, with a toss deciding the batting order and a selectable skill level.
descriptions.c64:144981: Cricket management against the computer as one of the top seven international sides, in single matches or series of three or five one-day games lasting 40 to 60 overs.
descriptions.c64:144983: The manager of an English cricket team bound for the Caribbean island of St. Malcolm, secretly sent to win rights to its guano, survives a hijacking and a plane crash on the way.
descriptions.c64:144984: Breakout without a paddle: steer the constantly bouncing ball sideways to dissolve blocks of its own color, using asterisk blocks to change that color.
descriptions.c64:144985: Act as a judge passing sentence on defendants already found guilty, in cases ranging from perjury and theft to murder, earning up to ten gavels for matching the sentence a real judge chose.
descriptions.c64:144986: Mystery adventure controlled by clicking words beneath the pictures: two hitchhiking friends stop to shelter from a downpour and stumble into a mystery.
descriptions.c64:144990: Verb-noun adventure with optional graphics: answer King John the Good's call to find Princess Sabrina, missing for two weeks, in Transylvania's dark forests.
descriptions.c64:144993: Fly a hovering craft mostly eastward to destroy alien anti-matter machines before they push the solar colonies' power sources to critical mass.
descriptions.c64:144995: A shooter with platform elements built with the Shoot 'em Up Construction Kit and clearly modeled on Thalamus' Creatures.
descriptions.c64:144998: Question all the suspects after a bank robbery; crack the case to keep your job.
descriptions.c64:145004: Your unarmed friends cross dangerous landscapes toward the Evil Master's castle to recover stolen treasure, and you protect them with a crossbow, shooting enemies and obstacles in their way.
descriptions.c64:145005: Crossword-meets-Scrabble trivia game for 1 to 4 players: roll a die numbered 1 to 9 to earn either a trivia question or the right to place a tile directly.
descriptions.c64:145073: Build crossword-style words from letters the computer deals out, holding up to four in reserve and discarding unusable ones, aiming for a high score.
descriptions.c64:145075: Pilot a copter drone shooting down alien devices before they hit the cities.
descriptions.c64:145119: Side-scrolling shoot-em-up with Wally Beben music: spy sensors reveal that an evil scientist in an alien base on the moon of Evans has deployed mind control generators.
descriptions.c64:145135: Pac-Man clone: eat dots in a maze while avoiding the ghosts Zippy, Stilty, Gippy and Chris, turning on them with power pellets and grabbing fruit for bonus points.
descriptions.c64:145173: First in MicroProse's Command Series, designed by Sid Meier and Ed Bever, a heavily researched World War II wargame of the campaign in Europe.
descriptions.c64:145174: Second Command Series wargame, covering World War II's North African theater across five scenarios with the same system as Crusade in Europe.
descriptions.c64:145176: A Boulder Dash-like game without deadly falling boulders or a time limit.
descriptions.c64:145212: Search an ancient castle's uncharted depths in the land of Perlain for the crystal orb of the wizard Mylor the Cruel.
descriptions.c64:145350: A three-dimensional brainteaser: assemble a 3x3x3 cube from six oddly shaped pieces made of smaller cubes, across three increasingly hard puzzles, with the option of designing new ones by altering the program.
descriptions.c64:145352: A tile-matching puzzle based on Rubik's Cube, with selectable music for each game and level passwords.
descriptions.c64:145358: Rubik's Cube reimagined from above with all faces visible, letting the player choose from 4 to 25 sides and many starting positions grouped by difficulty.
descriptions.c64:145359: Q*Bert-inspired isometric game: hop on the cubes of a pyramid to change their color, with later levels needing several jumps per cube.
descriptions.c64:145361: Top-down 8-ball pool for one or two players, with a choice of 1 to 9 frames, table color and computer opponent.
descriptions.c64:145363: Educational map-reading program for ages 7 to 13, accompanying the Moving Into Maps pre-atlas book.
descriptions.c64:145365: A head-to-head sailing race against friends or family.
descriptions.c64:145367: Football management: pick one of 40 European teams and steer it through a group stage of five-team groups into the knockout rounds and the cup final.
descriptions.c64:145369: Text adventure: peering into a fairground fortune teller's crystal ball transports you to ancient Egypt, and you must find a way back.
descriptions.c64:145370: Monsters wiped out the people of Babylon, leaving it sealed off; play the lone adventurer who ventures in to destroy the evil ruling it.
descriptions.c64:145371: Sneak past the evil forces of Borgan Castle to find and rescue a princess, using special items to overcome obstacles; converted from 1984 BBC Micro programs.
descriptions.c64:145373: The evil Cult of Sagalia grips Sherwood Forest despite Robin Hood's resistance, and Friar Tuck arranges an exorcism with the Bishop of Derby.
descriptions.c64:145386: Graphic text adventure made with the Graphic Adventure Creator. As Oswald, son of a druid king, you must track down three scattered magic objects and carry them to the island of Rotena to break the wicked wizard Volcan's hold over it.
descriptions.c64:145387: Gothic text adventure as Ashar, who wakes strapped to a rack in a dank dungeon and must escape before the torturer blinds him.
descriptions.c64:145388: Locked inside the Mad Scientist's haunted house, solve puzzles to find the cursed key in an adventure inspired by Mikro-Gen's games.
descriptions.c64:145389: A computer version of the mancala board game Kalaha.
descriptions.c64:145390: Walk Cuthbert around all four sides of each grid cell to color it, filling the whole grid while avoiding the nasties that patrol it.
descriptions.c64:145391: Joust-like levels in two stages; the first has Cuthbert flying a small shuttle between platforms, collecting fuel pellets one at a time and bringing each back.
descriptions.c64:145392: Side-scrolling space flight through a vast industrial complex of halls, tanks and containers. Your craft drifts with convincing inertia, so steering takes practice; packs of bubble-like enemies and any brush with the scenery drain your 99 energy cells, and your gun fires slowly.
descriptions.c64:145393: Infocom text adventure: a professional scuba diver on the sleepy seaport island of Hardscrabble gets a chance to salvage treasure from one of four wrecks.
descriptions.c64:145397: Futuristic American football played in 2022 by two seven-robot teams with a 350-pound bomb in place of a ball, after bionic cheating forced the rules to change.
descriptions.c64:145398: Randomly falling Tetris-like pieces, with arrows marking where each drops and a window previewing the next shape, must be arranged within a marked region of the field.
descriptions.c64:145399: Chess teaching tool: set up a real board and follow four games between grandmasters, guessing each move from multiple-choice options.
descriptions.c64:145401: Follow-up to Bonka: in a flick-screen top-view maze aboard a cosmic space station, gather Platignum while dodging or shooting its Cybermen guards and slipping through open doors.
descriptions.c64:145429: The board game Othello on a standard 8x8 grid.
descriptions.c64:145430: Top-down maze of rooms: collect randomly placed items and touch the safe to finish the level, with eight-way movement and firing, electrified walls and enemies appearing as rooms are entered.
descriptions.c64:145432: Blast through the Cybership's base to hit the man inside, scoring for fighters and scanner ships while dodging the ship's laser.
descriptions.c64:145433: A colorful Armalyte-style horizontally scrolling shooter.
descriptions.c64:145434: Assigned to escort a mothership leaving Earth, a fighter pilot turns instead to defend the planet from an arriving invasion fleet across three parts.
descriptions.c64:145437: As a cyborg hunter, climb huge structures such as space stations, trees and pipes to destroy flying robots, in a game made with the Shoot 'em Up Construction Kit.
descriptions.c64:145438: A Robotron-style single-screen shooter: blast every Tron, Brain and Enforcer droid hunting the last humans and pick up wandering people for bonus points, with an option to aim the laser using a second joystick.
descriptions.c64:145439: Ride an armed, jump-capable motorcycle through several lands in isometric view to rescue the Queen and kidnapped villagers, with five skill levels.
descriptions.c64:145441: Grand Prix motorcycle racing against nine computer rivals in 125, 250 and 500cc classes, on a season of 8 to 15 international circuits.
descriptions.c64:145445: Based on the film: as He-Man, recover the eight chords of the Cosmic Key, which fell to Earth, before Skeletor does, fighting his minions first in the streets.
descriptions.c64:145455: A Space Invaders-style game with a finely detailed cannon sliding along the ground.
descriptions.c64:145467: Roll a ball through cave levels collecting ten magic pots, then reach the exit before time runs out.
descriptions.c64:145468: Puzzle of skill: reproduce the arrangement shown in the right pane on your own side, placing pieces in the correct order or starting over.
descriptions.c64:145469: Isometric puzzle exploration: to earn leadership of the Ostan race, recover 24 objects hidden in a virtual world and bring them back to base, carrying at most five at once.
descriptions.c64:145471: Chess program and sequel to Cyrus, switchable between top-down and 3D isometric boards, with twelve skill levels.
descriptions.c64:145477: Horse racing betting for 1 to 4 players, wagering virtual money on win, place and show or two-horse bets such as exacta, quinella and daily double.
descriptions.c64:145479: Captured by the Daleks, gather ten keys and reach the TARDIS without touching patrolling Daleks, then stand by its door to move to the next level.
descriptions.c64:145483: Robin Hood crosses Sherwood Forest to reach Nottingham Castle and free Maid Marian, held in the East Tower by the Sheriff until Robin surrenders.
descriptions.c64:145503: Arcade adventure with text adventure elements based on the TV school drama, following pupils Gonch Gardner and his friend Hollo.
descriptions.c64:145504: Based on Ade Edmondson's book: gatecrash a refined party and use objects around the house to behave as hatefully and immaturely as possible.
descriptions.c64:145505: Sporting events each with a world record and a qualifying target; missing one costs one of three lives, and a completed set repeats with tougher targets.
descriptions.c64:145506: Shoot-em-up as a film stuntman tackling seven scenes such as desert chases, forest rallies and Grand Canyon jumps, packed with bad guys and obstacles.
descriptions.c64:145507: Berk and little Drut head down through the trap door into the gloomy depths to rescue the captured Boni.
descriptions.c64:145564: Try to breach a dam while its defenses fire at you.
descriptions.c64:145614: Horizontally scrolling Scramble-like shooter through narrow passages, destroying wall-mounted guns with bonus weapons and shields over three boss-capped levels.
descriptions.c64:145618: As an astronaut on an alien planet, tunnel to the lowest pit for one or more large jewels, then climb back out via the upper pit to the waiting spaceship as an enemy tank and monsters close in.
descriptions.c64:145619: Amidar-style grid maze: trace all four sides of numbered boxes to add their values to your score while avoiding roaming enemies.
descriptions.c64:145620: Two-part scrolling hack-and-slash: find three magic scrolls in the first part, then enter its password to start the second and rescue the other wizards.
descriptions.c64:145622: Gauntlet-like top-down action: Storm and his wizard friend, alone or with two players at once, fight monsters and grab treasure on the way to rescuing Storm's wife Corrine from Una Cum's laboratory.
descriptions.c64:145623: Tag team wrestling as the heroic or villainous pair, relying on teamwork and stamina to win the World Super Championship title.
descriptions.c64:145624: Vektor Grafix's 1988 conversion of Atari's Star Wars arcade game, rebuilt from scratch after Parker Brothers' earlier cartridge: fly an X-wing against TIE fighters, over the Death Star's surface and down the trench.
descriptions.c64:145626: As a Troll, roam platform levels rescuing baby trolls, gathering a minimum number on each level before leaving through the Pigstop.
descriptions.c64:145650: Single-screen platformer: collect every object on each level before reaching the damsel, following safe routes since you cannot drop off platforms.
descriptions.c64:145651: Text adventure with no objects or inventory, where talking to the ever-present Melissa gives messages that vary with time and place.
descriptions.c64:145654: Music program: set bass, beat, tempo and endings in styles like jazz, rock, blues and boogie-woogie, play an instrument over it, and save creations to disk.
descriptions.c64:145655: Jump-and-run with a car: leap, dodge and shoot obstacles on the way to the destination, grabbing fuel to keep going.
descriptions.c64:145656: Steer a UFO through caves searching for swords.
descriptions.c64:145657: Colonel K sends Danger Mouse and his assistant Penfold into the Black Forest to destroy Baron Greenback's secret weapon, the Pi-beam.
descriptions.c64:145658: Baron Greenback has built a Danger Mouse clone; tackle three stages mixing platform and shooting action, starting with an Aerocar flight blasting villains.
descriptions.c64:145659: Two-screen platformer: jump between five floors collecting keys and shooting birds and bats.
descriptions.c64:145661: Pac-Man-style collecting game as the Eye of Sauron: eat every dungeon pellet without touching the Danger Stones, which multiply while cover shrinks on later levels.
descriptions.c64:145662: Text adventure: your power has been cut off over an unpaid bill you threw away, so track down the electricity board's office and settle up.
descriptions.c64:145663: Maze-like arcade adventure following Dante's journey through hell, carrying two objects at a time; the items needed all lie in the opening forest, so plenty of backtracking is required.
descriptions.c64:145664: Law graduate Frederick Davies, celebrating at The Swan pub, accepts a drunken dare that leaves him locked without his clothes inside a department store after closing, and must escape.
descriptions.c64:145665: Jump a motorcycle over a growing row of cars, with the ramps moving apart and a car added after each landing, plus a hoop jump midway through the course.
descriptions.c64:145667: From one captured city on an alien planet, build sea, land and air transport and train troops, ordering units to move, attack or hold as you expand your empire.
descriptions.c64:145673: H.E.R.O. clone: a treasure hunter with a jetpack, short-range beam weapon and few bombs descends underground, trying to reach the exit before energy runs out.
descriptions.c64:145675: First-person graphic adventure with RPG elements: armed with attributes such as strength, wisdom and intellect, explore a red dragon's dungeons for the casket holding their secret.
descriptions.c64:145677: A hacked version of Ulrich Mühl's vertically scrolling shooter Raid, modified by Stefan Vocke, with fresh music by Alexander Rotzsch.
descriptions.c64:145736: Eight offbeat events: sack race, throwing a boot, climbing a pole, running up a wall, plate balancing, river jumping, pillow fighting and pogo.
descriptions.c64:145742: As a rooster determined that his hen hatches at least one chick, guard the eggs she lays in two rows of nests so at least one survives.
descriptions.c64:145757: Text and graphics adventure: a treasure hunter on a Caribbean island seeks buried pirate gold, passing a tricky maze and fierce alligators to reach the chest of doubloons.
descriptions.c64:145758: After centuries of pollution, survivors live under an energy dome while creatures roam outside; as Doc, create a character and try to persuade people back to the surface.
descriptions.c64:145759: Role-playing on Dilmun, an island refuge twisted into a land of horror by Namtar; a party of four starts in the city of Purgatory with nothing, and magic has been outlawed.
descriptions.c64:145760: As Agent 17, codenamed Otto, grab secret documents from a 30-floor building and flee in the getaway car waiting in the basement while enemy spies try to kill you.
descriptions.c64:145761: Fly an F-16 on dogfights, bombing raids and reconnaissance, planning waypoints on the tactical map and optionally choosing weapons before takeoff.
descriptions.c64:145762: Collect parts across the 16 robot-infested rooms of Fred's factory against a strict time limit; unarmed, Fred can only jump over the dangers.
descriptions.c64:145763: Based on the TV series: a stuntman films five movie scenes, starting with a run across railway cars dodging rock-dropping birds and jumping stove pipes.
descriptions.c64:145764: Two modes; the first is a top-down mission to destroy Cobra HQ, enemy tanks and radar stations in woods, desert and tundra using vehicles such as Ace's jet and Steeler's tank.
descriptions.c64:145766: Step through a magic mirror into the alterworld to overthrow Nequam, the Dark Lord who murdered your grandfather, in an adventure of scene descriptions and one- or two-word commands.
descriptions.c64:145767: With your starship's engine blown in orbit, go down to the Dark Planet to collect the Viridian crystals needed for repairs.
descriptions.c64:145769: A text adventure set on a moonbase during a stalled Mars colony project: after a bomb attack by the terrorist Mining Group, uncover your own mission and the group's motives through typed commands.
descriptions.c64:145772: World War II strategy and action: as tank commander Lone Wolf, move across an overhead map of North Africa to protect Allied depots from Rommel's attacks.
descriptions.c64:145773: Help a circus raise a $10,000 loan payment in one night through six acts, while the bank's evil clown Fiendish Freddy tries to sabotage them.
descriptions.c64:145774: Formula One simulation with Ferrari's backing against 1986's leading drivers and teams, including development work at Maranello, in the wind tunnel and on the test track.
descriptions.c64:145809: Port of the 2013 mobile game: flap a bird through gaps between green pipes without touching them.
descriptions.c64:145810: Single-screen shooter: move a ship up and down along the left edge, blasting waves of aliens arriving from the right, each wave attacking three times in changing colors.
descriptions.c64:145854: Early real-time strategy for up to four players giving orders simultaneously, as dwarves, humans or elves battling for the kingdom of Darkhorn across nine regions of varied terrain.
descriptions.c64:145855: Opening half of a two-part story told in text: tramp through marshes, wear magic shoes and kiss a mermaid while saving the land from the Black Wanderer with the magic of the Silent Song.
descriptions.c64:145904: Leap through a strange world, defending against attackers by hurling a very elastic ball that knocks them down.
descriptions.c64:145905: Ultima-inspired RPG with dark dungeons that need a torch or light spell, and single-letter spells for each caster class as in Ultima III.
descriptions.c64:145917: Dunjonquest adventure: as mercenary Brian Hammerhand, recover the sacred stones and return with Rex the Reaver's head.
descriptions.c64:145918: After a plane crash in the African jungle, Stan sets off armed only with a rock to rescue his girlfriend Megan, whose scream he hears from the trees.
descriptions.c64:145941: Asleep by the open fridge, Garfield dreams of the Swiss Alps across three mini-games playable in any order: skiing to a lasagna factory, keeping mechanical chickens fed with chocolate, and skating a frozen lake while Odie makes mischief.
descriptions.c64:145942: Magnetic Scrolls text adventure set in Kerovnia: as an aspiring member of the Guild of Thieves, steal every valuable from an island castle and its surroundings.
descriptions.c64:145945: Guide a frog through three locations: up from underwater past alligators and fish, riding turtles, then across logs, birds and a whale to a life preserver trailing a tugboat.
descriptions.c64:145946: Rescue a friend held on the manor's top floor by passing five screens, starting with a game of tag with a friendly ghost or skeleton in the graveyard to earn spears.
descriptions.c64:145947: Isometric adaptation of the board game: lead a wizard, dwarf, barbarian and elf through 14 turn-based missions to defeat the evil wizard Morcar.
descriptions.c64:145955: Joust-inspired: as the Queen's Champion on a flying ostrich, defeat evil knights by striking from above, turning them into eggs.
descriptions.c64:145961: As a cop, run surveillance on a warehouse from a van's monitors to break a drug ring, directing a rookie who searches rooms, plants bugs and questions suspects.
descriptions.c64:145963: Rail shooter as an LA police officer: aim an Uzi's sight at gangsters as the view moves automatically, taking ammo and body armor from fallen gang members.
descriptions.c64:145964: Search underground for Lady Tut's sarcophagus through five mazes, gathering rings, avoiding creatures and finding each maze's key to unlock its exit.
descriptions.c64:145965: Isometric spin-off in the style of Crystal Castles: as Lode Runner's daughter, run and jump through 46 levels to free her father from the Bungeling Empire.
descriptions.c64:145966: Explore a multi-level diamond mine, gathering diamonds worth 1,000 points before seeking the hidden crown and escaping to the top alive.
descriptions.c64:145967: First game of the dungeon-crawling RPG series: six adventurers piece together the deliberately vague secret of the Inner Sanctum.
descriptions.c64:145968: Illustrated interactive fiction drawn from the opening two books of Roger Zelazny's Amber series, The Guns of Avalon among them, released under Spinnaker's Telarium label.
descriptions.c64:145969: Walk the beat as a constable on a crowded street, clubbing robbers and hauling each one into the waiting van before they can slip into a building and steal cash; troublesome punks can be clubbed too.
descriptions.c64:145970: Mama Pig rides a cable car up and down a cliff, shooting at wolves floating down on balloons to keep them from reaching the ground, climbing the ladder and grabbing her piglets.
descriptions.c64:145971: Keep a quirky toy factory running for Industrial Might and Logic, operating its machinery through the night so it turns out the right action figures, including Star Wars toys.
descriptions.c64:145972: Dave Speed roams a strange land stomping on the creatures that attack him; eating chicken legs makes him angry enough to destroy foes simply by walking into them.
descriptions.c64:145973: Text adventure that begins in 1927 aboard a lifeboat, the only survivor of the lost clipper Allana, carrying Big Jake, Pedro, Shamus, a woman and a small dog adrift in the open ocean.
descriptions.c64:145974: Davy has lost his gal, his clothes and his gear to raiders; cross each flick screen from left to right, collecting the item waiting on the far side while avoiding the hazards in between.
descriptions.c64:145975: Sequel to Motorhead in which the enemy forces return in a later age and must be driven back one section of the planet at a time. Published on the Game On disk magazine in 1989.
descriptions.c64:145976: Vertical scrolling shooter driving an armed vehicle past tanks, mines, helicopters and strafing jets while steering clear of walls and scenery. Published on the Game On disk magazine.
descriptions.c64:145978: Board-game style adaptation of C.S. Lewis's The Voyage of the Dawn Treader, sailing the ship through storms, hurricanes and sea serpents; it was packaged with the novel, cards and dice.
descriptions.c64:145979: Baseball instruction built with Dave Winfield: five lessons on grip, stance, pitching and other fundamentals, followed by a game mode called Slugfest.
descriptions.c64:145985: As a Maneuverable Armed Computer Human, free three planets from the robot Nektron by destroying a quota of specific enemy types in top-down, multi-directionally scrolling stages.
descriptions.c64:145986: Party-based fantasy RPG viewed from above: Lukas and his companions set out to keep the demon Dreax sealed inside the Magic Candle before the candle burns away.
descriptions.c64:145987: Defender-inspired scroller over a looping landscape, protecting a home base while Quarriers steal its parts to build an enemy base and Drayns drain energy to supply it.
descriptions.c64:145988: Help a penguin get home across a scrolling snowfield, jumping crevasses and dodging rolling boulders while a clock counts down.
descriptions.c64:145990: Space flight and combat combined with trading and character interaction, switching between fast Cruise Flight for travel and Newtonian Flight for dogfights as a main story unfolds.
descriptions.c64:145991: Graphic adventure set between the World Wars that gently mocks the attitudes of the late British Empire through its stiff-upper-lip heroes.
descriptions.c64:145993: The eleventh and last Mysterious Adventure: after a day at the fair, a nap in the waxworks leaves the player locked inside, unsure whether it is all a dream. The parser now accepts full sentences.
descriptions.c64:145996: Motorcycle racing in the 80cc world championship, licensed around Spanish champion Jorge Martinez 'Aspar' and featuring rivals such as Alex Criville, with practice, qualifying and race sessions.
descriptions.c64:145997: Laurel and Hardy try to hit each other with cream cakes, first locating the cake shop to stock up, on a split screen showing the town from the side above and below a central status panel.
descriptions.c64:146000: Two-part text adventure about piloting a stealth fighter into the Soviet Union to avert a global disaster, while uncovering why a contact was murdered and what is hidden in an old farmhouse.
descriptions.c64:146001: Vertical run-and-gun shooter starring a big-nosed, bird-like hero who fires ring-shaped shots that disintegrate aliens. Released on Commodore Zone issue 6 in 1996.
descriptions.c64:146002: Educational game in which Charlie Fix-it lives inside the computer repairing faults; each session starts with a round of the capture game Gotcha! against the computer.
descriptions.c64:146007: Third Ikari game, a brawler in which the commandos fight through enemy forces to rescue a presidential candidate's kidnapped daughter.
descriptions.c64:146015: Infocom mystery set at Tresyllian Castle in Cornwall, where Tamara Lynd, newly engaged to its owner, is being haunted by a White Lady and fears for her life amid rumors of hidden treasure.
descriptions.c64:146040: Command a squad of droids clearing bombs from a building, passing explosives between rooms linked by doors, trapdoors and poles and hurling them outside before they detonate.
descriptions.c64:146041: Private eye Sam Miller investigates how Miles Dunbar died; the story opens with a police interrogation, then flashes back a day so the clues and witnesses can be pursued.
descriptions.c64:146042: As sheriff of Dodge City, gun down the bandits who have taken over town, picking up ammunition from fallen foes and ducking into the hotel to quench a rising thirst.
descriptions.c64:146043: Illustrated text adventure spoofing the soap EastEnders, set in Herbert Square with renamed versions of the show's characters.
descriptions.c64:146044: Defend New Stratford from an alien fleet in a top-down shooter with rotational controls, ramming enemy craft and blasting the mothership bases that appear in each section.
descriptions.c64:146045: Night-and-day road race in which the driver must overtake 70 cars within 80 seconds; each later stage allows less time.
descriptions.c64:146046: Fly a Ford Prefect 2174 down a corridor through nine levels of Quasar Star Fighters to stop Darth Fader from destroying Earth with the Death Star.
descriptions.c64:146049: A warrior who survived a childhood raid by the monsters of The Evil Ones sets out to recover the stolen scrolls and the captured princess.
descriptions.c64:146050: Party-based fantasy RPG in Ashtalarea, where a custom group of adventurers sets out to rescue the Duke and the warrior Seggallion from the villain Pildar and defeat him.
descriptions.c64:146051: Two-player single-screen duel in orbit: each ship slides only left and right and uses drifting asteroids as cover while shooting at the opponent.
descriptions.c64:146053: Futuristic first-person race piloting an armored skimmer around a four-section ring, where the outer edge is the riskiest lane and rivals try to wreck the competition.
descriptions.c64:146054: Build a ladder from pieces on the far side of the screen to reach a yellow switch at the top, sheltering from acid rain in buildings that slowly dissolve too. From the Magic Disk 64 magazine.
descriptions.c64:146058: Stop the resurrected wizard Azazael from gathering five gems of power across the land of Mezron, exploring in 3D and fighting medusas, priestess cults and the undead.
descriptions.c64:146061: Star Wars inspired shooter that plays a version of the film's main theme: launch, fight off enemy fighters in space, then fly down the battle station's trench to hit its exhaust port.
descriptions.c64:146107: A detective stalled on a case against a crime boss finally tails one of the gang's stooges to a hotel, knocks him out and turns the items he carried into a fresh lead.
descriptions.c64:146120: Pilot a submarine rescuing fellow divers in flimsy scuba gear from giant fish; touching one of the fish costs a life.
descriptions.c64:146137: Ultima-style RPG with a Japanese flavor: Emperor Nakamoto calls on a party drawn from eight races and sixteen classes to defeat the Deathlord and his demon army.
descriptions.c64:146142: Wartime strategy game in which the outnumbered Allies must wreck The Enemy's nearly finished atomic research before it decides the war.
descriptions.c64:146149: Mini-game collection based on the 1950s TV sitcom: the Kramdens and Nortons scramble to earn enough money to hold the Raccoon Lodge meeting in Miami Beach.
descriptions.c64:146150: Sent to Hell by mistake after dying in hospital, the player is tasked by Lucifer with foiling Adolf Hitler's plot to raise an army of the damned and seize the underworld.
descriptions.c64:146155: Set of pseudo-3D arcade stages in which a mounted, spear-throwing knight fights his way into a castle to rescue a maiden held by a seven-headed dragon.
descriptions.c64:146169: Recover the treasures on each of eight levels by finding colored keys in other rooms, which unlock the cavern doors whose color matches the screen border.
descriptions.c64:146180: Logic puzzle in which a fixed path must be walked to the exit before time runs out, while the route itself changes underfoot. From Starlight Magazine #5.
descriptions.c64:146181: Space Taxi-style cave flyer: hover a craft from the white home pad to the blue target pad and back without grazing walls or obstacles, as visited pads turn yellow.
descriptions.c64:146183: A surface ship fights off submarines and armed jellyfish below, sidestepping the missiles and mines they send up and dropping its limited, slowly replenished supply of water bombs.
descriptions.c64:146184: Fly escort in a Second World War bomber raid on a Nazi fuel depot, shooting down incoming fighters, including red planes that fire back and black suicide planes, to protect the bomber ahead.
descriptions.c64:146186: Scuba diving game: collect the treasure chests on the seabed while dodging dangerous sea creatures, all before the oxygen supply runs dry.
descriptions.c64:146187: Mostly text-based simulation in which a Defense Department operative runs the Ballistic Missile Defense network of ground and space-based systems to stop incoming missiles from hitting the United States.
descriptions.c64:146191: Aliens have hijacked Earth's orbital Star Wars defense network to wipe out eight cities; Captain Nick Diamond flies an Eagle fighter to destroy them and the satellites, earning double lasers at 1000 points.
descriptions.c64:146197: Archaeologist Mac Steele, poisoned by an artifact he unearthed, races through Aztec ruins hidden in Mexico in search of the fabled Mask of the Sun, his one hope for a cure.
descriptions.c64:146205: Flash Gordon, the Phantom, Mandrake and Lothar storm Ming the Merciless's castle to rescue their kidnapped children; Flash shoots through side-scrolling areas and can summon his allies' help.
descriptions.c64:146208: Roam a dungeon gathering items while avoiding monsters and spiders, bouncing the robots' laser shots back to kill the spider that haunts the place.
descriptions.c64:146214: Point-and-click mystery set in Chicago, December 1941: the hero wakes with no memory and must piece together what happened, using several on-screen windows and bitmapped scenes.
descriptions.c64:146216: Robots Jim and Bob set out to rescue a kidnapped princess in a constantly scrolling platformer, jumping obstacles and shooting or dodging creatures without getting trapped by the screen edge.
descriptions.c64:146225: Harder sequel to Defuzion: grab the moving sticks of dynamite while avoiding monsters, all before the clock runs out. Released on Commodore Scene #31.
descriptions.c64:146231: Fifteen Dell crosswords of varying difficulty, with tools to check words and the grid and built-in hints for tough clues.
descriptions.c64:146270: Robin wanders Sherwood Forest robbing rich nobles and finding moneybags to buy gear from a tree spirit, then enters the Sheriff of Nottingham's contest to win back the Silver Arrow.
descriptions.c64:146271: A spy rides elevators up the floors of the Soviet embassy, dodging guards who constantly move on lifts, collecting the fragments of an encrypted message.
descriptions.c64:146272: Climb the outsides of 48-story buildings grabbing cases of cash while avoiding falling objects and monsters, which can be squashed flat but soon return.
descriptions.c64:146274: Tag-team wrestling for one or two players, choosing a pair from eight grapplers such as Mr. Cool, Sgt. Slam, Tomahawk, Viking and Ninja, each with a spoken intro.
descriptions.c64:146275: Based on the film: Roger, framed for Marvin Acme's murder, must locate the missing will that leaves Toon Town to the Toons and keep Jessica safe from the weasels and Judge Doom.
descriptions.c64:146287: Elvira fights through two big platform levels, one of fire and one of ice, gathering weapons and power-ups to slay the monsters in her way.
descriptions.c64:146339: Children's turtle-graphics program that teaches programming concepts by drawing colorful pictures through simple commands, aimed at ages 4 to 14.
descriptions.c64:146340: In 2027, a reporter who survived the nuclear destruction of Chicago thanks to an experimental robotic space suit explores the poisoned ruins.
descriptions.c64:146346: Railway management simulation written in BASIC about keeping British Rail's Class 55 Deltic locomotives running safely and to schedule.
descriptions.c64:146354: Breakout variant played sideways: move the bat up and down to knock the ball across the screen at blocks, with a construction kit for designing levels.
descriptions.c64:146355: Phoenix-style shooter: a laser cannon along the screen's lower edge faces waves of colorful demons that swoop in odd patterns and rain bombs and lasers.
descriptions.c64:146356: A small, shaggy blue demon runs and jumps through dungeons full of fallen angels, gargoyles and wasps, picking up gems, vials of energy, drops of blood and helper creatures.
descriptions.c64:146358: Ten years after the wizard Ashmeard took Drakon's Golden Mask from him, the shadow demons walk again, empowered by the Falcon staff Drakon carried off into the cave of Llindel.
descriptions.c64:146359: Gauntlet-style dungeon crawl through 99 mazes to the final demon, with a two-player cooperative mode and a menu-driven level editor.
descriptions.c64:146360: Horror adventure in which young people ignore a warning and spend the night in a woodland chalet, only to face a demonic creature and aliens hiding a spaceship nearby.
descriptions.c64:146361: A warrior searches a flick-screen castle for the maiden Alicia, held by a Demon Harpy, fighting creatures with a magic ball as well as punches and kicks.
descriptions.c64:146366: Stranded when his spaceship ran dry, Ozzy explores a planet and its underground caverns for the diamonds that fuel the ship, fending off aliens with a boomerang.
descriptions.c64:146384: Second World War submarine simulation in the South Pacific, hunting Japanese convoys in practice, campaign or historical scenarios.
descriptions.c64:146400: Top-down fantasy RPG returning to Ymros from Shard of Spring on a much larger map, with parties of Humans, Elves, Dwarves and Trolls across ten character classes.
descriptions.c64:146403: Collection of police training mini-games loosely tied to the films: blocking bullets, shooting only armed non-police targets in a pop-up range, and accuracy target shooting.
descriptions.c64:146405: The first WWF-licensed wrestling game: one or two players call the moves in Hulk Hogan versus Randy Savage over 10, 20 or 60 minute bouts, with TV-style presentation.
descriptions.c64:146406: The Rignalians are colonizing the Solar System with chlorine pools in captured cities; fly a space fighter over 16 infested cities shooting down their craft.
descriptions.c64:146408: Satirical text adventure starring Denis Thatcher trying to sneak out of Number 10 Downing Street, away from Maggie, to the Gravedigger's Arms; he needs a drink within 10 moves.
descriptions.c64:146409: Space shooter where destroyed enemies drop letters: S for a temporary shield, P for power rockets and V for extra speed.
descriptions.c64:146410: Puzzle adventure following Denny through caves, hidden areas, graveyards and desert in pursuit of an evil ghost.
descriptions.c64:146411: Railway simulation set at the Old Oak Common traction maintenance depot west of London, which services locomotives and multiple units running out of Paddington.
descriptions.c64:146412: Single-screen game moving a battleship left and right along the surface to drop depth charges on submarines cruising at various depths, protecting a fleet of five ships.
descriptions.c64:146413: Horse race betting for up to 10 players, each starting with 1000 pounds to wager on six runners at varying odds.
descriptions.c64:146414: Up to four players bet with the bookie Jolly Jack on seven races at a meeting, choosing Fun, Serious or Dead Serious odds and staking in pounds or pence.
descriptions.c64:146427: Choplifter-style side-scroller: take an army helicopter deep into hostile territory, land on safe ground beside stranded comrades, and ferry them back to base three at a time.
descriptions.c64:146428: Text adventure about a boat run aground on a former U.S. Navy island; equipment left behind by the Navy holds the key to finding fuel for the journey home.
descriptions.c64:146454: Battlefield rescue against a three-minute clock: drive across the desert and get within two steps of your stranded soldiers so they follow you back to headquarters, where the fire button drops them off to bank points. Hit a mine and you are patched up and sent back to base.
descriptions.c64:146455: Matching logic puzzle: pick a symbol on the left with up and down and one on the right with left and right to form the required number of pairs inside the flashing area; wrong guesses are penalized.
descriptions.c64:146456: Battle through the castle of the demon Kyros, smashing the mirrors that hold his captives; completing the quest turns the hero into the invincible Macho Man who flattens everything in sight.
descriptions.c64:146457: Command a destroyer escorting six merchant ships across the North Atlantic in the Second World War, choosing among routes linking Britain, America, Gibraltar and Murmansk.
descriptions.c64:146463: Boxing game following a prospect with a 20-fight record against weak opposition who now steps up to tougher fighters, needing the right combinations to break through their guard.
descriptions.c64:146465: In the year 5150 humans explore Krauze, the abandoned homeworld of the Deviants, a conquering race that nearly wiped itself out in a civil war 100,000 years earlier.
descriptions.c64:146472: Master thief Devon Aire searches a dead millionaire's isometric mansion for the jewels and cash he hid in odd places, hired by his widow who cannot find them.
descriptions.c64:146476: Sliding tile puzzle in which each tile carries a pipe section; rearrange them so a rolling red ball passes through every tile, which blanks out once crossed.
descriptions.c64:146481: Pac-Man meets Uridium without the shooting: steer a white muncher across a scrolling playfield gathering items. From the German Golden Disk 64 issue 4.
descriptions.c64:146483: Fiona, the foulest of witches, flies the night sky across various locations to recover the tools of her trade stolen by her sister witches.
descriptions.c64:146498: Push patterned cubes together so matching ones touch and vanish, watching the counts in the side panel so that no single cube of a pattern is left stranded.
descriptions.c64:146500: Breakout variant without a paddle: steer the ball itself to clear the blocks and reach the diamonds at the center of the field. From Game On magazine.
descriptions.c64:146501: Boulder Dash-style dig through unstable caves that hold up for only 40 seconds before collapsing, grabbing the scattered diamonds in time. Published in 64'er magazine.
descriptions.c64:146502: Sequel to Diamond Jones: gather every diamond in nine caves within 45 seconds before an avalanche buries the cave. Guards march straight until blocked and then turn 90 degrees, a pattern you can learn to slip past them.
