descriptions.c64:151226: An intergalactic marathon where you steer a pair of sneakers between four lanes on an endless conveyor-like track, stepping forward and back to grab items as they come. Solo or two-player races, twelve difficulty levels, and adjustable speed, laps, lap length and track density.
descriptions.c64:151227: Fly a 2:00 AM air ambulance run for Airsik Flight Service, fetching a patient from another airfield and bringing him back using only instruments, whose gauges show altitude and other readings.
descriptions.c64:151228: Command an aircraft carrier carrying F-14 Tomcats for dogfights, A-6 Intruder bombers and RF-4 Phantoms for photo reconnaissance; launch planes carefully from the deck, then steer them on an overhead map.
descriptions.c64:151229: Fly a cargo plane delivering urgent medical supplies, then switch to a support jeep guarding the Albatross while it rides on a train. A sample game from Psytronik's SEUCK-based Destruction Set.
descriptions.c64:151231: Squash an insect invasion in the house with a fly swatter while a second player can join with a spray can, all over a static background picture. Also included with Commodore Zone #10.
descriptions.c64:151232: In medieval Japan, the katana-wielding Nukenin cuts down renegade ninja and samurai, and a second player can drop in at any time as the shuriken-throwing Ronin.
descriptions.c64:151233: Silkworm-inspired horizontal shooter for one or two players: one flies a VTOL jet while the other can join at any point in an armoured jeep on the ground.
descriptions.c64:151234: As Prince Damien, rightful heir of a dying king, contest the crown against his wicked sister, Princess Yssylda.
descriptions.c64:151238: Before Fred can go bowling with Barney for the weekend, Wilma insists he redecorate the living room with paint, in a game based on the Hanna-Barbera cartoon.
descriptions.c64:151239: Help Fred win Wilma by building a house from collected rocks while avoiding ankle-biting turtles, pterodactyls dropping stones and neighbours who pinch pieces while he is away.
descriptions.c64:151247: Othello-style board game against the computer: outflank its pieces to capture more of them than it takes of yours. Part of the Board Games pack and the Greatest Hits 1 collection.
descriptions.c64:151248: Toggle squares on a grid, each press also flipping the squares around it, until the board matches the target pattern shown in the corner, across more than 100 levels.
descriptions.c64:151249: A Tetris variant where falling blocks slide left and right while their patterns scroll up and down; each level demands a set number of matching-pattern rows formed horizontally, vertically or diagonally.
descriptions.c64:151250: Push a ball into green stones to knock them across the board and sink them in blast holes: a single target on the frantic first stage, one hole per corner on the second, then a chessboard stage where touching a small star blows up the ball. Three lives per screen.
descriptions.c64:151253: Flubble, a kindly little dragon, rounds up his timid Squij friends, who fled and hid when nasty aliens arrived, to keep them safe.
descriptions.c64:151254: Steer Fluff through the air collecting credits against a time limit for each level; gathering enough moves you on to the next stage.
descriptions.c64:151255: A Solomon's Key-inspired platform puzzler with 30 levels, originally a 1994 Data House Software release, later distributed with GO64! issue 2000/11.
descriptions.c64:151256: Breakout-style game for one player or two cooperating at once: locked in the cellar of the villain Magniform's palace, use a paddle to bounce a ball through the brick wall holding you prisoner.
descriptions.c64:151259: Pilot a ship into eight Thargoid bases and use energy pods to overload their reactors, in a side-view thrust game that strongly resembles Oids.
descriptions.c64:151260: Vertically scrolling shooter built with SEUCK: blast your way up the screen to rescue a pig held hostage by villains.
descriptions.c64:151270: Loop a biplane over a side-scrolling road and strafe enemy supply trucks while dodging patrolling aircraft and flak guns; destroying too few trucks costs spare planes.
descriptions.c64:151271: A slow-paced take on Fort Apocalypse with no shooting at all, released through Digital Marketing PD #029.
descriptions.c64:151272: As master falconer in the icy mountains of Arctovia, defend your birds' nests against armed half-human falcons swooping down to attack.
descriptions.c64:151273: As a warden in a boat, aim a crosshair to shoot eagles diving toward the water before they carry off any of the five fish you protect.
descriptions.c64:151274: A James Bond-flavoured mix of flying machines, old castles, missiles and egg guns, starring one of the deadliest agents of SUSSED, an elite elimination squad.
descriptions.c64:151276: Text adventure that begins lost in the desert beside an abandoned mine shaft, with more than 150 locations, treasure to find, wild beasts to fight or evade and 150 points to score.
descriptions.c64:151285: Soccer management in one of three UK leagues, chasing the League Trophy and FA Cup through training and player transfers; matches unfold as text rather than animation.
descriptions.c64:151286: All-text UK football management: handle trades, pick the line-up and decide who plays when in pursuit of the championship.
descriptions.c64:151287: Run an English football club, starting with a top-division side or a small fourth-division team and climbing toward international competitions; an expansion of the original Football Director.
descriptions.c64:151288: As manager of Grimsditch Rangers, get the team ready for Saturday's Cup final despite a crisis of dirty kit, unpaid bills and strikers who want to leave.
descriptions.c64:151289: Kevin Toms's sequel adds team formations, man-to-man marking, individual player skill and fitness ratings, and half-time substitutions.
descriptions.c64:151290: Manage a British football club through menus reached by clicking objects in a drawn office, setting tactics, line-ups and individual training for each player.
descriptions.c64:151373: As women's javelin coach at the 1988 Seoul Olympics, discover why two medal hopefuls are underperforming and fix it before Saturday's event.
descriptions.c64:151454: Farmer Fred, ruined by a storm, raids the dark cellars of Castle Kadenza in Transylvania for fruit in a single-screen overhead maze game, gathering fruit or heading for each room's exit.
descriptions.c64:151459: Trapped with 10 stationary Spongs and 10 fast Gulpers inside a force field, escape and destroy the Gulpers; Spongs eat both you and Gulpers, so hiding behind them helps. Part of Cassette 50.
descriptions.c64:151460: In the 2nd Solar War of 2430, rescue the defenceless escape pods of the cargo ship Saturn Voyager, abandoned by its crew deep in the enemy's Fifth Star System.
descriptions.c64:151489: Lead a seven-member squad, each with different skills, into an energy plant on the planet Karis to rescue survivors and burn away the aliens holding them with a flamethrower.
descriptions.c64:151490: Single-screen shooter where layers of force fields around a UFO must be chipped away, in the vein of Star Castle and Yars' Revenge, until it can be destroyed.
descriptions.c64:151491: As forester Robin, save the dying forest by turning leaves cursed brown by an evil witch back to green, while dealing with woodland animals she has also bewitched.
descriptions.c64:151492: Woken repeatedly by a stormy night, you dream of an endless woodland path and then wake to find yourself really standing on it instead of in bed.
descriptions.c64:151493: Fighting Fantasy adaptation: armed with magic items from the wizard Yaztromo, cross Darkwood Forest to recover the dwarves' lost runes for Gillibran, mayor of Stonebridge.
descriptions.c64:151495: Forbidden Forest tribute in which you shoot spiders, bees, bats and other creatures with a machine gun instead of a bow; created for a 2011 SEUCK contest for sideways-scrolling games.
descriptions.c64:151496: Follow-up to the 1,000 Kung-Fu Maniacs game: a sideways-scrolling ninja brawler across odd locations such as the stage of a 'Lord of the Bland' concert.
descriptions.c64:151497: Drive an armoured car on a combat assignment in this Alf Yngve game, shelved in 1994 and finally released with enhancements as a sample in the second Destruction Set from Psytronik.
descriptions.c64:151500: Wake on an unfamiliar shore with no memory of who you are and piece together your past in this text adventure.
descriptions.c64:151501: Recover a missing formula and rescue Nic Allot in this Guild text adventure.
descriptions.c64:151555: As one of the last good wizards, drive a hovercraft toward the fortress of the evil Narzod, blasting the minions that pour from its gate.
descriptions.c64:151556: Strategy and role-playing hybrid: earn gold by defeating roaming bands to recruit wizards, fighters, scouts, clerics and raiders, then march the army on the Witch King's fortress. Encounters play out in text alongside an overview map.
descriptions.c64:151557: Fly a cannon-armed battle chopper with limited fuel through a maze-like underground cavern to destroy a hostile power station, stopping at way-points to rest, save and refuel.
descriptions.c64:151560: Cross scrolling 3-D countryside, desert, industrial and forest landscapes armed only with a roll of film, gathering six pieces per stage to complete photofits of four famous faces.
descriptions.c64:151561: Steer a particle through strange machines in an underground physics laboratory by placing rotating and semi-transparent mirrors so it reflects onto the target.
descriptions.c64:151562: Find the Fountain of Youth, fill a bottle with its water and escape to safety; planned as the first half of a two-part Flying Fox adventure.
descriptions.c64:151564: Connect 4 conversion, known in Germany as Vier Gewinnt, played against the computer; published on the Magic Disk 64 issue of March 1988.
descriptions.c64:151566: Interactive fiction based on Frederick Forsyth's Cold War novel: as John Preston, newly appointed head of C1(A) in British intelligence, uncover the AURORA plot to seize power in the Soviet Union.
descriptions.c64:151567: Peg solitaire: jump balls over one another to remove them until one remains, ideally finishing in the centre of the board, with moves that can be taken back.
descriptions.c64:151568: Play a fox out for revenge, foraging above and below ground for rabbits, hens, apples and milk in a reversal of the usual hunter and hunted.
descriptions.c64:151569: Educational platformer: break out of a mad professor's basement by correctly answering the fraction questions of gatekeepers guarding electric gates; wrong answers bring up an explanation screen.
descriptions.c64:151609: Washed onto a South Seas island by a tropical storm, find a way off before the volcano erupts, starting from a mysterious message written in the sand.
descriptions.c64:151611: As the last Frankenstein descendant, summoned to the family manor, follow envelope messages from Victor Frankenstein himself to reanimate the monster in the basement laboratory.
descriptions.c64:151614: Offbeat English-language text and graphics adventure in which a spaceship named Frankie crash-lands on Jupiter, a planet with no solid surface to land on.
descriptions.c64:151615: Italian release of the Giana Sisters, renamed Paola and Luisa, who must escape an enchanted world area by area, alone or with a second player, knocking gems loose by hitting platforms from below.
descriptions.c64:151616: Fan modification of The Great Giana Sisters by Merlin and Chrille, a scrolling platform game for one or two players that continues the sisters' adventures.
descriptions.c64:151618: Clear every bucket of gold from single-screen levels while each level's own type of monster gives chase; ladders serve both as routes around the screen and as barriers that cannot be walked through.
descriptions.c64:151619: As the Galactic Police Force's Agent One, stop a Professor breeding gruesome creatures in five factory laboratories, riding lifts between the two floors of each side-on screen.
descriptions.c64:151621: Fan-made Giana Sisters level set created with the official construction kit by Manfred 'Frankie' Trenz, one of the original game's graphic artists.
descriptions.c64:151622: Manfred Trenz's second Giana Sisters Construction Kit level set, with 33 new stages of baddies to avoid, coins to grab and power-ups to collect.
descriptions.c64:151685: Guide Fred, a head-shaped creature with a waddling walk, to collect every diamond and walk off each map's right edge, eating food to refill an energy meter that constantly drains.
descriptions.c64:151686: Sequel released outside the magazine: the waddling, head-shaped Fred again gathers all the diamonds on each level and exits on the right while keeping his falling energy topped up with food.
descriptions.c64:151687: Third Fred's Back platformer: collect every diamond, leave each level by walking off its right side and eat food before Fred's ever-draining energy runs out.
descriptions.c64:151688: Fred series platformer: explore each level for diamonds, avoid or shoot enemies, head-butt bricks and hunt for secret levels. Published on Magic Disk 64, November 1995.
descriptions.c64:151689: Drop space mines in the path of enemies so they crash into them, advancing once enough have been destroyed; Richard Bayliss's first larger game project.
descriptions.c64:151690: Defend a cross spanning the screen from 40 levels of aliens attacking from all angles, using the Statron, a screen-wide line of arrows that can be moved vertically or horizontally.
descriptions.c64:151696: Fly through the zones of Frexel-Kejland shooting aliens, collecting flashing pods for extra firepower and jump energy, and destroying every laser lock to open the way to the next level.
descriptions.c64:151697: Frogger-style crossing: hop over four lanes of traffic, past a snake and across rapids on sinking turtles and swirling logs while avoiding snapping alligators.
descriptions.c64:151698: Educational maths game for ages 4 to 8 in which children practise counting and ordering numbers against the computer or a friend.
descriptions.c64:151699: Train frogs by rewarding wanted behaviour, following B. F. Skinner's shaping principle, in a sport combining elements of football and rugby, for one or two players.
descriptions.c64:151840: Get each frog across a busy road and back again as fast as possible without being run over by cars.
descriptions.c64:151841: Frogger-based single-screen game: bring five frogs across, one after another, over a busy road and a log-strewn river into five holes at the top, each against its own timer.
descriptions.c64:151847: As Hickey the Kreezer, an elastic spring that hops, slides and shoots, rescue fellow Kreezers on the monster-filled planet Cosmica before its Twang energy runs out; momentum helps clear some hazards.
descriptions.c64:151849: Fruit machine for 1 to 4 players, each starting with £1.50, featuring 1980s machine options: Cash Box, Nudge Box, Hold, Mega-hold, Cash Gamble, Winning Streak and a Skill Climb.
descriptions.c64:151850: Sequel fruit machine for 1 to 4 players, each given £1.50 in coins that are fed into the machine with number keys.
descriptions.c64:151854: Mastermind-style logic puzzle with more colours to deduce, where feedback must be interpreted quickly under heavy time pressure.
descriptions.c64:151879: Single-screen Space Invaders variant: fly a fighter in any direction to defeat an alien fleet in planetary orbit, losing energy on every collision. Published in Commodore Scene #16.
descriptions.c64:151881: Based on the children's TV game show: two contestants compete in stunt and trivia rounds, and the winner runs through a maze grabbing prizes.
descriptions.c64:151884: Spelling game starring the cartoon cat Heathcliff, who catches balloon-carrying mice emerging from pipes to pick the letters needed to complete a word shown in a sentence.
descriptions.c64:151885: Midi-Maze-style game supporting up to eight simultaneous players. Published on Game On, August 1995.
descriptions.c64:151886: Fungus, who eats only mushrooms, leaves his floating space island to gather them from neighbouring islands full of hostile creatures, where he cannot stop running.
descriptions.c64:151887: Collect every mushroom in the area before the hourglass runs out, then return to the start; unlike the first game, the screen scrolls in all directions and Fungus now carries a gun.
descriptions.c64:151890: Race on the Rim, a 20 km wide circular desert track in Arizona, in a deadly future motor-racing championship.
descriptions.c64:151891: In 1999, after motorcycles are banned, ride an armed hover-bike and shoot slower road users, who leave money behind when destroyed.
descriptions.c64:151893: As Future Knight, fight out of a huge maze-like crashed spacecraft overrun by aliens with a laser gun, then cross the hostile planet to rescue the captive Amelia.
descriptions.c64:151894: Calm fishing game on a pond: dig for worms as bait and find the best spot to cast.
descriptions.c64:151896: Toolkit for making interactive fiction, with a picture editor for location graphics and room for up to 255 nouns, verbs and adverbs and 9999 rooms within a 23k limit.
descriptions.c64:151897: Blast through eight waves of attacking aliens of rising speed and difficulty to reach and face a giant command vessel.
descriptions.c64:151898: Release a spaceship from a mothership sweeping back and forth, then guide it past moving orbs onto one of four pads at the bottom, slowing its fall by burning fuel.
descriptions.c64:151900: Space empire game for one to six players: command hundreds of starships to conquer worlds while contending with black holes, photon storms, novas and the villainous General Badguy.
descriptions.c64:151901: Elected to run a colony on a frontier planet, manage the world and its star system while sending spacecraft out to find new planets for a growing population.
descriptions.c64:151903: Two-player dogfight from Cassette 50: shoot down the opponent's five planes with rockets or air mines, rationing five mines and five turbo boosts across five rounds.
descriptions.c64:151904: Fly a helicopter through low cave passages to rescue people held captive by villains.
descriptions.c64:151906: Pilot a gardener in a flying chair through side-scrolling maze caves to recover ten stolen power flowers, avoiding the walls and the creatures inside.
descriptions.c64:151907: Fixed-position shooter mixing Asteroids with Space Invaders, in which meteors falling toward the ground must be shot down, much like Astrosmash; also released in Italy as Meteoriti.
descriptions.c64:151908: Slide a muncher sideways to avoid hazards and snap its gaping mouth at foes; filling the left dial advances the level, while the right dial reaching bottom ends the game.
descriptions.c64:151909: In the year 5000, fly a Delta Glider into a new intergalactic war and conquer the final worlds, Tyrus and Erebus. Published on Magic Disk 64, September 1990.
descriptions.c64:151910: Terrorists have mined every Plutamnite mine on Galaxia 7, the galaxy's only source of the mineral; gather objects scattered through the mines and use them to defuse the bombs.
descriptions.c64:151911: Galaxian-style shooter from Sensible Software against waves of kamikaze vultures, chickens, swans and budgies, firing two shots at a time.
descriptions.c64:151930: Raise a fleet of Eon-cruisers and move from bridge to bridge commanding each ship in a battle for control of the galaxy.
descriptions.c64:151931: Expanded version of the arcade space shooter with two extra levels, revised and rebalanced stages and all four missiles fired with one button, across six worlds from a garden to fire and ice.
descriptions.c64:151932: Dutch hangman: guess the hidden word letter by letter as each miss adds part of the gallows.
descriptions.c64:151933: Hungarian graphic and text adventure in the style of Level 9 and Melbourne House titles, with a parser of about 1,400 words that handles Hungarian inflection.
descriptions.c64:151934: Sail the Spanish Main hunting for gold, braving storms, shipwrecks, collisions and pirate raids while following clues to the treasure and trying to keep it.
descriptions.c64:151936: Board game for 2 to 6 players starring Lucky Luke, building wealth through Wild West activities and answering questions quickly enough to win money.
descriptions.c64:151937: Steer a craft around a playfield with no borders, nudging coloured globes into matching ones to clear the screen; globes can also be knocked off the sides.
descriptions.c64:151945: Rescue a fellow explorer captured on Phantis, the fourth moon of the Sotpok system, through horizontal R-Type-style shooting stages and platform levels against 24 types of enemy.
descriptions.c64:151948: Trivia quiz show for one or two players, each aided by teammate Joe or May, who reveals up to 10 clues per answer; fewer clues needed means more points across 12 questions per topic.
descriptions.c64:151949: Tetris modelled on the Game Boy version, published in Commodore Zone issue 6.
descriptions.c64:151952: Game construction kit built from the in-house editors its authors used to write their own games, letting users make games without machine code or programming knowledge.
descriptions.c64:151953: Xevious-style vertically scrolling space shooter whose enemy shots are hard to see.
descriptions.c64:151954: Turn-based text gangster game for two or more players, running from the start of Prohibition until one becomes the Godfather or the Feds close in, through extortion, gambling, pay-offs, contracts and jail time.
descriptions.c64:151956: Adventure in which Adam must find Eve and rouse her from a deep sleep, then track down the key of life and set it inside a magic box in the sacred room.
descriptions.c64:151957: Gauntlet-style overhead dungeon crawl through more than 100 levels for up to five characters with differing strengths, gathering potions, gold, scrolls, keys and magical items.
descriptions.c64:151958: Garry Kitchen's all-in-one game design kit, an early consumer tool with editors for building complete games; also released for Apple II and IBM PC.
descriptions.c64:151959: Text adventure that opens in an enchanted forest whose locations all look alike; find the Sorcerer's Castle and rescue the princess while a Jester pops up unexpectedly.
descriptions.c64:151960: Treasure-hunting text adventure in the lost city of Atlantis: explore, solve simple puzzles, face hostile sea creatures and drop treasures at the marked starting spot.
descriptions.c64:151968: Six-a-side soccer reworked from Superstar Ice Hockey, letting you control the centre-forward, the goalkeeper, the manager or any mix of those roles.
descriptions.c64:151970: Soccer training game made of timed mini-events: gym exercises built on button mashing, timing-based ball juggling and field events.
descriptions.c64:151971: Top-down soccer with a partial view of the pitch, where control switches between the player on the ball and the nearest defender; team size, half length and AI level are adjustable.
descriptions.c64:152022: As a knight unravelling the mystery of the mind, collect iron, stone, fire and ice from a 64-room 3-D maze so he can go through the Gates of Dawn.
descriptions.c64:152023: Sequel action adventure in which the knight continues his quest to solve the mystery of the Gates of Dawn, battling the monsters that guard them.
descriptions.c64:152024: Real-time 3-D submarine simulation: command a US sub in the World War II Pacific, tracking and intercepting Japanese patrol boats, destroyers and other warships.
descriptions.c64:152025: Text-based train management simulation built around the Gatwick Express service linking London's Victoria station with Gatwick Airport and Brighton.
descriptions.c64:152033: Sequel to Gemstone Warrior: the restored Gemstone has lost its power because its pieces were damaged, so return to the Netherworld dungeons to find a way to heal it.
descriptions.c64:152034: Colour-tile puzzle across increasingly hard levels: change tiles in the left grid, whose colours cycle in a fixed sequence, until it matches the control grid on the right.
descriptions.c64:152035: Enemies from a neighbouring star system have seized settlements on an outlying planet and guarded it with their best defences and sensors; fight to take them back.
descriptions.c64:152036: Tempest-like action set in an ancient epoch when life on Earth was young: as a scorpion, fight off an invading swarm of killer spiders.
descriptions.c64:152037: Crosshair shooter for one or two players defending Earth from destruction in 2285; a pirated Italian version appeared as Meteore.
descriptions.c64:152038: Hawkeye-like platformer: as Shimon, travel back and forth across three levels destroying the eggs of a genetically engineered dragon that escaped Dr. Klein's lab.
descriptions.c64:152040: Strongman contest endorsed by shot-putter Geoff Capes, with six timed events including truck pulling, tug of war and wrestling, scored on time remaining.
descriptions.c64:152088: Logic puzzle set in 2077, when a virus infects a mad scientist's giant computer capable of reshaping a whole world into an egg. Published on Magic Disk 64, May 1995.
descriptions.c64:152089: Economic simulation leading the USA against the USSR across seven scenarios, the 1984 situation plus six hypothetical 1990 setups, with national success tracked through gross national product and prestige.
descriptions.c64:152091: Opening game in SSI's When Superpowers Collide wargame series: Soviet forces strike NATO across West Germany in the Advance to Combat and Invasion scenarios.
descriptions.c64:152092: Final When Superpowers Collide wargame: Soviet ski troops invade Norway and NATO answers in kind; whoever holds the most towns after the set number of turns wins.
descriptions.c64:152093: As Gerry the Germ, expelled from the Illtitute of Infectology without his Stinkploma, infect a human across five single-screen body parts to earn your way back in.
descriptions.c64:152094: Help Gertie Goose recover eight eggs taken by a Demon King, searching a scrolling forest for eight coloured keys past obstacles and soldiers, with no way to lose a life.
descriptions.c64:152095: Educational game in which Gertrude the Goose helps the player roam linked rooms solving puzzles of logic, pattern recognition and visual perception; for slightly older children than Gertrude's Secrets.
descriptions.c64:152096: Educational object-sorting game for young children, modelled on Atari's Adventure: explore Gertrude the Goose's maze of rooms solving logic puzzles.
descriptions.c64:152131: As a General Agricultural Robot Functionary, grow six Aquaronum Upshootus plants, filling up at the tap to water them while shooting or dodging the creatures attacking you.
descriptions.c64:152132: Collect every cross, then take the key that opens the exit, in this Forget Me Not-inspired maze game made for the RGCD 16KB cartridge competition in 2011.
descriptions.c64:152133: Single-screen maze escape as Getty or Emma, imprisoned once again by a Troll King in his infinite Nyarlu dungeons after having broken out before.
descriptions.c64:152134: Grand tactical wargame of the 1863 Battle of Gettysburg, built on an improved form of the system from SSI's Antietam and played over 42 one-hour turns.
descriptions.c64:152137: Shooting gallery of separate lanes: dart the laser cannon to the mouth of whichever lane a target is coming down and vaporise it in time.
descriptions.c64:152139: Guide Harry the Ghost Chaser through sixteen screens of haunted Fairport Manor, from attic and kitchen to library and sewers, avoiding or leaping over roaming ghosts.
descriptions.c64:152140: Drive a blue car around collecting every flag while dodging a suicidal red car steered by a phantom. Published on Magic Disk 64, October 1993.
descriptions.c64:152143: Pac-Man variant whose main twist is a simultaneous two-player mode where rivals steal points from each other and try to leave the opponent at the ghosts' mercy.
descriptions.c64:152144: As Hunk Studbuckle, armed with an anti-matter phantom-splattering gun, enter Nightmare Mansion to rescue his brother Chuck, missing for three days after going in to clear out its ghosts.
descriptions.c64:152145: As the adventurer Kra, collect every diamond across five levels of a haunted castle guarded by ghosts, spiders, snakes, traps and dark magic, with different dangers in every room.
descriptions.c64:152146: Move freely through the rooms of an old castle collecting a fortune in diamonds while avoiding the traps and guards protecting each one.
descriptions.c64:152147: Story and arcade hybrid for one or two Keepers of Time: rescue parapsychologist Dr. Helga Smith from the ghost of Genghis Khan, brought to his castle by a time portal, and send him back to his own era.
descriptions.c64:152152: Climb a mountain across five screens, starting each attempt at the foot of the path, where flags mark how many stages have been reached so far.
descriptions.c64:152292: Pac-Man clone with an unusually wide variety of maze layouts.
descriptions.c64:152294: Cassette 50 maze game in the Pac-Man mould: touching a ghost is fatal unless a power pill has been eaten, bonus fruit adds points and eating an asterisk lets you kill a ghost.
descriptions.c64:152305: Third Scott Adams adventure: race the clock inside a nuclear power plant to complete your mission before the reactor is lost, using one- or two-word commands.
descriptions.c64:152306: Starting beside the coffin of Count Cristo, struck down by an enemy's Voodoo curse, search his castle for the recipe and words needed to break the hex. Scott Adams adventure number 4.
descriptions.c64:152307: Sixth Scott Adams adventure: a space traveller whose ship breaks down in orbit around a remote asteroid begins with only a phase pistol and space suit, using a two-word parser on a split screen.
descriptions.c64:152308: Scott Adams adventure number 8: gather every treasure from a newly discovered Egyptian pyramid and escape alive, using the series' two-word parser.
descriptions.c64:152313: Final game of the original Scott Adams series: sail to distant magic lands of temples and fountains to fetch an elixir that will cure the ailing king.
descriptions.c64:152314: As apprentice to the Master Wizard Solon, recover his 13 lost Stars of Power from Claymorgue Castle in Scott Adams adventure number 13.
descriptions.c64:152322: Variant of Ghosts 'n Goblins differing mainly in a modified title screen and a few small gameplay changes.
descriptions.c64:152356: Throw a spear to kill ghosts trying to catch you, moving left and right with keys or joystick. Published in Germany under the name Geisterjäger in the magazine Homecomputer.
descriptions.c64:152456: Third Jack adventure: with treasure from his beanstalk and giant adventures he has bought a house to explore, with basement rooms, caves, gardens, a big maze and a roof that leads to the moon.
descriptions.c64:152457: Follow-up to Jack and the Beanstalk: months after crushing the giant, Jack finds a freshly dug hole under his garden where the giant fell, and goes down to investigate.
descriptions.c64:152458: Christmas horizontal shooter: as Father Christmas, fire snowballs at deadly festive objects. Richard Bayliss's first scrolling shoot 'em up, released in GO64! 2003/12.
descriptions.c64:152459: Collection of pool variants: Straight Pool, Rotation, One Pocket, Trick Shot, Hustler, Player and Set-Up.
descriptions.c64:152460: Based on the cartoon: Gilbert, an obnoxious alien star, must leave the planet Drill to sign his next TV contract, but locals fed up with his arrogance have stolen things he needs.
descriptions.c64:152463: Tetris variant where completing each level's quota of rows reveals a new picture, with five difficulty levels that change the row target and how fast bricks fall.
descriptions.c64:152465: Side-scrolling platformer across 32 stages as Gitty or her sister Maria, with two players alternating and dream crystals to collect for points.
descriptions.c64:152466: Based on the 1984 film: as Paul McCartney, drive around London before midnight Saturday to find seven band members holding parts of the erased 'No More Lonely Nights' master, then return to Abbey Road.
descriptions.c64:152470: As a famed Roman gladiator in the Empire's greatest tournament, face fierce beasts using weapons scattered around the arena.
descriptions.c64:152471: As a Gladiator Squadron helicopter pilot answering a distress call, destroy enemy forces across eight strategically vital islands so they can be secured.
descriptions.c64:152483: Glider simulation over a 160 km course: choose one of five weather levels or set conditions manually, cross the runway to start the clock, round two turning points and land.
descriptions.c64:152486: As a member of the Silent But Deadly force, ride a hang glider and motorbike across the Abraxas Corporation's plastic island to destroy its 10 reactors and end the arms dealers' regime.
descriptions.c64:152525: Side-scrolling future sport: keep a basketball bouncing with a freely movable bat from the left side of each level to the basket on the right before time runs out.
descriptions.c64:152527: As a UN loyalist pilot, shoot down planes and warships seized by the rogue Citizens Defence Force across 8 stages divided into land and sea sections.
descriptions.c64:152529: As a deep-sea diver tethered to a diving station, descend through infested waters to grab sunken treasure one piece at a time and haul it back up past crabs and other sea life.
descriptions.c64:152530: Use elevators to reach each level's letter while avoiding a witch, then carry it to the pegs below to hang it; switching to a background layer lets the gnome slip behind stairs and shafts.
descriptions.c64:152532: Quiz pack about microcomputers, bundled with a beginner's introduction to what the machine can do, how it works and what software to use.
descriptions.c64:152533: Trivia board game for up to six players based on the Milton Bradley original: roll dice to move desk by desk through classrooms, racing to graduate first, at three difficulty levels.
descriptions.c64:152534: Gobang against the computer: place stones to make five in a row.
descriptions.c64:152536: Follow-up to Hercules: guide the hero across more than 50 single-screen platform levels, collecting the item on each screen to move on, using springs to jump higher and avoiding creatures that cost one of three lives.
descriptions.c64:152564: Turn-based grid game over Japan and its waters: deploy Japan's ground, sea and air forces plus nuclear weapons against Godzilla, who starts at a random spot and wanders erratically.
descriptions.c64:152565: Top-down scrolling go-kart game: drive through a maze collecting every bonus on the level while avoiding other drivers, who cost one of three lives on contact.
descriptions.c64:152567: Dig out the gold on each screen, planning carefully because some deposits are walled off and dynamite is limited. Part of The Big 100 collection.
descriptions.c64:152568: Strategy game for 2 to 5 stranded players on a tropical island with a well, a forest for boat timber and a gold field, each collecting the most gold they can before sailing away.
descriptions.c64:152590: Educational historical simulation exploring life during the nineteenth-century gold rushes, with suggested activities for primary and secondary students.
descriptions.c64:152591: In Bedlam City, 1976, overrun by dealers, robbers and corrupt police under the boss Ugly Fat Joe, play Goldshaft, the one man able to clean up the streets.
descriptions.c64:152592: 18-hole golf for one or two players taking alternate shots: enter name and handicap, choose a club on the overhead hole view, then set direction from a side view of the golfer.
descriptions.c64:152596: Golf with a course editor for designing new courses; one to four players compete in match or tournament formats with handicaps, under wind, temperature and ground conditions set by hand or at random.
descriptions.c64:152597: Recreation of the Old Course at St Andrews, playable from novice to professional handicaps, choosing club, strength and angle for each shot.
descriptions.c64:152602: As a frog-like dinosaur, defend the red gem that gives your kind its power from creatures crossing the screen one at a time in different directions on each level.
descriptions.c64:152618: Preschool game in which conductors Goofy and Mickey ride a train across colourful scenery while children match the coloured squares, circles and triangles puffed out of the smokestack.
descriptions.c64:152619: Crosshair shooter bundled with the Magnum Lightphaser light gun.
descriptions.c64:152621: Montezuma's Revenge-inspired flip-screen platformer: a relic hunter explores a pyramid for a hidden treasure room, collecting and using tools to pass obstacles and reach blocked areas.
descriptions.c64:152625: Teaches BASIC programming through a space story with an illustrated storybook: Gortek trains the Microchips to program a great computer to defend the planet Syntax from invading Zitrons.
descriptions.c64:152628: Second Gortek BASIC programming course, continuing the space story on the planet Xerat, where the Kryptobytes guard information gathered from distant corners of the universe.
descriptions.c64:152631: An evil lord has split the druid Hasrinaxx's body into six parts hidden across the four towers of his lands north of Belorn; find them to restore the druid.
descriptions.c64:152632: Real-time fantasy text adventure where animals, thieves and other characters move about independently, illustrated with small animated scenes at key moments instead of location pictures.
descriptions.c64:152633: Manage a tennis pro starting at the bottom of the Top 100 with $50,000, handling finances from the office and playing matches on four court surfaces against stars such as Lendl, Agassi and Sampras.
descriptions.c64:152634: Fly a GR9 Harrier over terrorist-held territory, destroying as many land and air defences as possible so ground troops can advance.
descriptions.c64:152635: From a ship hovering above, lower a grabber to collect the eight Nadium blocks lying at the bottom and carry them home to the planet Cort across six levels.
descriptions.c64:152636: Pac-Man-inspired maze game: as Hobbler the Gobbler, eat every old turtle egg in a cavern while four crabs patrol the maze.
descriptions.c64:152676: Soccer for one or two players seen from an elevated angle over part of the pitch, with control passing to the player nearest the ball; half length, team size and kit colours are adjustable.
descriptions.c64:152679: Football management: take any club from the Conference up to the highest English division, picking a starting eleven rated for ability and fitness and signing players on the transfer market.
descriptions.c64:152684: As a graffiti artist, get through four locations while old men, police, skaters and women dropping flowerpots pelt you with objects; touching anyone costs a life.
descriptions.c64:152687: Enter a hotel and search its many rooms and floors for the blueprints of a super computer, using objects in the right places and dealing with the other characters you meet.
descriptions.c64:152710: 1000cc motorbike racing for one or two players on a horizontally split screen, over a full season or single races on 12 tracks including Assen, Mugello, Spa and the old Hockenheim, with an optional manual gearbox.
descriptions.c64:152711: Overhead Super Sprint-style racing sequel across tracks with hairpins and oil slicks; each race must be finished within a time limit, and leftover time carries over to the next.
descriptions.c64:152713: Track down Grandell Island and work through a trail of clues leading to Commodore Grandell's treasure.
descriptions.c64:152714: Chess against the computer at ten skill levels, with options to watch it play itself, ask for hints, force it to move and change board colours; moves are typed in.
descriptions.c64:152756: Educational adventure, first released on the BBC Micro in 1983, in which typed answers guide the rescue of three pairs of royal children held by an evil witch through a series of whimsical puzzles.
descriptions.c64:152759: Graphical text adventure in an old deserted graveyard, searching for a dead man's diamond; later rereleased as Pirate Cemetary.
descriptions.c64:152804: Educational exercise from a Rainbow book of BASIC listings: a ball is thrown upward at a random speed and you calculate its time in the air and maximum height.
descriptions.c64:152806: Final Gravity game: collect medical cargo from a delivery ship above Planet Zerox and land it on the Lunar HQ pad despite an alien empire that has learned of the mission.
descriptions.c64:152808: Constantly scrolling horizontal shooter starring a hamburger that blasts or dodges flying burgers, cola cans and fences, losing a life on any contact with food, obstacles or the screen edges.
descriptions.c64:152811: Muppets reading game: Gonzo rides to a castle to save his girlfriend Camilla the chicken from becoming the Swedish Chef's dinner, using words supplied by Dr. Bunsen Honeydew.
descriptions.c64:152825: Side-scrolling arcade conversion: a gladiator fights through a castle, angling his shield against incoming objects, striking foes with his sword and grabbing icons for armour and points.
descriptions.c64:152827: Command the armies of the Great Northern War, in which a Russian-led coalition fought the Swedish Empire, choosing the strategy and timing when the cavalry swings around the flank to charge.
descriptions.c64:152830: Sequel to Green Beret: after aliens ruin Earth and drive humanity underground, the Vindicator sets out to kill the Dark Overlord, starting with a hunt for blueprints in an underground complex.
descriptions.c64:152832: Golf endorsed by Greg Norman with two courses, modelling of how the ball's lie and the swing style affect shots (which can be switched off), optional weather and wind, and match and stroke play.
descriptions.c64:152833: Side-view platformer starring Grell, a dwarf, and Fella, a fairy, who use spells to cleanse the insects and flowers of a sorcerer's garden still tainted by a witch's dark magic.
descriptions.c64:152834: Based on the film: as Billy, catch the Mogwai running around the living room after midnight and put them back in the cage before they turn into Gremlins.
descriptions.c64:152835: Isometric action game in which Norman the cat sets out for the castle of the evil magician Mauron to recover the Orb of Life stolen from Greyfell, a realm populated by humanoid animals.
descriptions.c64:152836: Thrown back in time by a time machine accident, run, jump, crouch and shoot through six themed levels, including Stone Age, Dark Jungle and Modern Times, on the way home.
descriptions.c64:152838: Steer a white arrow across a scrolling field of coloured tiles, erasing the yellow ones as you pass. Tiles with clipped corners add super jumps that carry the arrow over gaps; clear the screen inside two minutes to advance.
descriptions.c64:152856: American football management: guide a team with a budget, buying and selling players to raise energy, morale and skill and swapping squad positions once a week; matches show side-view touchdown highlights.
descriptions.c64:152881: As a US special forces soldier armed with a knife and captured weapons, infiltrate a Marshaling Area, Harbor, Air Base and Siberian POW Camp to free prisoners facing a firing squad.
descriptions.c64:152906: Steer a diamond to the arrow in the lower right corner before time runs out, avoiding solid circles and donuts that get faster and smarter every level.
descriptions.c64:152908: Jeff Minter's second Gridrunner sequel: a corps of pilots attacks the droid home planet to wipe out every droid before they can launch a nuke at Earth.
descriptions.c64:152909: Cross a grid to defuse each bomb before its timer expires; every square you leave vanishes, so routes must be planned, and a roaming boot and skulls must be avoided.
descriptions.c64:152910: Defend gardens of Pigmy Pines with a spray gun, shooting down creatures until four pines have grown; any creature reaching the ground costs you.
descriptions.c64:152911: Crosshair game of shooting grouse with the Stack Light Rifle, sold only bundled with the gun.
descriptions.c64:152912: With Grover's help, children recognise animals and sort them onto land, into the sky or into water across four environments, building colourful pictures as the animals come to life.
descriptions.c64:152913: Graphic adventure as pilot of the Earth ship USAC 9400, travelling the solar system to find fuel for warships stranded at the front and deliver it to a cargo ship on Pluto, battling aliens along the way.
descriptions.c64:152914: Clue-style murder mystery: explore an estate and question characters about where they were when the killing happened, spotting the one who is lying.
descriptions.c64:152915: As the Gryphon, protect his gold from the Id Monsters, who have poisoned the rivers and lakes that link the Mystical Woods, Surreal Cities and Darklands of his dream realm.
descriptions.c64:153017: Command US aircraft, ground troops and warships, aircraft carriers among them, through the six-month battle for Guadalcanal that began with the August 1942 Marine landing.
descriptions.c64:153025: Defender clone: protect humanoids on mountainous terrain from aliens using a rapid-fire laser and limited smart bombs, with an extra bomb every 10,000 points.
descriptions.c64:153028: In a Mk.II Fighter, stop faster Raiders carrying Earthlings to the top of the screen to turn them into Mutants; shooting a Raider drops its captive, who must then be caught.
descriptions.c64:153030: Wargame of the 1941 Smolensk campaign on the road to Moscow: the German side uses blitzkrieg tactics to encircle Soviet divisions and push far enough east to threaten the capital.
descriptions.c64:153046: Word guessing game: guess a letter, try the whole word or have the computer reveal a letter at a cost of 2 points.
descriptions.c64:153048: Timed word puzzle based on a TV show: guess a five-letter password within five tries, with correct letters shown in white and letters in the wrong position in yellow.
descriptions.c64:153060: As a gumball factory worker, rise through the ranks by meeting each day's quota from 08:30, routing coloured gumballs through a Rube Goldberg-style sorting machine.
descriptions.c64:153063: Wild West crosshair shooter: as a famous bounty killer, gun down Billy Destroyer's gang, who have seized Gun City, while sparing innocents such as a little girl carrying physics books.
descriptions.c64:153068: Command a hydrofoil armed with deck cannons, homing missiles, torpedoes and depth charges to infiltrate an enemy's inland waterways and destroy all its naval bases.
descriptions.c64:153071: As ghost hunters Trev and Georg, each with a different playing style, shoot demons, skeletons and other foes for a high score across 72 single-screen platform levels.
descriptions.c64:153078: Vertically scrolling shooter set in 1997: fly a Pulse Fighter of the Gunstar Fleet, built at a hidden Moon base, to destroy the aliens who invaded and enslaved Earth.
descriptions.c64:153079: Oil business game in which players compete to become the richest oilman, coping with wellhead disasters and other outside events.
descriptions.c64:153088: Pilot a balloon around an amusement park, watching windsocks for gust strength and direction and inflating or deflating to change altitude without bursting it.
descriptions.c64:153089: Vertically scrolling shooter as commander of the starship Gutt Blaster, heading into hyperspace to face alien hordes and their wheel-shaped ship capable of destroying all life.
descriptions.c64:153090: As Greedy Guzzler, gather keys in overhead mazes to open food cells and eat their contents; once full he grows too fat to squeeze through narrow gaps, while Deflator Dennis patrols the border.
descriptions.c64:153091: On the day King Myrridian of Hillsborough is to marry Princess Klaudia, an army of dwarves snatches the bride away, setting off a rescue quest tangled up with the grudge of his exiled younger brother Joel.
descriptions.c64:153092: A three-part adventure in Gypsum Cave: a conventional illustrated adventure hunting for a jewel, then a guessing round about objects shown in the pictures, with treasure to gather and a safe exit to find.
descriptions.c64:153093: One or two players pilot the Galaxy Ranger, a ship built around a docking supply pod, on a mission to wipe out every planet of an alien system while fighting off waves of its defenders.
descriptions.c64:153095: In 2124, Emperor Hades steals the plans for ten colony ships sent out to find new worlds; a fault aboard Colony 7 leaves it exposed, and the player fights through his forces in this vertically scrolling shooter.
descriptions.c64:153096: Hägar the Viking runs and jumps through platform stages based on Dik and Chris Browne's comic, gathering the shopping list Helga hands him at the start of each level before reaching the exit, with sword and shield against enemies.
descriptions.c64:153098: A hobby-made scrolling platformer: the witch Prosperina has cursed King Zold's gold into the underworld, and Hercules descends into Hades to recover the scattered treasure.
descriptions.c64:153099: Hop between platforms to collect coins across a series of stages while cavemen and hungry dinosaurs roam; unlike Roc 'n Rope, which it resembles, there is no stun weapon, so dodging is the only defence.
descriptions.c64:153100: As drum major of the Scrimmage Stompers marching band, design a field formation and compose a new march to entertain the halftime crowd at Jazz Scat Stadium, alone or against a second player.
descriptions.c64:153101: A colour-matching puzzle from Magic Disk 64 in which pieces built on a binary scheme must be placed so that touching edges agree, recreating a target image shown on screen.
descriptions.c64:153102: Earn the command of a space shuttle mission to fire a probe into the trailing tail of Halley's Comet, first proving your piloting ability in a series of trials.
descriptions.c64:153104: A star pilot flies missions between bodies of the solar system, setting out from a base built on Halley's Comet, flying to Earth and back, and rising in rank with each completed mission until a final code is awarded.
descriptions.c64:153106: A vertically scrolling Halloween shooter made with SEUCK for two players at once, gunning down ghosts, zombies, grim reapers and demons; it appeared on Commodore Zone issue 6.
descriptions.c64:153107: Explorers descend floor after floor of caverns and rooms in search of treasure, with a split screen showing text, a map of the current floor and character stats; the real goal is getting out alive.
descriptions.c64:153108: Command a corps of US Marines in historical battles, working with incomplete reports from the front, since commanders only learn what their units radio back.
descriptions.c64:153109: A short text adventure that begins with a single rat and leads through the halls of the Dwarven Kings toward a hero's welcome in the player's home town.
descriptions.c64:153110: Explore a randomly generated tower from a long hallway of seven doors, each leading to dungeon areas of different difficulty, in an action adventure whose engine was later reused for The Warlock of Firetop Mountain.
descriptions.c64:153111: Defend a fort by bashing attacking Native Americans on the head with a huge hammer before they reach the tower, and douse the fires hurled in from the sides; later levels change the scenery.
descriptions.c64:153114: A single-screen platformer for two simultaneous players, built as an homage to Mario Bros.
descriptions.c64:153116: Two malfunctioning droids, the male Hammerfist and the female Metalisis, turn against Centro-Holographis, the regime controlling people through disguised genetic copies, swapping between the two characters to fight through each stage.
descriptions.c64:153117: A comic text adventure about climbing London's social ladder from a dole cheque and a shabby flat to the posh borough of Hampstead, gaining entry to the right places, meeting useful people and buying a cottage.
descriptions.c64:153118: A top-down golf game written in BASIC, where each shot is entered as a clock-face direction and a power value from 0 to 250, with wind shown alongside to factor in.
descriptions.c64:153159: A hangman word-guessing game distributed by Keypunch on its Fun in Learning collection.
descriptions.c64:153162: A 1996 take on hangman from SecTech Developments: guess the hidden word letter by letter before the figure is completed on the gallows.
descriptions.c64:153171: Hangman with five word categories to choose from, distributed through the CBM Public Domain disks.
descriptions.c64:154142: A text adventure starring Dr. Watson, who explores London locations, questions suspects and solves puzzles through typed verb-noun commands; location descriptions hold clues needed to recover the crown jewels.
descriptions.c64:154299: A public-domain hangman with five difficulty levels, found on the CBM Public Domain English and Games disks.
descriptions.c64:154300: Hangman again, this time with a fresh set of words to guess, written by Harry J. Saal and released by CUE.
descriptions.c64:154302: A Polish platformer loosely based on the TV drama about agent Hans Kloss (Stawka większa niż życie): Kloss infiltrates a Nazi base to gather every piece of a set of secret plans.
descriptions.c64:154303: Accused of stealing the headmaster's wallet, a troublemaking schoolboy roams the school, its grounds and the town nearby, carrying items to the right places to clear his name.
descriptions.c64:154306: A Danish platformer starring Harald Hardtooth, a tooth with arms, legs and a bow tie, who squirts toothpaste at bacteria across levels of stacked platforms.
descriptions.c64:154314: Steer a submarine through three single-screen stages to reach an enemy harbour and sink a cargo ship, starting with a side-on run past mines and nets before the air supply gives out.
descriptions.c64:154315: A 3D driving conversion of Atari's arcade game: race a sports car around a course full of traffic in both directions, hitting checkpoints to extend the time limit.
descriptions.c64:154316: A tough platformer from Multisoft's Arcadepack set in the kingdom of Sammon, where the power-hungry Corak's pact with evil has left Princess Lavina in a deep enchanted sleep.
descriptions.c64:154317: Hardhat carries bricks to build walls while dodging a lazy supervisor who pinches them, a mad company doctor with paralysing injections and a deranged welder.
descriptions.c64:154319: A rhythm party game in the style of Dance Dance Revolution, designed for a PlayStation 2 dance mat wired to a joystick port through a custom adapter; it is named after a feature of the SID sound chip.
descriptions.c64:154322: Fly a Harrier jump jet over the Strait of Hormuz to destroy seven captured military bases that have cut off oil supplies, fending off MiG-21 fighters without losing your carrier.
descriptions.c64:154323: A side-view Harrier mission: fly to the enemy island with bombs and a gun, destroying aircraft and ground targets along the way, level the enemy base and return home.
descriptions.c64:154324: An early Harrier flight simulator set over Grenada in 1984, featuring vertical take-off and landing, VIFF manoeuvres, heat-seekers, IFF radar and supersonic speeds against SAMs, jets and tanks.
descriptions.c64:154325: A single-screen duel between two portly drinkers, Harvey Headbanger and his rival Hamish Highball, who claim squares of a 64-square floor in their colour; completing a 3x3 block releases cocktails that restore energy.
descriptions.c64:154326: A horror adventure in which newlyweds must spend their honeymoon week in an ancestral mansion on a storm-lashed island and produce an heir to claim an inheritance, unaware of what awaits them.
descriptions.c64:154348: A diagonally scrolling shoot 'em up in the vein of Highway Encounter, made up of 30 training levels for the recruit facing an enemy no one else is qualified to fight.
descriptions.c64:154354: On the planet Edos, the Nevik warriors have stolen all but two of the giant crystals that store energy through the freezing nights, and the warrior Hawk Storm sets out to recover them.
descriptions.c64:154356: A strategy puzzle duel against the computer from Magic Disk 64, where luck plays no part and careful planning several moves ahead decides the winner.
descriptions.c64:154357: American football management from the makers of Football Manager: coach an NFL team, trade players and draft picks, pick the offence, defence and kicker, and call plays each week.
descriptions.c64:154358: Drive a car around concentric tracks collecting dots while avoiding a computer-driven crusher heading the other way; switch lanes to dodge it, with four cars and bonus levels.
descriptions.c64:154360: Graftgold's bouncing action game, issued on a Commodore Format covertape in 1992: collect gems while avoiding creatures called sproingers.
descriptions.c64:154362: A storybook's last six pages have gone missing, and the hero enters its world to save the white pages and destroy the black ones so evil cannot win, across six cartoonish levels.
descriptions.c64:154363: Race an offshore powerboat against four computer rivals, managing engine temperature and trim; released in Europe as Powerboat USA.
descriptions.c64:154365: Work as a radar controller at London Heathrow or Amsterdam Schiphol, guiding at least ten aircraft safely down within 30 minutes across selectable levels of difficulty.
descriptions.c64:154366: Help a small pink elephant reach Heaven by jumping between clouds, shooting monsters and grabbing the power-ups some of them drop.
descriptions.c64:154367: A mix of Tetris and shooter: shoot falling blocks of matching colour back up to where they started, across 32 levels that gradually speed up, in two game types.
descriptions.c64:154387: A cat burglar collects every painting on levels of three floors joined by ladders, relying solely on jumping to clear pits, security systems and patrolling robot sentries.
descriptions.c64:154390: A single-screen platformer from Game On where robots are shot to collect disks, which are then carried to flashing terminals.
descriptions.c64:154391: Modelled on Space Panic: dig holes in the walkways, wait for chasing monsters to fall in, then fill them so the trapped monster plunges to the floor below and dies.
descriptions.c64:154392: Rufus, a young magician eager to become a hero, sets off after a magical diamond marked on his grandfather's old treasure map.
descriptions.c64:154393: As helicopter pilot Joe Starbuck, ferry supplies to your country's besieged embassy in war-torn Moldavia and drop them on target to keep the people inside going until a rescue can be arranged.
descriptions.c64:154394: A horizontally scrolling shooter in the style of Scramble, shipped with a level editor written in BASIC and assembler.
descriptions.c64:154395: Steer a boat to catch as many of the parachutists dropped from your helicopter as possible.
descriptions.c64:154397: Fly a helicopter between a barge and an island, carrying bricks one by one to stack a hotel as tall as possible over six days, each day marked by the sun crossing the sky.
descriptions.c64:154417: A two-player cooperative SEUCK shooter that moves the action of Hell Zone from the jungle to an urban warehouse, with tougher play than the original.
descriptions.c64:154421: Jeff Minter's early shooter where one joystick drives two zone gunners at once, one running up and down a side wall and one along the bottom, blasting waves of creatures before they get through.
descriptions.c64:154422: Dropped behind enemy lines, a soldier fights aliens across side-scrolling platform levels on the way home, collecting weapons and boosts such as Teflon bullets that pierce enemies and upgrades to firepower and fire rate.
descriptions.c64:154423: A shooter spanning 101 levels, with an option to restart a level or two short of where the last game ended.
descriptions.c64:154424: A lava giant that has slept for centuries inside the volcano Titus awakens and threatens the village of Tibis and its neighbours with constant earthquakes and eruptions.
descriptions.c64:154425: A Lich keeps the stolen Helm of Immortality deep in his castle; explore the surrounding lands to gather the objects needed before storming the castle to defeat him and claim the helm.
descriptions.c64:154427: A game made for mini Ludum Dare 45 in which Van Helsing battles hordes of undead in Transylvania on his way to drive a stake into Dracula's heart.
descriptions.c64:154431: Pinball crossed with Marble Madness: roll a ball into moving alien targets before time runs out, guided by a yellow arrow to the next one, with hazards, bonus items and sequence bonuses on later levels.
descriptions.c64:154434: A text adventure in which He-Man must stop Skeletor's Earthquaker, a device that uses hypnotic rays to command Rockbinders, huge boulder beasts able to chew through solid rock.
descriptions.c64:154439: Herakles, a would-be hero in an ancient Greece plagued by supernatural beasts and cruel kings, undertakes a series of trials to prove himself while the gods ignore the people's prayers.
descriptions.c64:154440: Guide Herby through 100 chambers of lasers, monsters and moving electrified walls, picking up keys, potions of life and mysterious bags.
descriptions.c64:154445: The second Herby game sends him through ten levels where the key to each room's exit must be found and the purpose of every bag worked out.
descriptions.c64:154446: A punishingly hard flick-screen platformer in which Hercules must complete a series of titanic tasks.
descriptions.c64:154447: A beat 'em up starring Hercules, son of Zeus, who must collect icons representing the twelve labours set by the King of Argos while fighting through enemies.
descriptions.c64:154448: Ambrose, a medieval monk, is ordered by the archbishop to kill a hermit believed to be the devil reborn, but a sudden searing pain in his head changes the course of his journey.
descriptions.c64:154452: An evil wizard has broken the Golden Talisman that guarded the hero's town into five pieces and hidden them in a monster-filled labyrinth; recover all five and defeat the wizard.
descriptions.c64:154464: An expansion for HeroQuest adapted from the board game supplement, with linked quests sending the heroes into the ruined city of Kalos to defeat the returning Witch Lord.
descriptions.c64:154466: Control a Herobot sent by a rebel faction into the base of the Alliance of Space Pilots, finding the six parts of the stolen Z-Ray weapon and downloading data from the main computer past 12 kinds of enemy droid.
descriptions.c64:154467: The third Midgard game: Eris, the Huntress of Midgard, fights the creatures of Morrigan, who are hunting for the pieces of a talisman that would let them seize the holy city.
descriptions.c64:154468: Up to six players compete in six track and field events, with replays of each attempt and simulations of the era's world-record runs and throws to train against.
descriptions.c64:154473: An isometric Q*Bert-style game: hop Bert around a pyramid of hexagons, changing each one's colour by landing on it, while dodging bouncing balls and a snake sent by the witch Zoganaar.
descriptions.c64:154475: An educational program that builds reasoning skills in young children through nursery rhymes, split into storytime, a storybook paged by the player and a rhyme game.
descriptions.c64:154476: Cartwheel around as Mr. Bounce from the Mr. Men books, helping characters such as Mr. Tall across four screens, each with eight increasingly difficult versions.
descriptions.c64:154477: Gem-matching puzzle in the style of Shisen-Sho: pick two identical gems on a 16x6 grid and they vanish if a path with no more than two turns links them. Each board must be cleared before the timer expires, and a built-in editor lets you design new layouts.
descriptions.c64:154488: Learning to read the time on an analogue clock is the aim of this children's program from Valueware's Educator II collection.
descriptions.c64:154489: A text adventure about a hunt for the fabled treasure of the Incas.
descriptions.c64:154492: A classroom program in which students put the ideas of an excerpted literary passage into the correct order and write about the reading.
descriptions.c64:154493: Bill must rescue his girlfriend Greta from giant ants planning to eat her by crushing every ant egg on each of three levels while three gi-gants hunt him; warp tunnels sit on either side.
descriptions.c64:154494: A game about evasion rather than shooting: dodge the streams of aliens flying at you and escape using your thrusters.
descriptions.c64:154497: A strategy game about developing America's Strategic Defense Initiative to counter a feared Soviet missile attack, run through icon-driven screens and information panels.
descriptions.c64:154498: A two-player memory game of coloured stones: memorise the board, then pick pairs; a correct pair scores, while a wrong guess swaps the two stones and costs a try.
descriptions.c64:154499: A crosshair shooting game for the Stack Light Rifle.
descriptions.c64:154501: Three Card Brag from the Cassette 50 collection, where three threes is the top hand, followed by three aces, kings and queens, then running flushes.
descriptions.c64:154502: An adaptation of the TV game show High Rollers: two contestants roll dice and knock out numbers, buzzing in to answer a trivia question for each roll.
descriptions.c64:154505: Naval combat from the age of fighting sail, played from a graphical deck view with a chart for checking position in fleet actions, in 10-minute turns or interrupted to give orders.
descriptions.c64:154506: One or two players compete in five Scottish events such as the hammer throw, each based on timing and fast joystick movement.
descriptions.c64:154522: Steer a Vorton droid along an isometric highway, pushing a bomb through 30 screens of barrels, mines and aliens to deliver it into the alien base at the end.
descriptions.c64:155258: A Mastermind-style logic game of deducing a hidden code, published as a listing in 64'er magazine.
descriptions.c64:155259: A board game quiz for between two and four players, who roll dice and move around the board answering questions in four colour-coded subjects, needing one of each before returning to the centre for a final question.
descriptions.c64:155260: A head-to-head Tetris variant for two players, released on Magic Disk 64 and Tiger-Crew-Disk.
descriptions.c64:155266: Prince Zanock of Altoris crosses the hobgoblin swamps to recover the stolen Golden Orb in this Ghosts 'n Goblins clone, jumping through a spooky landscape of monsters in little more than his underwear.
descriptions.c64:155270: Junior photographer Jeremy is sent by the Daily Shocker's editor to snap the strange inventions and mutants in an arrested professor's underground lair.
descriptions.c64:155275: A series of holiday-themed events, from cramming suitcases into the car boot to a run of competitions on arrival at the beach.
descriptions.c64:155276: A follow-up to Hollywood Poker: choose one of four opponents and play draw poker against her until one of you runs out of money.
descriptions.c64:155278: A conversion of the 1980s Hollywood Squares game show: two contestants play tic-tac-toe on a board of celebrities, agreeing or disagreeing with each celebrity's answer to capture squares.
descriptions.c64:155311: Early-cinema actor Buster Baloney searches a side-scrolling movie studio for five missing Oscars, climbing ladders between floors and entering film sets while the cameras roll.
descriptions.c64:155342: Hong Kong Phooey leaps from his filing cabinet to track down Baron Von Bankjob, who has broken out of jail, in a platform game based on the cartoon.
descriptions.c64:155343: A superhero defends his home planet from the Mighty Alien Presence of Kerllis IX and its Boolagrop invaders, who did not realise the world they invaded had a protector.
descriptions.c64:155344: Fill every square on a grid across a range of levels, either by collecting the dots on its edges or by laying dots along its lines, depending on the level.
descriptions.c64:155345: A 2-kilobyte platformer that won a 64'er magazine competition: guide Benny through 19 levels of water holes, awkward platforms and flying cannonballs.
descriptions.c64:155346: A 5-kilobyte sequel for 64'er magazine with 21 levels of water holes and chasms, guarded by flying cannonballs, ghosts, crawling pigs and a fourth, jumping enemy.
descriptions.c64:155347: Grove Town's policeman must round up four criminals within a time limit, bouncing around town on a space hopper because the crooks have hidden every vehicle.
descriptions.c64:155348: Collect balloons while avoiding contact with too many enemies, with a cameo from Bub of Bubble Bobble; published in Game On.
descriptions.c64:155353: Licensed from the arcade game Bongo: cross 27 flick screens of a vast cavern from left to right, moving quickly before a T-Rex appears and gives chase.
descriptions.c64:155360: Pac-Man-inspired maze action in which Horace races through a quick run of small mazes full of corridors, a wrap-around section and a tunnel, with one power pill per level.
descriptions.c64:155361: A crosshair shooter from Novotrade where Sinclair shoots her way through a futuristic city's streets and subway concourses full of aliens.
descriptions.c64:155391: Pilot a hot air balloon on air currents and changing weather, dropping traps to capture endangered elephants and bring them to protected reserves.
descriptions.c64:155392: Milk climbs ladders and hops between platforms to gather every piece of fruit on the screen and free his girlfriend from a house, while his rival Nuts tries to stop him.
descriptions.c64:155397: A tile-flipping colour puzzle written for the 1K category of the 2006 Minigame Competition.
descriptions.c64:155398: Play the commandant of a WW2 prisoner-of-war camp, patrolling the grounds around the central barracks to stop tiny prisoners digging escape tunnels across the screen.
descriptions.c64:155571: Free Houdini from three death traps with two, three and four locks by guessing each lock's number between 1 and 75, guided by too-high or too-low hints, all within 60 seconds.
descriptions.c64:155585: Larry Atkin's chess program for Odesta, written in 6502 assembly and derived from the Capablanca modules that powered the Great Game Machine and Chafitz Modular Game System dedicated chess computers.
descriptions.c64:155586: Chess 7.5 by Larry Atkin, co-author of the Chess 3 and 4 series of programs that dominated computer chess through much of the 1970s.
descriptions.c64:155603: A Q*bert variant in which Hubert jumps around a pyramid of cubes, recolouring each tile he lands on until all match the target, with some levels needing several hops per tile and enemies in pursuit.
descriptions.c64:155605: Every level takes place at a different stage of human evolution, with the hero progressing from ape to caveman and beyond while jumping around a single screen to collect objects for points.
descriptions.c64:155606: In 2850 AD, Captain Gyro escapes captivity on the planet Vulso by crossing three environments of robots, comets, UFOs and aliens to reach his Super Star Cruiser, sealed behind a door with a four-letter password.
descriptions.c64:155607: Jet-pack across a horizontally scrolling landscape shooting waves of aliens, catching the B icons they drop before they hit the ground to unlock a final wave.
descriptions.c64:155608: A Q*Bert-style game in which Humphrey hops across blocks to change their colour while atomic bombs drop from block to block.
descriptions.c64:155609: Two educational whodunits for ages 7 to 10: work out by elimination which of the King's men pushed Humpty off the wall, and who killed Cock Robin.
descriptions.c64:155610: Quasimodo goes for Olympic gold in a joystick-waggling athletics game covering the 100m sprint, 110m hurdles, long jump, high jump, shot put, discus and javelin, with well-timed releases needed in the field events.
descriptions.c64:155815: Steer a ship around a solar base and bump the invading Space Nasties off it, some far harder to shove than others, until each screen is clear.
descriptions.c64:155893: Fly to the planet Darx to mine the minerals Earth needs for a defence shield against alien invasion, only to find the planet is inhabited and your ship has been spotted.
descriptions.c64:155899: A winter extreme sports game with five events, including Downhill Blitz with jumps and moguls and Innertube Thrash, where two players race down a mountain in inner tubes collecting items and popping each other.
descriptions.c64:155906: Pole Position-style Formula 1 on the Hungarian Hungaroring circuit, timed by a clock that counts up, with a manual four-speed gearbox and adjustable lap count and number of rival cars.
descriptions.c64:155908: A Tom Clancy adaptation in which Captain Marko Ramius guides the submarine Red October across the Atlantic to defect, meeting the US Navy and faking the sub's destruction while the Soviet fleet hunts him.
descriptions.c64:155912: Move a spacecraft between the rectangles of a 6x5 grid firing missiles at Roboships, which try to ram you while sidestepping missiles fired in a straight line.
descriptions.c64:155921: Set in 3002, this follow-up to Knight Games is made up of three futuristic contests: Combat Robot, the orbital In Orbit and the Final Tournament; Combat Robot borrows from Dropzone, with Robby the Robot rescuing friendly robots and shooting enemies.
descriptions.c64:155928: A spaceship pilot short on ammunition after a ground crew blunder must flee to Earth with aliens in pursuit, relying on dodging and outmanoeuvring them.
descriptions.c64:155931: A two-player overhead pool duel known in Europe as Pottit: each player shoots their own white or black ball at the red, worth two points when potted, racing to be first to 50.
descriptions.c64:155932: Huxley Pig left his door open, and creepy crawlies have hidden his toys and his pilot, chef and sailor outfits; he must collect everything before he can go to bed and dream.
descriptions.c64:155933: A tour guide on the planet Cubos shepherds a group of Blobpods, mindless balls that bounce until they hit a block, through 100 side-scrolling levels of stairs and gaps.
descriptions.c64:155934: Venusian aliens held in a jail designed to keep rescuers out rather than prisoners in are growing too strong and must be destroyed before they break free.
descriptions.c64:155935: A champion speedboat racer works for the government of Hydra, couriering parts of a secret weapon through narrow swamp channels while its enemies try to stop the deliveries.
descriptions.c64:155936: An action adventure through a vast underground world of puzzles, riddles and hostile creatures, ending in a battle with the dragon Hydrax.
descriptions.c64:155938: A futuristic team sport for two, the human Hawks against the Vipers, each fielding three players picked from a pool of ten with different strength, agility and speed, passing a ball to shoot into a moving central basket.
descriptions.c64:155940: A one-button timing game: a ball bounces sideways above a narrow platform, and pressing fire drops it straight down; land on the platform to continue, miss and the game ends.
descriptions.c64:155942: A two-player strategy puzzle meant to teach binary numbers, played on a board of red, blue and grey neutral fields each marked 0 or 1.
descriptions.c64:155943: Motorbike trials for up to four riders, racing a human or computer rival, where each event demands a set of manoeuvres and the fastest qualifying time earns a place in the next.
descriptions.c64:155947: Two pink blobs float around the screen trying to drop weights on each other; the first to land nine hits wins.
descriptions.c64:155954: Built with the Hyper Car construction set, this racer pits one or two players against the computer or a computer-controlled rival, to a Euro dance soundtrack.
descriptions.c64:155956: Move through the maze-like circuits of 6510 processor chips inside the computer, protecting 35 base units by destroying 20 creatures in a scrolling overhead view.
descriptions.c64:155957: A two-player-only duel modelled on Super Dogfight: wear down the other spacecraft's shield before yours is drained, with options for game length and speed.
descriptions.c64:155958: Steer a snake to collect every dot, growing longer with each one and never biting your own tail.
descriptions.c64:155960: A scrolling overhead maze where every snake on the level must be eaten from behind; approaching one head-on gets you eaten instead.
descriptions.c64:155961: A homeless vagrant works his way up through four districts of a city, starting by getting a haircut and cleaning up, with the aim of amassing a million dollars.
descriptions.c64:155962: A futuristic one-on-one ball game seen from above: each player picks one of ten spaceships with different speed, inertia and fire direction, with a scanner tracking both ships and the ball.
descriptions.c64:155963: A damaged space pilot on a final mission before going home flies through chambers collecting randomly appearing pods while the walls close in.
descriptions.c64:155964: Unpublished shooter by Chris Caress and Lee Cawley, rushed together for a PCW show, with every alien attack pattern recorded by hand on a joystick. Turned down by Mastertronic, the submitted disk ended up with Jason Kelk, who released it years later along with a lost Matt Gray tune.
descriptions.c64:155965: Space Academy cadets race a spacecraft low over a constantly scrolling surface, alone or two at once on a split screen, with some shooting, to complete the course and graduate.
descriptions.c64:155966: On the planet Gumball, a pair of rubber balls speed over rough terrain collecting points within a time limit, in three modes: Shootem Double, a solo variant and Double Tactics.
descriptions.c64:155968: Roll a ball across enemies around the screen to protect your own underpants.
descriptions.c64:155969: Catch every leprechaun while avoiding holes, frogs and the fairy folk with their magic attacks; published on GO64! magazine.
descriptions.c64:155970: A memory game in which pictures hidden under numbered squares are revealed two at a time, with matching pairs staying face up until the board is cleared.
descriptions.c64:155971: One of the first 3D football games, played from just behind a single footballer; signalling teammates for a pass is central, since the team will not win without the player's own involvement.
descriptions.c64:155972: Simulmondo's 3D tennis has a career element: create or choose a player whose forehand, backhand, serve and volley improve with each victory, earning prize money and climbing the rankings.
descriptions.c64:155973: An expansion of I Play: 3D Soccer adding team tactics planning and a fuller league season in Italy, England or Germany, with squad selection before each match.
descriptions.c64:155974: Homage to The Great Giana Sisters in which Giana travels to the planet Troll-Land after a meteor strike to gather its diamonds, running and jumping through side-scrolling levels. Treasure chests hide rockets, knives and ninja weapons, and the Wall-Breaker rocket can smash through obstacles.
