descriptions.c64:155975: An FBI agent stranded on an island of cannibals must escape before he ends up eaten; first written with Adventure Writer as a short sample adventure.
descriptions.c64:155976: A bouncing ball descends mines to learn its people's history, finding a key and the exit on each of 50 screens and picking up a sacred artefact every fifth level.
descriptions.c64:155977: After nuclear war wiped out Earth's livestock, humans scour space for protein; as a captured alien, escape through the ship via colour-coded transporters in a side-on view.
descriptions.c64:155978: Cricket for one or two players with limited-overs, one-day and full Test match modes, played by keyboard or joystick, with an armchair mode that names the teams for you.
descriptions.c64:155979: A management game for up to ten players, each running an ice cream stall bought with piggy bank savings and competing for customers.
descriptions.c64:155980: After the biggest snowfall ever, everyone is out building snowmen until nasty creatures scare people away and carry off the snowmen.
descriptions.c64:155981: The castle's lord hurls blocks onto a see-saw; standing on the far end launches you skyward, but green monsters on the wall grab you or the block, and five blocks at once jam the see-saw.
descriptions.c64:155984: Terrorist group Stirling demands a billion dollars to spare New York, issuing threats from a captured polar research station, and a lone agent must slip past its defences to shut them down.
descriptions.c64:155985: A two-player ice hockey game loosely based on the arcade Hat Trick; it has no connection to the drink.
descriptions.c64:155986: Galactic dustman Nick Razor tracks his stolen Space Cruiser, accidentally hyperspaced by the thieves, to the remote Ice Temple, which turns out to be much more than it seems.
descriptions.c64:155987: A bouncing ball that can only jump must collect every diamond across floating platforms on single-screen levels, steering clear of aliens, bombs, lasers and spikes while watching its air pressure.
descriptions.c64:155988: A horizontally scrolling cave shooter: weave around stalactites and stalagmites while gunning down aliens, losing energy each time the ship touches rock.
descriptions.c64:155989: An interstellar pilot must shoot down as many crafty, aggressive aliens as possible, chiefly with a laser, without making mistakes.
descriptions.c64:155990: A mostly text-based, turn-based ice hockey management game for up to four players.
descriptions.c64:155991: A text adventure about escaping Isiseros, where a 12-gauge shotgun and a passport both play their part.
descriptions.c64:155993: Santa returns from holiday to find the presents strewn about and buried in snow, and must dig them out while avoiding avalanches and grumpy penguins and polar bears.
descriptions.c64:155994: To join I.C.U.P.S., an international commission devoted to solving universal problems, a recruit must pass two tests, the first an overhead space shooter against assorted enemy craft.
descriptions.c64:155995: A first computer program for children aged 2 to 8: assemble a face from a range of features using just two keys, with fifteen thousand possible combinations.
descriptions.c64:155997: A Cessna 172RG Cutlass simulator flown entirely on instruments, with no outside view, only a panel of gauges: altimeter, rev counter, artificial horizon, airspeed, turn and climb-rate indicators.
descriptions.c64:156011: A Joust-style duel between two phoenixes: tap fire to flap and climb, steer only while flapping, and score by striking the opponent from above.
descriptions.c64:156012: One-on-one martial arts fighting where, alone, the player takes on a series of ninjas in different coloured outfits across several difficulty levels, needing two round wins to advance; a two-player mode is included.
descriptions.c64:156013: A best-of-three martial arts duel between blue and red ninjas in a castle, from Magic Disk 64; the title is Japanese for roughly 'duel'.
descriptions.c64:156052: Silicon Warriors compete to program five chips in a row, horizontally, vertically or diagonally, while rivals steal programmed chips, fire lasers and black-hole glitches threaten to swallow them.
descriptions.c64:156093: Sergeant Seymour stars as a futuristic Robot Cop, arresting every villain across 30 overhead maze levels, which destroys each level's boss automatically.
descriptions.c64:156098: Your ship circles the Earth and can fire in eight directions but never change course, defending the planet from alien ships whose shots sink parts of the Northern Hemisphere into the sea.
descriptions.c64:156104: Fight waves of aliens that mutate into deadlier forms the longer they live, with a formation attack on every third or fourth wave and a radar at the top showing their positions.
descriptions.c64:156180: A Qix variant from 64'er in which an area is gradually filled with a picture by cutting off segments one at a time, with many additions to the original idea.
descriptions.c64:156181: A text adventure built from four parodies of well-known games: Panic Miner, Raid over Margate, Lords of Half Past Nine and a space spoof titled 2002.
descriptions.c64:156182: Imperium astronaut Roberto runs, ducks and jumps past aliens whose touch kills on his way to destroy the alien command at Antezium.
descriptions.c64:156183: An early 4X space strategy game featuring ship design, troop transports and guerrilla resistance on conquered planets, though without tactical space battles.
descriptions.c64:156186: As Punch, search the streets of Bridlington in summer 1989 for the pieces of his puppet tent and the missing cast before the tide comes in, moving screen by screen in side view.
descriptions.c64:156201: Time traveller Wyatt Hunter must gather 100 Golden Masks from a flick-screen maze in Zulu territory before he is pulled back to his own time, avoiding the warriors who roam it.
descriptions.c64:156239: A GAC text adventure that opens with the horror of waking to a tidy bedroom; the quest is to track down the missing bag of rubbish and put it back where it belongs.
descriptions.c64:156256: Based on the TV series: Super Gran foils Scunner Campbell and his henchmen Tub and Rent-a-muscle over eight levels in four different styles of play, beginning in a flying machine.
descriptions.c64:156296: On 8 May 1941, command the battleship Bismarck and try to break through the British Home Fleet, sinking enough convoys to starve Britain into surrender; victory depends on merchant ships and warships sunk.
descriptions.c64:156298: An illustrated text adventure in which Rikka, a warrior friendly with the ruler Arrel, faces Traklan, an evil lord risen after an eternity imprisoned underground to threaten the land of Armosin.
descriptions.c64:156304: Six-a-side water polo on a pseudo-3D pool about two screens wide that scrolls with the ball, with demo, one-player, two-player and championship modes.
descriptions.c64:156403: A mad doctor gathers corpses by robbing graves or murdering villagers, then dismembers them in the lab and stitches the parts together into a monster.
descriptions.c64:156501: Monty Mole is beamed up by aliens and sent across five worlds to recover the sacred scrolls of their Guardians.
descriptions.c64:156504: Based on Jules Verne's story: as Phileas Fogg, wager your entire 20,000-pound fortune at London's Reform Club and set off with Passepartout on 2 October to circle the globe in 80 days.
descriptions.c64:156505: Uncle Smoke Bailey lost The Most Amazing Thing, an object holding the secrets of the universe, somewhere in the Mire, and the player sets out in his B-Liner to recover it.
descriptions.c64:156506: Evolve from a lone molecule 3,000 million years ago up to the first humans through ten timed single-screen mini-games, each a step in the process.
descriptions.c64:156507: Run a Silicon Valley software company with an initial $100,000 investment, growing market share against a rival firm run by the computer or a second player, one fiscal period per turn.
descriptions.c64:156508: An educational problem-solving game where a mad scientist experiments with chemicals like Fuzzy Mold, Bubbling Mud and even StinkySocks to work out which body part each one gives a monster.
descriptions.c64:156509: An original Indiana Jones adventure in which Indy hunts for a lost civilisation across six screens, each with monsters and puzzles blocking the exits, to reach the treasure and escape.
descriptions.c64:156513: A Super Sprint-style overhead racer endorsed by Danny Sullivan: four cars per race, one or two players and nine tracks, ending at the long, double-points Tradewest Speed Bowl.
descriptions.c64:156514: A Reversi-inspired board strategy game, completed but shelved by Virgin, whose idea later became Ataxx and Spot: spread your pieces across the grid to convert neighbouring enemy pieces, against the computer or in a four-player mode, with a level editor.
descriptions.c64:156515: Trapped in a house full of deadly traps, a runner must collect every key, open every chest and find food to survive, roaming freely back and forth through the rooms.
descriptions.c64:156519: An Infocom text adventure: abandoned by his crew in the Egyptian desert, a fortune hunter seeks the riches hidden inside a pyramid, at risk of starving before finding them.
descriptions.c64:156520: A groom-to-be wakes up hungover in a box, where his friends left him after his farewell party the night before his wedding.
descriptions.c64:156522: On a planet devoted to administration, build a start-up delivery company into a major player, sending droids along five streams of differing speeds to deliver information and packages.
descriptions.c64:156523: A French point-and-click adventure in first-person view: Peter Stone flies to Las Vegas to collect his late aunt's fortune after a notary's telegram.
descriptions.c64:156524: The sequel to Panic in Las Vegas: to claim the castle left by his aunt in Scotland, the hero must find the family book proving his identity while fake nephews keep appearing.
descriptions.c64:156534: A hot-seat strategy and role-playing game for up to four players competing for a crown, with menu settings for provinces, villages and their costs, among others.
descriptions.c64:156537: Shinjitsu Software's tile-matching puzzle, with selectable music, tile sets and colour schemes.
descriptions.c64:156538: A Defender-style side-scrolling shooter: after insects wipe out humanity except for a few babies, the mystical St. Helen flies to the ruined Earth to rescue them.
descriptions.c64:156540: When the circus arrives in town, people start vanishing and Penny and Brains are kidnapped; Inspector Gadget jumps over enemies through side-scrolling levels to reach each goal.
descriptions.c64:156541: A text adventure in which John, a patient held against his will at an asylum called the Institute, endures raving inmates, mocking doctors and a sinister psychologist insisting he is insane.
descriptions.c64:156542: Evacuate the alien-overrun space station Canis Major by flying a skimmer over single-screen levels and marking spots where a rescue drone ship can land to pick up the crew.
descriptions.c64:156543: Computerised detective Insector Hecti must undo the work of Victor Virus and his bugs, who have turned blocks the wrong way on 50 circuits of the sensitive Interchange.
descriptions.c64:156544: Demanding space flight simulator set in 2133 during the First Galactic War, putting you in the cockpit of an Interdictor Mk 3 fighter. Dozens of keys plus the joystick control the craft, and a training mode lets you practise against enemy ships.
descriptions.c64:156545: A wrestling game in an elevated-view ring floating in space, for one or two players, against five fighters from across the universe, where the aim is to scale the cage around the ring.
descriptions.c64:156547: Tennis with ten camera angles, 64 computer opponents across 15 skill levels, 72 tournaments modelled on real events and grass, clay, carpet and cement courts, plus a full-season mode and topspin and backspin shots.
descriptions.c64:156554: An accident has wiped the hero's memory, so he travels the world relearning the knowledge he has lost and seeking out the people close to him who can help piece his past back together.
descriptions.c64:156555: Lead an ice hockey team up the league table; with the puck, hold fire to wind up a shot, the longer the press the harder it goes.
descriptions.c64:156562: A budget management game for a European national football side: an initial eleven and two substitutes are picked from 24 squad members and 16 hopefuls, and the formation, playing style and tactics can all be changed.
descriptions.c64:156563: A rabbit in ninja garb fights thugs, ninjas, bears and frogs one at a time, mostly heading right but sometimes dropping into the sewers or metro.
descriptions.c64:156564: Motorcycle speedway on oval tracks: start in a local league and win promotion through tougher leagues of riders toward the world championship.
descriptions.c64:156565: Up to four players compete across 21 events in six sports, including springboard and platform diving and a 26-mile marathon, played individually in any combination or in sequence.
descriptions.c64:156566: Two players represent countries competing for medals in five team sports, choosing seven athletes from a list and assigning them to sports according to how many each one needs.
descriptions.c64:156570: An overhead truck racing simulation with six trucks per race on international circuits, where deliberately heavy handling mimics real trucks and refuelling stops come every few laps.
descriptions.c64:156572: Summoned to interview for the post of chief programmer at Front Runner within 15 minutes, first dash to the bank for money to buy a suit, across two arcade sequences.
descriptions.c64:156574: A text adventure made with The Quill, unrelated to the Van Morrison song, that opens with the problem of evading a gang of orcs and may lead to a meeting with Merlin.
descriptions.c64:156576: A film-noir mystery set at real Washington D.C. locations: your detective brother Joe has disappeared while probing a scheme to spread a virus through the city's air, and you take up the case by questioning suspects.
descriptions.c64:156579: In 3897 the Galactic Imperium rules nearly every world except Octapolis, whose telekinetic powers baffle pilots and machines alike, until a pilot immune to them is finally found to lead the attack.
descriptions.c64:156585: Capcom's side-scrolling shooter set around the airspace of Area 88: pick Shin Kazama, Micky Schymon or the veteran Greg Gates, each pilot with different strengths, and fly a series of military missions.
descriptions.c64:156586: A one-on-one future sport loosely based on netball, played by droids on an isometric court where the joystick moves diagonally and the goal is to outscore the opponent.
descriptions.c64:156587: An air hockey-like future sport in which two ground skimmers, human or computer controlled, plan their moves by drawing a movement line before taking turns to knock a puck into the other's goal.
descriptions.c64:156589: A tape fast loader by Richard Aplin that let players shoot their way through a small Space Invaders clone while the main game loaded from cassette.
descriptions.c64:156593: A single-screen take on Space Invaders: slide a laser base along the bottom and shoot a formation of aliens that sweeps across the screen, dropping lower at each edge.
descriptions.c64:156607: Direct army units by cursor in an overhead strategy game on an alien planet, where units engage enemies automatically; the target is the weather control station, which falls when at least two bombs explode beside it.
descriptions.c64:156609: Pilot a ship out through the planet's Mushroom Farm, avoiding giant mutated mushrooms and dodging or shooting runaway harvesting robots; an entry in the 2006 Crap Game Compo.
descriptions.c64:156610: A Cassette 50 game in which a bug creeps up the screen avoiding mushrooms whose spores keep spreading downward.
descriptions.c64:156612: Turn-based business for up to four players: buy companies, sell the goods they make and reinvest the profits in new businesses, shares and upgrades.
descriptions.c64:156613: A timed puzzle: flip 2x2 blocks of squares between black and white until the whole board is white, with the starting patterns growing trickier each level.
descriptions.c64:156614: A utility that keeps a running digital clock in 24-hour time on screen, placed in the lower border and shown in hours, minutes and seconds with a small AM/PM marker.
descriptions.c64:156615: A baseball trivia quiz from Davka with ballpark sound effects, surprise events and even rain delays.
descriptions.c64:156616: A light-hearted baseball trivia quiz built around Jewish themes, presented as coming from the authors of IQ Baseball.
descriptions.c64:156623: A horizontally scrolling shooter in the vein of Uridium whose default high score table is filled with characters from Frank Zappa songs; released in Italy as Fleet.
descriptions.c64:156628: Fly a plane over 21 levels against Dr. Destructo, shooting his aircraft down so they crash into the large ship or island target below, with repeated hits on one spot eventually breaking through.
descriptions.c64:156630: A Clue-style murder mystery from Loadstar where the detective questions suspects to identify the killer.
descriptions.c64:156631: First of the Nick Hardy trilogy from the Commodore Pro-Pak: Nick has wrecked his interstellar missile cruiser on a strange alien world and must recapture it, repair it and escape.
descriptions.c64:156632: The second Nick Hardy adventure, from the Commodore Pro-Pak, follows him through the South American tropics after a hidden Inca treasure.
descriptions.c64:156635: The third Nick Hardy adventure begins as enemy fire knocks out both engines of the hero's plane over a spy-infested island, forcing a parachute drop into the enemy stronghold.
descriptions.c64:156701: Based on the French comic, the Grand Vizier Iznogoud schemes to take the Caliph's place, exploring magical Baghdad, talking to characters and collecting objects.
descriptions.c64:156702: Steer a sphere through isometric levels of four linked sections, in the spirit of Marble Madness and Spindizzy, using special squares that among other things change the ball's size.
descriptions.c64:156706: Football anticipating the 1990 World Cup in Italy, shown in side-scrolling third person: pick a team and steer either the ball carrier or the nearest player in eight directions.
descriptions.c64:156708: Explore a mansion haunted by four ghosts, fending them off by throwing heavy objects, to find eight musical boxes and play each one at the way out, working out what the items in the many rooms are for.
descriptions.c64:156709: A World War II strategy game on the US invasion of Iwo Jima: command American forces on a full map of the island against a computer-controlled Japanese defence with five difficulty levels.
descriptions.c64:156710: A dazzling Empire logo has broken into four pieces inside a soap-bubble factory; in a robot suit, track down a Mini Interdimensional Storage Unit that can hold them, then recover each piece.
descriptions.c64:156733: An overhead football game tied to the 1990 World Cup with the full tournament structure, all 24 teams, a choice of formations and team selection before each match, and the ball sticking to players' feet.
descriptions.c64:156736: Operation Iceberg: command the Allied invasion of Okinawa on a map of the island in this World War II strategy game, against computer-controlled Japanese forces with eight difficulty levels.
descriptions.c64:156767: A two-player light cycle duel: each rider leaves a solid wall behind, and hitting a trail or the edge of the board loses.
descriptions.c64:156768: Crush the eight spinning heads on each level by landing on them or shoving blocks onto them, with later stages adding platforms and deadly water.
descriptions.c64:156769: A gallery shooter set in a city at night: move the crosshair across apartment windows to find and gun down gangsters quickly, while sparing the ordinary residents who also appear.
descriptions.c64:156770: A coarse fishing contest endorsed by footballer Jack Charlton, in which as many as eight anglers compete at the same match.
descriptions.c64:156772: A private eye text adventure: hired by Mrs Gloria F. Bannister to recover her stolen necklace before her husband notices, you roam a city gathering clues, quizzing people and taking on other jobs along the way.
descriptions.c64:156774: A reworked edition of the text adventure Insanity in San Francisco, with new graphics, revised play and extra contributors, again built around an attempt to break out of Alcatraz.
descriptions.c64:156775: A squash simulation viewed isometrically, enforcing legal shots under the real rules, with three ball speeds, adjustable match lengths and an easy mode.
descriptions.c64:156818: Opera Soft recreates Basque pelota: teams of two take turns catching the ball in the wicker cesta and flinging it back against the front wall of a three-walled court, scoring only while they hold the serve.
descriptions.c64:156819: As Rankin Rodney, gather four musical instruments and return each to its home across 20 single-screen levels, hopping between coloured zones on moving circles that only accept a matching colour.
descriptions.c64:156951: Pilot a ship through the hazardous levels of the Netherworld, grabbing diamonds against the clock to advance while dragons, drifting mines and acid-spitting creatures attack; the craft can fire back.
descriptions.c64:157017: Steer Pierre around single-screen stages to hoist every flag, dodging lightning, snowball shooters and electro-generators and using helpful items to get about.
descriptions.c64:157118: A stray cat prowls dim city streets eating fish bones to prove it rules the neighbourhood, moving to new territory once fed while watching out for hawks, hedgehogs and frogs.
descriptions.c64:157175: An illustrated text adventure: a late uncle's map of Captain Kidd's treasure leads to two remote South Pacific islands, Jara-Tava and Jara-Mau, with sharks in the water and a volcano about to blow.
descriptions.c64:157179: A 2011 homebrew take on the Atari 2600 hit Yars' Revenge: a creature at the left edge chips away at the shield guarding a Quotile base opposite before blasting it, level after level.
descriptions.c64:157180: Bounce a ball through a series of mazes, picking up every dot; the name stands for Just A Simple Game, and it appeared on the Magic Disk 64 issue of April 1990.
descriptions.c64:157182: Java Jim explores eight regions of a square-tiled tropical island, digging holes for treasure while the central volcano rains fireballs onto squares every few seconds and warp holes shift him around.
descriptions.c64:157183: Unlike other versions, this one is not a maze game: eat every candy across five horizontal lanes to earn a tooth brushing and a tougher level, avoiding the roaming happy faces.
descriptions.c64:157184: A Q*Bert-style game: hop J-Bird around a pyramid to turn every tile the target colour while a snake, frogs, cats and dropping balls interfere, with four rounds per level.
descriptions.c64:157185: Drive a lunar jeep across 900 kilometres of cratered surface in the vein of Moon Patrol, jumping boulders and gaps, shooting rocks out of the way and racing a time limit.
descriptions.c64:157186: A spider crawls over seven rows of cabbages to infect them and change their colour, moving in eight directions before a bonus timer runs out.
descriptions.c64:157187: Carry stars to the pot while avoiding biting bugs and a ticking clock; filling the pot moves Jeffy to a level where the bugs move at a new speed. Released on GO64! in August 2005.
descriptions.c64:157197: On the planet Andromadous, a droid herds alien sheep called Ramboids into a teleporter, first crossing a chamber full of them and then guiding them to the receptor in a set order, with 20 minutes per level.
descriptions.c64:157201: The TV quiz show where contestants answer in the form of a question: three players compete over two rounds of six categories worth $100 to $1000, with daily doubles and a final round.
descriptions.c64:157204: A sports-themed Jeopardy! with over 1000 answers covering Olympic events like swimming, gymnastics and athletics as well as football, golf and baseball, for one to three players.
descriptions.c64:157205: A junior edition of the Jeopardy! quiz show aimed at younger players, keeping the format of responding to each answer with a question.
descriptions.c64:157209: Fly over city skylines while weaving through crowded airspace in this avoidance game, published in Game On in August 1989.
descriptions.c64:157212: Ride a jet ski against computer opponents, alone or with a friend, over lap-based courses set in docks, lakes and coastline, finishing within the time limit to unlock the next course.
descriptions.c64:157213: Taken from the Cassette 50 compilation: in this Blitz-style bomber, a plane low on fuel must level the enemy city one bomb at a time before it can land, with difficulty rising after successful runs.
descriptions.c64:157214: Jack is held prisoner by the warlord Nogrob and must collect fuel pods for his flying saucer, wrestling with a hard-to-control jet pack while dodging aliens, in the manner of Jetpac.
descriptions.c64:157223: Get a fighter-bomber off the runway before enemy raids destroy it, climb to altitude, hold the right bearing to the target while evading air attacks, then strike it.
descriptions.c64:157225: A flight simulator derived from subLOGIC's Flight Simulator: fly an F-16 over land or an F-18 from a carrier, with free flight and aerobatics, dogfights against MiGs, ground and sea strikes and subLOGIC scenery disks.
descriptions.c64:157226: Jet-Boot Jack chases escaped music notes down through ten platform levels, dropping through gaps, riding moving platforms and switching off the enemies that hover over the holes; five levels can be chosen from the menu.
descriptions.c64:157227: The sequel to Jet-Boot Jack: Jack descends into a dragon's lair, the Knucker-Hole, to slay the beast that seized the king's only daughter and lead the princess out.
descriptions.c64:157228: Part of Cassette 50: a jet-powered caterpillar has two minutes to munch lettuce leaves in a box, without biting itself, hitting the walls or being caught by a hungry blackbird.
descriptions.c64:157229: Rich minerals on Saturn's moons draw a despot who buys one moon, arms a reactor and threatens to irradiate every deposit unless handed the rest; the Jet-Boys set out to stop him.
descriptions.c64:157230: Climb from the bottom of a single-screen vault past moving forcefields to snatch two jewels and carry each back down through the Green Window as a member of the Galactic Jewel Raiders.
descriptions.c64:157231: A text adventure set in the 19th century: the 3000-year-old Jewels of Babylon, meant as Queen Victoria's wedding gift to an Indian princess, are taken by pirates off West Africa and must be recovered.
descriptions.c64:157235: On a space tour of the solar system, the ship loses control near the planet Jhothamia 6 and crashes, leaving you to survive there. Given away with Commodore Format issue 35 in 1993.
descriptions.c64:157236: Place the supplied pieces onto a grid to rebuild the picture in this 1983 jigsaw puzzle from Island Software.
descriptions.c64:157237: Manage Kettering Town, starting in Division 5, and try to lead them up the leagues in this management game loosely tied to TV pundit Jimmy Greaves.
descriptions.c64:157238: Run a football club against Europe's top sides in a league, working from a first-person office where different spots let you pick the team, trade and scout players, take loans and check the table.
descriptions.c64:157241: A Breakout variant on a horizontally scrolling screen, where the triangular paddle moves freely up, down and sideways and can be flipped, set on a planet whose exploration mission has gone wrong.
descriptions.c64:157246: The evil Ilfreet rules the Golden City from a guarded inner sanctum; free the imprisoned wise man from the dungeon below, since only his magic can capture Ilfreet and liberate the city.
descriptions.c64:157247: A text adventure set in Aquatania, a land cursed with bad luck by plotting witches, where you must recover a magic bracelet and five charms while suffering a string of comic mishaps.
descriptions.c64:157251: Darts with the whole board on screen, offering a 16-player tournament with up to four humans, two-player matches, and a solo round-the-clock race against time.
descriptions.c64:157252: A broader darts game than Jocky Wilson's earlier title: aim by steering a hand that drifts in a random arc to mimic nerves, with standard 501 and other game types.
descriptions.c64:157259: In a lawless London of 1995, Joe Blade must free 20 civilians and kill 100 thugs inside ten minutes to restore order in this sequel.
descriptions.c64:157261: Begin outside the old Anderson Mansion and search it for the files that will break the case, then escape with your life.
descriptions.c64:157267: Joe the Whizz Kid is trapped in a shop and must cross its departments, such as food and hardware, avoiding anything that floats or rolls along the floor to reach the end of each level.
descriptions.c64:157268: Single-game American football for one player against the computer or two head to head, with fictional city teams and four accelerated 15-minute quarters.
descriptions.c64:157269: A collection of darts games across ten difficulty levels, where the board scrolls so only part shows at once, making some targets tougher, plus a practice mode.
descriptions.c64:157291: The first entry in EA's Madden series, an American football game the sportscaster helped design, putting play calling and tactics ahead of raw action.
descriptions.c64:157292: Command Union or Confederate forces in turn-based Civil War strategy for one player or two, choosing the mix of infantry, cavalry and artillery before battle begins.
descriptions.c64:157293: A Civil War strategy game for one or two players, seen from above the terrain, with a menu for adjusting some parameters and a choice of which side to lead.
descriptions.c64:157294: A scoring card game for 2 to 90 players where five-card hands earn points by poker rank, card values and suits; discarding to chase a better hand risks lowering the score.
descriptions.c64:157295: A text adventure about a sailor on one night's shore leave after three months at sea, wandering the town of Sharksville with 50 pounds to spend on a good time before making it back to his ship.
descriptions.c64:157296: Shove lettered tiles around each level to spell a word on the spot marked by the arrow tile; by Thomas Koncina, published in Game On in 1993.
descriptions.c64:157297: A Quill-made text adventure with a verb-noun parser, centred on scientific genius Eddie Smith, who is developing an improved atomic weapon for Britain's government.
descriptions.c64:157298: Search hundreds of underground tunnels for 11 priceless treasures, dodging or shooting trolls, vampire bats and giant lizards.
descriptions.c64:157300: A colourful preschool program for children aged 3 to 6 that teaches up and down, left and right, and early reading skills.
descriptions.c64:157301: Part board strategy, part dance contest: hop from square to square in time with the music to create gold records and keep the jukebox playing.
descriptions.c64:157312: A Lunar Lander variant with a jumbo jet: each turn, enter a new climb rate and thrust while watching altitude, velocity, acceleration and the distance to and length of the runway.
descriptions.c64:157322: A climbing and jumping platform game that comes with an editor for designing and playing your own levels.
descriptions.c64:157323: Livewire's Frogger clone: get the frog over the road and across the river on turtles and logs into one of five bays, here with a pseudo-isometric look plus a lady frog and a bug to grab.
descriptions.c64:157324: A kangaroo collects fruit and lost joeys across four scrolling platform levels, dropping onto the nearest ledge at the start of each and avoiding the creatures that roam them.
descriptions.c64:157325: Two players race at once to reach the screen's upper edge, running to escape gaps opening underfoot and leaping through gaps that pass overhead; based on the Spectrum game and published in Game On in December 1991.
descriptions.c64:157326: An isometric shooter in the style of Zaxxon but with more freedom, flying over islands to destroy fuel tanks, helicopters, planes and patrol boats and landing on a carrier to refuel and rearm.
descriptions.c64:157328: Explore 14 levels of a perilous jungle to find a key, learning more of the mission as you go while man-eating plants, spiders and skeletons stand in the way.
descriptions.c64:157329: Scroll sideways through a Moon Patrol-like shooter, shooting fuel to collect it and avoiding alien fire; by Konrad Wieclawski for Game On, January 1990.
descriptions.c64:157331: Teenage agent Orion of the Adventure Connection Team is pulled out of high school to travel to deepest Africa and neutralise an alien artifact's boundless energy before rival BRUTE agents seize it.
descriptions.c64:157333: George Chesthair is dropped behind enemy lines and must shoot his way through everything that moves. Published in Radio Elettronica & Computer in 1988 and in Bogies Pick Value Pack 5.
descriptions.c64:157334: Mowgli dodges spears coming from the left and elephants and snakes from the right as the jungle scrolls constantly across several levels.
descriptions.c64:157340: Gather car parts across two flick screens per level to assemble a car, first reaching the junkyard by hopping over tyres, on screens split into five platform tiers.
descriptions.c64:157355: Drafted by government agents one January morning to fly a solo mission to Jupiter, you progress through a storyline that mixes illustrated adventure, space combat role-playing and joystick arcade sequences.
descriptions.c64:157356: Following Jupiter Mission 1999, this blend of story, role-playing and arcade action strands you in an unknown galaxy, fighting other craft and travelling the Labyrinths of Kamerra while trying to get home.
descriptions.c64:157357: A bilingual vocabulary tutor for more than 500 everyday French words in five areas, covering food and drink, shopping, travel, people and essentials, translated either way through games or typed answers.
descriptions.c64:157358: Build animated stories by combining 48 objects and 25 animations across 9 scenes.
descriptions.c64:157359: Protect one of the last giant cacti in the desert from a gun-armed insect hidden underground, firing at wasps and other attackers up through a pair of openings in the soil.
descriptions.c64:157373: Place cubes divided into four coloured triangles onto a board so every edge matches its neighbours, against a human or computer opponent or alone in practice mode.
descriptions.c64:157375: Platoon-level armoured combat on the Russian Front of 1941 to 1945, commanding a German or Soviet battle group in four historical scenarios, such as a meeting engagement east of Bryansk, or random ones.
descriptions.c64:157381: Hop a kangaroo across seven levels of a Q*Bert-style game, sold by mail order in 1983.
descriptions.c64:157382: Drive a van with a kangaroo bouncing on its roof along one of four routes, adjusting speed to keep the animal landing on top and choosing which slopes to take.
descriptions.c64:157384: An ice hockey tournament between national teams with surprising tactical depth, made to advertise Karamalz malt beer and published in 64'er in August 1993.
descriptions.c64:157385: Win two rounds out of three by flooring your rival with a range of karate techniques, earning full or half points, in contests at nine locations for one or two players.
descriptions.c64:157388: Race two opponents, one of whom can be a second player, around eight overhead circuits in wet, dry or icy conditions, choosing tyres to suit and avoiding contact that wears the kart down.
descriptions.c64:157390: In the 24th century humans return to an Earth abandoned after solar explosions, only to find it taken by the Kat Men; the war droid MT-ED is sent down to drive them out.
descriptions.c64:157391: Paddle a kayak down river courses from a first-person view against the clock, steering through gates with the white pole kept on your left and adjusting speed.
descriptions.c64:157393: A role-playing game in which four undercover agents investigate a surveillance station that vanished into the prison planet Kayden Garth along with its crew.
descriptions.c64:157394: Players take turns removing bottles, and whoever takes the last one wins, in this 1983 logic puzzle by Island Software.
descriptions.c64:157398: The tyrant Kayleth has enslaved the peaceful Zyroneans with android armies, forcing them to mine the rare mineral Chromazin; as a Zyronean, carry out your plan to free the planet in this adventure.
descriptions.c64:157399: Ride the 687-mile 1988 Kellogg's Tour of Britain from Newcastle to Westminster, competing for the King of the Mountains, sprint, stage-win and overall leader's jerseys.
descriptions.c64:157400: Hungarian chess program by Attila Kovacs, co-written with grandmaster Istvan Bilek and named after Wolfgang von Kempelen, builder of the chess-playing Turk automaton. It offers ten playing levels and also competed in microcomputer chess championships.
descriptions.c64:157402: A football management game run entirely through icons and menus, with no match action, where your chosen club starts in the Fourth Division.
descriptions.c64:157403: A side-scrolling football game of single matches, the second title licensed by the former Celtic, Liverpool and Scotland star.
descriptions.c64:157407: Keno, the casino number-picking game, as included in Keypunch Software's Club Casino pack.
descriptions.c64:157550: A tough Boulder Dash Construction Kit creation by the cracking crew Alpha Flight, with 17 caves and music borrowed from Commando.
descriptions.c64:157551: In 1999 a huge alien fleet attacks Moon Base Alpha; command the last Laser Blaster and hold off wave after wave of invaders.
descriptions.c64:157552: An unofficial fan-made sequel to Archon and Archon II, never released commercially but widely copied among users.
descriptions.c64:157572: Humgruffin the troll is trapped in the Netherworld of Narc and must collect a crystal from each chamber for his amulet to undo the spell, avoiding goblins and the walls they build.
descriptions.c64:157579: A reworked Arkanoid with a new intro and fresh screens: steer the Vaus ship to bounce an energy ball into the coloured blocks.
descriptions.c64:157582: A dice-and-board party game for 2 to 10 players who drink a magic potion, roll and move around the board, meeting characters such as the Mad Mugger and Kindly Jack.
descriptions.c64:157767: Introduces programming logic while building estimation and spatial reasoning; Tom Bretl designed it, Larry Bank wrote the code and Sunburst Communications released it.
descriptions.c64:157779: Darkness has fallen over the kingdom of Almahagor, and the evil can only be driven back by defeating its beast and sealing the Gate to hell, surrounded by six guardians according to an ancient book.
descriptions.c64:157781: Commander Ray Harrison flies the Full Metal Megablaster in search of a legendary New World as humanity nears extinction, in a shooter for one or two simultaneous players with five difficulty levels.
descriptions.c64:157782: Mickey and Goofy round up escaped zoo animals by having young children find numbers hidden in colourful scenes and press the matching key, rewarded with a short animation.
descriptions.c64:157785: A three-game compilation of board game adaptations: Cluedo, Computer Scrabble and Monopoly.
descriptions.c64:157855: Roland Rat, the 1980s breakfast TV star, is late for work with a dead car, so he dashes through London's flick-screen sewers against the clock, freeing his kidnapped friends on the way.
descriptions.c64:157857: In 2011 a Soviet reactor disaster on Koala Island contaminates 300 square miles, and months later the radiation has spawned monstrous mutated animals that must be dealt with.
descriptions.c64:157891: Cursed into a scarab by the wicked priest of Amenhotep III, escape a pyramid full of savage creatures and traps to reach the sun, beginning with the key that opens a hidden door in the west hall.
descriptions.c64:157894: Datasoft's puzzle-action game: guide a crusader through 100 trap-filled mazes to plant a bomb beside the stationary Saracen chief, evading patrolling guards and bouncing cannonballs.
descriptions.c64:157975: Steer a ship around a grid of solar cells, sweeping up every cell to clear the round while two sentinels patrolling the edges launch fireballs.
descriptions.c64:158006: Adapted from Arthur C. Clarke's novel: a giant object heading for Earth turns out to be an alien starship, and as commander of the Endeavour you rendezvous with it and explore its interior.
descriptions.c64:158018: An illustrated Quill adventure: Seafaring Gazette reporter Ed Lines is aboard a submarine for a feature when an enemy power attacks it, and he must hide and find a way out.
descriptions.c64:158110: Collect all the cherries on each screen as Mr. Do, crushing pursuing monsters with falling apples or hitting them with a thrown power ball.
descriptions.c64:158111: The first Questprobe illustrated text adventure starring Marvel characters: wake as Bruce Banner bound to a chair in a desert bunker, break free, change into the Hulk when needed and collect the gems to get out.
descriptions.c64:158112: Quasimodo hurls rocks at soldiers climbing ladders up the cathedral walls, then the button switches to jumping as he swings across bell ropes and climbs to carry gems down to altars, each delivery opening another area.
descriptions.c64:158126: Like Qix, fence off sections of the playfield to claim them while each level's boss and minions roam inside; the ship Monotros has answered a distress call to save its home world Volfied from invaders.
descriptions.c64:158201: On Frontier Alfa, a moon whose human settlers were enslaved by aliens, a newcomer with a trading licence works toward owning every base, factory and station.
descriptions.c64:158215: Dying King Markham longs to see his heir Prince Gideon, said to be captive of the evil Dolmir; only Gideon can bring together the Clans of the Reaches against him.
descriptions.c64:158288: The BBC sports quiz show: two teams of three answer sports questions for two points, with misses passed to the other side for one, across six rounds including the picture board and what happened next.
descriptions.c64:158329: Three runaway chemical reactors inside the Citadel are heading for meltdown, and the last SpiderDroid is sent in to find and shut them down before they wreck the surrounding electronic jungle.
descriptions.c64:158437: A 2011 homage to Jeff Minter's Laser Zone in which mutant camels return to Earth, mixing a Gridrunner-style shooter, shooting mutants while saving sheep, and a Breakout-style bonus game.
descriptions.c64:158441: A side-on shooter from 2008: mutant fish created by a botched government experiment trap swimmers, and your sub rescues them with torpedoes while dodging agents' subs sent to cover things up.
descriptions.c64:158442: Defend the skylines of nine major cities from 18 kinds of aliens, and play a mini game while the main program loads.
descriptions.c64:158444: An insurance company promotional game: the Victoria-Vesta slogans have been stolen and cut into pieces hidden in the rooms of two houses; gather the pieces, then reassemble the slogan.
descriptions.c64:158445: Earth has run out of food, and past expeditions failed against the aliens guarding supplies; search 15 star systems for food transporters, rising through 11 ranks with each successful trip.
descriptions.c64:158446: Based on the 1978-80 TV series: Monkey fights through four levels to rescue a princess from a dragon, beginning on a cloud firing lightning at three waves of flying creatures and then gathering fruit.
descriptions.c64:158452: A lone trooper whose ship has exploded hunts across an alien world for its pieces in a side-scrolling platform shooter, jumping, shooting droids and aliens and ducking airborne robots.
descriptions.c64:158505: Fly a World War II plane against enemy ground installations, dodging fighters and flak, until enough damage opens the way to the main target.
descriptions.c64:158506: Ride a jet scooter across forest, temple and sea toward the Golden Treasure Chest, aiming twin laser cannons at the Vortex's guardian creatures, which must be wiped out five of each kind at a time.
descriptions.c64:158507: A budget rugby sevens game seen from the side, switching to a view from behind the posts for kicks, with scrums, line-outs and tournaments for up to eight participants.
descriptions.c64:158509: Tiles tumble down a conveyor belt; catch them with a paddle and drop them into bins to form same-coloured lines horizontally, vertically or diagonally.
descriptions.c64:158532: Run a rollercoaster track in single-screen stages to rescue a girl from a giant ape, mixing Donkey Kong characters with ideas from Mr. Do's Wild Ride.
descriptions.c64:158533: A firefighter climbs ladders and girders across several Donkey Kong-style stages to save a girl from a gorilla that escaped the city zoo, dodging various creatures and objects.
descriptions.c64:158534: Drive up a constantly scrolling road through four seasons, ramming other cars into the verges or jumping to crush them from above for bonus points.
descriptions.c64:158535: Inspired by Lunar Lander: a trainee space commander earns his wings by steering through tunnels under gravity and touching down on landing pads on four worlds, including Zolopira and Alinduir.
descriptions.c64:158609: Pilot the mind-linked Z-Fighter, shooting down attacking aliens before they overrun the known universe.
descriptions.c64:158620: Video poker at a casino machine, starting with 20 coins and aiming for hands such as a Royal Flush or Four of a Kind, with five skill levels.
descriptions.c64:158621: An Infocom comic adventure set in 1936: abducted by the Leather Goddesses of Phobos as part of their plan to conquer Earth, the hero must escape and save humanity.
descriptions.c64:158622: Father Time recruits a modern-day programmer to collect nine treasures across nine eras and thwart the evil Time Lords in this text adventure.
descriptions.c64:158624: Follows Lord and Lady Macbeth's ruthless climb to the Scottish throne through Shakespeare's play in three illustrated text adventures, plus a comic interlude.
descriptions.c64:158627: Manage Manchester United through a season in pursuit of trophies, choosing the squad and training, with arcade sections for the matches.
descriptions.c64:158628: Shield 30 healthy cells in the Mangrove Swamps from cancer cells that creep in from the edges, moving a sight to zap the invaders while trying to grow more healthy cells.
descriptions.c64:158630: Play tennis under the full rules against the computer or a friend, or sit back and watch a demo match; also known as Match Point.
descriptions.c64:158649: Gather 39 keys to get out of a labyrinthine complex in a scrolling platform game, avoiding spikes, laser beams and liquid pools, with platforms that switch on and off and moving ladders.
descriptions.c64:158657: Help Merlin cast spells against the evil creatures sent to defeat him, restoring his power with a magic brew in the cooking pot when it runs low.
descriptions.c64:158658: As cop Don Ferrari in a souped-up F40, spend 48 hours hunting Miami's seven top crime lords for the mayor, chasing down the red cars and shooting them off the road within time limits.
descriptions.c64:158664: Sent to destroy the city of Zyto, drive a rocket-carrying truck down through its six levels to collect six bomb parts, detonate them at the bottom to breach the outer defences, then shoot the inner ones.
descriptions.c64:158672: Special forces agent McArra leads Operation Cephalopod to locate and destroy the nuclear submarine U-5544, whose existence has upset the balance between Earth's two great powers.
descriptions.c64:158677: Train a stable of racehorses through a season, buying horses, scheduling training and hiring jockeys, aiming to win the Derby and Grand National and be crowned top trainer.
descriptions.c64:158744: A night rally where every car carries a timed explosive that can be disarmed only at official checkpoints, so each stage is a race to the next one.
descriptions.c64:158873: Turned into a hideous creature and locked in the wizard Zolt's molecular prison, the Octoplex, you refuse to accept your fate and try to break out.
descriptions.c64:158877: A festive horizontal shooter: Santa and Rudolph fly over winter landscapes delivering gifts, pelting renegade pixies with presents as they throw gifts and bombs back, over three sections.
descriptions.c64:158879: Craps for up to four players at a side-on table with a croupier, placing a range of bets on an options screen after each roll.
descriptions.c64:158885: Fly a Soviet MiG-29 against the World Terrorist Army in an After Burner-style shooter on a cartridge with a switch for US or European machines.
descriptions.c64:158886: Based on Radio 1 DJ Mike Read's pop quiz, with questions on music from the 1950s to the 1980s; pick a specialist subject and two team-mates, against the computer or a friend.
descriptions.c64:158887: Cycle the 1000-mile Milk Race from Newcastle to London through towns such as Birmingham, Sheffield and Ipswich as one of 84 riders, dodging potholes, cars and other bikes and facing surprise time trials.
descriptions.c64:158888: Shrunk down and injected into the brain of Zyco, the indestructible alien ruling Earth, you must reach and destroy his one weak spot, a huge sensory neurone, over two single-screen stages.
descriptions.c64:158889: A computer specialist infiltrates a hidden command complex, locates the main computer room and erases its program by entering a destruct code hidden somewhere inside.
descriptions.c64:158890: Lead Molecule Man out of a 256-screen radioactive maze by finding 16 circuits, buying radiation pills with the coins scattered about to stave off poisoning.
descriptions.c64:158892: A licensed version of Nichibutsu's 1980 arcade shooter: battle ten alien waves with a ship of three stages that can dock together, each larger stage adding firepower but making a bigger target.
descriptions.c64:158893: Race a motocross bike against the clock through corners, hills, ruts and straights, jostling for position and keeping to the course.
descriptions.c64:158894: Defrost a giant fridge, one of six compartments at a time, by climbing from the lower left of each to the de-icer at the upper right, using ladders and gaps while avoiding falls that are too high.
descriptions.c64:158896: A hotel photographer searches behind doors for a pass, key, camera and flashbulb, then must snap a guest in the far-left room, dodging the inspector, manager and a bar patron, plus the furious Mr. Angry if he is woken.
descriptions.c64:158897: Paint every disc on a 7 by 6 grid before time runs out, moving only in right angles and avoiding gaps; on later levels discs need several passes to colour.
descriptions.c64:158898: A Pac-Man-style maze game: Munch Maniac eats every devil dot while four ghosts give chase, and the flashing senior devil dots in the corners let him turn the tables.
descriptions.c64:158901: Monty seeks fortune and glory by collecting gold nuggets across 40 rooms seen from an elevated angle, clearing each room of nuggets to exit, on his way to rescuing a princess.
descriptions.c64:158902: Chess from novice up to championship strength, shown on a 2-D or 3-D board in colour or black and white.
descriptions.c64:158903: Sid Meier's first wargame: command NATO's Western European armies against a Warsaw Pact invasion of central Europe in a hypothetical Third World War, a design that later underpinned MicroProse's Command Series.
descriptions.c64:158912: A Defender-like shooter flying over an alien landscape in four directions, progressing from beginner levels 1 to 4 up to Ace levels from 13 on.
descriptions.c64:158980: Guide a robot seeker drone across the planet Nonterraqueous to destroy its master computer, swapping forms at swap stations to resist acid drops at the cost of weapons and recharging at psyche stations.
descriptions.c64:158981: With Earth's fossil fuels exhausted and its Uranium 235 used up, the planet's power now hinges on vast deposits of the mineral found on Saturn's moons and an agreement struck to obtain them.
descriptions.c64:159045: An educational platformer over twelve levels: a builder climbs around a building site collecting sums that add to or subtract from his starting number to hit a target.
descriptions.c64:159054: Four noughts-and-crosses-based maths games for two players or one against the computer: Magic Square, Addition, Subtraction, and a mixed Adds & Subs.
descriptions.c64:159067: Shilmore Castle has been sold to Eugene Portcullis III Jnr, who plans to ship it stone by stone to America; ghost Sir Humphrey has lost his scaring powers and needs Olli and Lissa's help to drive the buyer off.
descriptions.c64:159088: Play 8-ball pool or snooker on a full-table overhead view against a friend or a computer opponent of chosen skill, with the rules of both games closely observed.
descriptions.c64:159090: American football against the computer or a friend from an elevated third-person view, with options for 5 or 15 minute games and a demo mode.
descriptions.c64:159092: A tennis game that positions your player automatically, leaving timing and shot placement to you, so angled volleys, lobs and drop shots decide the match.
descriptions.c64:159096: Steer a Quadroid around maze-like platforms across 32 single screens, picking up eight gravity pods per screen while avoiding roaming nasties.
descriptions.c64:159097: Oswald the Orange tries to escape from his packing case in a Spanish fruit processing factory before he becomes juice, climbing platforms and sliding down ropes to reach each screen's flag.
descriptions.c64:159098: As the last fighter pilot defending the planet Hyperion, move around the screen shooting or dodging waves of alien invaders.
descriptions.c64:159099: Defend your castle by sliding along the top of its wall, fighting your own momentum to stop in the right place, while hordes of orcs climb up from below.
descriptions.c64:159101: Modelled on Pooyan: Boss Roo rides a pulley-driven lift up and down the right side of the screen to save nine joeys from swagmen, needing to kill 32 swagmen to advance across three levels.
descriptions.c64:159102: Learning games starring Paddington Bear, with a storybook in which Jonathan and Judy give him a glow-in-the-dark bedside clock that has lines instead of numbers.
descriptions.c64:159103: Aimed at five to eight year olds, this flick-screen maze game sends Paddington Bear around the countryside during a week's holiday catching butterflies.
descriptions.c64:159104: Stop the world's evils escaping Pandora's box by having Pandora blow on each creepy creature as it reaches the lid, timing the gust for when it is at its largest.
descriptions.c64:159105: A Space Panic-style platformer: clear each screen of invading monsters by digging holes on the five ladder-linked floors and waiting for the creatures to fall in.
descriptions.c64:159106: Train like a paratrooper on four assault courses, racing for the best time solo or against a friend in competition or practice mode, with three difficulty levels and course previews.
descriptions.c64:159107: Four single-screen games for children aged five to eight starring a rabbit, Mr Grub, a frog and a kangaroo, including a carrot-collecting rabbit maze and a 10 by 7 picnic maze.
descriptions.c64:159109: Pedro's famous Mexican flower beds are under siege by hungry animals, and he must build barriers and blockades across their paths to the flowers.
descriptions.c64:159114: A computer version of the funfair horse race stall, where landing a ball in a hole moves your horse forward, with farther holes moving it farther.
descriptions.c64:159115: A book and software set where children build sentences from the book's words and watch Kermit, Miss Piggy, Gonzo and other Muppets act them out as an animated story.
descriptions.c64:159117: Fly a kettle through 30 side-scrolling underground levels, searching the bowls scattered around each for the one hiding a tin opener that unlocks the exit.
descriptions.c64:159120: Gardener and globetrotter Nebraska Joe falls into a vast underground labyrinth and must find his way out through four levels spread over 128 screens. He jumps, climbs ladders and collects keys and gear while robots, bouncing eyes, bats and spiders roam, and lasers and high-voltage traps kill instantly.
descriptions.c64:159121: Touch-typing course with a science-fiction framing, using 3-D graphics and animated hands that demonstrate the correct finger reaches. Lessons take learners from beginner to advanced level.
descriptions.c64:159125: Gather treasures until a key appears, then make for the door to the next level while avoiding tunnel trolls; includes a maze editor. Written by Randy Ubillos and David Dixon for the Arcade Action pack.
descriptions.c64:159127: One or two players race to reach the ceiling first on a crowded playfield, with steadily rising difficulty, a cheat mode and customisable sets. Published in 64'er Sonderheft 85.
descriptions.c64:159128: Fly five missions to smuggle defecting scientists out of East Germany, where the authorities want them kept for a weapons project; the first four each require ferrying six scientists to a safe house.
descriptions.c64:159129: Masters at the Siandown Temple, convinced no Westerner can master kickboxing, invite you to face their four best fighters.
descriptions.c64:159131: Ride a unicycle as a clown, catching falling balloons on your head to pop them, and later stacking them into ever-taller columns that leave less time to react.
descriptions.c64:159132: Claim squares on a grid by tracing their edges to clear each level, using agility and a stun gun that briefly freezes the four pursuers trying to trap you.
descriptions.c64:159136: Three reading and typing drills for young children, each with four speed levels, beginning with falling letters that must be typed before they reach the bottom.
descriptions.c64:159137: Art Linkletter puts questions to children and weaves their answers into humorous stories.
descriptions.c64:159138: Children design colourful scenes from 99 characters and objects in settings ranging from a farm or theatre to outer space, then write a story to go with them, with music.
descriptions.c64:159139: A peg solitaire puzzle based on an old Japanese game: jump pegs over one another to remove them, aiming to finish with one peg in the centre, over multiple levels.
descriptions.c64:159174: Caterpillars are devouring your orchard; spray them before the trees are bare, while their eggs hatch into deadlier pests.
descriptions.c64:159175: Pilot a craft through side-scrolling underground tunnels, shooting 12 bulbs to reach the next level and fending off creatures that drain your shield.
descriptions.c64:159176: Shoot everything that moves, then blast the spaceman's heart for bonus points if you reach him, with difficulty climbing each game.
descriptions.c64:159178: Forced down onto a planet thought dead since the giant brain that ruled its life died out, the survivor of a space battle finds something is still alive and hostile on the surface.
descriptions.c64:159184: George the bear must stock up on food and get safely back to his cave to hibernate, dodging poisonous apples, careless skiers and bear-eating spiders across three stages.
descriptions.c64:159192: Six early learning games for children aged 3 to 8, practising reading, counting and the keyboard: Letters, Names, Match, Sequence, Draw and Scribble.
descriptions.c64:159193: A side-on football game licensed by Peter Beardsley, built around the European Championship, with 8 teams picked from 26 European nations and a two-player option.
descriptions.c64:159195: Pick up, rotate and place blocks to recreate a hidden image across 16 grid levels called MicroKinema; peeking at the target speeds up the clock.
descriptions.c64:159197: Blast through four stages of alien fleets, each with its own backdrop and respawning enemies, destroying a target number to advance; the first three scroll vertically.
descriptions.c64:159198: Command Pegasus-class hydrofoil missile boats in eight missions, also directing helicopters and convoys to patrol, survey and clear areas of hostile ships.
descriptions.c64:159200: Fly a 30-seat Leander Class 454 prop plane by night from Norwich Airport, setting wind speed and fuel load before takeoff.
descriptions.c64:159201: Lay down pipe sections offered in random order to build a route for the flowing flooz, routing it through as many pieces as possible before it spills.
descriptions.c64:159204: Guide a round spaceship through more than 44 screens under realistic gravity and inertia, collecting the letters P, A, X in sequence and avoiding or shooting foes that drain energy or steal items.
descriptions.c64:159205: An illustrated text adventure starting at a deserted trading post, where trade with the locals may get you over a ravine on the way to the fabled mines.
descriptions.c64:159208: Play as a sorceress, barbarian, paladin or knight, raising an army of creatures to defeat villains and locate the Sceptre of Order in turn-based play with a time limit set by difficulty.
descriptions.c64:159209: A two-player SEUCK shooter themed on early Hollywood comedies, with heroes called Charlie and Harold; by Carsten Manshusen for Game On, February 1989.
descriptions.c64:159211: A Tron-style light cycle duel on an enlarged arena, whose computer opponent learns from its errors so it avoids repeating them. Published in Magic Disk 64 in November 1994.
descriptions.c64:159212: Klemens searches a 256-room labyrinth to free eight twin brothers from cages that only dynamite can open, and since he holds one item at a time he must remember routes back.
descriptions.c64:159213: An Arkanoid variant with familiar cartoon pictures hidden behind the bricks, adding indestructible and regenerating blocks, erratically flying birds and assorted bonuses; it has no sound.
descriptions.c64:159214: A simple Croatian platform game in the mould of Manic Miner with monochrome graphics; its title means The Key, and a fan English translation appeared in 2008.
descriptions.c64:159218: As the knight Sir Legless, equip yourself at the armoury and then fight in all directions to free King Eric and fellow knights held by the wizard Anthrax.
descriptions.c64:159222: Despite the title, you play a hunted gorilla escaping captors on a grid of uneven rectangles before taking on the fearsome Teddy Twins.
descriptions.c64:159238: Earth's pyramids were built and sold by the planet T-Pyge, each needing one transporter for the structure and another for its power supply until a cheaper scheme was devised.
descriptions.c64:159253: An operational simulation of Rommel's North African campaign from March 1941 to February 1943 in 12 two-month turns, with each side trying to push the other back along the coast and seize key towns.
descriptions.c64:159254: Two to four players move mythological creatures on an isometric 8 by 8 board, each starting with four pieces in a corner, aiming to wipe out every opposing piece.
descriptions.c64:159255: Hunt for keys across the castle's screens to raise portcullises and reach the tiny princess in her cell, picking up weapons and food while avoiding items that slow you down.
descriptions.c64:159258: A game version of the 1962 book by psychologist Hans Eysenck, letting players measure their own IQ and personality.
descriptions.c64:159259: Skate through seven levels from Codemasters, each pairing an isometric skate park, where every flag must be grabbed against a strict clock without straying off the tarmac, with a top-down cross-country run.
descriptions.c64:159261: Downhill skiing from an isometric overhead view, racing a friend or the computer through every checkpoint within a time limit on ever harder slopes, with the screen following the leader.
descriptions.c64:159264: An illustrated adventure in which you undergo the Kobyashi Naru trial for immortality, gathering the required objects in its knowledge, wisdom and understanding sections.
descriptions.c64:159265: Koko trades blue skies for a musty underground cave on his hunt for a wish-granting Magic Ball, in this platform game from Aackosoft.
descriptions.c64:159268: A super kangaroo with a jet pack and gun hops across a right-to-left scrolling landscape, leaping obstacles, dodging enemies and grabbing bonuses on the way back to his spaceship.
descriptions.c64:159269: Fly a MantaRay fighter from the cockpit through the Kromazone, the Terran Space Fleet Academy's elite proving ground for pilots who will face the Maranzar.
descriptions.c64:159270: On a 6 by 6 grid, move every coloured ball exactly once, each colour travelling a set number of squares, after which the ball turns into a fixed stone.
descriptions.c64:159273: A Polish platform adventure: Kulfon's fiancée is locked in a castle, and he must rescue her using objects found around it, inside and underground, carrying up to two items and talking to characters.
descriptions.c64:159276: The Redhawk sequel: newly promoted to reporter at The Daily Trumpet, Kevin Oliver is sent to investigate Dr Lee's strange mansion, ready to turn into the superhero Redhawk.
descriptions.c64:159279: Get through three labyrinth levels as slowly as possible, since the slowest time is the one recorded. Published by Polsoft in 1997.
descriptions.c64:159281: Grab flags while dodging fast enemies and a rival player, laying mines to trap the opponent but risking your own. From 64'er Software Extra Nr. 20.
descriptions.c64:159282: Slide a flashing orange square over coloured keys to open matching doors, not all of which yield, and collect the numbers 1 to 5 in order through the labyrinth.
descriptions.c64:159284: Two players go head to head solving mazes, with a built-in editor for designing new ones.
descriptions.c64:159297: Rearrange tiles with the joystick to recreate the picture shown at the start of each of ten levels, with a password given for every level.
descriptions.c64:159298: Maze collect-em-up modelled on the arcade game Lady Bug, played out over a long run of levels with rotating doors that change the routes through each maze. The 2011 release added a level editor.
descriptions.c64:159302: Joust astride an ostrich against rival knights; each one beaten leaves an egg that must be smashed before it hatches into a new foe.
descriptions.c64:159303: A lone mercenary rescues eight space kids stranded in hidden silos by escorting each to a building on the planet's right side, shooting the hostile inhabitants.
descriptions.c64:159304: A text adventure retelling Jack and the Beanstalk, in which you must rescue two children taken by a giant.
descriptions.c64:159310: One of Infocom's InfoComics: in 2029 the Blubbermen invade Earth and only Lane Mastodon can stop them, told in the style of 1950s science fiction.
descriptions.c64:159313: Take $250 into a Las Vegas casino and play blackjack, baccarat, roulette and craps under their usual rules, betting whatever you can afford.
descriptions.c64:159322: The Psycastria keep their energy pods in four installations, on land, aboard a giant carrier at sea, on the Moon and in deep space, and you are given command gifted with the cunning of the famous Boggles.
descriptions.c64:159323: A cute Gauntlet-like overhead maze game over 20 levels, steering either the strong Puffy or the faster Puffyn through an alien world of traps.
descriptions.c64:159324: A Breakout and Arkanoid-style game: bounce a Laserpulse with an Energy Mirror across levels to raise a planet's evolution grade.
descriptions.c64:159325: Cross a river five times on a bridge of four bobbing purple turtles, fetching fruit from a tree on the far bank before the timer expires.
descriptions.c64:159326: Help Santa on Christmas Eve, starting with a flip-screen hunt around his home for the parts of his sleigh; the player's name appears in a personal letter to Santa.
descriptions.c64:159328: Robot Liberation Front rebels storm Titan, a robot-run geothermal power plant built under the Atlantic on the Mid-Atlantic Ridge, and take over its robots.
descriptions.c64:159329: A droid collects mushrooms in eight dangerous caves, planning routes past rocks and poisonous shrubs that can box it in while enemy droids and Quango birds pursue it.
descriptions.c64:159339: Defend the eight circular sectors of the Hyperspace Causeway from aliens planting bombs, firing from a ship at each ring's centre.
descriptions.c64:159340: Martial artist Aarzak punches and kicks through the side-scrolling forces of the evil Duke, finally facing the three generals who kidnapped his girlfriend.
descriptions.c64:159342: The Galden Tribe has seized the planet Bacula and invaded peaceful Mu, abducting Queen Sheets, and Mu sends its best fighters to win her back.
descriptions.c64:159350: Two arithmetic games in one package. In Sum Vaders you type the sum or difference of the numbers on a passing spaceship and its falling alien robot before it lands; Robot Tables drills multiplication through a machine that builds robots.
descriptions.c64:159351: Pilot a craft over a grid of dots, firing in eight directions at mutants advancing up from the bottom before any reach the top.
descriptions.c64:159353: Overhead rallycross for one or two players across five tracks, earning points from each race to spend on car upgrades.
descriptions.c64:159356: Guide a snake that never stops moving at right angles, eating eggs that show up singly until enough are eaten to escape through a gap in the top wall.
descriptions.c64:159357: A target-shooting challenge of six events testing the strength, reflexes, stamina and nerve of a new soldier, all of which must be passed to qualify.
descriptions.c64:159358: The second part of Level 9's Time and Magik trilogy: recover the stolen Red Moon Crystal to save Baskalos from ruin.
descriptions.c64:159360: Explore a maze collecting 500 units of treasure through randomly assigned tasks to enter the Sphinx's tomb, then answer its riddle for the Treasure of the Sphinx.
descriptions.c64:159361: Investigative journalists Harper and Elliot join the Alterian Corps and are sent to Rigel V, where one region holds out against Federation invaders.
descriptions.c64:159362: Elite insectoid warriors riding runner creatures keep planetary forcefields charged before invading arachnoid aliens can break through.
descriptions.c64:159369: An Armalyte-style horizontal shooter: condemned for past misdeeds, you are loaded into a spaceship and cast down into the depths of hell. From Magic Disk 64, February 1995.
descriptions.c64:159370: Carry Later, trapped by Kropop in an underground maze, from one side of each chamber to the other without touching walls, traps or monsters, at one of three speeds.
descriptions.c64:159371: A vertically scrolling Wild West shooter made with SEUCK, playable co-operatively by two.
descriptions.c64:159372: Five-set tennis against a friend or the computer on an isometric full-screen court, with accurate scoring and five skill levels; originally Lawn Tennis.
descriptions.c64:159373: Fly rescue missions to stranded spaceships, shooting meteorites, aliens and flying eyes while avoiding collisions and cannon fire.
descriptions.c64:159374: A tank duel with puzzle elements against a second player or an AI opponent, where shots must be lined up to rebound off walls to hit the enemy.
descriptions.c64:159377: Based on the infrared tag sport, carrying its non-violent idea of tagging opponents rather than hurting them into a science fiction setting.
descriptions.c64:159442: Fill a 96-square board with 76 symbol stones before time runs out, placing each next to stones that share its shape or colour. A question mark occasionally appears and must be reached within three seconds or it blocks a square or wipes out surrounding stones.
descriptions.c64:159468: Take over one of 64 renameable clubs at the bottom of four divisions with only 11 players, signing up to 15 and building them into a winning side.
descriptions.c64:159469: Steer a boat down a river flowing across the screen, avoiding islands, crocodiles and logs while picking up explorers stranded in the jungle.
descriptions.c64:159470: Football management in which a club starts in Division 4 and aims for the Division 1 championship plus cup glory, handled through team and formation picks, coaching and transfers.
descriptions.c64:159473: Play as Road Runner, staying a step ahead of Wile E. Coyote and his traps across two stages that recur four times, in an action game modeled on the Looney Tunes cartoons.
descriptions.c64:159474: Text adventure adapted from Isaac Asimov's novel: as Earth detective Elijah Baley, travel to the Spacer planet Aurora and solve the killing of roboticist Han Fastolfe, maker of humanlike robots.
descriptions.c64:159483: A music program for composing tunes at home: record pieces, edit them and play them back.
descriptions.c64:159485: Children aged 3 to 7 choose a digit between 1 and 9, then solve a problem about it by steering an animal to the group with the right count of balloons, building up a rainbow as they go.
descriptions.c64:159486: A spelling game for kids: as a dolphin, hunt the ocean for lost letters that complete the words on a submarine so it can sink down to the sea floor.
descriptions.c64:159487: A bridge tutor drawing on columnist Charles Goren's teachings, using quizzes to train hand evaluation, bidding and competitive play.
descriptions.c64:159489: Educational spin-off of Sierra's Lunar Leeper: steer a Leeper onto one of four icons to choose among its four learning games.
descriptions.c64:159492: Arcade conversion set in 2011: race along elevated skyways that wind up a vertically scrolling screen, using a jump device to leap obstacles and hostile traffic.
descriptions.c64:159502: Roll and hop a ball around a grid of tiles, touching exactly the required number of each target tile type shown at the top while jumping gaps and dodging enemies.
descriptions.c64:159516: As Lady Wilde, the only survivor of a plane crash deep in the Amazon jungle, fight through the legendary tribe of Amazon warriors believed to have taken your baby daughter Penelope.
descriptions.c64:159526: First-person rail shooter set aboard a roller coaster, designed for Tynesoft by the Subway Software team of Bill Kunkel, Joyce Worley and Arnie Katz.
descriptions.c64:159527: A maze chase in the spirit of Pac-Man: a tuba gathers musical notes along staves while guitars, cymbals, triangles and pianos give pursuit, and cymbombs scatter extra notes.
descriptions.c64:159531: Officially licensed tie-in to the 1991 Rugby World Cup, following the real tournament format with all 16 nations and streamlined rules such as simplified scrums for faster play.
descriptions.c64:159532: Platform game starring Rupert Bear, the cartoon character created by Mary Tourtel, who must reach the Toymaker's castle to join his friends at a party.
descriptions.c64:159533: Climb a yachting league by challenging boats up to two places above you, adjusting your vessel's design, such as its overall length, to suit the rival and the weather forecast before each race.
descriptions.c64:159537: Lightgun compilation of five games: RoboCop, Rambo III, Hyper Sports, Combat School and Platoon, the last cut down to its Bunker and Tunnel Network stages.
descriptions.c64:159564: Play a complete round on one golf course alone or against as many as three friends, with Novice, Amateur and Professional settings that change how hard the wind blows.
descriptions.c64:159566: Commander of the three mineral planets Glaciax, Solarix and Terrax, you must clear the radiation pods that alien starships have planted on their surfaces, along with the creatures guarding them.
descriptions.c64:159598: Multidirectional scrolling shooter in which a far-future ox breeder flies the ship Badjak to stop aliens carrying off the herd, armed with a laser and a rear-firing boomerang.
descriptions.c64:159600: Tie-in to the British comic Oink!: editor Uncle Pigg is short of pages near deadline, so three mini-games are played to fill the issue, with the earned comic pages readable afterwards.
descriptions.c64:159601: Three skiing events, slalom, ski jump and downhill, are tackled in turn for a total score and a final rating; failing one event still lets you continue to the next.
descriptions.c64:159602: Fly through horizontally scrolling caverns in a Scramble-style shooter, steering clear of the jagged walls while dodging radar installations and homing missiles.
descriptions.c64:159603: Pilot a submarine through a side-scrolling sea in 2007 to reach an undersea British nuclear base whose malfunctioning Vax 3000 computer is about to launch missiles worldwide, and shut it down.
descriptions.c64:159605: Popeye returns to Sweethaven to save Olive Oyl and beat Bluto across four levels, while also minding Swee'Pea, feeding Wimpy and watching over Jeep.
descriptions.c64:159606: Guide Solo the Synthelman as he protects the baby Nejo on an escape from Wardlock's mechanical world, crossing the Ice, Vegie, Tech and Fire Zones connected by teleports.
descriptions.c64:159608: Overhead snooker with spin, adjustable shot power and color nomination after legal pots, plus a practice mode where balls can be set up anywhere on the table.
descriptions.c64:159609: Horizontal shooter with constant left-to-right scrolling: alien invaders threaten Earth, and the only defense is to switch on the Galactic Shield by fighting through their levels.
descriptions.c64:159612: Fly the Northall Q15, a helicopter-jet hybrid with heavy weaponry and a zoomable radar, against the attacking Peradusins at Ursa Minor Delta-V.
descriptions.c64:159614: Martial arts fighting game in which you weight your samurai's training toward skill, speed, stamina or strength, choose a training regime and attack tactics, then duel to win.
descriptions.c64:159615: Military shooter following an SAS soldier through four jungle, desert and swamp levels, each split into two phases that begin with a Commando-style overhead section.
descriptions.c64:159616: First-person slot car racing modeled on Scalextric model car sets, later sold in Europe under the name Gran Prix.
descriptions.c64:159617: Unofficial take on Scramble: fly a plane over mountainous scrolling terrain to reach and destroy an enemy base, dropping bombs that fall horizontally rather than at an angle.
descriptions.c64:159619: As a pearl diver, dodge sharks, squid and jellyfish on the sea bed, waiting for clams to open so their pearls can be snatched along with other sunken treasure.
descriptions.c64:159620: Illustrated adventure in which the warrior Se-Kaa attempts to breach the fortress of the Dark Hordes, spanning over 170 pictured locations with a full-sentence parser.
descriptions.c64:159629: Quill-made illustrated text adventure continuing Subsunk: Ed Lions is still aboard his sunken submarine after calling base for help.
