descriptions.c64:159630: Jeff Minter shooter in which a flying sheep defends a planet from aliens charging a planet-buster gun, using gravity fields at both the top and the bottom of the screen, much like Ancipital.
descriptions.c64:159631: Illustrated mystery adventure: as Sherlock Holmes, investigate a double murder in Leatherhead alongside Dr. Watson while Inspector Lestrade pursues the case too.
descriptions.c64:159633: A 17th-century naval captain seeks wealth and renown, choosing on meeting each enemy ship whether to fire on it, board it with crew or flee, and tracking losses in men after every battle.
descriptions.c64:159635: Paddle a canoe through gates on a vertically scrolling river against the clock, working the joystick left and right to stroke while currents of varying speed push the boat around.
descriptions.c64:159638: Sensible Software's game maker for building scrolling shooters: draw the sprites and backdrops, edit how enemies attack, and start from four bundled sample games.
descriptions.c64:159639: As Rik, roadie for the band Alternative Rock, drive their gear to the venue through oncoming traffic, haul it inside and adjust the sound before the show begins.
descriptions.c64:159640: Side-scrolling skateboard game in the vein of Kickstart: ride through each level over obstacles, losing one of three boards with every crash.
descriptions.c64:159641: Sequel to Superkid: having lost his powers, Tom Essex rides a skateboard and fires a catapult to rid six levels of New York streets of thugs in a flick-screen platformer.
descriptions.c64:159642: Spike the Viking washes up in Transilvania after crossing the North Sea and must break out of captivity, then free his shipmates held below the village castle.
descriptions.c64:159644: Roller skating in a multidirectionally scrolling car park arena: kick cans and gather litter while avoiding cones, ramps, sand, bouncing balls, frisbees, tyre mazes, rocks and rival skaters.
descriptions.c64:159645: In the 24th century a dictatorship pacifies people with the drug SKY; ride with the rebel underground on the planet Moloc to wreck the harvesting machines, fighting sky bikers and defense towers.
descriptions.c64:159646: A word game for several players: letters appear in a central pool and players form words from them, while rivals may grab an existing word by extending it with more pool letters.
descriptions.c64:159647: Pinball oddity in which the Slamball family of ball bearings lives on a table that the Americana monster has swallowed, so the game plays out inside its stomach.
descriptions.c64:159648: Snooker simulation also known as Snooker '83, where players alternate shots under standard rules, setting strength and spin with the space bar and cursor keys.
descriptions.c64:159656: Skate through city streets in a Paperboy-like scroller, grabbing flags before time expires and dodging pedestrians, cars and obstacles over 10 levels to earn a place among the Slime Rat Skaters.
descriptions.c64:159657: Futuristic sport blending ice skating and football on a three-screen pitch whose middle section holds obstacles, with digitized player faces shown at the bottom.
descriptions.c64:159666: Board-game styled football management for up to three human or computer players, taking one of 32 teams from Division 4 to the Division 1 title at five difficulty levels.
descriptions.c64:159668: Biomech 1, a droid nicknamed Sydney, is stranded somewhere strange thanks to his forgetful creator Foley and must find his way home in one piece, or Foley's boss takes it out on Foley.
descriptions.c64:159698: Spores have escaped in a lab and will soon spread outside; travel through its fixed-screen levels using up every canister of antidote stored inside to stop the outbreak.
descriptions.c64:159699: Horizontally scrolling space shooter set in 2150: a lone deep-penetration fighter goes behind enemy lines, needing to shoot down a set number of alien convoy craft in each level.
descriptions.c64:159700: As the robot BLOB, explore a 512-screen unstable planet, gathering a combination of parts that changes every game and bringing them to the core to prevent its explosion.
descriptions.c64:159701: Tank combat against the Arcturan Empire of Gir Draxon, whose warplinks let it shift troops instantly, fought as the Terran force sent to Arcturus.
descriptions.c64:159702: To save Joe Lebrinski's East Side gym from developers demanding $50,000, its members train in two exercises and then box the yuppies' West Side thugs in the street.
descriptions.c64:159717: Steer a fast spacecraft through seven space tunnels in a row to reach the promised land beyond.
descriptions.c64:159727: Santa flies his sleigh through a horizontally scrolling sky, catching presents from his helpers and avoiding the Red Devil's gifts, clouds and mountains, then lands on houses to deliver in person once he has enough.
descriptions.c64:159734: For one to four players: a spider spins a short web trail as it moves, enclosing flies to catch them, and loses its web on hitting a fly or crossing its own trail.
descriptions.c64:159743: A treasure hunter must find all 40 diamonds on an island overrun by the undead, moving across an island map and entering 21 buildings that each play as a platform level.
descriptions.c64:159744: Fly a Spitfire over the English Channel to bomb flying-bomb launch sites and down enemy aircraft, while also intercepting flying bombs headed for your home base, all before the fuel runs out.
descriptions.c64:159747: Up to four players manage horse racing stables, entering horses in races and hiring jockeys based on form and conditions, then watch the races play out from the side.
descriptions.c64:159753: On a pyramid of platforms, hop on each one to change it to the target color while enemies close in from the sides and from above, across 15 rounds that grow harder.
descriptions.c64:159786: Fight through Chicago's streets, a cemetery and the docks to reach the warehouse lair of a crime boss, beating his trained thugs and collecting the cash they drop.
descriptions.c64:159788: Command the four-man Strike Force Cobra on a mission to stop a mad scientist known only as The Enemy, who has built a nuclear bomb powerful enough to wipe out humanity.
descriptions.c64:159790: Stuntman Chad Adams must complete five dangerous motorbike stunts to prove himself, such as riding under a hang-glider to catch him as he drops while avoiding road obstacles.
descriptions.c64:159791: Pilot the T-Bird, a craft capable of 1346 mph, blasting swarms of flying saucers, space jellyfish and other aliens with a standard zapper and smart missiles while dodging their fire.
descriptions.c64:159838: Earth faces a final devastating attack, and the Mission A.D. plan unites the world's defenses against it; one country has refused to join.
descriptions.c64:159839: Terrorists have planted a bomb in a skyscraper hotel housing an FBI unit; climb through it in eight-floor sections, finding the porter who holds the key to each next segment, and defuse the bomb.
descriptions.c64:159840: Illustrated text adventure in which the knight Sir Tappin sets out to find the Holy Grail.
descriptions.c64:159841: Second M.A.S.K. game, based on the 1980s toy and cartoon line: a side-scrolling shooter in which Matt Trakker's agents again battle the villains of V.E.N.O.M.
descriptions.c64:159843: As billboard paster Bill Stickers, climb a ladder and line up rolls of paper on hoardings around town; pieces placed correctly stay put, while badly aligned ones fall off.
descriptions.c64:159847: Conversion of the Games Workshop and Milton Bradley board game: up to three players each lead a commander and four marines on missions aboard alien starships, with the commander rising from sergeant through the ranks.
descriptions.c64:159878: Woken from cryosleep when Bogloid aliens attack the ship, grab a proton beam that both kills the invaders and seals the hull breaches they leave, draining its power with each repair.
descriptions.c64:159882: Race seven computer cars over three laps of a long street circuit, with the first lap in daylight, the second at night and the third in snow, after choosing your car's color.
descriptions.c64:159885: One or two fighters punch their way rightward along corridors as enemies come from both sides, facing a large boss near the end of each level, with a gun available as a pickup.
descriptions.c64:159900: First-person space combat sequel: the Zylons strike the Celos IV system, and the Liberty Star warps between endangered planets to fight Fly Fighters and Destroyers, refueling at friendly space stations.
descriptions.c64:159905: Wearing a jet pack and carrying a laser, fend off waves of strange aliens, splitting cluster missiles and meteors, returning to dock with the mother ship for fuel.
descriptions.c64:159906: In 2746 the Space Thugs threaten the Rubicon, an anti-matter buffer zone created by eight allied planets; defend it from the cockpit of a Starfox fighter with lasers and side and rear mirrors.
descriptions.c64:159907: Aliens with a time machine have altered key events in Earth's past; rookie pilot Starion patrols 243 sectors, one per year, destroying enemies and solving historical puzzles to restore them.
descriptions.c64:159959: Up to nine players take turns racing for points on Loonies Loop or Devils Deathtrack, picking manual or automatic gears and a race length of one to nine laps.
descriptions.c64:159960: Pilot a powerboat out of enemy territory in a side-scrolling game, steering up and down and speeding either way while gathering the map pieces allied planes drop on the water.
descriptions.c64:159961: Mr Megafat pedals his home-built Velocipede S.T.A. to the beach half a mile away, riding a screen that scrolls constantly to the right.
descriptions.c64:159962: Mr Megafat returns on the Velocipede II, a unicycle that fires, crossing four timed, sideways-scrolling levels where you set the speed and jump hazards but cannot steer up or down.
descriptions.c64:159963: Vertically scrolling space shooter inspired by Star Force: a laser starfighter heads into an asteroid belt against starbases and fighter waves, avoiding mines and meteor showers that wear down its shields while picking up power-ups.
descriptions.c64:159965: Soccer management sim where you run a club's finances and results, taking a third division team in a league of Europe's best toward the top, mostly through menus.
descriptions.c64:159980: Overhead racing for one or two players on circuits that grow more complex, with hazards from traffic cones to tornadoes and wrenches to collect for car upgrades.
descriptions.c64:159981: Pursue Alana across the galaxy aboard the starship Andromeda to recover the crystal, seizing star bases to hem her in and searching planets for the Lance and the elements that power it.
descriptions.c64:159982: A shuttle pilot ferries goods from supply planets to the orbiting starcruiser, weaving through dangerous asteroid belts and landing and docking with care.
descriptions.c64:159983: Snooker or pool against yourself or another person, with no computer opponent; choose a short ten-red game or a full frame, controlled by joystick or keyboard.
descriptions.c64:159984: Bertie Bee defends his hive and queen from invading swarms of rival bees.
descriptions.c64:159985: Top-down stock car racing on six selectable tracks, where one or two players in red cars race yellow computer cars, with optional oil slicks and adjustable skid levels.
descriptions.c64:159986: Young readers build their own picture stories, which the program animates with color graphics and music, in scenes such as a dog chasing a cat or a frog named Freddy on a see-saw.
descriptions.c64:159987: Five-card draw poker against two digitized photo opponents, Suzi and Melissa, with more opponents sold on expansion disks.
descriptions.c64:159988: As Johnny Alpha, the mutant bounty hunter from 2000 AD, you crash-land on the Planet of Renegades after an ambush by the Stix Brothers while heading to meet friends Wulf and Gronk.
descriptions.c64:159989: In 2492, race a craft through the Sub-Terranean Underground Network at over 900 mph against the clock, shooting or avoiding cycles, armored drones and birdlike flyers.
descriptions.c64:159990: Side-scrolling aerial shooter with missions to destroy an enemy headquarters, where speed and maneuvers burn fuel and enemy planes, SAMs and gunships attack from every direction.
descriptions.c64:159991: One-button bomber game like Air Attack: a light plane low on fuel descends over a city and must level the buildings to land, with bonuses for landing and for hitting King Kong on a skyscraper.
descriptions.c64:159992: Two-player-only World War I aerial duel seen from above, with clouds forming the arena, similar to Atari's Air Combat games.
descriptions.c64:159993: Move a head along the lines of an 8 x 8 grid to paint them, filling each box once it is enclosed, while avoiding scorpions that cost one of three lives.
descriptions.c64:159994: Motorbike trials against the clock, one rider at a time, with a side-scrolling view of the rider above a smaller overhead map of the obstacle course.
descriptions.c64:159995: Taito's update of Space Invaders with tougher alien formations, boss fights, power-ups for extra weapons and varied backdrops.
descriptions.c64:159996: Turn-based American football strategy using teams and player statistics drawn from the real league, choosing plays against the computer or a human opponent.
descriptions.c64:159998: Tom Essex drinks his uncle's formula and becomes Superkid, able to fly and throw a super punch, then cleans up the crime-ridden streets of future New York for its mayor.
descriptions.c64:160004: As Prince Imrahil, journey to Baghdad over eight levels of guards and hazards to rescue his sister from Sultan Saladin, who has his brides killed after their wedding night.
descriptions.c64:160014: Warhawk sequel: called out of boredom on the planet Sloar, fly the Quariad stealth fighter over the surface of Tanium to destroy the alien force that has taken it.
descriptions.c64:160018: Battlezone-like tank combat: a lone tank holds off homing missiles, robot attackers and hard-to-hit saucers on the horizon.
descriptions.c64:160082: Turned into a monkey by a witch doctor, Tarzan gathers six ingredients, a necklace, mask, plant, crossbones, bottle and gem, for the cauldron, throwing stones at snakes, birds, lizards and cannibals.
descriptions.c64:160083: Football management where a club climbs from the English Fourth Division to the First Division title and cups, choosing from 40 teams split into divisions of 10.
descriptions.c64:160085: Adventure driven by one-letter keyboard commands, each shown as a side-view animation, as an adventurer trapped at the cave entrance works through the Oracle's cave complex to escape.
descriptions.c64:160088: Adapted from James Herbert's novel, this mix of strategy and text adventure has several characters fighting a rat swarm overrunning London, starting with Foskins and a map of the city; the game ends if the rats spread beyond it.
descriptions.c64:160089: James Sydney has been shot in the head by a sniper in the building opposite who had watched him all day; lead a team gathering clues at the crime scene to track down the killer.
descriptions.c64:160090: Wargame covering the first 30 days of a feared Cold War conflict in Europe, commanding NATO or Warsaw Pact air and ground forces with the option of nuclear and chemical strikes.
descriptions.c64:160091: As The Boss, plan a robbery: hire criminals skilled in explosives, driving and more who want money up front and a cut of the take, and buy information and plans on the target.
descriptions.c64:160092: Spelling practice for young children featuring Thomas the Tank Engine, with six games using three or four letter words in lower, upper or mixed case.
descriptions.c64:160094: Malmor, Demonlord of Darkness, once banished to Limbo by a council of wizards, has found the Ring of Skulls and again threatens the land of Aelandor from the Tower of Despair.
descriptions.c64:160095: International football management: lead a national team through qualifying and into the European Championship and World Cup, picking a 22-man squad from 100 eligible players with no transfer market.
descriptions.c64:160096: Inspired by Richard Branson's 1987 balloon crossing: race a friend or the computer across the Atlantic, controlling an eagle rather than the balloon itself.
descriptions.c64:160097: Based on the 1980s British TV show, decode cryptic clues to send a presenter and camera crew by helicopter from location to location, with a printed booklet of over 60 pages.
descriptions.c64:160098: Football management with four divisions of 20 teams and a pool of 1,500 invented players, each with attributes, covering selection, training, transfers, injuries and the chase for trophies.
descriptions.c64:160099: Ekim, a giant ant trained by pirates in 1647, hops across the backs of turtles between islands to gather treasure.
descriptions.c64:160100: Sabreman's second adventure after Sabre Wulf: lost in caverns spanning nearly 600 side-view screens, escape by one of three exits, each with a guardian beaten by a specific weapon.
descriptions.c64:160101: Star Trek-like strategy: command the ship Andromeda for the Federation against the warlike Vagan race across a galaxy of 4096 sectors in 64 quadrants, managing crew and combat.
descriptions.c64:160102: Starting at the bottom of the social order in the Norse gods' Valhalla, undertake six quests for named magic items such as Ofnir and Grimnir, finding or buying weapons and armor along the way.
descriptions.c64:160103: A message on an answering machine revives the Valkyrie 17 case from 40 years ago; after the leads run dry, the investigation picks up at The Glitz hotel, the last remaining clue.
descriptions.c64:160104: Second Phantomas game: work through 95 rooms of Count Dracula's castle to destroy him, evading his servants and collecting as much food as possible.
descriptions.c64:160106: Fruit machine simulation with one pay line, using holds and nudges when offered to line up winning combinations.
descriptions.c64:160107: Take on the Tangent Empire's invasion fleet by destroying 14 space stations, each with three sub-levels playable in any order, driving a tank through multidirectionally scrolling levels.
descriptions.c64:160111: Six-a-side volleyball under standard rules in single matches against the computer or another player, with a tactics menu for setting defensive and offensive plans.
descriptions.c64:160112: Galaga-flavored shooter where space vultures leave their nest above your ship one at a time to attack, bouncing back and forth across the screen instead of wrapping around.
descriptions.c64:160113: Cursed into a werewolf, hunt down every relative of the family responsible to lift the curse, while each kill raises police pressure and arrests can be escaped with the right gear.
descriptions.c64:160116: New York, 1998: with half the city in ruins and ruled by gangs and the other half home to drug barons, fight through the wrecked streets.
descriptions.c64:160117: An outlaw named Big Nose Bill and his men have seized Fort Snake; stranded in the desert with nothing, search the surrounding lands to reach him and retake the fort.
descriptions.c64:160118: Seymour, an aspiring film producer, recovers the equipment that the mysterious El Bandeeto scattered around his studio after tearing up the script for his western movie.
descriptions.c64:160119: Jet fighter flight sim defending an island home and its nuclear plant from enemy aircraft, with Novice, Pilot and Ace skill levels and takeoffs from the runway.
descriptions.c64:160121: Platform action in which Wizard Willy gathers ten magic eyes over four levels and defeats demonic guardians to reach the dark fortress where an evil emperor holds Princess Fifi.
descriptions.c64:160122: Spelling game for children 8 and up: move around a grid avoiding word-wobbling aliens while spelling 1500 words split into five difficulty levels.
descriptions.c64:160123: Football management in a 16-team super league, picking the side and substitutes for each match while handling injuries and suspensions; also released as Premier II and Premier League.
descriptions.c64:160127: Pick one of 24 national teams for a World Championship that copies the 1990 World Cup format, choosing which players take the field to balance the side.
descriptions.c64:160128: First-person flight shooter: fly into enemy territory and knock out the 10 beacons that cloak the enemy base, making it visible so it can be destroyed, using radar to navigate.
descriptions.c64:160129: Atari arcade conversion: one or two players, on a split screen, explore Gauntlet-like underground mazes in third-person pseudo-3D, shooting robots and grabbing bonuses from flying saucers.
descriptions.c64:160130: First-person shooter protecting Defense Sphere 7 from enemy attack ships, turning a solar-powered positron accelerator through 360 degrees to find and destroy them.
descriptions.c64:160146: A pared-down two-player version of Cult's British Super League, a text and statistics based football manager tracking finances, skills and league position, with matches reported in text.
descriptions.c64:160147: Motorbike racing viewed from behind the rider over 12 world circuits, alone or against a friend on a vertically split screen, with a nine-lap championship against six riders and a two-lap training mode.
descriptions.c64:160152: Updated Pong for one player against the computer or two head to head, with six variants that include tennis, football and two forms of squash.
descriptions.c64:160164: Vertically scrolling shooter along roads full of gaps, blasting aliens and recurring mini-bosses that break apart as they take hits; released on a 1994 Commodore Format cover tape.
descriptions.c64:160165: Scrabble played by the official rules at eight difficulty levels, improving on Computer Scrabble with better graphics, a bigger dictionary and a timer.
descriptions.c64:160216: Command a wartime submarine hunting eight destroyers and four transports carrying munitions within 18 hours, using torpedoes, steerable guided missiles and long-range radar.
descriptions.c64:160222: Educational game made with the RSPB and set at Loch Garten in Scotland: as head of the project, assign wardens so the ospreys can nest, raise chicks and survive the dangers they face.
descriptions.c64:160226: Lief the Viking gathers money to purchase the black key to the throne room of Castle Osk in Narvay, where he must kill the usurping ogre Smoth, past his two goblin guards, and free the jailed Queen Dana.
descriptions.c64:160247: Dizzy searches the islands for the pieces of a stolen magic crystal treasure, facing pirates and dangerous island creatures, with his friends on hand to help.
descriptions.c64:160251: Platform game across more than 200 screens, fighting trolls that menace humanity with a gun and energy bolts; a construction kit is included.
descriptions.c64:160295: Stop seven riot leaders within 15 minutes by tracking them down and hurling them off the prison roof, first solving word scrambles to disarm their booby traps, in a flick-screen fighter like Joe Blade.
descriptions.c64:160337: Tennis endorsed by Jimmy Connors, with tournaments and single matches on several court surfaces, using a crosshair to aim each shot across the net.
descriptions.c64:160341: Paradroid with metallic Morpheus-style graphics: take over robots with the 001 Influence Device, aiming to clear ships entirely and to transfer into the unstable 999 droid, in a fleet that never runs out.
descriptions.c64:160346: As Captain Clutch of the S.S. Slipshod, which has hit an iceberg, lead passengers to the lifeboats in a side-scrolling platformer.
descriptions.c64:160379: Real-time strategy in which Caesar leads up to 10 legions plus cavalry against larger barbarian armies in increasingly big battles to conquer Gaul.
descriptions.c64:160382: Star Trek parody aboard the starship Enterpr1se on its five-year mission, exploring space and shooting aliens with charged particle weapons.
descriptions.c64:160383: Joust clone published by COMPUTE!'s Gazette: a hero on a winged horse flaps to rise and fall, beating flying foes by striking them from above.
descriptions.c64:160400: Role-playing adventure set in the world of The Magic Candle: choose one of several adventurers with differing strengths, take a job from the mayor and save the town of Maramon.
descriptions.c64:160442: Board the generation ship Pandora, which is set to infect Earth with deadly flowering spores, and stop it with help from the surviving crew, obtaining ID at the entrance to avoid a ceiling laser.
descriptions.c64:160443: After bailing out of a crashing Star Hopper near the spaceport of the unstable planet Stank, finish the journey on foot through its hazards.
descriptions.c64:160444: Framed for murder, Jake Stalin is exiled for life to the planet Souzel to process rubbish from a dozen nearby worlds into raw materials, and tries to escape.
descriptions.c64:160445: Early space shuttle simulation of a satellite recovery mission, played in five stages beginning with an automatic launch, a rendezvous and an approach to the dead satellite.
descriptions.c64:160446: Two robots, Limes and Napoleon, compete in skill tests; the winner is sent to hunt precious metals on far planets and the loser is scrapped, starting with flicking a flashing Glidstar in the center.
descriptions.c64:160447: Operation Wolf-style shooter that starts behind enemy lines: escape with the captured Rapier machine gun through eight varied levels with vehicles, pursued by its makers.
descriptions.c64:160448: The ruler of a race of little green aliens has escaped his captors but is stranded on a strange world, and must cross a scrolling platform landscape to rejoin his spaceship.
descriptions.c64:160449: Puff the little dragon is lost outside Dragonland; guide him through levels of puzzles and traps to find the four parts of the pass that gets him back home.
descriptions.c64:160450: Liverpool FC football game with an overhead Kick Off-like view, offering cup and full season modes, adjustable match lengths and basic statistics for each player.
descriptions.c64:160453: As a Royal Engineers lance corporal in wartime London, locate and defuse unexploded German bombs before their delayed fuses go off.
descriptions.c64:160454: Non-canon Lone Wolf adventure: the Kai Master climbs the flick-screen interior of Gorazh's tower, which widens toward the top like an upturned pyramid, to claim a Lorestone of Nyxator at its summit.
descriptions.c64:160455: Puzzle game where randomly shaped pipe pieces, such as straights, corners and S bends, are rotated and placed anywhere on a grid to form closed loops.
descriptions.c64:160456: Mouse-controlled adventure role-playing game across 101 locations, where four characters must destroy a supreme vampire, werewolf, zombie and mummy.
descriptions.c64:160467: Early British baseball game for one or two players over three, six or nine innings at three computer skill levels, played in an arcade style without team statistics.
descriptions.c64:160471: First-person space combat in which a starfighter flies missions ranging from finding lost artifacts to wiping out enemy forces.
descriptions.c64:160481: Robots aboard the space station Sigma 7 have gone haywire; reach the central controls by beating three stages with different gameplay, starting with a diagonally scrolling shooter.
descriptions.c64:160486: Pinball with a single table for up to four players with five balls each, plus an editor for reshaping the table and arranging its parts; the default table has several bottom flippers.
descriptions.c64:160487: Turn-based Korean War simulation as Douglas MacArthur leading UN forces or as the Chinese command, with the option to keep the conflict limited or widen it into an Asian or global war.
descriptions.c64:160488: In 1936 a murder takes place aboard the airship Zinderneuf; as the sole investigator aboard, explore its decks from above and collect evidence to accuse the killer before landing.
descriptions.c64:160489: Dust Brain wants to lead the Madballs who run planet Orb's parliament, and wins over the other Madballs by bumping them off multidirectionally scrolling platforms.
descriptions.c64:160490: Cockpit-view shooter escorting an airliner: after an automatic takeoff, the Flyer Fox shoots down enemy fighters to protect the jumbo, using radar, compass and artificial horizon.
descriptions.c64:160491: Aliens have devastated civilization's worlds; the last hope is Mag Max, a weapon left unfinished by scientists who hid its parts underground, which must be found to complete it.
descriptions.c64:160492: Fixed-screen shooter against enemy formations massed overhead, with a fuel tank acting as a time limit that refills after clearing several waves.
descriptions.c64:160494: Centipede-inspired shooter: a small blue creature along the lower edge moves sideways and a little forward and back, firing up at a big maggot descending level by level.
descriptions.c64:160495: A witch recovers four magic scrolls stolen from Neverland by the sorcerer Colo and his henchmen, using a cape, cross, wand and hourglass that each work differently against his creatures.
descriptions.c64:160496: Sequel to Reckless Rufus: evil witches have taken Antwicky, so Rufus dons a cape and learns spells, freeing prisoners across platforms and ladders while battling witches, demons and Vikings.
descriptions.c64:160497: Illustrated text adventure scored with Mike Oldfield's Tubular Bells: the magician Caro must kill an evil wizard to lift the spell that turned a little girl to stone.
descriptions.c64:160499: Shield three llamas from invading aliens by steering a killdroid over the attackers while holding fire; any llama can die, but the game ends when Mama is lost.
descriptions.c64:160500: Qix variant: draw lines with a dot to enclose and color areas while avoiding enemies confined to colored or uncolored zones, aiming to fill 75% of the screen.
descriptions.c64:160501: Captain C T Cobra drives a Battlecar up the vertically scrolling planet Mergatron to recover the captured jewels of Ozymandias, destroying turrets and enemy cars along the way.
descriptions.c64:160503: Commodities trading simulation for one to eight players, where each turn opens with a market analysis hinting at which goods may rise in value.
descriptions.c64:160505: Early Westwood turn-based RPG on Mars: a stranded space jockey assembles a team to search for a lost city, building characters with attributes and 21 improvable skills.
descriptions.c64:160509: Educational math race for one or two players, where runners advance by solving problems, with four skill levels from Walker to Olympian and a choice of operations such as multiplication and division.
descriptions.c64:160514: Chess under the standard rules on a 2D board, moving pieces by placing a pointer on the starting square, pressing space, and repeating on the destination.
descriptions.c64:160515: Football against the computer or a friend, or a cup for up to eight players, with half lengths of 5, 15 or 45 minutes, three computer levels and editable team names.
descriptions.c64:160516: Football management licensed from the BBC highlights show, covering training, transfers and tactics through an unusual interface where a diary on a desk is dragged around to pick options.
descriptions.c64:160517: Based on the Max Headroom TV movie and series, set in a cyberpunk near future ruled by ratings-hungry corporations, with Network 23 reporter Edison Carter attempting a rescue.
descriptions.c64:160518: Ride six timed stages of a motorcycle circuit, choosing one of seven riders with different bike traits and switching between low and high gear with the fire button.
descriptions.c64:160519: Professor Arabesque, sent by the Psychical Society, jumps and shoots his way through Maxwell Manor in overhead and side-on sections, gathering treasures to break the hold of the Skull of Doom.
descriptions.c64:160522: Memory and word guessing combined: two players, human or computer, flip boxes on a 36-box grid to match animated figures of the same type and color.
descriptions.c64:160523: Terrorists of the Red Legion hold the Lutheran embassy and threaten to blow it up, while the ambassador's daughter hides inside; three Mayday Squad commandos go in to rescue her.
descriptions.c64:160524: As Mick or Mac, chase down the Hamburglar to recover Ronald's stolen bag of magic tricks, collecting Ronald's cards in platform levels such as Ronald's Clubhouse and Birdie's Treehouse.
descriptions.c64:160525: After nuclear war, mutants roam the wastelands outside the cities; as the mutant Sante, break into a city to free your father Hante.
descriptions.c64:160526: Overhead vertically scrolling racing: overtake rival cars and finish each lap within the time limit to reach the next race, watching for drivers coming up behind.
descriptions.c64:160527: Rebels bored with matter transporters race on the Battletrack, an abandoned orbital road; ride the armed Mean Streak motorcycle along its isometric, Mad Max-like course.
descriptions.c64:160528: Platoon-level wargame of a hypothetical NATO versus Soviet armored battle for two players, human or computer, with four historical scenarios and a scenario builder.
descriptions.c64:160529: A doomsday machine orbiting the satellites Xylos and Pholos was set long ago to stop nuclear war between galactic empires, triggering if nuclear activity climbs too high; eight smooth-scrolling scenarios follow.
descriptions.c64:160530: Medieval politics and war strategy beginning in 1028 AD and lasting up to five centuries or 100 turns, for up to 10 players with as many as six run by the computer, with optional limits on actions per turn.
descriptions.c64:160531: Logic game where a sphere rides around rotating cogs, switching between them where they touch, to gather the parts of a formula in order while avoiding enemies on some cogs.
descriptions.c64:160535: Into-the-screen 3D shooter viewed from behind the Mega Hawk as it seeks a new universe, through stages in a tunnel, in deep space and over a planet's surface.
descriptions.c64:160536: On Midsummer Night, Mr Megafat, melon grower and TV personality, runs along a side-scrolling landscape protecting his ripe melon patches from Melonmonsters.
descriptions.c64:160546: Ikari Warriors-style shooter in which an anti-terrorist soldier frees an ex-President held by African revolutionaries across eight mostly horizontal levels, sometimes shooting trees and scenery to advance.
descriptions.c64:160547: Myrtle, a heavyset mermaid who has finally found her dream man, the diver Gordon, must rescue him through an underwater maze after he flees and gets stuck beneath a ship.
descriptions.c64:160548: Expansion for Mercenary with the same controls, sending the player back to Planet Targ for a new adventure in the Second City.
descriptions.c64:160549: Inside an asteroid complex lives Garth, a two-headed alien bent on destroying Earth; fill flasks with acid and use them to blow up the four power units that sustain him.
descriptions.c64:160550: Single-screen platformer where a spaceman with a jet pack walks over fuel pods to color them in, collecting all of them to move to the next screen.
descriptions.c64:160551: Defend a city at the bottom of the screen from waves of aliens that fly in from the edges and crash into it, losing once the Metro-Blitz lettering under the city is wiped out.
descriptions.c64:160552: Add-on for MicroLeague Baseball, which featured licensed MLB teams and real players, letting users trade between teams or build their own.
descriptions.c64:160553: Steer a small robot through a vertically scrolling, overhead circuit maze inside a supercomputer, repairing its broken circuits instead of trained engineers.
descriptions.c64:160560: Text adventure set in Egypt: a desert wanderer finds the lost city of Xeiops and explores its tomb, said to hold over 100 rooms, carrying the treasures out.
descriptions.c64:160590: As the maintenance engineer of the stricken freighter Nimbus, walk or jet-pack around single screens, carrying seeds singly from the upper edge to save the priceless Terran Plant cargo.
descriptions.c64:160591: Interactive fiction built on the SWAN system and adapted from an Anna Popkess novel, set after an apocalypse where guards rule mutant mobs with frequent executions, following a boy named Robin.
descriptions.c64:160592: A Wild West multi-event game: cross the desert, win gunfights, compete at beer drinking and arm wrestling in the saloon, and milk a cow.
descriptions.c64:160593: Robot aliens have invaded; Minit Man flies a helicopter to carry materials and rebuild the bridge needed to move missiles to the silos, then loads and fires three warheads.
descriptions.c64:160595: After the Bad Star Empire ravages the planet CRYS-CIT, fly a star fighter over the empire's world wrecking fighters and installations to blunt any future attack.
descriptions.c64:160596: A mysterious alien craft codenamed Omega carries deadly missiles; board it and shut down its four reactors within an hour so it can be studied without firing or falling to the enemy.
descriptions.c64:160599: Science fiction action by the creator of Maxwell Manor, in two parts, The Final Appeal and Operation Tempest, striking the hated Eternals' underground power base on the planet Thunderhead.
descriptions.c64:160600: A boat crosses the surface left to right at an adjustable speed, dropping depth charges in pairs to sink submarines passing beneath in the opposite direction.
descriptions.c64:160601: Real-time strategy for one or two players commanding infantry, cavalry, artillery and spies in a hunt for the enemy's command center, with the two-player game played over a modem.
descriptions.c64:160602: Side-scrolling shooter in which the space mercenary Moebius fights the creatures and robots of The Controller, ruler of the empire, on a distant planet.
descriptions.c64:160604: Pac-Man-style maze game: guide Munchie around eating every dot while four monsters roam the maze, with three lives to spend.
descriptions.c64:160605: Casino simulation with five gambling games, including poker, playable in any order, starting with $10,000 and trying to grow the bankroll.
descriptions.c64:160613: Vertically scrolling shooter set in an alien-invaded asteroid belt: blast a route through the asteroids first, then take on the enemy craft.
descriptions.c64:160616: Mordon, one of the dying Ancient Ones who guide the universes, recruits an adventurer after the younger Ancient One Bostafer ruined the time machine they built.
descriptions.c64:160617: Fly into 50 sub-universes called Aithers, each a Nucleus ringed by 32 Orbitals; destroy enough Orbitals to kill the Nucleus, then shoot the Morphi it releases for points and money.
descriptions.c64:160618: Defend the home planet from a huge mothership and swarms of fast drone fighters, steering a ship down the Zarway space corridor while dodging and shooting.
descriptions.c64:160620: Flick-screen run and gun: a commando sent by a UN narcotics task force into the jungles of South America must destroy the drug Duke of Colombia's underground cocaine refinery and kill him.
descriptions.c64:160621: Based on Mr. Do!: dig through dirt to gather every cherry on each screen while pursuers stick to existing tunnels, stopping them with a bouncing ball.
descriptions.c64:160630: A dead soul climbs toward heaven through single-screen levels while Mr Mephisto sends minions to block the ascent.
descriptions.c64:160642: Prohibition-era strategy in which a gangster in 1919 profits from illegal alcohol, told through detailed comic-like pictures and brief animated scenes, with hints given in text conversations.
descriptions.c64:160643: In 1930s Chicago the Mouse Mafia controls the cheese supply, and ten of its members now plan to steal the cheese moon; Murray Mouse, SuperCop, sets out to stop them.
descriptions.c64:160645: Solve 12 crimes plaguing the town of Huxley by questioning suspects, searching locations for clues and analyzing evidence with police station resources, all within a time limit.
descriptions.c64:160647: One to four detectives race to crack 12 murders in Micropolis, interviewing witnesses and reading lab reports, with every action, especially travel, costing time on the game clock.
descriptions.c64:160649: Historian Sir James Wentworth of the London Archaeological Society travels to the Indus Valley to recover two relics, the Scythian Tablet and a Starstone, from a region no one has returned from.
descriptions.c64:160651: In 2099 a plasma storm forces the spaceship EPIC to land on an uncharted planet for repairs, where an unknown virus gets aboard the ship.
descriptions.c64:160652: Top-down shooter in which Mobile Attack Droid 471 of the Nemesis Organisation, steering with heavy inertia, moves through a city to stop Cyrus T. Gross and his Earth-bound TALOS asteroid.
descriptions.c64:160696: In a 21st century run by drug barons, deploy three squads of elite police around a perimeter, adjust their loadouts and guide them through tunnels to blow up the drug factory.
descriptions.c64:160697: Three standalone missions as a US Navy SEAL against terrorists and hostage takers, each split into parts with different mechanics, including swimming and submarine sections.
descriptions.c64:160708: Racing set on Ramsay Street from the soap Neighbours: Scott Robinson skateboards against one to four other characters, such as Charlene in a go-kart and Henry on a lawnmower.
descriptions.c64:160709: Neptune searches the ocean depths for his daughters held by the sea snake, first navigating caverns while destroying jellyfish and cutting back weeds that keep regrowing.
descriptions.c64:160711: Real-time strategy against the alien Insignians: build giant battle robots at factories and send them to capture the bases Kerberus, Tarras, Faretra and Diolkos.
descriptions.c64:160712: Swap-like tile puzzle: exchange adjacent tiles so that two or more identical symbols touch horizontally or vertically and vanish, racing a time limit.
descriptions.c64:160714: Protect the outpost Alpha IV at the galaxy's edge from alien ships of varying size, speed and firepower over up to five levels, with more ships to destroy at higher levels.
descriptions.c64:160715: An engineer proves his remote-controlled tank beats the old model by solving overhead mazes, finding the exit of each past locked doors and energy barriers.
descriptions.c64:160717: Isometric scrolling arcade adventure in a once-peaceful valley near the sea and the purple mountains, now overrun by a darkness from which no visitor has returned.
descriptions.c64:160719: Metrocross-style side-scroller: race a scooter through city streets against a strict time limit, swerving or jumping barriers, rough ground, ramps and, from level 3, rival riders.
descriptions.c64:160721: Operation Wolf-like military shooter from Golden Disk 64: move a crosshair over the screen to gun down enemies, with the space bar launching rockets.
descriptions.c64:160722: Nobby the Aardvark hunts for Antopia, an ant paradise he heard of from an ant about to be eaten, over eight levels mixing platforming, scrolling stages and top-down mazes, with balloon and submarine sections.
descriptions.c64:160723: Pun-based text adventure in the town of Punster, where figures of speech have turned into physical things; seven scenarios can be tackled in any order before a final one unlocks.
descriptions.c64:160725: Aliens have taken over the Northstar space station; walk left to right through its floors, clearing them with a lance.
descriptions.c64:160726: Cyril the Squirrel must store enough nuts before hibernating, collecting every nut on each of eight sideways-scrolling platform levels.
descriptions.c64:161749: Third Olli and Lissa game: Olli's car parts have been stolen and hidden around the Spooky Castle, so he hunts them down with a magnifying glass and rebuilds the car in stages.
descriptions.c64:161750: Frank Cohen platformer in which Ollie wanders into a factory run by evil robots and must clear 24 hard screens of layered horizontal platforms in sequence.
descriptions.c64:161751: French role-playing game: after King Jorian's death, Lord Yarod-Nor rules by tyranny, and a party of four custom or premade characters sets out to end his reign.
descriptions.c64:161752: Football management covering the top four English divisions over several seasons, from expanding the ground and checking pre-season accounts to chasing league and cup honors.
descriptions.c64:161753: Constantly scrolling shooter seen from an elevated angle, traveling by car, speedboat, ski and other vehicles, with animated scenes between them, to blow up a submarine at a base.
descriptions.c64:161755: World War II wargame: as an armored battalion commander, capture a defended city 15 km away within 35 turns using infantry, engineers, recon, tanks and artillery.
descriptions.c64:161756: Flying the experimental RP2-16 as its test pilot, you are thrown by strange flashing lights into an alien world and must shoot aliens across eight horizontally scrolling levels to get back.
descriptions.c64:161757: Side-view volleyball in matches of 1, 3 or 5 sets to 15 points, with teams including CoCo, the Geniases, the Rollers and the Beach Boys.
descriptions.c64:161758: Squad-level simulation of late 20th century combat in Europe and the Middle East, leading infantry, armor, artillery and helicopters for Arab states, Iran, Israel, NATO or the Warsaw Pact.
descriptions.c64:161759: The super-villain Zargo beams creatures from a parallel dimension to stop the Oxxonians eating their staple food, popcorn gateaus; explore mazes to undo his scheme.
descriptions.c64:161764: Wargame of the September 1944 airborne operation: command the US 82nd and 101st Airborne, British 1st Airborne and 30th Corps toward their historical objectives, scoring for ground held.
descriptions.c64:161778: Platformer of over 2500 screens in which P. P. Hammer uses a pneumatic hammer to dig through the ground in caves and castles to gather all the treasure, while the broken blocks soon reappear.
descriptions.c64:161779: Side-scrolling World War II shooter flying the rugged P-47 against Nazi forces, starting with a machine gun and picking up extra weapons.
descriptions.c64:161780: Plant bombs on the platforms where red monsters walk; the blasts open holes, and monsters that fall through drop a level and are destroyed.
descriptions.c64:161782: Hex-based World War II wargame on the Battlefront engine, commanding corps in scenarios based on real battles involving Soviet, German, British and American forces.
descriptions.c64:161783: Solitaire Eastern Front wargame leading a regiment of the Grossdeutschland Panzer Grenadier Division with attached tanks, artillery and mortars.
descriptions.c64:161784: Joystick-waggling paratrooper training across six disciplines with quotas to meet; completing all six earns a promotion and a harder round.
descriptions.c64:161785: Sega coin-op tennis conversion touring France, Australia, the US and England, with each nation's anthem, four computer skill levels and one or two players.
descriptions.c64:161787: Two players jump for stars at the top of the screen, using springboards on both sides for the higher ones, to power a machine that makes peanut butter sandwiches.
descriptions.c64:161788: Percy the penguin sails 30 miles out from Port Stanley in the Falklands to hunt pearls, then swims underwater through levels to get home with as many as he can.
descriptions.c64:161789: Illustrated text adventure based on Erle Stanley Gardner's Perry Mason, influenced by Infocom: defend a jailed woman accused after her wealthy husband is found dead.
descriptions.c64:161790: Pengo clone: a penguin survives two minutes in each ice-block maze while dodging creatures, earning bonuses for lining up special blocks.
descriptions.c64:161791: Lead one of 27 specialist teams parachuted behind enemy lines on 14 March at 06:00 to cut the enemy's main communication lines and end the war.
descriptions.c64:161792: Peter Pack Rat gathers a quota of objects around his junkyard home and carries them back, climbing platforms, ladders and pipes in a side-view platformer.
descriptions.c64:161820: Early construction set for designing pinball tables by placing parts, reshaping the table, adjusting gravity, bounce, kick and speed, painting backboards, wiring targets and saving the results.
descriptions.c64:161821: Pinball meets Breakout on one overhead screen, using bats at the bottom and middle to knock out blocks, hit bumpers and light the letters spelling COMMODORE.
descriptions.c64:161822: Side-scrolling adventure in which the Pink Panther steers his sleepwalking employer around the house without waking him, using items such as a small bell to lure him.
descriptions.c64:161823: Base 3, a space station near Earth since 2091, screens the crews and cargo of all visiting spacecraft before they may continue to Earth.
descriptions.c64:161837: Side-scrolling shooter in 3216 AD: fly the Star Eagle to Mars, where aliens from Tritan have set up base, and destroy the Time Scalers that let them reach Earth.
descriptions.c64:161841: Based on the Bruce Forsyth-hosted ITV game show for a single player facing the computer or for two, combining a question round with higher-or-lower card guessing.
descriptions.c64:161842: Arcade puzzle where a small yellow character fires symbol blocks marked with shapes like circles or crosses at a shaped wall so they rebound into matching blocks and clear them.
descriptions.c64:161848: Five pogo stick events on side-on screens that scroll from right to left, where a falling score is topped up by completing tasks and a target must be met to advance.
descriptions.c64:161849: Bouncing on a Turbo-Pogo, a stranded hero searches horizontally scrolling planets for six spacecraft parts, returning each to a landing pad guarded by two forcefields.
descriptions.c64:161850: Xevious-inspired vertical shooter: a mercenary flies ten levels over a planet, shooting alien waves and bombing ground targets with a sight to reach and destroy Point X.
descriptions.c64:161851: Pilot a ghost-hunting spacecraft across 32 levels, blasting the Poltergeist's minions and the flashing generators that spawn them, then touching down on a teleport pad to move on. Weapon upgrades help with the final showdown.
descriptions.c64:161852: With Earth abandoned to recover, humanity has settled an eleven-planet system, but a crash shattered the energy crystal needed to colonize the last world. The player sets out to recover its scattered pieces.
descriptions.c64:161853: Pat's van has broken down, so the morning post must be delivered on foot to houses marked with black arrows. First collect the letters, dodge loose hens, and keep his energy up with cups of tea.
descriptions.c64:161855: A Cold War strategy game for one player or two: pick the West or the East and try to bring as many countries as possible under your side's control on a world map where neutral nations sit in white.
descriptions.c64:161856: A sliding puzzle game in the vein of Atomix: the blob Max must gather every heart on a level and reach his girlfriend Mimi before time runs out, but once he starts moving he keeps going until a block stops him.
descriptions.c64:161857: A vertically scrolling shooter in which a lone fighter defends Earth from an invasion fleet, skimming low under the force fields of alien cruisers to knock out their solar panels.
descriptions.c64:161858: Govern a small nation and stay in office through elections held every two years, keeping famine and disease down while building up the treasury and the army and spending to win voters back before polling day. Hidden resources lie in the land.
descriptions.c64:161859: To win the princess, the hero must gather the scattered parts of a rescue craft, score enough points to prove his courage, and amass enough gold and jewels to persuade her to run away with him.
descriptions.c64:161860: A side-on, split-screen mountain bike race over obstacle-strewn courses, versus a second player or a computer rider, held by day or by night, with gears changed by holding the fire button.
descriptions.c64:161861: Powerboat racing on mostly one-way courses where fjords and inlets split the water into two lanes and ramps must be hit at the right speed to leap bridges, with the chance to land on rival boats.
descriptions.c64:161862: Gangsters have taken over 1930s New York and a hired gun works for the police: facing a row of buildings, shoot each mobster who appears before his countdown runs out and he fires first, or duck into cover.
descriptions.c64:161863: Ride a magnetic hover-board down through an abandoned military silo, ramp by ramp, to reach Level 60 and wipe out the source of a mysterious power. Damage slows the board until it barely crawls.
descriptions.c64:161873: A side-scrolling romp set on Dreams, the most popular holiday planetoid in the universe, located near the Belt of Unreality, where a vacationing hero hops through its bizarre landscape.
descriptions.c64:161874: Follow-up to Athena: Athena Asamiya, descendant of the princess, uses newly awakened psychic powers to fight the mutants overrunning a post-apocalyptic world in this side-scrolling action game.
descriptions.c64:161876: A Punch and Judy adventure across sixteen theater stages: as the hunchback Bobby, rescue Judy from Punch while avoiding crocodiles, flying custard pies and rotten tomatoes.
descriptions.c64:161896: Claim most of a rectangular playfield by drawing lines to wall off sections, while the Qix, an erratic stick-like creature, roams inside. Lines can be drawn quickly or slowly.
descriptions.c64:161897: Command a space fighter sent to wipe out the Etron rockets based on Hagon, starting with a run down a tunnel full of astro-fighters attacking from ahead and from the sides.
descriptions.c64:161898: The third Questprobe illustrated text adventure based on Marvel comics: switch at will between the Thing and the Human Torch to rescue Alicia Masters from Doctor Doom.
descriptions.c64:161900: A baseball game with all 26 major league teams and full rosters plus the 1989 All-Star squads, for one or two players, with passwords to carry a full season of games against each division rival.
descriptions.c64:161901: Cue sports for two with five rule sets: standard pool, 8-ball, 9-ball, Bumper Pool and English snooker. Practice modes allow shots to be retaken, and a built-in editor creates Bumper Pool tables.
descriptions.c64:161903: Lay a railroad across the American West from Base City to Junction City, hiring and firing surveyors, laborers and guards to fend off bandits, and building stations to raise money for wages and new stock.
descriptions.c64:161930: Mervyn, a wizard's apprentice, botched a charm meant to make him irresistible and ended up attractive only to female frogs. This top-down maze action game follows his efforts to set things right.
descriptions.c64:161934: As a crusader with only a sword and shield, enter the netherworld and shatter the Seven Planets jewel, which Rasputin's spirit draws on to threaten the universe.
descriptions.c64:161936: Two players race each other in a 100-meter sprint by hammering keys on the keyboard. This Olympic-themed game was never published.
descriptions.c64:161944: Guide the damaged droid MSB around the crippled starship Rasterscan as it drifts toward a star. Left alone the droid can only fix toasters, so the player must help it repair the ship's systems.
descriptions.c64:161955: A computer version of Monopoly playable in English, French, German, Swedish or Finnish, with the bank and the board handled by the program.
descriptions.c64:161958: Down-on-his-luck stuntman Fred MacMuscle takes the stunt work on the series Ricky Steel, Secret Agent, but must pay his own insurance; each completed stunt scene earns the money to cover the next.
descriptions.c64:161964: Caught stowing away on an Astro Cruiser, Rufus earns his passage to Earth by gathering five rare crystals per level on the hostile planet Killey.
descriptions.c64:161966: Kevin Oliver turns into the superhero Redhawk by shouting 'Kwah!' in this comic-panel adventure driven by a text parser, where heroic or villainous deeds raise or lower his popularity around the city.
descriptions.c64:161968: Repton digs for treasure through 24 levels of rockfall traps while avoiding monsters and spirits, mixing quick reflexes with puzzle solving. This second sequel adds sprite and level editors for making new screens.
descriptions.c64:161969: Edward Egg, one of the egg-shaped inhabitants of planet Egg who are all called Edward, is chosen to fly his egg-shaped craft against the returning Space Warriors.
descriptions.c64:161970: Adapted from Disney's dark 1985 film, a follow-up to The Wizard of Oz without songs. Back in Kansas, nobody believes Dorothy's tales, and the game follows her return to Oz much as the movie does.
descriptions.c64:161972: A beginner-friendly fantasy role-playing game by Ali N. Atabek, later creator of The Magic Candle, with no character creation, simple play and cut scenes that favor atmosphere over statistics.
descriptions.c64:161975: A public domain shooter on a grid by David Kinder: rack up kills until a life is lost or the clock runs out.
descriptions.c64:161995: After a holocaust, Dr. A Noid has turned people into zombies with his artificial food SLU. Drive an ATV through the city destroying hostile vehicles and dodging mines and gun turrets on the way to stop him.
descriptions.c64:161996: A Crush Roller style maze game: drive a road roller to paint every road purple while dodging ghouls, painting both ends of the railway bridge to dispose of them, and flattening rats and cars whose tracks spoil the paint.
descriptions.c64:161998: An illustrated adventure based on the 1980s British TV series: Robin breaks out of the Sheriff's castle alongside Scarlett and Much, and Herne the Hunter sends him after the six Touchstones of Rhiannon foretold by Gildas.
descriptions.c64:161999: Shut down the source of deadly pollution on a nearby planet across three shooting stages: a multi-directional scrolling maze, a fast into-the-screen 3D section and a final level.
descriptions.c64:162000: A real-time puzzle game steering a spotted ball through a labyrinth: it picks up speed, rebounds from obstacles, loses energy in traps, and is lost if it rolls off the edge.
descriptions.c64:162001: A boulder-and-gem game across six themed worlds of rising difficulty, where Rockford appears as explorer, cook, doctor and more, grabbing coins, apples or hearts while avoiding falling rocks and enemies.
descriptions.c64:162002: A turn-based dungeon crawl rendered in text characters: descend the Dungeon of Doom level by level, claim the Amulet of Yendor and get back out alive.
descriptions.c64:162003: Fairies Tam and Rit set out to free their mother from a castle across 40 screens, grabbing enemies with their magic rods and slamming them from side to side until they are beaten.
descriptions.c64:162017: The overture's notes are jumbled, so the maestro must dash around climbing ladders, reversing conveyor belts and stepping on the music ball to put each note back in its correct order.
descriptions.c64:162036: A pinball game for up to four players, released in the German magazine Game On in November 1991.
descriptions.c64:162037: Hanna-Barbera characters have been flung into space by Professor Flipnoodles' Pocket Rocket and captured by the Lilli-Punies, and Ruff and Reddy must carry out a rescue for their captors to win their friends' release.
descriptions.c64:162038: Following the Toymaker's Party, Rupert ventures into the Ice Castle of Jack and Jenny Frost to free four frozen friends, each held on a separate screen, while slippery ice and hostile creatures get in the way.
descriptions.c64:162039: A turn-based hex wargame of the Eastern Front, commanding the German OKH or Soviet Stavka through a 47-turn campaign covering 1941-1945, with three shorter scenarios drawn from parts of the campaign.
descriptions.c64:162041: A mercenary pilot hired by his home planet battles alien attack waves in a constantly upward-scrolling shooter, fighting through to a guardian at the end of each level.
descriptions.c64:162095: A Shanghai-style tile matching game over 40 levels of stacked tiles decorated with butterflies, masks and other symbols. Pairs must be cleared before time runs out, and only uncovered tiles free on one side can be taken.
descriptions.c64:162144: Former football star Harry Johns and his girlfriend Conny are stranded on the island of Dr. Graves, a deranged surgeon who has turned its people into ghosts, mummies, witches and werewolves.
descriptions.c64:162163: Lab assistant Alphonse T. Nurd snoops in his boss Bogdan Schtunk's laboratory and splits himself in two with the Atomic Particle People Splitter, then must put himself back together before Schtunk finds out.
descriptions.c64:162169: On planet LRV 1168, one or two players ride aquaglyders through underwater tunnels leaking toxic gas, fighting the minions of a huge beast that guards the depths in a horizontally scrolling shooter.
descriptions.c64:162170: A conversion of Sega's futuristic take on 1943: an old, underpowered fighter battles big aircraft, tanks and ground installations, with a close-up section and a boss at the end of each level and smart bombs to pick up.
descriptions.c64:162171: LINDA, a sewer maintenance droid, hunts the monsters infesting the city's drains with a laser gun. Some creatures destroy her outright while others sap her power, which batteries scattered around the sewers restore.
descriptions.c64:162181: An Infocom text adventure for younger players: as a celebrated young inventor, use your gadgets to protect the undersea Aquadome from a sea monster and a traitor on the inside.
descriptions.c64:162194: A flick-screen arcade adventure inside a castle: starting outside carrying a dagger and a banner, find a key to the front door, then roam split-level rooms joined by stairs and doors in search of a secret object.
descriptions.c64:162201: A tennis game viewed from a fixed side-on angle, so both players are always seen the same way, with single matches or full tournaments against the computer or a second player and the option to resume earlier progress.
descriptions.c64:162202: Seymour arrives in Hollywood for his first starring film role, only to learn the studio boss Dirk has vanished in Miami, so he must get production started himself in a Dizzy-style platform adventure.
descriptions.c64:162203: A Gauntlet-like maze game converted from the arcade: Kevin frees his friends from their cells, and the rescued prisoners trail behind him fighting enemies while he leads them to each level's exit.
descriptions.c64:162209: The second officer of a spaceship is locked out when the main computer fails during an engine inspection. Fly the Shadow Skimmer glider through three top-down mazes to another hatch while ship defenses treat you as an intruder.
descriptions.c64:162210: The Elfin Eharin once used the magical Inovar to shield themselves from the Nagroma, a plague that killed every living thing it touched at the start of winter. The Inovar now lies shattered and its pieces must be recovered.
descriptions.c64:162211: A horizontally scrolling shooter in the style of Katakis and Armalyte: the ship starts with a small plasma laser and gains mines, missiles, bouncing bombs, guided missiles and shields from wrecked enemies.
descriptions.c64:162212: An Atomix-like puzzle game where colored blocks slide in a chosen direction until they hit a wall or another block. The aim is not to build a shape but to group the blocks by color.
descriptions.c64:162214: In a future where big cities are ringed by moving walkways, ride all the way around a three-lane shockway whose lanes travel at different speeds, getting past gang members and angry citizens blocking the route.
descriptions.c64:162232: A first-person shooter where a crosshair sweeps left and right across the screen to find and shoot waves of aliens. The aliens hurl cubes that wear down the shield gauge.
descriptions.c64:162234: A Wild West shooter set in Gulch Creek: gunslinger Quick Hand Luke first practices by shooting a set number of cans, then faces outlaws, with two scenes on every level.
descriptions.c64:162235: Ride a horse over a show-jumping course of walls, water jumps and five-bar gates, judging each approach to clear the obstacles, in rounds scored against the clock, on faults or both.
descriptions.c64:162271: Thieves have taken your motorcycle apart, and you have from 3pm until 7.30pm to recover the parts and rebuild it in time to collect your girlfriend for the Live Aid concert before rival John does in this timed adventure.
descriptions.c64:162278: Fly through an energy-venting tunnel to destroy an alien battle station in a vertical shooter, with defenders lining the walls and patrolling the ducts and extra weapons to pick up.
descriptions.c64:162280: Strap on a jetpack to drive evil invaders off four planets that can be tackled in any order, in a horizontally scrolling shooter that allows movement in every direction.
descriptions.c64:162282: A compilation of three Level 9 science fiction text adventures: Worm in Paradise, Snowball and Return to Eden. Each can be played separately, but the top score requires finishing them in order and carrying the score forward.
descriptions.c64:162283: A rookie cop drives a patrol car through the city, avoiding traffic that tries to ram him while chasing down three villains: Slit-throat Steve, the buggy driver Jon and the mastermind Dr J Davies.
descriptions.c64:162285: Turn-based man-to-man gunfights in the 19th-century American West, with ten scenarios against the computer or another player, some inspired by events such as the O.K. Corral, others by films or invented outright.
descriptions.c64:162288: In a future where skateboarding rules, ride around chambers full of obstacles and knock out rivals by launching your skateboard at them, clearing each wave of enemies to advance.
descriptions.c64:162292: Skel, a superhuman skeleton that is half bone and half machine, was made by the gods to guard the universe but turned against them and now lays waste with a plasma gun that loses energy as it fires.
descriptions.c64:162332: Pirates Red Beard and One Eye battle ninjas, skeletons and other foes on ships, in forts and beyond to win back their loot from an evil wizard; a second player can take the other pirate.
descriptions.c64:162333: Director Steven Squealburgh hires a stuntman to film four action scenes in a helicopter, a balloon, a jet fighter and a biplane, in a top-down vertically scrolling shooter with a limited number of takes.
descriptions.c64:162335: Run and jump across eight constantly scrolling stages on Zetta Kenntaury's third planet, gunning down invading aliens with a laser while hopping over obstacles.
descriptions.c64:162336: Fly a helicopter across five side-scrolling levels to find parts marked ET and carry each one to the site of a supply base under construction.
descriptions.c64:162337: Based on the 2000 AD comic: the last Drune wizard of Lyonesse is dead, but his power lingers until his secret name is spoken, and only his daughter, trapped in Small Sky Tower, knows it. Sláine sets out to reach her.
descriptions.c64:162373: Slightly, nephew of the wizard Bigwiz, is left alone when his uncle rushes off, leaving the castle overrun with dragons, in a short Dizzy-style platform adventure from Codemasters.
descriptions.c64:162374: Slurpy is a small creature with an enormous snout who never stops eating, slurping up Glowbugs and Cave Birds while dodging the enemies that prey on him.
descriptions.c64:162383: Late on Friday night a giant mechanical hand snatches Slug's sweetheart right out of the room as they settle in to watch a horror movie, and he sets off to get her back.
descriptions.c64:162486: A blend of Breakout and shooter across 16 levels: the Snoball battle tractor moves up and down the left side of the screen, bouncing a ball to knock out every brick.
descriptions.c64:162501: Valuables keep vanishing from Mystery Mansion, where the Snodger family lives alongside odd creatures called snodgits. The bumbling butler Benton tries to crack the case ahead of the visiting detectives while still serving the household.
descriptions.c64:162540: A trial for a top football club: pass four skill tests to the required standard, then run an assault course combining all four, after choosing kit colors and difficulty.
descriptions.c64:162541: From the maker of Football Manager, a business simulation of running a computer games company: earn a £10,000 profit and hold the title of Software Star for ten months running, hiring staff and deciding how long each game is developed.
descriptions.c64:162542: A one-man army lands on an island seized by a mad general, fighting through seven stages to storm his fortress before he launches more invasions, with a power bar tracking health.
descriptions.c64:162573: An updated version of the Solo Flight simulator with a redesigned cockpit panel for the Ryan ST-A light plane, offering practice flights or mail runs over a choice of six American states.
descriptions.c64:162576: A turn-based fantasy wargame: the Shadowlord's army is closing in on Galanor, and the player coordinates the alliance of races defending the country.
descriptions.c64:162577: An illustrated text adventure: Megron, a world where magic and science meet, has fallen after its Great Council unleashed Darkon, and the player and the robot Komputa are its last hope.
descriptions.c64:162578: A space academy recruit completes a series of tests of dexterity and joystick waggling, finishing fitness training, which starts with running, before moving on to weapons training.
descriptions.c64:162625: Return to Fantasy Land as the Space Harrier for 13 stages of flying and shooting from behind the hero while the 3D landscape rushes toward the screen, with bosses to defeat.
descriptions.c64:162629: Bounty hunter Clint Westband roams Wild West streets shooting desperadoes for reward money, gathering dynamite to blast obstacles, money bags and keys, and items that deal with ghosts, scorpions and hornets.
descriptions.c64:162630: Ride a GTX armored bike through a series of levels, shooting down hordes of aliens.
descriptions.c64:162654: As the gladiator Spartacus, fight a series of side-on sword-and-shield duels to escape slavery and free the other slaves held by Crassus, while also fending off a swooping eagle.
descriptions.c64:162679: A surfing game with a practice mode where energy is never lost and a ten-round competition scored for performance. Known in Italy as Surfwave.
descriptions.c64:162689: A World War II commando mission against a heavily guarded forest compound hiding an underground lab close to combining a bacterial virus with a new rocket.
descriptions.c64:162690: A Centipede clone for one or two players that sticks closely to the original: shoot the segmented Spectipede as it winds down through the forest toward the player, for as high a score as possible.
descriptions.c64:162722: Spiky Harold the hedgehog has 24 hours to eat his fill before hibernating. Explore flick screens gathering food in this platform game, avoiding hazards that cost one of his 20 lives.
descriptions.c64:162723: A volunteer wizard enters the Magic Maze to hunt down the evil sorcerer Ashlaa, picking up spells and a shield on the way while monsters wear down his strength.
descriptions.c64:162724: Two worm-like creatures circle a pair of tracks in either direction, hopping between them and firing balls into a central field of deflectors; touching the opponent costs a life. For one or two players.
descriptions.c64:162765: Based on the British satirical puppet show: a prophet foresees a world war in seven years, so six world leaders, Ronald Reagan among them, fight it out in a beat-'em-up to decide who rules the planet.
descriptions.c64:162766: Steer a spider around a maze that scrolls in random directions, eating every patch of grass while keeping clear of the walls, whose layout changes from level to level.
descriptions.c64:162841: Fight off invading hordes with photon bombs in 3D space combat spread over six difficulty levels, from training up to Kamikaze.
descriptions.c64:162842: An illustrated text adventure adapted from Harry Harrison's novel, with a 200-word vocabulary: as James di Griz, rescue your wife Angelina and save the world by defeating the villain known only as He.
descriptions.c64:162843: In a bar, hunt down the seven fragments of the fabled amulet belonging to Wonga, the great budgie, shooting hallucinations and taking care not to spill other drinkers' glasses while managing energy, hunger and drunkenness.
descriptions.c64:162846: Kormath has taken Excalibur and the Holy Grail from Merlin. A knight, with occasional help from Lancelot, descends into the dungeon under the Standing Stones to recover them and gather treasure.
descriptions.c64:162866: Cosmic invaders, galactic pirates and the Sausonic Raiders have nearly halted trade, and mines clog the space lanes. A rookie pilot sets out to clear them and earn his Star Commando wings.
descriptions.c64:162867: The captain of a remote space station is thawed out of cryogenic sleep when the RB-130 computer spots an alien battle fleet approaching Federation space, and must shoot down as many attackers as possible.
descriptions.c64:162872: A thousand years after the fall of an empire of four races, Humans, Velox, Thrynn and Elowan, powered by Endurium, the people of the colony world Arth rediscover space travel. Captain a starship to explore, trade and uncover the past.
descriptions.c64:162874: Earth is losing a long war against the Imperial Forces of Dalsarn, whose factories outbuild its own, and the stretched Terran Star Force sends a fighter pilot into battle.
descriptions.c64:162875: A slow-paced side-scrolling shooter where the ship fires in two directions at a low rate, and enemies stay on screen, pressing the attack until they are destroyed rather than flying past.
descriptions.c64:162877: A bounty hunter hired by the Galactic Federation teleports between star colonies taken over by pirates, clearing each one of the vermin.
descriptions.c64:162878: A run-and-gun game as a bounty hunter: choose weapons and energy packs, scan the star system for planets, read their job offers and land to carry out missions for credits.
descriptions.c64:162879: After a sudden attack, leaking coolant has spoiled the Enterprise's protein stock used for synthesized food, and with warp repairs needing over a week, Kirk's crew must find a new food source in this text adventure.
descriptions.c64:162880: A mutiny is spreading through the Federation in the Sagittarius Arm, with every investigating starship joining the Klingons. Kirk's Enterprise must find the cause before Starfleet seals the region inside a Klein Sphere forever.
descriptions.c64:162918: The second sequel in the series, released with Commodore Zone issue 8: a star circles while fire is held and shoots off in a straight line when released, used to collect items around each screen.
descriptions.c64:16295: An arcade conversion that mixes castle building and artillery: enclose a castle with Tetris-style wall pieces, place cannons, bombard the enemy, then rush to repair the damage before the next round.
descriptions.c64:162977: With their planet Alpha One dying, the humanoids send out their bravest to find a new home, and a Space Federation fighter pilot clears a path through the galaxy for them.
descriptions.c64:162978: A Pong variant set in 2164: the people of Utalis can only win freedom from the Jitter-Bobs by beating them at Spaceball, played with paddles on the left and right of the screen by one or two players.
descriptions.c64:162979: An Infocom science fiction text adventure set in 2186: a black-hole miner investigates a huge alien starship that has entered the solar system and must work out how to get inside and what its builders want.
descriptions.c64:162980: In 5112, after endless wars and alien invasions have left Earth ruined and its survivors in government shelters, the planet's defenses lie destroyed and a lone pilot must hold off the next attack.
descriptions.c64:162981: Guard a lone outpost by rotating a laser and shooting the aliens that tumble toward the base, including the occasional superalien flying a flickering spiral path.
descriptions.c64:162982: Roll a ball up great isometric mountains to gather misplaced objects and bonus items such as money, avoiding holes and critters that cost a life.
descriptions.c64:162987: Protect the colonies from waves of attacking aliens in a side-scrolling shooter with layered parallax scrolling and new backdrops and enemies for each of its 7 levels.
descriptions.c64:163001: A flight simulator with three aircraft, the F-19 stealth fighter, the X-29 experimental plane and the F-14 Tomcat, four missions each at easy or advanced level, selectable weapon loads and 10 skill levels.
descriptions.c64:163002: On the robot-run spaceship Steel, the machines have gone rogue. Disguised as a robot, the player sneaks aboard to disable the security system, though the other robots attack anyway.
descriptions.c64:163009: A first-person space shooter: move the sight and fire twin lasers to destroy as many stellar fighters as possible within 100 seconds.
descriptions.c64:163022: Grand-strategy World War II in Europe, directing land, sea and air forces while managing limited production and research, with six historical scenarios from Autumn 1939 to Summer 1944 and a scenario builder.
descriptions.c64:163160: Bare-bones street football for one or two players, where the only rule is to hit the crate standing in for a goal more often than the other side. Teams of five are picked from 24 players, including the game's programmers.
descriptions.c64:163161: A text adventure that opens with the hero waking up behind bars in a police station after a night of drinking, killing time until the pubs reopen by settling on a quest that drives the rest of the game.
descriptions.c64:163212: Lucasfilm's follow-up to PHM Pegasus moves from hydrofoils to command of a whole naval task force, with missions tied to the political flashpoints of 1987.
descriptions.c64:163231: Man the BB2 gun to shoot down reconnaissance helicopters, then waves of bombers with fighter escorts, and finally enemy vehicles weaving behind buildings, including armored cars that stop to return fire.
descriptions.c64:163232: Ten-pin bowling against a second player or a computer opponent with four skill levels, played over 10 frames under standard scoring with two balls per frame unless a strike is rolled.
descriptions.c64:163321: A wizard fights through flick screens above and below ground, in the style of Switchblade, to defeat Trogan the Diabolical, cutting down his henchmen with a sword, avoiding skeletons and collecting energy refills.
descriptions.c64:163325: A gust of wind has scattered belongings all over the Hundred Acre Wood. Find each object, work out who owns it and return it before the wind blows again, meeting Pooh and his friends along the way.
descriptions.c64:163357: Table football on the computer: with 30 seconds per turn, pick a player, aim, and hold the button to decide how hard the flick is and how much it curves, while the side without the ball may first make a blocking flick; hitting an opponent hands over possession.
