descriptions.c64:163359: As a beret-wearing vigilante in the London Underground, check the subway map for trouble spots, ride the trains there and fight the violent criminals in each station.
descriptions.c64:163360: A top-down, freely scrolling space shooter through several star systems, dodging or blasting asteroids and enemies that pour out of circles, with energy pods sometimes dropped by destroyed foes.
descriptions.c64:163361: A dragon holds a princess in his lair, and with no knight to hand a magician fights through four levels of the dragon's minions to free her.
descriptions.c64:163363: A 3D action game where the hero takes on the Guardians armed with a magic warhammer that comes back when thrown, Boots of Power, ESP and teleport activators, or ends up in the Dead-Zone.
descriptions.c64:163394: A football management game featuring match-fixing offers from organized crime, the membership card scheme and the cost of modernizing grounds.
descriptions.c64:163395: Manage a first division football club where relegation means the sack: buy and sell players, negotiate contracts, train reserves and pick the side before watching the match.
descriptions.c64:163396: A first-person Formula One racer around Monaco: set a grid position in a solo qualifying lap of a shortened circuit, then race 19 rival cars.
descriptions.c64:163403: A one-player fruit machine with 10, 20 or 30 starting credits and five reels, four of which make up the paying line while the fifth serves a separate purpose, plus a high score table.
descriptions.c64:163473: Ride Super Rider through the Firebird Arena course against the clock, dodging giant pyramids, leaping ravines and clearing fences, with five seconds added each time the rider falls.
descriptions.c64:163482: Seymour stars as an eco-minded superhero in a Bomb Jack-style game, hopping around single-screen areas to collect barrels of toxic waste, with one highlighted barrel worth extra points at a time.
descriptions.c64:163483: A Scramble clone: fly over hostile ground and through caverns, shooting enemy craft, bombing ground installations and dodging missiles, able to drop only one bomb at once, with three lives.
descriptions.c64:163484: A Breakout-style game presented as a world championship racquetball final, where fast reflexes are needed to return the speeding ball.
descriptions.c64:163487: An overhead stock car racer with a scrolling track: beat three computer drivers over a set number of laps, since only a win unlocks the next circuit and anything less ends the game.
descriptions.c64:163496: A horizontally scrolling adventure released as a preview of the second Shoot Em Up Destruction Set compilation from Psytronik: rescue Elena from an evil Minotaur, facing spear-throwing Spartans, Cyclopes and spike traps.
descriptions.c64:163498: Work a supermarket shift: fetch stock and carry it to the right aisle to keep the shelves full and the floors clean, handling over 30 products such as bread, milk, eggs and carrots.
descriptions.c64:163499: Genetically enhanced Superkid defends mankind's resources from alien invaders, exploring five alien planets to gather the four detonator parts needed to blow up each one, and taking hidden pills to keep his strength up.
descriptions.c64:163531: Five comic events played in turn, with the highest total winning: Crack Shot has players firing at cans in a back alley, where hitting a cat loses points, and Dare Devil Dive resembles a circus high dive.
descriptions.c64:163533: Lay down spreads of torpedoes in the path of attacking PT boats, wave after wave, with each wave moving faster than the last. Also released for the VIC-20.
descriptions.c64:163537: Table tennis against the computer or a second player, seen in 3D with only the bats shown. More options than Imagine's Ping Pong, including whether the table is split horizontally or vertically.
descriptions.c64:163539: Texas Pete and his henchmen Bulk and Skeleton have kidnapped Spotty, who switched on a homing device as he was bundled into their car. SuperTed follows the signal to rescue his friend.
descriptions.c64:163551: An Infocom text adventure: on the colony Contra, the sleeping Central Mentality runs transport, weather and resources by thought. Roused after five centuries of stasis, direct six robots with different senses to repair the failing systems.
descriptions.c64:163552: A burglar raiding a millionaire's mansion stumbles into a fancy dress party and is chased by the guests. Gather the colored Master Code Cards hidden in its maze of rooms to make a getaway with the loot.
descriptions.c64:163553: Rescue nearly a thousand survivors from a hibernation dome damaged in a nuclear war by guiding three droids with different jobs, one of which bores rapidly through earth, through seven levels and teleporting the survivors out.
descriptions.c64:163574: A tile puzzle: swap tiles to form same-colored groups that disappear, on boards of squares, triangles or hexagons; stranded tiles can be cleared using pieces from a small reserve pocket.
descriptions.c64:163575: Sweep every chimney in the dark while hungry rats and fires block the way, earning a bonus game for finishing.
descriptions.c64:163576: The evil Havoc has broken the Fireblade of the Switchblade clan into 16 pieces. As Hiro, search platforms and ladders indoors and out to recover them, with the map revealed only as it is explored.
descriptions.c64:163578: Comdata has lost $1.5 million to the rival firm Realco and the police cannot recover it. Use a simulated computer network to break into systems and get the money back, a premise set out in a letter from a friend named Mike.
descriptions.c64:163582: A text adventure from The Thriller Series: search the South American jungle for the lost City of the Sun and its golden idol of the Moon Goddess, with deadly dangers on the way.
descriptions.c64:163583: A text adventure from The Thriller Series: to claim the Musgrave fortune, recover the locket Aunt Bedilia was buried with twelve years ago, and live through a night when the dead walk.
descriptions.c64:163584: A text adventure from The Thriller Series that sends the player across Africa in search of jewels from King Solomon's mines, with some dated portrayals of local characters.
descriptions.c64:163607: A war game played on a fold-out hex board alongside the computer, with four countries of varied terrain, each fielding a division of eight tanks and four armored cars, and the aim of destroying the other nations' bases.
descriptions.c64:163626: In the year 6038 a defeated emperor threatens the Cybernetica Galaxy again. Prince Troma flies to the emperor's star system to destroy his forces over 16 levels of laser combat around scattered platforms.
descriptions.c64:163627: Snide Gaintree's mercenaries have seized a secret South Pacific air base and will control its cruise missiles in under four hours. Fly a jet fighter through the caverns beneath it in this flick-screen side-view shooter.
descriptions.c64:163628: Tazzman roams room to room zapping bugs with a laser that fires in four directions but only while he stands still, using bombs to get rid of the two creatures chasing him.
descriptions.c64:163663: A cross-country bicycle race of over 3000 miles across the United States: overtake other riders, grab bottles for energy, and follow the trainer's advice and the map through regional courses and obstacles.
descriptions.c64:163664: Adapted from the Fighting Fantasy gamebook: the sage Yaztromo sends a lone adventurer across the Desert of Skulls to reach the lost city of Vatos and stop Malbordus, champion of the Dark Elves, braving monsters, traps and the cult of Leesha.
descriptions.c64:163665: Mining engineers flee the planet Krion after accidentally setting off its destruction in a vertical shooter of over 100 screens with barriers, narrow passages, force fields and time-shift fields that push the ship forward or back.
descriptions.c64:163666: A comic text adventure: a family man takes his wife and children on a disastrous Spanish holiday, dodging bulls, sharks and heatstroke and trying to keep the family from wandering off.
descriptions.c64:163667: The planet Colian is rich in Aluma metal, explosive Detonite and Quaza crystals, but the Empire controls its mines and uses them to build Terrorpods. The player battles these walking war machines.
descriptions.c64:163668: A Mario-like side-scrolling platform game with blocky graphics and many ledges, where Terry fights with a yo-yo aimed by pushing the joystick while holding fire.
descriptions.c64:163674: Find a way through the tomb of King Batutu to its centuries-old treasure. Each game draws a new maze, shown for ten seconds before the timed trek begins.
descriptions.c64:163683: Fly a dragon rightward through a land of soldiers and monsters such as sea snakes, giant spiders and a two-headed dragon, burning them with fire breath or snatching them in its claws to drop on others.
descriptions.c64:163685: A Puzznic-style puzzle game of 150 side-view levels: push blocks bearing symbols or numbers left or right so matching ones touch and vanish, clearing every block before time runs out.
descriptions.c64:163689: Based on the Dumas novel: Cardinal Richelieu schemes to discredit Queen Anne over her affair with the Duke of Buckingham, and the musketeers must retrieve the diamonds she gave the Duke.
descriptions.c64:163695: The sequel keeps Thrust's physics and controls of rotating and thrusting, as the Federal Resistance captures a strategically vital artificial planet in its war.
descriptions.c64:163696: Fly a spaceship around a single level holding eight yellow eggs that hatch creatures, crushing them with a separate egg that reappears on another platform each time it is used.
descriptions.c64:163699: Madame Q has kidnapped thousands of women for experiments in her underwater fortress. As part of a government strike team, swim in from a submarine and storm the base to free the hostages.
descriptions.c64:163712: A helicopter simulation of the Hughes 530 MG Defender with training to learn its handling, followed by rescue and combat missions and then sea rescues and armed escorts.
descriptions.c64:163716: The ship Thundercross is being dragged toward a huge enemy vessel whose pull its thrusters cannot escape, while smaller craft launched from the giant ship attack.
descriptions.c64:163736: Trapped in Empress Min's castle with mind and body separated, the hero's body bounces around in a green ball that cannot be steered directly; use the mind to guide it out through 100 rooms.
descriptions.c64:163737: A puzzle game across 15 mazes with names such as The Decoder, Dolly's Revenge and Patience Pending, playable in any order: switch between Magus and Questor, who have different abilities, to collect every balloon within 2000 moves.
descriptions.c64:163738: An educational word puzzle mixing crosswords and Scrabble: given all the letters of a grid of interlocking words, place each one in its correct square to complete the grid.
descriptions.c64:163739: After a distress call from orbiting space stations goes silent, a team of engineers boards them to wipe out the Xenos, aliens that hatch from pods and spit acid, before they overrun everything.
descriptions.c64:163740: A first-person adventure on the asteroid mining station Atargis, where a crash-landed pilot explores mines that are deserted of all 200 workers and searches for a way off the rock.
descriptions.c64:163741: Rookie commando Jaid Ray of the elite X-Terminators is sent into the complex identified as the nest of alien Bio-morphs that have wiped out most humanoid colonies in the galaxy.
descriptions.c64:163742: Spend a week as Prime Minister Jim Hacker from the BBC comedy Yes, Prime Minister, juggling public popularity, party demands, foreign governments and the civil servants around him.
descriptions.c64:163744: Mahjong solitaire with tiles piled in five layers that are removed in matching pairs, plus a two-player tournament mode, separate views of each layer and an undo option.
descriptions.c64:163746: William Wobbler searches caverns beneath an alien planet's cratered surface for ten clues, jumping with the fire button and getting past barriers and puzzles.
descriptions.c64:163747: An overhead action game with light role-playing: an apprentice wizard seeks to beat seven master wizards and become chief wizard, returning six treasures to their owners and learning stronger spells beyond his four starting ones.
descriptions.c64:163748: A spell binds the good land of Midgard to the evil Neflheim, and evil is leaking through. A novice wizard earns points to rise in rank and cast the spell to separate the worlds, while senior wizards stand in his way.
descriptions.c64:163749: An illustrated adventure based on L. Frank Baum's novel: Dorothy, swept to Oz by a cyclone, travels with Toto, the Scarecrow, the Tin Woodman and the Lion to the Emerald City to ask the Wizard for a way home.
descriptions.c64:163751: A Centipede-style shooter where a small craft moves along the bottom of the screen, able to edge forward and back, to shoot spiders that creep downward and sometimes stop to fire.
descriptions.c64:163752: A jealous green-faced demon has murdered the contented monk Brother Jeffrey and buried his bones deep underground. As the monk's ghost, descend to recover them so he can rest in peace.
descriptions.c64:163753: A demon has carried off a princess along with the White Viper's armor and sword to an evil wizard's castle. Cross the land, get inside and rescue her across five parts.
descriptions.c64:163754: Eight Winter Olympic events played back to back, with the highest total winning; events can be deselected, and players compete two at a time on a split screen.
descriptions.c64:163773: Based on the Hanna-Barbera cartoon: as Dick Dastardly and Muttley, finish each course in the required position by waiting for rivals to drop out from damage or by wrecking them with the car's weapons.
descriptions.c64:163774: A maintenance droid must switch on all fifteen video machines in a millionaire's castle arcade every day while avoiding the meanies, finding keys scattered around the building to reach machines behind locked doors.
descriptions.c64:163776: An action game drawn from the blue-and-white willow pattern found on china since the late 18th century, with graphics and locations taken from the design and a story based on the legend made up to explain it.
descriptions.c64:163777: Up to three players bet on greyhound races at different tracks across a season, with a scoreboard tracking each gambler's fortunes and race winners advancing to Wembley to decide the champion dog.
descriptions.c64:163778: Chase Carmen Sandiego's gang across American cities, following clues to track down the henchmen who have stolen outlandish treasures of US history and heritage.
descriptions.c64:163779: Pilot a helicopter through five vertically scrolling levels to destroy the enemy's base waiting at the finish, using the cannon on ground-based attackers and a limited stock of smart bombs.
descriptions.c64:163780: A 2009 C64 remake of the Firebird Wild West adventure from the ZX Spectrum and Amstrad CPC, mixing adventure with graphics and arcade sections as a wanted man works to clear his name.
descriptions.c64:163781: Alexey Pajitnov's Tetris follow-up: pieces drop down the four walls of a square well viewed from above and slide onto its floor, where complete lines vanish.
descriptions.c64:163782: Fly in orbit above a planet across fourteen levels, steering past satellites and other enemies and firing a powerful cannon when evasion is not enough.
descriptions.c64:163784: Raised by foxes, the Vixen is the only human left on Granath, a world ruled by dinosaurs, and has vowed to wipe them out. Each left-to-right level must be cleared within a time limit, using a whip as her main weapon.
descriptions.c64:163785: Wallie P. Jones completes tasks on five levels based on nursery rhymes including Little Miss Muffet, Humpty Dumpty, Hey Diddle Diddle and the tale of the Owl and Pussycat, each split into two parts.
descriptions.c64:163786: A strategy game on a 6x6 board against the computer: place counters on empty squares or ones already held, and a square explodes when its counters equal its number of neighbors.
descriptions.c64:163801: A gnome who dreams of ruling his people must recover the seven lost pieces of a document explaining how to become king, scattered across time zones from 9600 BC through 1692 and 1849 to 9999.
descriptions.c64:163813: The Black Wizard Velnor has found the tomb of Grako and is preparing to become a demon. A lone hero enters Mt. Elk to find him in the Goblin caverns before the change is complete.
descriptions.c64:163815: A lone pilot fights off an alien attack on the galaxy, collecting pods that boost speed and firepower or give energy and extra lives, plus a droid that can teleport aboard enemy ships.
descriptions.c64:163875: The first of Gargoyle Games' trilogy blending arcade and adventure: as Cuchulainn, restore the Sidhe to their former wisdom and civilization, exploring a side-on world whose view rotates to change direction.
descriptions.c64:163876: Fight waves of monsters among ancient Greek ruins, with a winged horse on hand.
descriptions.c64:163879: A lab mishap with prototype cybernetics gives Dr Mulliner's pet tortoise super powers, so Turbo travels to six eras, from Prehistoric and the Ice Age to Egypt, the Middle Ages and the 20th Century, to collect the parts for a working machine.
descriptions.c64:163881: A Breakout game with 64 levels and a level editor where the paddle layout changes per level, from top and bottom pairs to side paddles or four stacked ones, alongside unbreakable blocks and monsters.
descriptions.c64:163932: Archangel Bertram descends from the gates of Hell to its depths to reclaim the Ten Commandments and his own horn from Mephisto, and destroy him.
descriptions.c64:163935: A bio-mechanical fighting toad with a jetpack and laser descends five levels below a planet's surface to destroy the central computer of a defense network, while the hostile atmosphere drains his resources.
descriptions.c64:163936: A text adventure that begins with a tale told by an old crone in a tavern, of how King Ghall's kingdom fell to the dark hordes of Lord Cthullo and how the king summoned the long-dead warrior Ghunlh.
descriptions.c64:163938: Guide Jerry through five levels, collecting every piece of cheese against the clock while avoiding Tom, who can be dealt with briefly using the scenery, such as by dropping a bowling ball on his head.
descriptions.c64:163956: Collect 40 items from a shopping list in a perilous supermarket full of creatures and obstacles, carrying only five items at a time and losing one of four lives to creatures, falls or hazards.
descriptions.c64:163960: A major league baseball simulation covering a full season, named after the Oakland Athletics manager, with statistics for every team, play for one or two players, and the option to manage while the computer plays.
descriptions.c64:163966: Twins Twinky and Reg race across the countryside for the affection of Twinka on a split screen, two players or player against computer, jumping obstacles and eating food along the way.
descriptions.c64:163967: A single-screen platformer by The Mojon Twins in which the greedy Uwol, already rich from selling retro games in Spain, raids rooms full of coins in pursuit of even more wealth.
descriptions.c64:163968: A scuba diver searches underwater caves for kidnapped friends, surfacing to refill air or finding tanks to stay down longer.
descriptions.c64:163970: Drag racing named after three-time Top Fuel world champion Shirley Muldowney: choose and tune equipment, run qualifying, and compete in races if fast enough.
descriptions.c64:163971: American football where plays are called and then run with the keyboard or joystick, with digitized speech for the crowd, signal calls and referee decisions.
descriptions.c64:163983: Fly a plectrum-shaped ship around single-screen levels shooting Zoids that start as dots and morph, needing more hits the longer they survive; firing drains energy, which is restored by collecting drifting spacemen.
descriptions.c64:163989: Konami's athletics game: compete in the 100 meter dash, long jump, javelin, 110 meter hurdles, hammer throw and high jump, beating ever tougher qualifying marks to move on.
descriptions.c64:163998: A 3D vector strategy game controlled by mouse, set on a brutal TV show of the future: command a fleet of Skimmers to destroy groups of Cycloids, Scouts and Defenders and become the first to win.
descriptions.c64:163999: Turn-based business game in which each player runs a transport depot, shipping food, oil and textiles by truck, barge or tanker. The computer takes one seat, leaving room for one to three human traders.
descriptions.c64:164003: An isometric scrolling shooter: fly down a corridor into the fortress of the Zylogon, an android race threatening mankind, bombing or dodging their craft and avoiding the walls.
descriptions.c64:164006: Earth intercepts signals revealing a threat from the Cygma Elite, and a strike team is sent to the distant planet where the aliens have built their facilities.
descriptions.c64:164007: Pilot a blimp across five side-view screens of Los Angeles, rescuing stranded people while fighting gravity and the airship's sluggish handling; it cannot reverse.
descriptions.c64:164008: A constantly scrolling side-view shooter through the underground tunnels of a secret alien force, shooting or dodging their craft and avoiding walls over eight levels.
descriptions.c64:164009: A hunter armed with grenades and a Lee Enfield rifle enters the forbidden territory of the Yeti to capture it, battling weather, terrain and hostile enemies.
descriptions.c64:164010: A helicopter pilot works toward the rank of Xenon against the clock on a split screen, with a side-scrolling shooting section above and a platform section below.
descriptions.c64:164012: World War II naval warfare in three phases, starting with a destroyer escorting Atlantic convoys against U-boats until enough supplies reach England for the invasion.
descriptions.c64:164013: Golf on over a dozen famous courses such as Pebble Beach and Augusta, shown on a split screen with an overhead map and a 3D view, with club range overlays and a driving range for practice.
descriptions.c64:164014: Football management in a world league of two 16-team divisions plus a cup: take one of six invited UK clubs, win promotion, then chase the league and cup double.
descriptions.c64:164015: Darts with a cartoon look: throw at a standard board with segments worth 1 to 20, double and treble rings, and a 50-point bullseye.
descriptions.c64:164017: An enemy holds a heavily fortified island. Destroy its network of bunkers to uncover the island's defenses and pinpoint the commander, who keeps relocating his headquarters.
descriptions.c64:164020: Explore the five levels and more than 500 rooms of Count Kreepie's castle to kill him and find his loot, carrying no more than three items, weapons included.
descriptions.c64:164022: A former ally has turned hostile, and a lone spacecraft defends the home planet across 10 levels, each made up of three separate tests beginning with a stretch of open space full of incoming mines.
descriptions.c64:164023: Tie-in with the 1980s British TV ads where Weetabix biscuits became characters such as Dunk, Bixie, Crunch and Brains: Dunk sets out to wipe out the Titchies, who are out to destroy the biscuits.
descriptions.c64:164028: Design and fight turn-based battles from any era, ancient, 1800s, modern or future, setting each unit's firepower, movement, strength and aggressiveness. For one or two players, with eight ready-made scenarios.
descriptions.c64:164031: A point-and-click horror adventure in the style of Déjà Vu and Shadowgate: after a figure on a dark road causes a car crash, wake to find your brother gone and search the eerie mansion he must have entered.
descriptions.c64:164032: As Van Helsing, rid 160 side-view screens of vampires before time runs out, bouncing a beam of light off mirrors to destroy them and keeping it under control.
descriptions.c64:164033: A casino collection of four games, Keno, Blackjack, Draw Poker and Lucky 7 Slots, playable alone or with friends.
descriptions.c64:164034: Casino craps with a mouse-driven interface: pick up chips, place bets on the table and click the dice to roll, starting with $1000 and playing on until the money runs out.
descriptions.c64:164035: Aliens have raided a research center, and a driver races across the land to save abducted scientists and retrieve stolen weapons, computers and microfilm, getting out on foot to grab each one while dodging aliens.
descriptions.c64:164036: Drive back a great evil by purging the twelve signs of the zodiac, three levels each, where portals release good and evil spores and the good ones must spread far enough to destroy every evil portal.
descriptions.c64:164037: One or two players race craft through 3D tunnels seen from behind to grab an orb and bring it back to the finish, firing lasers at each other and at hostile craft. Includes a track editor.
descriptions.c64:164038: Cinemaware's American football presented like a TV broadcast, with a TV-style intro before each game and cut scenes for dramatic moments, mostly action play with plays chosen beforehand.
descriptions.c64:164039: A creative program for young children, guided by a friendly turtle, where they use the joystick to paint pictures and play with color, music and animals, saving their artwork for later.
descriptions.c64:164040: Follow-up to Panzer Strike, simulating small-unit World War II combat: Americans versus Japanese in the Pacific, British versus Japanese in Asia, and Americans versus Germans in Europe.
descriptions.c64:164041: From Ajax HQ, remotely pilot a drone that switches between a jet fighter seen from behind and a top-down helicopter gunship, battling through eight levels to destroy the alien fortress.
descriptions.c64:164042: An interactive audiovisual piece rather than a game: Mike Oldfield's Tubular Bells rearranged for the SID chip and paired with on-screen visuals.
descriptions.c64:164043: Landing ten minutes ahead of a mind-probe at the Triaxos maximum security prison, locate the one prisoner able to activate the galaxy's most powerful weapon and bring him to your ship inside 30 minutes, blasting robot guards.
descriptions.c64:164044: An illustrated take on Colossal Cave: wander a forest and caves gathering treasures and handling odd creatures, using one- or two-word typed commands, with plenty of jokes in the responses.
descriptions.c64:164050: Texas billionaire Arthur J. Hackensack kidnaps scientist Frobisher Goonhilly and uses his matter transformation weapon to turn the Isle of Wight into a custard slice and New York into a sponge, and Blinky the ghost steps in.
descriptions.c64:164051: A quiz for one to four players on a fruit machine theme, with an optional answer timer of up to 995 seconds and a choice of short or long games.
descriptions.c64:164053: A side-scrolling shooter where the ship flies in either direction and must shoot down a quota of enemies per stage, using a radar to track them and matching their speed without colliding.
descriptions.c64:164054: Guide a cat through the dangers of everyday feline life, first crossing roads and pavements to fetch an important item while avoiding cars, foxes, people, light bulbs and potted plants.
descriptions.c64:164056: A spelling and grammar learning game with three levels, created by Mercer Mayer, following Tink as he wakes early in Tink Tonk land for a day of learning.
descriptions.c64:164057: Destroy enemy starships by planting bombs found on their hulls next to the nuclear reactors. Each placement requires cracking three locks by pressing fire while LOG ON is lit; a mistake gets you destroyed.
descriptions.c64:164058: A Pac-Man-style maze game with the fish Supercuda in the lead, chased by a new set of deep-sea predators on every screen and powered up by electric eels in place of power pills.
descriptions.c64:164059: Recreates Super Bowl XX, where Chicago beat New England 46-10, mixing play calling with action. Kick power and accuracy are set by timing the fire button, and the C64 version includes a computer opponent.
descriptions.c64:164061: Ride an eagle through the vast tomb of King Tut, past chambers of spears, enchanted saws and boulders, and then a hall full of the Devil's minions.
descriptions.c64:164086: Heading home after five years patrolling Province 4, a damaged ship is pulled into a black hole and the pilot must find a way back out.
descriptions.c64:164089: A multiple-choice trivia quiz across five categories, sports, music, science, TV and general knowledge, with an option to type in answers instead of picking them.
descriptions.c64:164090: Following Thundercross, Flight Commander McCoy is sent by Space Control 25 against 32 giant spacecraft in the stratosphere, flying alongside each one in his Advanced Flight Capsule and blasting everything on its hull.
descriptions.c64:164097: One or two players search seven sectors for Tarkus and Eugene's kidnapped friends, choosing any sector, where higher sectors hold more Wheelies to free and more enemies to shoot or dodge.
descriptions.c64:164099: A Donkey Kong-style platform game across four single screens: climb ladders and leap rolling barrels to rescue a girlfriend held at the top by a giant ape.
descriptions.c64:164102: Would-be agents pick their training missions from a set of corridors, tackling four arcade-style tests that include a sabotage job; pass all four to move up a level.
descriptions.c64:164103: Space shoot-out aboard the starship Interceptor: blast a meteor shower that knocks out shields and controls, spend repair units earned from destroyed meteors, then fight off attacking alien craft.
descriptions.c64:164105: The first expansion of questions for Trivial Pursuit, aimed at children and teenagers, adding 3,000 questions split into ages 7 to 12 and 12 and up, with categories such as People and Places.
descriptions.c64:164107: A space-faring take on Trivial Pursuit: each player pilots a ship around the galaxy, answering questions to win over Genus's Elders to their people's plan to colonize the planet.
descriptions.c64:164109: A Moon Patrol variant on the surface of Zon: drive a patrol wagon over obstacles and mines while fending off LasaSlamma tanks and missile-firing HeliChargers for as long as possible.
descriptions.c64:164145: Go-kart racing against a friend or the computer on an overhead split screen, with limited turbo boosts and track icons that repair damage and refill turbo.
descriptions.c64:164146: With Earth's silicon reserves running out, the mercenary Sillo travels to a distant part of the galaxy to harvest a new, highly explosive source.
descriptions.c64:164216: A Mahjongg variant where matching tiles can be removed only when they line up with no other tile between them, clearing a set number of each symbol to empty the board.
descriptions.c64:164223: A Polish platform game: clear radioactive items from a fortress by carrying them to a special container, using precise jumps and accurate shooting against mutated creatures and collecting extra lives and ammo.
descriptions.c64:164249: A naval simulation with action sequences set in 1995 as the Persian Gulf boils over between Iran, Iraq and the US: captain the US destroyer John Young and secure the region.
descriptions.c64:164250: Inmates Warmonger and Mandroid, the second player, try to break out of a maximum security prison orbiting Earth, fighting through waves of guards with a gun and a laser.
descriptions.c64:164257: A Snake variant in scrolling maze levels of narrow passages: Lenni the snake eats every fruit, growing longer with each one and turning by himself when he hits a wall.
descriptions.c64:164261: A single-screen shooter in which the Cyclonic Megawarz Uniship Mk1 rotates and thrusts, drifting to a stop, as it warps from planet to planet on the way to Earth, starting at Pluto.
descriptions.c64:164262: An updated Phoenix: move left and right at the bottom of a single screen shooting several waves of attackers, with a short-lived shield that must recharge between uses.
descriptions.c64:164265: Three card games in arcade form, played with a set number of credits: Poker Royal, a five-card draw where cards are held or discarded, Twenty One, and High Low.
descriptions.c64:164266: Erik the Viking must rescue his warrior queen from Death Island and loot its Main Fortress, starting on Stoney Island where he gathers gear and finds a way off while dealing with the unwelcoming locals.
descriptions.c64:164269: Wee Willie washes windows at an apartment block and has only so much water in his bucket and needs to remember which tenants want their windows cleaned and which do not.
descriptions.c64:164292: A curse called Shades has struck the island of Arulan, making people vanish and reappear elsewhere and bringing monsters and traps. A hero sets out to lift it and restore the island.
descriptions.c64:164302: Break into five buildings of increasing size and security, from a jewelry store, museum and bank to a research facility and an embassy, to find the loot while getting past security.
descriptions.c64:164310: Adaptation of the board game in which players guess a word or phrase from a sketch. Clues come from five categories, including a hard puzzle set and an All Play round; the guessing time is adjustable, and drawings are made with a simplified paint program that can be practised separately.
descriptions.c64:164349: Run an 8-bit era computer and software distribution business: buy machines and games, then deliver them to shops at a profit. Getting there means crossing platforms and traps, and stock dropped from rival trucks can be picked up along the way.
descriptions.c64:164372: A Lemmings-like puzzle where walkers stroll along paths between doorways. A single movable bridge must cover the gaps for several walkers heading in different directions at different speeds across multiple paths.
descriptions.c64:164373: A stock market trading simulation for up to four players. A share-trading quiz at the start sets each player's opening capital, after which shares and funds are bought and sold while market news shifts prices.
descriptions.c64:164418: Sequel to Psi Warrior. Sent by RadCom Corps into an old storehouse out in the nuclear wasteland, the warrior goes down ramp after ramp toward a Biocomputer believed dead that now gives off intense psychic activity.
descriptions.c64:164433: The official Mexico '86 football tie-in: run a World Cup from the quarter-finals with human or computer teams, playing 90-minute matches on a scrolling three-screen pitch where you steer the player nearest the ball, shoot with fire and dive with the keeper.
descriptions.c64:164434: An illustrated text adventure loosely inspired by The Frog King. Turned into a toad by the witch Hazel and trapped on her island, the hero must gather ingredients and brew them in her cauldron to regain human form.
descriptions.c64:164435: A naval wargame of the age of sail, in which frigates and ships of the line maneuver and exchange broadsides in battles involving the Spanish and British empires.
descriptions.c64:164436: Based on the TV puppets: the young Wombles head out onto the common to collect litter, with Great Uncle Bulgaria asking them to keep an eye out for a discarded copy of The Times.
descriptions.c64:164437: Sent by Global Weapons Inc to fix a generator fault, a troubleshooter finds the plant in meltdown, all 30 generators failing and its automated machines running wild. They must be switched off remotely, since going inside is too dangerous.
descriptions.c64:164440: Follow-up to Lode Runner with unchanged gameplay and 50 very hard levels aimed at experts. There is no level editor and stages must be cleared in sequence; progress can be saved, but each restore costs a life.
descriptions.c64:164454: A side-scrolling game in which Wallie floats above his wheel and both travel together across the ground, eating dots and three flashing dots for points on the way to the end of each level.
descriptions.c64:164455: The third Carmen Sandiego game: chase Carmen and her gang of thieves across 34 European countries, using the bundled Rand McNally Concise Atlas of Europe to follow the clues.
descriptions.c64:164467: Escort a clumsy, scatter-brained brother, newly hired as a research scientist, past hazards by whistling to direct him; the hero is a former student who spent university learning to whirl like a dervish.
descriptions.c64:164473: Defend 22nd-century Earth from the beings of Cirrus Major across 108 zones. Instead of conventional weapons, the defence relies on the energy beamed down by the giant solar platforms that power the planet.
descriptions.c64:164474: A no-frills tennis game for one or two players seen from behind the court with a slight 3D effect. Choose from three computer skill levels and matches of one, three or five sets; the shot played depends on the ball's height when struck, and full service rules apply.
descriptions.c64:164486: A single-screen shooter: steer a ship along the bottom of the screen and blast waves of aliens arriving from the top in changing formations as the levels progress.
descriptions.c64:164487: Fly over the planet Osmium in a constantly left-to-right scrolling shooter, destroying the Rexillian Blitztroopers or dodging them while steering clear of terrain obstacles across several levels.
descriptions.c64:164488: Lead a small strike force into Campuchia, where Lee Ho Fook enslaves the population in his Jade Mines, and destroy the super-tank he is building with parts smuggled in as oil refinery equipment.
descriptions.c64:164489: Based on the TV game show: a teammate sketches a common expression drawn literally, such as a light bulb over a head for 'bright idea', and the team has to work out what the picture means.
descriptions.c64:164521: Follow-up to Creator's Revenge. Roam a guarded fortress screen by screen from a top-down view, hunting for three keys that open the room holding a power source needed to reach the Creator's sealed chamber.
descriptions.c64:164526: Collect treasures on each screen while dodging monsters, then find the key that both opens the exit and grants spells such as fireballs and teleportation. Puzzle-solving and arcade action are mixed throughout.
descriptions.c64:164561: Known as Wizardry in Europe. A student magician, Drinn, faces his guild's final exam: recover the First Element from a perilous castle. Isometric action with puzzle elements, with rooms scrolling until a door is passed.
descriptions.c64:164566: A Scramble-style side-scrolling shooter; it is really Cave of Death from 1989, hacked and renamed by Eaglewing Software's Dennis van Marstricht and Richard de Groot.
descriptions.c64:164575: A typing tutor in game form: letters drift down on parachutes, and typing each one stops it before it lands.
descriptions.c64:164671: A single-player cricket management game. Pick one of seven national sides and take on the others in short, medium or long tours at home and abroad, covering one-day, three-day and full Test matches, all run through icon menus.
descriptions.c64:164673: A football management game: choose a squad, qualify and try to win the World Cup against 40 national teams, scheduling friendlies, coping with injuries and bringing young players through.
descriptions.c64:164674: A football management game with 240 club sides from 15 countries. The manager's career can move between clubs around the world while chasing league and cup success.
descriptions.c64:164707: Shoot advancing robots while dodging the bombs they leave behind and collecting rubies. The robots never fire, but touching one still costs a life, and levels grow harder as they go.
descriptions.c64:164710: A Polish adventure about escaping an island by applying items at the proper spots or handing them to the right characters. Inventory is unlimited and items cannot be misused; the screen splits into a location view and an information panel.
descriptions.c64:164712: A fast arcade shooter from the Arcade Games II pack, fending off attacking Centripods while Dactoes fall and Caruths hop across the screen.
descriptions.c64:164714: A Qix-style game: draw force fields to box in Kwixx, an energy creature bouncing destructively around the screen, and claim at least 75% of the area by joining lines to the edge or to existing fields.
descriptions.c64:164729: A computerised Scrabble board where the host, Monty, joins in as an extra computer player. Players draw letter tiles, form words from a rack of seven and can pass a turn when no word fits.
descriptions.c64:164741: Pong in three dimensions: move a bat both horizontally and vertically to return a ball flying toward it, with a split-screen display giving two different views of the court.
descriptions.c64:16476: Tom-Tom, now called Wonder Boy, returns to a Wonder Land overrun by monsters. A side-scrolling action game with role-playing touches, where gold from defeated enemies buys weapons, armour and magic in shops.
descriptions.c64:164765: Fly over the five worlds of Alpha Centauri shooting waves of aliens. Giant letters on the ground can be shot to release power-ups such as extra speed, smart bombs and extra lives.
descriptions.c64:164767: Steer Zoomer, a Pac-Man-like figure with arms and legs, around a grid tracing the edges of squares to light them up. Completing a square scores points, and a level ends once every square is lit.
descriptions.c64:164810: A speeded-up Paradroid with improved scrolling code, released only in a double pack with Uridium Plus.
descriptions.c64:164880: A public domain clone of Son of Blagger: software companies have caught all the crackers, and rescuing them means finding six keys while avoiding flowers and mines. Each key collected awards a bonus.
descriptions.c64:165016: A homebrew port of Super Mario Bros., made over almost seven years. Run and jump through the Mushroom Kingdom to free the Princess from the Koopa turtles.
descriptions.c64:165108: A text adventure set after a war in which the Orcs' Dark Lord was killed and his armies scattered. One roaming Orc band raided a monastery and carried off religious treasures, the legendary Golden Chalice among them.
descriptions.c64:165202: A mutant human able to fire energy bolts in eight directions battles the Robotrons, humanity's own creation, room by room. Movement and shooting are controlled separately, also in eight directions.
descriptions.c64:165230: Air hockey for two players only: each controls a paddle on their side of the table, knocking the puck toward the opponent's goal. A toss-up decides who starts each game.
descriptions.c64:165237: Build a party of three Warriors or Wizards, buy equipment, then explore a 3D wireframe labyrinth, fighting monsters and gaining experience on the way to a final showdown with the Balrog.
descriptions.c64:165253: A warrior king who wanted peace is betrayed by his generals and cursed by their wizard, his body twisted into a beast and his soul stolen, then sealed in a tomb from which he must escape.
descriptions.c64:165557: A Sierra graphic adventure starring Ulysses, ordered by the king to find the Golden Fleece. Starting in a small town, he sails to distant lands guarded by the gods and meets figures from Greek mythology.
descriptions.c64:165608: Protect the power rail on which the home planet depends from alien invaders, flying a ship left and right at varying speeds in a horizontally scrolling shooter with a crosshair sight.
descriptions.c64:165670: A puzzle quiz for one or two players: each round shows eight names, places or objects with a common link, and the two to six items that don't belong must be removed before time runs out.
descriptions.c64:165681: Play a tadpole in a realistically depicted pond, trying to grow a frog colony while surviving its many natural hazards.
descriptions.c64:165754: Home from a long sea voyage, Ninja Hamster finds his village terrorised by a gang under Sinister Rat and the reptilian Lizard of Death. A one-on-one fighting game against six gang members and then the two bosses.
descriptions.c64:165773: An expanded 64K remake of the 2014 P0 Snake, with 30 levels and one-button control: the snake turns clockwise by default and holding fire turns it the other way.
descriptions.c64:165774: A Sierra graphic adventure set in Serenia, where a wandering traveller hears the town crier read the King's proclamation and takes on the quest to rescue his daughter from a wizard.
descriptions.c64:166022: Fly F-15 missions over Southeast Asia, Europe and the Mideast, dogfighting enemy aircraft and bombing ground targets with modern electronic warfare equipment.
descriptions.c64:166089: A set of three gambling games, among them Pontoon, the British relative of blackjack that uses twist, stick and buy instead of hit, stand and double.
descriptions.c64:166107: A graphical roguelike: create a hero by entering a name and picking one of five classes, then explore the Valley, fighting monsters in semi-real-time combat and collecting treasure.
descriptions.c64:166109: Three-a-side street football with teams picked from neighbourhood kids, each with his own skill. The offence gets four downs to gain ten yards by passing or running, with a quarterback and two receivers.
descriptions.c64:166117: Help Micro Mouse defend his programs inside a computer: collect letters from cages in the four corners to fill gaps in a BASIC listing at the screen's centre while dodging software bugs.
descriptions.c64:166118: Pilot a hot air balloon between bases in a horizontally scrolling game, avoiding clouds, trees, kites, birds and rock-throwing people. Climbing burns fuel, and both fuel and sandbags are scarcer at higher difficulty levels (0-5).
descriptions.c64:166174: As Oscar, enter the clifftop research station of The Brotherhood, who have raised The Master and his minions, and put an end to the vampire and his blood-drinking servants.
descriptions.c64:166227: Drive a speedboat towing a waterskier around a buoyed course for six laps, avoiding mines and ramps with the boat and keeping both boat and skier inside the markers.
descriptions.c64:166228: Aliens have overrun the Regulus system and taken hostages. A vertically scrolling shooter in five levels: break through the outer defences, then fight across jungle, ice and desert planets toward the alien stronghold.
descriptions.c64:166247: A party-based fantasy role-playing game in a medieval land where a mysterious addictive drug is spreading. The heroes trace it to a single source run by an enigmatic stranger and set out to stop him.
descriptions.c64:166250: A short adventure from Adventure Pack 1: a meteor is hurtling toward the moon base, and unless it is destroyed every lunar colony will be wiped out.
descriptions.c64:166373: Sammy Lightfoot leaps over obstacles, bounces on trampolines and swings on ropes to climb to the top of each screen without falling into gaps. After three levels the cycle repeats at a higher difficulty.
descriptions.c64:166374: Zenos, a woman starpilot passed over for the Ace Starpilot post of Zigmundia, steals the retired ace's Tesscan starfighter to show the federation its supposedly unbeatable defence system can be broken.
descriptions.c64:166401: Ship-versus-ship space combat between the Alliance of Free Stars and the Ur-Quan Hierarchy, where each side fields its own warship types, every vessel with distinct weapons and abilities.
descriptions.c64:166402: Released as Sun Star in Europe. Fly a solar energy collector around 16 grids in space from a first-person view with a radar below, gathering ten energy crystals on each grid.
descriptions.c64:166419: An Infocom murder mystery: as a reporter framed for a killing at a costume party, find evidence of innocence before the police close in, while the real killer watches.
descriptions.c64:166420: An Infocom detective story set near Los Angeles on a stormy February night in 1938. A wealthy, frightened man asks for police protection, a death follows anyway, and the detective has only twelve hours to crack the case and make an arrest.
descriptions.c64:166423: A homebrew remake of Mine Storm from the Vectrex, which was itself modelled on Atari's Asteroids: pilot a ship and shoot drifting space mines.
descriptions.c64:166432: Infocom's sequel to Planetfall. The hero, promoted to Lieutenant First Class in the Stellar Patrol and buried in paperwork, is sent on a routine errand to a space station that turns out to be strangely deserted.
descriptions.c64:166449: Find hidden words in a grid of letters against the clock, with several difficulty levels and over forty themes. Part of The Complete Home Entertainment Centre.
descriptions.c64:166489: A diary program for 1989 that shows the date and time along with facts about each day, plus extras such as weather, a horoscope and a daily snack recipe.
descriptions.c64:166540: The Creator has raised an army of robots and insects and is bombing the world's great cities. Drive a tank against his forces and stop each bomb before it lands; followed by Labyrinth of the Creator.
descriptions.c64:166558: Isometric single-screen puzzle in which Dexter, Merlin's assistant, hops over a set of cubes. Pressing fire flips the colour of the cube he stands on and its neighbours, and every red cube must be made yellow.
descriptions.c64:166562: Ski downhill past odd hazards such as rabbits and snowmobiles that cut across the slope; after a crash, a dog comes to the rescue. Included in the Cymbal Software compilation 3 Arcade Games - Book 2.
descriptions.c64:166611: A Snake variant by Shaun Southern with extra obstacles, including animated mechanical devices such as robots. Released on the Triple Decker 8 compilation from Alternative Software.
descriptions.c64:166707: Waddingtons' version of Monopoly with the full board game rules and the London street names. Up to six human or computer players buy property, build houses and hotels and try to bankrupt each other.
descriptions.c64:166846: Two programs in one: a multi-directional scrolling shooter, and a game creator that uses the shooter as a base for making new games. The game is in English, while the creator is in German.
descriptions.c64:166852: From the author of Space Taxi, a three-part ambulance rescue game. First drive through a maze of city houses to a burning building without hitting houses or other vehicles, racing a timer that counts down from 1000.
descriptions.c64:166923: Licensed from the kids' TV show Round the Bend, set in a comic factory. Doc Croc has destroyed the press, so Lou Brush has to travel the sewers to recover all eight missing pages.
descriptions.c64:166945: A tiny early text adventure from On-Line Systems: an astronaut must launch a rocket to destroy an asteroid heading for Earth, but first needs to obtain the flight plan. Commands are one or two words.
descriptions.c64:167048: Rescue Maid Marian from the Sheriff of Nottingham's castle, crossing several screens with different objectives, starting with a trek through Sherwood Forest full of henchmen, and take gold for the poor along the way.
descriptions.c64:167053: A variant of Go on a hexagonal board of 21 lines forming triangles, with 55 points for stones. Up to four players take turns placing stones and try to capture each other's.
descriptions.c64:167366: Fly a small, advanced fighter escorting a massive bomber on its way to wipe out the hostile navy in the Persian Gulf. The fighter can create false radar images to stay hidden and keep the bomber unharmed.
descriptions.c64:167471: Bounce laser beams off mirrors and deflectors to hit target points, an idea that predates Deflektor by four years. Part of Commodore's Fantasy Five collection.
descriptions.c64:167474: A simulation of English billiards for two players, using two cue balls, one for each player, and a single object ball.
descriptions.c64:167489: A hacked version of Krakout by Met with tougher levels and faster play.
descriptions.c64:167497: An educational game for children: plan the cheapest, shortest pipe network to connect a neighbourhood's houses to the water supply, choosing pipe types and placement on a tight budget. The number of houses is selectable.
descriptions.c64:167538: Geologists at a research base are being abducted by aliens. A single-screen shooter: slide a craft along the bottom of the screen, firing upward at waves of aliens while trying to save the scientists.
descriptions.c64:167556: An educational package based on the cartoon The Shoe People, with a simple paint program and five mini-games such as Trampy Visits His Friends, where objects he trips over must be named by typing.
descriptions.c64:167594: Guide a mouse around platforms, clouds, moving ledges and ladders collecting cheese, cakes and balloons, jumping flowers and dodging bouncing balls and dinosaurs, any of which costs a life on contact.
descriptions.c64:167689: A graphic adventure based on the 1980s TV series. As Super Gran, track down Scunner Campbell, who has stolen valuables from Chisleton's museum and Town Hall, and recover them.
descriptions.c64:167816: A Boulder Dash clone squeezed into 1024 bytes: collect enough diamonds to open the exit while avoiding falling boulders and fireflies. The author says it contains 1024 levels.
descriptions.c64:167863: A phrase-guessing game modelled on Wheel of Fortune: spin a carnival wheel to set the cash prize and solve Hangman-like word puzzles. Part of Keypunch's Club Casino pack.
descriptions.c64:168010: Collects all three Ket adventures: Mountains of Ket, then Temple of Vran, then The Final Mission. Interactive fiction with role-playing elements where prowess, energy and luck develop, items are bought from merchants or found, and combat occurs.
descriptions.c64:168087: A collection of new Kikstart motorbike courses built with the Kikstart Construction Set by Nitro and The Illusion.
descriptions.c64:168089: A conversion of the C16 Kikstart, the motorbike stunt game: steer the rider quickly and carefully over obstacle courses, alone against the clock.
descriptions.c64:168116: A platformer set inside the mountain of the spiders: collect the keys while keeping away from the arachnids.
descriptions.c64:168117: Based on the Greek legend: Icarus flies on wings of feathers and wax in search of his father Daedalus, crossing the Greek countryside while dodging the evil Roc and giant bees.
descriptions.c64:168187: An educational reasoning program for upper-elementary pupils and older: uncover the king's hidden rules by forming hypotheses, testing them and weighing alternative explanations for the patterns observed.
descriptions.c64:168320: Compete as a contestant on the TV quiz The Krypton Factor, facing rounds testing different mental skills; in Observation, a story and picture are shown again with subtle changes that must be identified.
descriptions.c64:168355: A licensed squash game for one or two players with four difficulty levels and realistic rebounds, with Jonah Barrington calling the score.
descriptions.c64:168554: Based on François Bourgeon's comic series and closely following its plot. On the eve of the French Revolution, Hoel and Isa end up in Brittany and journey from Europe to the African coast, facing many dangers.
descriptions.c64:168557: A graphical adventure by Australian writer Daryll Reynolds that mixes PETSCII and custom characters with animated sprites and sound. It begins with a delirious explorer staggering out of the jungle raving about King Solomon's mines.
descriptions.c64:168568: An educational treasure hunt for children covering reading, map skills and decision making. Collect clues to rescue King Olin of Myrrh from the sorcerer Vargor, with Anara the wise woman as guide.
descriptions.c64:168571: Alien hatcheries drift toward Earth, their eggs cracking open to release monsters. As the lone fighter pilot, smash every egg as it hatches so that no creature escapes.
descriptions.c64:168572: Pilot a laser-armed spaceship and destroy enough enemy craft to move on to the next, tougher level. Touching an enemy costs a life.
descriptions.c64:168586: Adventure based on a legend: the knight Tristan must rescue Isolde from the castle of the wicked Baron Wumper of Wummerstein, where magic shoes let him fly.
descriptions.c64:168602: Alf Yngve's SEUCK shoot-'em-up casts you as a UNICEF aid worker, equipped with a rifle and bulletproof vest, who went missing for five years while vaccinating isolated tribes deep in South America's rain forest.
descriptions.c64:168603: Psytronik collection of Alf Yngve's Last Amazon shoot 'em ups: enhanced versions of parts one and two with weapon power-ups, a sideways-scrolling Special Edition remix, and Richard Bayliss's bonus game Amazon Tales.
descriptions.c64:168615: A platform game set in rat-infested sewers, where the hero must cut down the rat population while avoiding a furious monster that is fond of the rodents.
descriptions.c64:168700: Penniless in the Skintsville Saloon, Luke Warme hears an Indian chief has died and been buried with his gold. He drives his wagon off in search of the grave to see whether the legend is true.
descriptions.c64:168774: A text adventure in a castle and its grounds, full of monsters, mazes and magic items. The right objects must be gathered before facing Fordel, the Leopard Lord, with no second chance. Written by a science fiction author for Kayde.
descriptions.c64:168785: A menu-driven strategy game of the Punic Wars between Rome and Carthage, concentrating on naval battles, including the Roman boarding tactics that used their strong infantry against ramming ships.
descriptions.c64:168798: A karate tournament against six qualified opponents, closely modelled on Karate Kid II. Released in Italy as Scontro Finale and as Ito Joshi.
descriptions.c64:168799: Enter the Colosseum as a gladiator or gladiatrix. Each level begins with picking up a weapon, then strange creatures come into the arena singly and must be killed.
descriptions.c64:168827: Rebels set out to destroy Lincoln, a supercomputer ruling the universe that demands women as sacrifices. Its stages cover hopping hidden capsules between planets on transport ships, sniping defence systems so they can land, freeing the captives with a flute-playing creature, and infiltrating the city to plant nine viruses.
descriptions.c64:168829: A strategy game about Operation Deadstick in the early hours of D-Day, when British 6th Airborne troops landed by glider at night to seize the bridges over the Caen Canal and the Orne.
descriptions.c64:168835: Command the Enterprise through ten levels of multiple rounds, fighting Klingon fighters and other threats, before a final confrontation with NOMAD to save the Federation.
descriptions.c64:168890: An educational logic game: get Buddy or Betty down through a five-floor building from the roof to the ground by flying a bird that sets down bridges, springs, walls and ladders on the route.
descriptions.c64:168893: Trivia combined with bowling for one or two players: each little person bowls on a six-pin lane, with two balls per frame over ten frames.
descriptions.c64:168894: Railroad switching strategy on a small layout with a main line, six switches and seven places to load cars, in either a Flat Yard or a Hump Yard version, with detailed simulation of car movement.
descriptions.c64:168895: Direct the Magic Hand to place walls, bridges and springs in a maze so that a rolling ball hits as many prizes as possible.
descriptions.c64:168896: The last survivor of a company rides into hostile desert territory and enters an Indian camp's cave to free comrades taken prisoner.
descriptions.c64:168897: Steer a constantly swaying balloon, fighting gravity, along a path from its start point to a landing pad, picking up every object on the screen first. Each level is a single side-view screen.
descriptions.c64:168916: An illustrated text adventure: an explorer in the South American jungle searches a lost Mayan city for ten valuable relics hidden in its buildings and temples, among traps and red herrings.
descriptions.c64:168917: A top-down maze: find staircases to climb through the labyrinth's levels and reach the exit. Bumping into a creature switches to a close-up battle that must be won.
descriptions.c64:168920: A Uridium-style space shooter: command a powerful ship patrolling sectors held by alien fleets, each sector closer to the fleet's core and harder. Released in Italy as Planet Six.
descriptions.c64:168922: Pilot a small glider through a sprawling underground labyrinth of hell, picking up energy symbols, recharging at refuelling pads, braving teleporters, timed energy barriers and magnetic fields, and hunting hidden keys that open locked gates.
descriptions.c64:168961: Spin-off of the ITV series Magic Micro Mission. The first part is a cockpit shooter in which a crosshair is lined up on flying saucers sweeping across the screen on elliptical paths.
descriptions.c64:168992: Two basketball games in one: a realistic version with a saveable league for one or two players, and a faster game with Flow-Control for easier shooting. Shot clock, match length and team kits are adjustable, with three skill levels.
descriptions.c64:169002: A kit for hosting a murder mystery party, the parlour game where guests play characters, receive clues in turns and try to work out the culprit.
descriptions.c64:169005: Secret agent Uri Kurchatovium must find and eliminate a C.R.O.W. agent whose formula would turn Americans into zombies, but the adventure begins after his lemonade is drugged at Zazas.
descriptions.c64:169006: Guide Manchester United through the European club competitions, either playing the matches directly or picking the team and letting the computer decide the result. Sequel to Krisalis' Manchester United.
descriptions.c64:169017: A side-view fighting game defending the land from the forces of Sanjo, with special weapons such as blinding powder, throwing stars and katanas, and a practice mode beforehand. Paragon's first commercial release.
descriptions.c64:169020: A mystical knight able to vanish into walls and pass through doors evades tracker robots that pursue him relentlessly, in a mix of skill and strategy.
descriptions.c64:169050: A maze game with platform and shooting sections, played as a series of mini-games, in which an agent recovers stolen top secret papers.
descriptions.c64:169061: An educational history quiz: Earth's past has been erased, and a time-machine pilot moves across a 3D field locating time holograms to record historical events.
descriptions.c64:169064: A typing tutor set in space: the MasterType wizard defends a command ship in the middle of the screen from missiles launched from the four corners, each destroyed by typing the word or letters attached to it.
descriptions.c64:169072: Mathematics combined with racing: steer a formula car from above through a network of forks, where each branch's sign applies an arithmetic operation to the mileage, aiming for the target in the best route.
descriptions.c64:169073: Goofy climbs the Matterhorn in a side-scrolling jumping game, scaling ropes and leaping to ledges, empty bobsleds and gondolas, and hopping over goats and snowmen; icicles and crumbling ledges appear at higher levels.
descriptions.c64:169080: Golf from overhead: aim by placing the golfer's stance around the ball, then pick a club, one of five shot strengths from light to strong, and the amount of curve, with wind and terrain affecting the result.
descriptions.c64:169082: Find the treasure in a randomly generated, edgeless maze of about 100 locations and carry it back to the start. Prisoners give directions, food and swords help, and the maze is roamed by Maziacs.
descriptions.c64:169177: A short illustrated text adventure for children: on Christmas Eve at the North Pole, solve simple puzzles so Santa can finish his preparations and get the presents delivered in time.
descriptions.c64:169179: Three Metallamas are all that stand between the Zzyaxians and outpost OP/37 on the galaxy's rim, which the invaders want as a launching point for their attack.
descriptions.c64:169183: Solid Snake infiltrates Outer Heaven, a fortified nation led by a secretive war hero, to stop Metal Gear, a nuclear-armed walking tank. A top-down stealth action game where avoiding guards matters as much as fighting.
descriptions.c64:169203: Four single-screen stages inside the Creator's fortress. On the first, reach the exit at the top while robots roam and leave impassable walls behind them; the goal is to destroy the Creator and his robots.
descriptions.c64:169260: Baseball management with real stats for pitching, hitting, fielding and running. Manage famous teams from past and present, with a Quick-Play option menu.
descriptions.c64:169263: Coach an American football team: choose home and visiting sides, each human or computer, adjust rosters, then call plays and pass patterns during the game.
descriptions.c64:169378: Jet combat over MiG Alley in the Korean War, where F-86 Sabres battled Soviet MiG-15s near the Chinese border in the first large jet-versus-jet air battles.
descriptions.c64:169404: A Centipede-style shooter: move a ship left, right and a short distance up and down at the bottom of the screen, firing at a Millibug that splits apart each time it is hit.
descriptions.c64:169410: Software by Timothy Leary for mapping thoughts on a scope, comparing them with others and role-playing, usable as a party game along the lines of Scruples.
descriptions.c64:169412: A trivia game for one to four players on various subjects, with three modes: race to a points target, score as much as possible against the clock, or play on a board moving by dice rolls.
descriptions.c64:169445: An abstract sliding-block puzzle with 999,999 levels: use a crosshair to rearrange up to 24 dice-like spotted blocks, stacked in columns of up to four, so each column matches its number.
descriptions.c64:169621: A Centipede-inspired shooter in a summer garden: blast the mutant mushroom monster Minipede to clear each of 15 levels, and shoot spiders, snails and ladybirds for extra score.
descriptions.c64:169647: Follow-up to Mission 1: Project Volcano, a mostly text adventure with some pictures. A Soviet spy has got inside a nuclear complex on Gibraltar; enter the secure zone, learn what the Blue Room hides and remove the agent.
descriptions.c64:169680: Fly an Eagle craft low over the lunar surface to protect moon bases from enemy time bombs, grabbing them quickly and dumping them in the fusion disposal site before they explode.
descriptions.c64:169692: An experimental piece by Jaron Lanier in which a spacewalker and six bouncing spaceships drift across the screen, and the player's movements both steer the action and generate the music.
descriptions.c64:169731: Rescue Princess Lalena from the Dark Lord across four levels of flick-screen platforming, armed with a sword against creatures that sap energy on contact.
descriptions.c64:169733: Drive and fly the transforming car Morphicle to find and defuse a bomb that threatens the world. Each level has three parts, starting with a road drive in search of an underground compound's entrance.
descriptions.c64:169734: MOT, a three-metre monster with horns and a tail who roams time and space at will, has taken to hiding in the hero's cupboard and wrecking the furniture around the house.
descriptions.c64:169742: Motocross racing through three timed scenes with different viewpoints, starting with a desert stage seen from behind the bike, where rocks, cacti and scorpions must be avoided.
descriptions.c64:169747: Manage a motorcycle racing team in Grand Prix world championship seasons, choosing the team and main sponsor and aiming for both the riders' title and the Constructors' Championship.
descriptions.c64:169748: An illustrated text adventure about a motorcycle rally that starts and ends at Ariel Castle, where the rider searches the countryside for the Award, using found objects and equipment in the right places.
descriptions.c64:169749: A tricky text adventure that starts on a mountain ledge beside the entrance to a lost palace in a mythical land, rumoured to hold great riches and full of odd surprises.
descriptions.c64:169809: A musical movie-making kit: pick locations such as the city, the jungle or outer space, cast the three Jazz Scats (Mr. Bassman, Wahoo and Swivel Hips) and compose the score for each film.
descriptions.c64:169810: Move a snowman around single-screen platforms collecting snowballs against the clock to build three giant snowmen while dodging killer penguins.
descriptions.c64:169814: Mr Wino, stuck in a drunken nightmare, must pick up every bottle on each multi-screen level to lift the barrier blocking the way out; some bottles also open doors on the way. A flick-screen platformer.
descriptions.c64:169815: A Mr. Do! variant: guide a wizard around a garden eating cherries and dodging gremlins, defeating them with a thrown crystal ball or by dropping apples on them.
descriptions.c64:169816: Mrs. Mop must clean a terrible school section by section while pupils, teachers and dogs attack her. Her back worsens as she works, and when it gives out she is off for a week, though she has weapons to fight back.
descriptions.c64:169817: Based on MTV's game show: three human or computer contestants answer questions about TV, films and their stars over two board rounds, followed by a rapid-fire final round.
descriptions.c64:169818: Football management for up to four players over four divisions of 16 clubs, each with squads of up to 16; every manager starts at a randomly assigned Division 4 club.
descriptions.c64:169820: A menu-driven detective game aboard the French liner Bourgogne in 1938, where wealthy passengers and spies after new computer technology mix, and two murders must be solved.
descriptions.c64:169824: A Centipede-inspired shooter: after overnight rain, mushrooms have sprung up in the garden and insects are moving in, so move along and slightly up and down the bottom of the screen shooting them.
descriptions.c64:170877: A farmer arrives at his field one morning to find every sheep gone, and has to track them all down in this typed-command text adventure.
descriptions.c64:170879: A short Magnetic Scrolls text adventure set in ancient Greece: as Poseidon, journey into the Underworld to obtain the Dark Helmet of Hades.
descriptions.c64:170907: The first computer game based on C.S. Lewis's first Narnia novel, packaged with the book, game cards and dice used in play. The witch has put Narnia under ice and dispatched wicked dwarves to stop the player.
descriptions.c64:170908: A Dutch game in which a scuba diver collects every key on a level before escaping.
descriptions.c64:170909: A strategic and tactical simulation of the 1942 Guadalcanal naval battle, commanding the US Navy's task force, its aircraft squadrons and ships against the Japanese.
descriptions.c64:170920: Command a naval cruiser in the Persian Gulf on one of three missions (escorting a convoy, patrolling, or Dawn of Death), protecting shipping and destroying hostile forces.
descriptions.c64:170931: A statistics-driven basketball simulation with animated play, coaching pro teams based on player data from the bundled 1985-86 season disk.
descriptions.c64:170935: As Illuminar the wizard, fight the necromancer Tetragorn and his spiders, ogres and Hammerfists across three stages, steering a long-range Wisp from the centre of the screen.
descriptions.c64:171041: Cross a park from top to bottom through a simple maze, viewed from above; points along the way trigger random single-screen mini-games.
descriptions.c64:171050: An icon-driven adventure with pointers and drop-down menus, 110 locations, animated graphics, over 35 objects to examine, interactive characters and built-in arcade sequences, centred on an inhuman killer.
descriptions.c64:171069: Strategy with light role-playing and trading: the old king's son must find five magic rings to defeat the sorceress Medusa, who has seized the kingdom.
descriptions.c64:171094: Terrorists have taken hostages on a North Sea oil platform and hidden a nuclear bomb. A special agent has 30 minutes and several weapons to free the captives and disarm it.
descriptions.c64:171129: An enhanced version of Not Even Human: two players each control a squad of eight small aliens, switching between them one at a time, in quick battles across single-screen arenas.
descriptions.c64:171147: MASTA, the NORAD supercomputer, has taken over the nuclear defence system and is about to start a global war; only the absent-minded, recently fired Dr. Norton sees the danger.
descriptions.c64:171296: A 3D space shooter with three-axis control: a split screen shows the instrument panel and the view of space while invading ships are destroyed and their fire avoided.
descriptions.c64:171297: An Epyx turn-based strategy game for up to eight players, played with a physical board and 200 pieces: survey terrain from arctic to desert, pick drilling sites and strike oil to build the largest fortune.
descriptions.c64:171318: Move a crosshair around single-screen levels to shoot abstract-shaped Oisac soldiers that appear in the centre and head for the edges before they escape.
descriptions.c64:171320: Fly a UFO armed with lasers for approaching aircraft and bombs for ground targets, levelling enough buildings and ground defences to advance without losing a life.
descriptions.c64:171382: A one-day international cricket tournament between Australia, England, New Zealand and the West Indies, played under floodlights at the M.C.G., batting to keep up the run rate.
descriptions.c64:171383: Captured after crash-landing on the alien world Oo-Topos with valuable cargo bound for Earth, escape from prison, recover the cargo and patch up the ship to leave. Interactive fiction with optional graphics.
descriptions.c64:171384: A spelling game: each everyday word spelled correctly opens Ali Baba's treasure cave door a little further, while mistakes bring the forty thieves leaping out.
descriptions.c64:171386: A text adventure about a chorus singer suddenly lifted out of obscurity to sing at the Palace Theatre, where the National Opera Company is based, whose dream of stardom gets complicated soon after arrival.
descriptions.c64:171387: A text adventure: the expedition camp lies in ruins, Lord Townsend is dead, and the only other person who knows the radio frequency for rescue, Kate Mallender, has been carried off by the QA tribesmen.
descriptions.c64:171392: In 1942, captain a lone submarine near an Allied Mediterranean landing site and sink as many enemy ships and shoot down as many planes as possible before they can strike the invasion convoy.
descriptions.c64:171415: Based on the CITV puppet show: Cheep helps Orm organise his birthday party in three parts, with a reaction test at the start setting the difficulty.
descriptions.c64:171417: Four mini-games starring the CITV puppets Orm the worm and Cheep the bird: three single-screen side-view stages and a final vertically scrolling one.
descriptions.c64:171428: A flick-screen platformer based on Jack and the Beanstalk: climb the beanstalk, hop across clouds and search the Giant's 23-screen castle for the golden harp, golden egg and bag of gold.
descriptions.c64:171430: Hop Alex from cube to cube to colour every one while dodging gumdrops, Grody the Witch, Buzzbat, Eraser Rabbit and Croak the Frog; ride a cloud to melt the witch with rain or hit Buzzbat with lightning.
descriptions.c64:171433: Educational arithmetic with Paddington Bear: help him through a muddled shopping trip from 32 Windsor Gardens by working out simple sums.
descriptions.c64:171434: A Paddington Bear storybook-and-cassette pack for young children: left in charge of Mr Gruber's antique shop for the morning, Paddington drops one of the pictures, which turns out to be a mosaic.
descriptions.c64:171447: A paddle-controlled game that placed third in the 2011 16KB cartridge competition: keep Redhead alive in his cave by catching falling water droplets and fireballs.
descriptions.c64:171448: As Agent X, walk forward along the roofs of 14 carriages, one per screen, to reach the engine and halt a runaway train before the enemy gets hold of it, all against the clock.
descriptions.c64:171461: Tactical WWII simulation of small unit combat on the Eastern Front, in North Africa and in Western Front campaigns without US forces, with over 250 weapon types modelled.
descriptions.c64:171465: Command 25 armoured and infantry platoons on the WWII Eastern Front, advancing across randomly generated maps full of ambush points; survivors carry over to the next encounter.
descriptions.c64:171466: A solitaire strategic simulation of Germany's 1941 invasion of the Soviet Union: direct the whole Axis force and take objectives within 24 weeks while destroying the Soviet army.
descriptions.c64:171474: Swim Parky through underwater rooms gathering gold tokens against the clock, avoiding sea creatures such as crabs, jellyfish, clams and stingrays; several rooms have multiple exits, so routes vary.
descriptions.c64:171498: A single-screen shooter: Heinz 'Hurricane' Solo uses a Sauce Squirter with limited Pasta Powda to stop the Pasta Pinchas carrying off six ravioli tins. The ship rotates freely and drifts on when thrust is released.
descriptions.c64:171500: A first-person space shooter from the cockpit of the last scout ship in a squadron after an alien attack, with twin forward lasers and limited shields against waves of enemy fighters.
descriptions.c64:171506: A puzzle game in which a bulldozer driver pushes lemons into rows next to each other to complete each level.
descriptions.c64:171508: Leppard, a diamond-collecting robot, must gather twenty diamonds in a labyrinth to reach the next level while four hostile pursuers try to touch him.
descriptions.c64:171512: A Bomberman-style game: bomb every target and ghost to clear a level. While any target remains, each destroyed ghost is replaced by another, returning ghosts are tougher, and a timer runs throughout.
descriptions.c64:171513: A sequel to the 1988 shooter Lethal by the same team, now playing like Bounder but with horizontal scrolling.
descriptions.c64:171514: A German R-Type-style horizontal shooter: fly a spaceship blasting enemy craft and obstacles while dodging enemy fire and the cave surfaces.
descriptions.c64:171516: Guide gyrocopters through caves, avoiding blocks, falling weights, walls and trolley cars; any collision costs one of six lives and restarts the cave. Released in Italy as Sea Chopper.
descriptions.c64:171520: A small text adventure with a verb-noun parser where the first puzzle is working out whether the vessel you escaped was a spaceship or a cruise liner.
descriptions.c64:171529: In 2197, alien infiltration has wiped out all life on Platar. Starting aboard the mother ship beside a teleporter to the base Amigar, find the aliens and destroy them if they prove hostile.
descriptions.c64:171536: A Children's Television Workshop thinking game: build and control energy networks, experiment with how they behave and guide the Light-riders to the source.
descriptions.c64:171537: A side-scrolling space shooter much like Armalyte: fight through maze-like territory against waves and lone enemies, picking up weapon-boosting tokens that lie in the open.
descriptions.c64:171538: A text adventure starring a robot that wakes in a refuelling sphere after a power failure, with no memory beyond that and no visible way out.
