descriptions.c64:171539: Guide a little figure around collecting puzzle pieces; touching anything else is fatal.
descriptions.c64:171542: Light every tile on 24 single-screen grids; stepping on a lit tile switches it off again, which some levels require to be exploited by doubling back.
descriptions.c64:171543: An unreleased platformer by Fairlight with two levels themed on LEGO Town and Classic Space. A preview appeared in 1992 between the scenes of Fairlight's LEGOLAND 2 demo.
descriptions.c64:171544: A scrolling platformer: jump through the level collecting stars while avoiding Owlbats, a bee, saucers and other monsters.
descriptions.c64:171553: An arch-enemy has trapped the hero in a maze of twisting passages to make him miss a dream job appointment; unlock the doors with the keys found inside and get out in time.
descriptions.c64:171585: A text adventure navigated by choosing from offered answers: as a Texas ranger, put on a mask and bring the villains to justice.
descriptions.c64:171586: A word game for up to four players on a diamond-shaped grid of 109 letters. From their own side, players take turns forming words by moving horizontally, vertically or diagonally within a time limit.
descriptions.c64:171589: A tactical naval simulation of World War II in the South Pacific for one or two players, commanding American or Japanese forces, with a computer opponent for solo play.
descriptions.c64:171590: Two educational games: Old MacDonald's Farm, with Memory, Observation and Reflections sections featuring farm animals, and SORT, the Space Observer Recruitment Test.
descriptions.c64:171595: Text adventure in the land of Golconda, where you earn karma through good deeds, offerings and prayer to reach Heaven; the map shifts between games, characters follow you around, and dying means rebirth on a mountain with your belongings scattered.
descriptions.c64:171601: A text-only adventure about a poor gambler deep in debt to Luigi of the New Jersey mob, looking for the one way out that doesn't end in pain or an early grave.
descriptions.c64:171603: Guided by the ghost of Backpack Sam, search Arizona's Superstition Mountains for the legendary Lost Dutchman's Gold Mine.
descriptions.c64:171606: A multi-screen platform shooter: a lonely robot lost in a strange world searches for the way home, fending off attackers.
descriptions.c64:171607: Escape an ancient pyramid room by room, collecting treasures, dodging traps and fighting enemies such as scorpions.
descriptions.c64:171608: Based on Conan Doyle's novel: as reporter Edward Malone, reach the plateau where his friend Maple White discovered a lost world, find out how he died and explore it.
descriptions.c64:171610: A two-player game of forfeits and rewards with over 13,000 possible combinations.
descriptions.c64:171611: A quiz-format party game for as many as 18 players with playful trivia and an unusual scoring system.
descriptions.c64:171612: A questionnaire program: one or more people answer a series of questions to learn about themselves and build a compatibility profile to match with others who have used it.
descriptions.c64:171613: Hurdle fences, leap spiders and dodge crows on the way to rescue and reunite with Trampette.
descriptions.c64:171616: Low on fuel over an alien planet, a pilot can only land in a city, so the buildings must be bombed flat to make a runway. A single-screen game flying left to right.
descriptions.c64:171620: A shooter in the vein of Uridium where a lone fighter takes on the defences of a huge space station.
descriptions.c64:171621: Lupenio, history's greatest thief, breaks into an old house full of guardians and deadly traps to steal King Solomon's diamond; each key opens just one door, so they must be used carefully.
descriptions.c64:171622: A personality test based on preferences for colours, shades and shapes, producing a profile of the respondent's current attitude to work, relationships and life.
descriptions.c64:171628: Play goalkeeper in a penalty shootout: save 10 shots before the striker scores 10 to advance. Over ten levels the game speeds up while the keeper slows down, and the choice of penalty taker sets the difficulty.
descriptions.c64:171631: A clone of Sega's Pengo: Willy the penguin pushes ice blocks around a maze to crush mutant sea lions against the walls.
descriptions.c64:171634: A Pengo-like game with normal and fast modes: a penguin slides ice blocks around the board to rearrange it and crush enemies shaped like green balls.
descriptions.c64:171635: An Amidar-style grid game: Peter the Painter carries out three tasks for the King, first moving along the lines of a grid of rectangles to clear the dots of dirt around them.
descriptions.c64:171636: A French role-playing game with an open world and turn-based play, set on the small planet Kalvor, with its two continents Primaterra and Kalimater, once peaceful under the good King Philoxal.
descriptions.c64:171637: Solve mazes to reach safety while evading a computer or human opponent, across 200 levels plus 50 advanced ones unlocked after finishing the main game.
descriptions.c64:171638: A puzzle game in which a banished deity uses ancient stones to overthrow the gods: each of 50 levels is cleared by swapping coloured gems so that two or more of a colour meet, while black gems and fixed bricks block the way.
descriptions.c64:171642: Phileas Fogg pauses his round-the-world trip to help the Allies, flying his hot-air balloon over enemy territory to map it and bomb enemy shacks, controlling height with thrust, wind, hydrogen and sandbags.
descriptions.c64:171643: Barney the Bellhop inherits his late Aunt Mabel's fortune, but must earn it by finding treasures hidden in her 90-room mansion and getting past the traps and puzzles she left behind.
descriptions.c64:171645: A Pac-Man variant: clear each single-screen maze of dots while avoiding three ghosts, using the power pills in the corners to turn the tables.
descriptions.c64:171646: Split-screen shoot 'em up by Lars Sneftrup in which waves of aliens attack in repeating patterns; rejected by Hewson, it leaked through crackers with only 8 of its 16 stages and later appeared in Italy as Son Guay.
descriptions.c64:171648: A falling-block style puzzle: rearrange columns of symbols so that each column holds only identical symbols, at which point it disappears.
descriptions.c64:171671: A simple platformer in which every green key must be collected and taken to the exit at the foot of the screen.
descriptions.c64:171672: A conversation program in the vein of Eliza: Maggie invites the user to talk about problems, thoughts and fears.
descriptions.c64:171677: As a space pirate, raid 21 cargo ships for precious materials, each raid made up of three stages that must be completed in turn. Three craft are available to choose from at the start.
descriptions.c64:171678: A single-screen platformer based on Raymond Briggs' book: gather snow, clothes, toys and ice and take them to the right spot to build the snowman, eating food to stay awake and avoiding gas flames that melt him.
descriptions.c64:171692: An educational Pac-Man variant about dental care: move a toothbrush through a maze of teeth, turning them from yellow to white, while three plaque blobs give chase and stain teeth they pass.
descriptions.c64:171693: A two-player duel between wizards in which the one landing the most successful attacks wins. An entry in RGCD's 2013 16KB cartridge competition.
descriptions.c64:171694: A multi-event sports game made for the 1988 Seoul Olympics, featuring swimming and several track and field events, with music by Markus Schneider.
descriptions.c64:171695: A puzzle with 99 levels: pressing fire flips the surrounding fields in four directions, and the goal is to clear every visible mussel from the board.
descriptions.c64:171697: A platformer in which the hero searches for a magic book, throwing stars at the witch Anabel's goblins while racing against time.
descriptions.c64:171698: Sequel to Magic Duel: two players control rival wizards attacking each other, and the first to reach the set points total wins.
descriptions.c64:171699: Poker in a Wild West saloon, sitting down at a corner table with four tense card players on a hot afternoon.
descriptions.c64:171700: An educational program teaching children aged 6 to 10 spelling and grammar rules through three animated mini-games, with words drawn from categories such as animals, the orchestra and fruit.
descriptions.c64:171703: A puzzle in which every available piece must be placed on a chessboard to clear the level; the number of pieces left is shown at the bottom and an arrow marks the current piece. Also known as Duddo.
descriptions.c64:171704: Collect mushrooms, some of which may be poisonous, while bats, a snake and a lightning-throwing witch attack; survivors face ever more dangerous enemies.
descriptions.c64:171705: Skeletons have raided Snail Meadow, looting homes, killing cattle and kidnapping the snails, and Sonny the Snail, about to marry Dawny, sets out to put things right.
descriptions.c64:171706: A sample adventure written with AdventureWriter: it begins south of a dark castle beside a sign demanding the return of the Orb and the Scroll.
descriptions.c64:171707: As Wuntvor, apprentice to the vanished magician Ebeneezum, find and rescue his master.
descriptions.c64:171708: Based on the BBC children's series: over ten educational activities for ages three to eight with the show's characters, including Why, Bird, Lizzie and Peggy, covering numbers and word recognition across four self-adjusting difficulty levels.
descriptions.c64:171709: Fly a World War II plane over a single screen, bombing the man-eating plants that grew from seeds brought back by botanist Sir Hubert Flog and have since eaten him.
descriptions.c64:171718: As Red O'Blair, save a gold research base in Lee Valley from a rockslide by replacing the broken lever that powers the giant pneumatic hammers driving bridge pillars into the river bed.
descriptions.c64:171724: A two-player board game on a 10x10 grid: players take turns placing tiles of their colour, and a single opposing tile sandwiched between two of a player's tiles changes to that colour. The most tiles wins.
descriptions.c64:171730: A side-scrolling quest: a dragon has stolen the Magic Orb from the village hall, leaving the village defenceless, and Pod, whose grandfather brought the orb there, must get it back.
descriptions.c64:171731: Bounce Pogo Joe from barrel to barrel, recoloring each one he lands on until the entire level has changed color; a Q*Bert-inspired game whose layouts take a variety of shapes.
descriptions.c64:171736: An upgrade of a 1993 mahjong solitaire: remove matching tiles to clear the board, either racing the clock or in untimed solitaire mode.
descriptions.c64:171749: A race-around-the-board game for two to four players in the vein of Sorry, written by Laze Ristoski.
descriptions.c64:171754: Five-card stud poker against Pokersam, a computer dealer with personality, humor and a voice of his own.
descriptions.c64:171762: An Arkanoid variant for one or two players, with paddles on the top and left edges; clearing the cubes uncovers a manga-style picture, and bonuses range from twin balls to penalties like shrunken paddles.
descriptions.c64:171763: Somewhere near Upper Puddleton stands the mansion of your eccentric late uncle; track it down to claim your inheritance in this adventure.
descriptions.c64:171764: Fly over a map of Canada and halt exactly on named cities, testing Canadian geography solo or racing a second player.
descriptions.c64:171766: Geography teaching software for the United States with three modes: Search, where names of states, rivers, seas and mountains are typed in, a Test mode, and a helicopter game.
descriptions.c64:171767: A Dutch geography trainer for primary school pupils built on a mid-1980s world map, offering look-up, quiz and helicopter game modes.
descriptions.c64:171768: A Breakout-style game where each level replaces the wall of bricks with a moving, segmented centipede-like creature that the ball must knock apart.
descriptions.c64:171769: Aboard a stolen space yacht drifting toward a pirate ship, find the pirates' treasure and dymenthium ingots for your own vessel, carry everything back to the ship's utility room, and learn what became of the pirates.
descriptions.c64:171786: A modification of I Want More Diamonds by AEG Soft that puts Mario in the lead role and adds multiple levels.
descriptions.c64:171787: A Donkey Kong clone that puts a beer machine in place of the giant ape.
descriptions.c64:171788: A multi-event sports contest with more than seven disciplines, playable alone or with several people, released on the Golden Disk 64 magazine disk.
descriptions.c64:171789: Bundles two text adventures: Dial M for Marlo and The Museum Caper.
descriptions.c64:171790: Filling in for Delivery Man Dan, who has broken his leg, Pat drives his van to drop telephone directories at as many houses as he can over five days, dodging obstacles without running out of fuel, in a Paperboy-like game.
descriptions.c64:171792: Bring a rocket down onto Martian landing pads with keyboard thrusters; the border color shows descent speed and turns green when touchdown is safe, and good landings earn bonus fuel. Included on the compilation 4 in 1 Game Pack.
descriptions.c64:171794: A free text adventure in the style of the original Zork games, made to promote Zork: Grand Inquisitor. In 1066 the hero, a seventh-class private in the Inquisition Guard, has just come off duty at the Port Foozle gift kiosk.
descriptions.c64:171810: A top-down driving game for children aged four to six, based on the British TV series: drive Pat's van around the scrolling village to find vehicles and animals, including his cat Jess.
descriptions.c64:171821: Ice hockey between the USA and USSR, with either one skater or five per side and periods of two, twelve or twenty minutes, featuring wrist and slap shots, drop passes, face-offs and body checks.
descriptions.c64:171822: A home version of the TV game show for four to eight contestants, recreating many of its pricing games along with the big wheel and the showcase.
descriptions.c64:171823: Run the campaign for any candidate in US presidential elections from the 1960s onward, or design a custom candidate through a character-creation process.
descriptions.c64:171826: A football management game built for two: each player runs a club, taking turns over managerial decisions and playing out their matches.
descriptions.c64:171834: An espionage puzzle game: a COPNET agent investigating the car-crash death of the head of the secret S.D.I. project New-wave soon finds himself the prime suspect.
descriptions.c64:171835: Starting from nothing but a logon prompt, break into an unfamiliar computer system and explore what is hidden inside.
descriptions.c64:171838: A Sokoban variant: as a warehouse keeper, push crates one at a time onto marked spots, with a single-move undo on the P key.
descriptions.c64:171843: Boxing against a friend or the computer, with eight joystick moves for guarding and landing punches.
descriptions.c64:171844: An educational quiz about the computer hardware and technology of its day.
descriptions.c64:171895: Instead of running a team, steer one player's career through the top four English leagues, the cups and European competition, after choosing position, nationality and starting year.
descriptions.c64:171897: Strategic top-down golf for one to four players, who can also face computer-controlled versions of great golfers from the past; wind and weather affect every shot.
descriptions.c64:171899: An educational trivia game for one or two players: timed logic games earn credits, and after each round those credits claim squares on the board.
descriptions.c64:171905: As a droid aboard the cargo ship Dreadnought Nine, search flick-screen platform rooms for the nine lost pieces of the pulsebomb Earth needs to survive.
descriptions.c64:171909: Broke after a night of drinking and unable to pay the landlord, find the right equipment to venture into the sewers, the one place money is known to be hidden.
descriptions.c64:171911: A statistics-driven baseball simulation for replaying single games or whole seasons, keeping permanent team records with its Stat Compiler; great teams such as the 1927 New York Yankees are included.
descriptions.c64:171913: A statistical football simulation with rosters and stats for NFL teams from the 1986 season: let the computer play a game out, or coach and call the plays.
descriptions.c64:171914: A text adventure where a trainee's final test to earn the title of Matchmaker is seeing the royal couple, a Prince and his Princess, wed at the church in suitable clothes, along with a properly attired page boy.
descriptions.c64:171915: Teacher-designed geography drills built on matching U.S. facts with words and phrases, with an authoring mode for typing in your own quizzes and games.
descriptions.c64:171930: Guide Benny the light bulb through small pattern puzzles; each level can be played alone or in sequence and holds a symbol needed for the final puzzle, and some stages are timed.
descriptions.c64:171933: A Swedish take on Q*Bert: recolor the block pyramid against the clock while two opponents give chase.
descriptions.c64:171934: A maze game for one to four players: steer Mr Quadro along dotted paths linked by gapped discs, eating every dot while avoiding spirits and other creatures.
descriptions.c64:171937: As Yucatan Sam, scale the outside of the temple of Quintana Roo past snakes and lightning bolts, then search inside for the hidden vault and its treasure.
descriptions.c64:171940: Travel back through history to stop Adam eating the apple, dodging hazards such as Robert Bruce's spider, Cleopatra's asp and Dr. Livingstone's gorilla; play in arcade mode, adventure mode or both.
descriptions.c64:171944: An educational math adventure from the Math Magic collection that mixes shooting demons with solving arithmetic problems.
descriptions.c64:171945: Part of the Let's Count collection for children aged four and up: at the fairground, help Maths Muscles ring the bells in ascending order to practise the numbers 0 to 9.
descriptions.c64:171946: Answer arithmetic problems quickly enough to outdraw Bad Math Mac in the town of Math Tombstone.
descriptions.c64:171947: A Space Invaders-style shooter from Australia's Satchel Software that drills addition, subtraction, multiplication and division.
descriptions.c64:171953: A text adventure with still pictures, made with the Graphic Adventure Creator: Florida private eye Matt Lucas follows clues and infiltrates the underworld after his partner John Harpinger is kidnapped.
descriptions.c64:171954: As Merravid, son of Aranoid, recover the Dwarves' magical firestone from a dragon-guarded mountain in Thargon, but only after finding the right armour.
descriptions.c64:171967: A computer version of the moral-dilemma board game for three to ten players, any of whom can be computer-controlled; human players set their personality traits and choose a face before play.
descriptions.c64:171972: A quiz program derived from Quiz Master on the VIC-20 that also lets users write their own quizzes and save them to tape or disk.
descriptions.c64:171973: A Q*Bert-style game: hop R-Nest diagonally across a pyramid of cubes to paint their tops, with later levels needing several visits per cube.
descriptions.c64:171974: Made by Hungarian programmers, this early flight game stood out for drawing a moving horizon on such limited hardware; PSS advertised it, but Commodore and Markt & Technik ended up releasing it.
descriptions.c64:172001: Control rail traffic around the Crewe locomotive works, routing every train movement so passenger services keep to time and contracts are met.
descriptions.c64:172003: Play a mother rabbit searching a maze for her four babies while a hunter, hired by a gardener tired of losing crops, moves around taking shots at her.
descriptions.c64:172004: Tied to Sport Aid '88 and its worldwide 10km charity run against hunger, poverty and disease, with the player in the role of the runner Omar.
descriptions.c64:172007: As secret agent Mr. White, collect every microdot in a maze while guards hunt you down, using speed boosts to escape. Survival mode has no gun; Escape mode gives you bullets but fewer exits. Unused boosts and bullets add bonus points.
descriptions.c64:172012: A reworking of the text adventure Nogard with PETSCII graphics: an elite Nogard warrior must bring six items to the king, who hides under a bed in his storeroom, starting out with a plastic-bag battlepack, a newspaper and clean underpants.
descriptions.c64:172015: A constantly scrolling top-down racer over six courses at the closing day of the Interplanetary Terra-Races, now in their 17th year, with a split screen so two players can race at once.
descriptions.c64:172049: The medicine man's excess has put the village at risk of flooding, so the elders summon Copecoee, ancient god of energy; move him with the cursor keys and fire energy rays with Shift.
descriptions.c64:172060: A pool game offering eight-ball, nine-ball, rotation and straight pool.
descriptions.c64:172062: A rail traffic simulation covering the 85-mile Bristol to Exeter line, once part of the Great Western Railway, with every locomotive movement under your control.
descriptions.c64:172067: A strategy game of 19th-century railroad speculation for one to eight players, up to four of them computer-run; the long scenario spans 1870 to 1900, while the short one starts in 1890 and ends in 1895 or 1900.
descriptions.c64:172068: Help the Rainbow Dragon escape a cave system by destroying ten magic chests, using magic to clear the obstacles that block them.
descriptions.c64:172072: A baby owl hops square by square across a rainbow high above the clouds, coloring in its gray bands.
descriptions.c64:172078: Create a boxer and train him through weeks of bag work, running and sparring between fights to climb to the top at heavyweight, middleweight or welterweight.
descriptions.c64:172080: A side-scrolling jet fighter shooter over four levels with bosses, a charged laser alongside the normal shot, and extra weapons dropped by enemies.
descriptions.c64:172084: Race three rivals over three laps of three maze-like circuits, following arrows on the road; straying too far, running dry or suffering too much damage ends the game.
descriptions.c64:172090: A vertically scrolling shooter with a medieval theme, made with the Shoot 'Em Up Construction Kit.
descriptions.c64:172092: A dueling shoot 'em up for one or two players by Paul Kubiszyn and Jonathan Hunt, published with Commodore Format issue 52.
descriptions.c64:172093: A four-stage game: a space shooter, a stop where the right three ship add-ons must be chosen, a very long snake game, and a safe-cracking finale.
descriptions.c64:172095: A Space Invaders variant with power-ups and boss stages.
descriptions.c64:172105: Based on the late-1980s TV game show: pick the 11 correct answers out of 16 on the board while avoiding the 5 wrong ones, with a Hot Spot prize hidden behind one correct answer.
descriptions.c64:172112: Find the exit from one of 26 mazes in smooth first-person 3D with full 360-degree turning; movement units are counted, and best scores and up to nine games in progress are saved to disk.
descriptions.c64:172113: A Ghosts 'n Goblins-style action game: hunt down the ancient relics needed to defeat The Unspeakable One, collecting drops of vitality, magic, armor, treasure and risky mystery items.
descriptions.c64:172114: A single-screen space shooter: wipe out snakes of smiley faces and descending alien ships, picking up power-ups left behind by fallen enemies.
descriptions.c64:172115: Chronoclasm bomb experiments in the war between humanity and Proxima go wrong and tear apart the space-time continuum, leaving the player to fly a Thunderbolt jet through the aftermath.
descriptions.c64:172116: A board game for one to four players racing to a cash goal between $10,000 and $90,000 through lotteries, investments and spending.
descriptions.c64:172118: Based on the TV drawing show: a teammate sketches on the board and you guess the phrase, often a common expression drawn literally, like a light bulb for 'bright idea'.
descriptions.c64:172119: Pinball over eight rounds on three tables, mostly soccer-themed: knock out the defenders guarding the goal and score three goals to move on.
descriptions.c64:172120: Guide a rabbit across the screen past critters to grab a dangling carrot, which turns it into Super Bunny.
descriptions.c64:172121: A forced-scrolling shooter in which AL, a globular droid, enforces the Ransack clause against the Ryvian System's eight planets for failing to pay the Democratic Council of Planets.
descriptions.c64:172123: Seymour the stuntman works through four themed movie sets in a side-scrolling platformer, shooting enemies and keeping out of the water with five lives.
descriptions.c64:172125: A light-cycle duel in a future arena: box the opponent in with your bike's energy trail, using a force field up to three times to avoid crashing.
descriptions.c64:172126: A top-down stock car race against the clock from Florida to California across the southern USA, on freeways, bridges, back routes and rural roads.
descriptions.c64:172127: A former mercenary captured by the CIA and pressed into the US Navy flies one-man helicopter missions.
descriptions.c64:172129: As a rat in a cheese warehouse, eat the six cheeses spelling THE RAT on each floor; once the first is eaten, the others start moving around.
descriptions.c64:172130: As Mike the Spy, travel through Europe, including Switzerland and Venice, to recover vital plans left behind by a dead fellow agent, beginning by boarding a plane with fake ID.
descriptions.c64:172131: Explore the flick-screen caverns of Pylpapa as Sqij, gathering the six scattered pieces of the Enertree, key to eternal life, and returning them to the Lotz-Too-Weet cave.
descriptions.c64:172132: A vertical shoot 'em up: pilot a new spacecraft against alien hordes bent on destroying the space federation, protected by a shield of limited energy.
descriptions.c64:172133: Testing jet packs for the Space Rider company, fly to the test site on the 23rd planet, which turns out to have been taken over by aliens.
descriptions.c64:172167: The Planetary Orbiting Co-ordinator has failed and the planets are drifting from the Sun; send robot XR3 into its core to repair it and find the missing planets.
descriptions.c64:172181: Outmaneuver an opponent to break into missile control and fire the missile.
descriptions.c64:172184: A tile puzzle framed as debugging a virus-hit nuclear plant computer: toggle tiles with a cursor until the whole board is in the same state, all colored or all blank.
descriptions.c64:172186: Simulates the Confederacy's last major Civil War offensive at Chickamauga, built on a refined Gettysburg engine and played in 13 two-hour turns over two days, scored on casualties and objectives.
descriptions.c64:172188: A remake of Megamania made for Visionparty 2002: from the bottom of the screen, fend off waves of bizarre attackers such as flying hamburgers, bow ties, steam irons, space dice and diamonds.
descriptions.c64:172194: A keyboard-controlled board game with spaces lettered A to X; place characters by typing letters, then move them around the board.
descriptions.c64:172195: A snake game written to fit in 2 KB.
descriptions.c64:172196: A memory game: uncover matching pairs of pictures on a 6x6 board within a limited number of moves.
descriptions.c64:172197: A pairs memory game where matched pictures vanish from the board and a counter shows how many more mistakes are allowed.
descriptions.c64:172198: Memorize 25 pairs of icons shown for 10 seconds, then find all the matches before time runs out. Released in Italy as Memoteca.
descriptions.c64:172199: As an agent of the SAROS resistance disguised as a merchant, fly the Caydia to the colony worlds Tropos, Halmuris and Arcadion, meeting freedom fighters and gathering intelligence against the alien Arcadians.
descriptions.c64:172202: Pilot a jumping buggy-like scout capsule across eight side-scrolling planets, shooting aliens and gathering the scattered parts of your spaceship.
descriptions.c64:172203: Steer Fisher-Price's school bus along country roads, collecting the Little People and dropping them off, in a game that trains coordination, judgement and recall.
descriptions.c64:172204: Buy your way into football club ownership: win by holding at least 501 shares in each of the ten top clubs when a season ends.
descriptions.c64:172205: A horizontally scrolling shooter about saving Mars colonists from hostile aliens.
descriptions.c64:172206: Sequel to Snowball: on the planet Eden, being colonised by Snowball's command robots, native plants and animals fight back, and Commander Kim must survive around the crumbling walled city.
descriptions.c64:172207: Football trivia for one to four players: throw a ball across a row of stadiums using a power bar, and answer questions based on where it lands.
descriptions.c64:172208: A two-player duel between a submarine firing missiles and an aeroplane dropping bombs, both constantly moving across the screen, where neutral ships must not be hit.
descriptions.c64:172209: Drive an armed car, seen from above, shooting down a biker gang during their annual race; kill too few before refueling and you die.
descriptions.c64:172210: An Asteroids-like shooter where your shots rebound off the edges of the play area instead of wrapping around.
descriptions.c64:172211: A point-and-click adventure: control four travellers who have landed a helicopter on a shopping centre roof in search of fuel while zombies roam the earth.
descriptions.c64:172212: Roll a ball across single-screen platforms to the exit, planning the route carefully because each tile vanishes once crossed.
descriptions.c64:172215: A platform game with puzzle elements in the mould of Gods: Robin sets out to rescue Maid Marion from the Sheriff of Nottingham, gathering treasure and shooting gargoyles and trolls with his bow.
descriptions.c64:172216: The Xanthidian are spreading across Earth; from a South Pacific base, send four Raider Craft out over a world map showing alien-held and human-held regions to drive the invaders back.
descriptions.c64:172217: Explorers from the year 2891, unwilling to risk themselves, reach back to 1981 for help raiding the Star Maze, an alien artifact whose energy crystals are guarded by powerful aliens.
descriptions.c64:172218: A fruit machine modelled on English pub slots: start with a 2.00 stake, bet 10p per spin and use features such as hold to land winning combinations.
descriptions.c64:172219: A side-scrolling fighting game across an airport, a harbor and a military base, punching and kicking enemies and picking up weapons for an edge.
descriptions.c64:172229: A multidirectional scrolling shooter inspired by the Book of Revelation: descend through more than 40 caverns of Hell, constantly sinking unless thrusting, to reach the Monster of the Apocalypse.
descriptions.c64:172233: Wake up tied to a bed in what looks like a hospital room, with no memory of who you are or how you got there, and find a way to escape.
descriptions.c64:172234: A tile-flipping memory game for young children, one or two players, pairing pictures, tunes, words, colors and shapes across a variety of board layouts.
descriptions.c64:172235: As a knight inside a castle, memorize the instructions you are given, then answer questions on what to do next to move forward.
descriptions.c64:172236: A memory game playable with joystick or lightpen, with modes for matching pairs of shapes or of numbers.
descriptions.c64:172238: Three puzzles in one, including Free Fall, a 3D Tetris where complete layers vanish, and Mental Detector, which asks which of four flattened cube nets matches the cube shown.
descriptions.c64:172240: A turn-based what-if World War II war game pitting Patton against Rommel for control of Normandy, with points scored as the battle unfolds.
descriptions.c64:172241: Based on the 1975 Parker Brothers board game for two to four players: move around a board laid out as a monthly calendar, starting with $325, aiming to finish with the most money.
descriptions.c64:172243: Explore an alien planet collecting robot parts while keeping up your energy; the laser blaster kills enemies but drains that same energy.
descriptions.c64:172244: A Fisher-Price music program: listen to one of more than thirty songs, then play it note by note along with the computer, with no music reading needed.
descriptions.c64:172279: Disguised as a cassette operating system, this is actually a shoot 'em up about fighting the Zorn to protect the planet.
descriptions.c64:172280: Take a boxer from the bottom of the rankings toward the top in a side-view boxing game, with attributes governing his left and right high and low punches and his defence.
descriptions.c64:172288: A Uridium-style shooter from the Game On disk magazine, later heavily reworked and reissued as Counter Force.
descriptions.c64:172290: Foster pilots his spherosorb craft through a wormhole into the epsilon dimension, a radially structured world sending out waves of pure energy.
descriptions.c64:172321: Move a crosshair to shoot down a meteor shower before it hits your ship.
descriptions.c64:172322: As a silver orb, navigate a twisting labyrinth to collect puzzle pieces, shooting or dodging enemies and using teleporters and floor switches to open new areas before time runs out.
descriptions.c64:172324: Ring worlds are converging on the solar system and devouring all in their path: follow intelligence reports to find them, jump through hyperspace and battle each ring world's defense fleet.
descriptions.c64:172325: A real-time text adventure set in 1900 with eerie music throughout, featuring Florence Nightingale, Madame Curie and Sherlock Holmes among its characters.
descriptions.c64:172327: Fly a spaceship and destroy mines, cruisers and star bases; cruisers appear and circle you when you near their base, and red rocks hold minerals that add to your score.
descriptions.c64:172329: Command the German Army against the computer's Soviet forces on the Eastern Front between Finland and the Crimea, on a map oriented so east points up, with 10 skill levels.
descriptions.c64:172333: One-on-one basketball between Michael Jordan and Larry Bird, plus a slam dunk contest and a three-point shootout with five racks of five balls around the arc.
descriptions.c64:172334: Drive a car in an island-wide treasure hunt.
descriptions.c64:172336: A small game meant to be played while the main program on the tape loaded: rescue six stranded men from a planet's surface and bring them back to the mothership.
descriptions.c64:172337: A faster, graphically improved version of the PET port of Microchess, a chess program first released in 1977.
descriptions.c64:172339: A licensed baseball strategy game with real teams and players and classic teams from the past; each play is shown graphically with running commentary.
descriptions.c64:172361: Guide the robot Robbo through 76 levels of Boulder Dash and Sokoban-style puzzles, collecting the screws needed to repair his ship and reach his escape capsule while avoiding aliens and traps.
descriptions.c64:172362: An add-on for MicroLeague Baseball that compiles box scores for stored teams across a full season, with printable statistics.
descriptions.c64:172363: A single-player version of Multi User Dungeon where the computer controls the other characters; reach wizard status by scoring 102,400 points through fighting other players and completing tasks.
descriptions.c64:172365: Under a spell and not quite yourself, escape a dusty study and brew a remedy in the cauldron before midnight.
descriptions.c64:172367: A vertical shooter: fly a jet with an unlimited-ammo cannon over Jupiter's surface to destroy the Communist rebel base, past fighters, tanks and unidentified craft.
descriptions.c64:172369: As a robot aboard a spaceship hit by a Space Virus and radiation, clear each level by carrying four Death Pods, one at a time, to an Assembly Unit.
descriptions.c64:172370: A simulation of the June 1942 Battle of Midway: command the outnumbered American forces against a large Japanese fleet sent to capture the island.
descriptions.c64:172371: Bloody Zenon terrorises the land with a Cyclops eye, and King Aldir must stop him by exploring forest and underground labyrinths, using single-use items in the right places to open passages.
descriptions.c64:172372: Fly a MiG-19 jet, dodging oncoming fighters and tank fire, and bring it safely back to the runway.
descriptions.c64:172374: A platformer written in BASIC: archaeologist Dr. Mike Holehead is trapped in an old pyramid and must find the way out before his air runs out.
descriptions.c64:172390: Help a reconnaissance probe returning from Astral 4 refuel by landing on planets along its route home to Earth.
descriptions.c64:172391: As Prince Kronos, son of Emperor Iridon I, undergo the ancient Iridani Test of Arms on the toughest battlefields to become heir to the throne and Prince of the Southern Nebular.
descriptions.c64:172394: Personality analysis software for building a profile of someone you know, revealing their likes, dislikes and hidden traits to help with relationships.
descriptions.c64:172397: An all-text real-time adventure: as a Mind Adventurer, journey through the minds of four dead residents of your world to find the Wheel of Wisdom and end the planet's chaos. It shipped with a hardbound book.
descriptions.c64:172399: A Minesweeper clone with selectable difficulty, custom board sizes, redefinable controls, a choice of background tunes and saving and loading.
descriptions.c64:172402: Christoph Cemper's take on Minesweeper, with sound and music by Patrick Peters.
descriptions.c64:172404: A turn-based scavenger hunt across Laustenfownd mixing strategy, action and board-game play: physical cards dealt to each player list the objects to find, and luck cards can swing the outcome.
descriptions.c64:172405: A text adventure about the dragon Cavilan, sole survivor of the Master's dragon slaughter, whose egg was seized by his orcs and stored away.
descriptions.c64:172413: A Pac-Man game on a single screen, with one unchanging maze and only two or three ghosts.
descriptions.c64:172415: A two-player-only Tron light-cycle game that requires two joysticks, with speed adjustable using the + and - keys.
descriptions.c64:172416: A condensed remake of Infocom's Zork I, best known for its 1990 magazine release.
descriptions.c64:172421: A question-and-answer game on the 50 states, covering capitals, major industries, history and geography.
descriptions.c64:172423: A hex-based wargame on the Battlefront engine covering the North African campaign, with eight scenarios playable from either side, including Operation Exporter in Syria and Sidi Rezegh, both 1941.
descriptions.c64:172437: Fly a jetpack into a heavily defended fortress maze, avoiding guns, traps and laser guardians, and destroy the generators at its heart; walls collapse once every brick is shot out.
descriptions.c64:172438: A text adventure in which Ebenezer Scrooge must perform twelve good deeds to make amends for his miserly life, first working out what those deeds are.
descriptions.c64:172439: The official Major Indoor Soccer League game: build an expansion team into a champion through trades, roster changes and training, acting as coach, general manager, player or all three, with stats kept for nine seasons.
descriptions.c64:172441: A Mastermind-style puzzle: guess a five-digit sequence in six tries, with symbols showing exact and partial matches after each attempt.
descriptions.c64:172443: Rebuild a passage of text by filling in its missing letters one at a time, winning by completing the most gaps while missing as few guesses as possible.
descriptions.c64:172448: A whimsical egg-collecting game set in 2020, after a nuclear war has left the world with giant chickens laying giant eggs.
descriptions.c64:172451: Collect and defuse bombs planted across several systems before time runs out, steering against shifting gravity and keeping clear of the walls.
descriptions.c64:172452: Descend through ten levels into the depths of Jupiter in a smooth-scrolling one- or two-player shooter, conserving fuel and laser power and collecting boosters from the planet's surface.
descriptions.c64:172472: During the Vietnam War, Sergeant Tan drives an armed jeep through a horizontally scrolling shooter on an urgent secret delivery, jumping mines and obstacles and destroying tanks and bouncing balls.
descriptions.c64:172479: A text adventure in which aliens carry you to a distant planet built to resemble an English village, and the goal is to get back to Earth.
descriptions.c64:172522: Clear intelligent bugs out of Igos Transputer mega-chips, entering each in a Vector Module and wiping out the bugs in every channel before moving on through a transition stage.
descriptions.c64:172527: Trapped inside a game a wizard invented for his own amusement, gather the pieces of an amulet on a grid; each collected piece blocks movement back in that direction, and breaking the rule unleashes a beast.
descriptions.c64:172530: A platformer about raiding the starbank of Astra, the galaxy's richest store of gems and metals, protected by advanced alarms and cyber guards.
descriptions.c64:172531: An Italian vertically scrolling shooter in the style of Moon Cresta, where rebels rise again just after an intergalactic peace treaty is signed.
descriptions.c64:172532: Design model cars by choosing engines, transmissions and fuel systems, then test their speed and handling on the track.
descriptions.c64:172533: Whack moles as they pop up at random from a 3x3 grid of holes, one of the earliest computer takes on Whac-a-Mole, released on a Japanese MAX cartridge.
descriptions.c64:172534: Defend the Roomlord inheritance against demons, cyclopes, Chinese dragons, gangsters and other foes across 16 screens to become Super Roomlord.
descriptions.c64:172553: Las Vegas-style roulette for up to eight players, each starting with 5000; play continues until the last human player is out of money.
descriptions.c64:172556: Protect a lunar module by launching rockets at incoming meteors; too many ground hits trigger an earthquake, while surviving 60 meteors earns a bonus and pickup by the mothership.
descriptions.c64:172571: Manage a rugby league club in the north of England from behind your office desk, using a joystick-controlled hand to click items before each match.
descriptions.c64:172576: Drive through mazes sown with mines, scooping up as many money bags as you can before you run into one. The playfield is drawn entirely in PETSCII characters.
descriptions.c64:172578: A Towers of Hanoi variant: move a stack of monkeys one at a time between three spots, never putting a bigger monkey on a smaller one, to reach two apples in a tree.
descriptions.c64:172583: A monkey on an assembly line must punch the right digit as numbers 0 to 9 scroll quickly past, answering addition, subtraction, multiplication and division problems.
descriptions.c64:172584: A vertically scrolling one- or two-player tank shooter made with the Shoot-'Em-Up Construction Kit, battling jets, enemy tanks and fortifications while dodging or destroying tank traps; part of ECP's War Games Pak.
descriptions.c64:172585: A Space Invaders and Gorf-style shooter at a carnival, where aliens disguised as smiling masks attack from every direction, even from below. Released in Italy as Le Maschere.
descriptions.c64:172586: Quarter-mile drag racing in nitro-burning top fuel dragsters, featuring Don 'Big Daddy' Garlits and three-time world champion Shirley 'Cha-Cha' Muldowney.
descriptions.c64:172603: The Sorcerer's Apprentice has brought every broom to life with a misjudged spell and must shoot them down over five levels, the first three set in flip-screen caves with movement in depth as well as sideways.
descriptions.c64:172610: A small ship that moves in any direction and fires straight up battles three huge aliens that cannot be destroyed; each hit scores points but makes the monster start shooting back. Five lives.
descriptions.c64:172611: Cross a labyrinth to the other side while monsters try to strike you down, never touching its radioactive walls.
descriptions.c64:172612: A Pac-Man variant with no power pills: eat every object on the board while dodging roaming creatures that drain energy on contact.
descriptions.c64:172613: A text-based role-playing adventure where the computer acts as Dungeon Master, rolling up a character with hit points and gold to spend on armor and weapons, then levelling them up through fights in monster lairs.
descriptions.c64:172614: A platformer about reaching and defeating a deadly creature hidden in a maze, finding and using items along the way while facing mummies, knights, bats and spike traps.
descriptions.c64:172615: A Cybernoid-like shooter with puzzle elements, built around matching keys to their doors.
descriptions.c64:172619: Investigate the 1899 loss of the steamship Victoria, which may not have been the weather's fault, to unmask a century-old spy and find the gold.
descriptions.c64:172642: A Frogger variant in space: dodge planets and meteors and hop between rocket ships to reach four docking bays, each closing once filled, with tougher rounds after all four are occupied.
descriptions.c64:172643: A vertically scrolling shooter built with SEUCK, with forward-only fire, several enemy types and bosses.
descriptions.c64:172645: In a jam factory, Sam eats drops of jam falling from a vat on a conveyor belt and bites into strawberries while avoiding a giant rat across several single-screen levels.
descriptions.c64:172668: In a bad year for Santa, with Rudolph's nose turned black and the goblins having eaten the elves, guide his sleigh over the world's rooftops past dangers and obstacles.
descriptions.c64:172673: A side-scrolling shooter: fly over the landscape protecting ten programmers who escaped prison on the planet Tubark as they walk the long way to a rescue ship at the far right.
descriptions.c64:172674: A Polish football management game: run one of eighteen Extraklasa clubs, or take charge of Poland in a League of Nations mode or Legia Warsaw in a Europa League mode.
descriptions.c64:172677: A Balloon Rescue-style game in space: steer a ship down into dangerous diamond fields, collecting crystals against tight time and fuel limits. It was the B-side of To Hell and Back.
descriptions.c64:172679: A fantasy-themed racing game for two players at once on a split screen.
descriptions.c64:172680: A single-player shooter in which an elite unit, called to arms by humanity's Central Council, battles enemy fighters.
descriptions.c64:172683: As janitor of the worst school imaginable, clean it section by section while pupils, teachers and dogs attack, all with a bad back that worsens the more you clean.
descriptions.c64:172688: A turn-based World War I strategy game for four human or computer players, each starting with one province and a small army on a map of Europe, aiming to conquer the whole continent.
descriptions.c64:172689: An illustrated text adventure set in Scarthorpe, a dreary 1980s English town no one visits and no one can leave; the goal is to escape it.
descriptions.c64:172691: As the Caliph, recover the sacred sceptre stolen by an evil wizard who turned your palace into a trap-filled puzzle maze; a Dizzy-like game of enemies, platform jumps and object use.
descriptions.c64:172701: An early edutainment title of seven games built around the Moppets of Moptown, teaching strategic reasoning, pattern recognition and problem solving.
descriptions.c64:172702: A logic game for children aged 4 to 7: pick traits for each Moppet creature so they line up in a parade, obeying a numbered rule.
descriptions.c64:172703: A flip-screen platformer: gather diamonds and treasure on each screen against the clock, creating a limited number of stepping stones to get around.
descriptions.c64:172711: A reporter at a struggling local paper goes through a morning routine, gets to work and investigates the jobs the boss hands out, hoping for the big scoop.
descriptions.c64:172714: A Scottish football management game with over 500 players, match commentary and graphics, the Scottish Cup, and coaching, training, injuries, wages and retirements to handle.
descriptions.c64:172716: An illustrated text adventure: search the walled desert city of Akbar Khan for the hidden scroll holding the secret of eternal life.
descriptions.c64:172718: A two-player aerial duel with three planes to choose from.
descriptions.c64:172722: A constantly scrolling horizontal shooter: navigate a deep underground tunnel over four stages, avoiding walls, bouncing balls and doors that switch their electric charge on and off.
descriptions.c64:172723: A vertical shooter: the Zogrons have seized the planet Scuttle and keep its people in line with a nuclear time bomb buried somewhere in the caverns below.
descriptions.c64:172724: Action sequences based on the film, including a dungeon escape, the ice caves and fleeing guards in the woods, played in order or reached by clicking keywords in a scrolling manuscript of the story.
descriptions.c64:172734: Pilot a submarine through underwater caves in a side-scrolling shooter to destroy a reactor under heavy guard, using missiles, torpedoes and a Big Kill weapon that hits everything onscreen against mines, turrets and other foes.
descriptions.c64:172746: A children's game for one or two players: guide a little seahorse to the shipwreck at the right of the screen, dodging lagoon fish and using tunnels to slip elsewhere.
descriptions.c64:172749: Captain the pirate ship Banshee across Khul's Inland Sea, hunting treasure and plundering to fill the hold, then carry the haul safely onward from Tak in the north.
descriptions.c64:172751: A schoolgirl adventure set at the real St. Brides School, a 1980s Irish holiday venue where grown women relived 1920s boarding school life, and which went on to make computer games.
descriptions.c64:172755: Dash across a road from left to right, dodging cars, to rescue a girl; part of the Cassette 50 collection.
descriptions.c64:172764: Fight inward to the innermost ring of a concentric enemy base past locks, keys and puzzles, plant an explosive, then escape within 90 seconds.
descriptions.c64:172765: A Battleships-style game: command your fleet to hunt down enemy submarines and battleships.
descriptions.c64:172769: A two-player board puzzle on a seven-by-seven grid where each player has 24 stones and one square stays empty, with players taking turns to move into the gap.
descriptions.c64:172770: A puzzle framed as saving the universe from runaway entropy by moving icons to recombine scattered energy structures.
descriptions.c64:172771: As a field service worker for CP-Verlag, push boxes down grates in a logic puzzle.
descriptions.c64:172772: Slide pieces to form matches that vanish from the board, clearing each level to reach the next.
descriptions.c64:172773: A computer version of a board game, against the computer or a second player: drive a path across the board to the far side while the opponent tries to block it.
descriptions.c64:172778: Two measuring games for young children: Growing Races and Climbing and Growing.
descriptions.c64:172779: Two number games for young children: How Many? and the Elephant Game.
descriptions.c64:172780: Two shape games for young children: Jigsaws and Shape Maker.
descriptions.c64:172781: Children build early programming skills by creating designs and drawings.
descriptions.c64:172782: Two memory-style matching games for young children: Animal Wildcard and Switcharoo.
descriptions.c64:172783: Guide a blobby character around a grid to collect sixteen piles of dynamite while avoiding lit fuses moving across it; the grid wears away wherever the player or the fuses pass.
descriptions.c64:172786: Steer a multi-segmented snake through a maze and eat the three enemy snakes that enter each level, taking care with rivals longer than your own snake.
descriptions.c64:172798: A computer version of Nine Men's Morris, the ancient board game also known as Mühle, Merels or Mill.
descriptions.c64:172799: A Pac-Man game for one player or two at the same time.
descriptions.c64:172805: The villain Shamus caught last time has escaped, so the detective descends into his underground lair, surviving traps, monsters and wrong turns to bring him back.
descriptions.c64:172812: A wargame of the April 1862 Battle of Shiloh in Tennessee, the bloody Western Theater clash where Ulysses S. Grant's Union forces defeated the Confederates.
descriptions.c64:172813: Three activities for kindergarten to first grade: Discovery for exploring the keyboard, Letters for recognising upper and lower case, and Numbers for counting pictures at several difficulty levels.
descriptions.c64:172814: Interactive fiction from Bantam's Living Literature series: Holmes, in his sixties, and Dr. Watson are drawn into a murder investigation on the steamship S.S. Destiny.
descriptions.c64:172818: Solve a murder at Lord and Lady Osbourne's castle; everyone stays where they were when the body was found, and the killer has thrown the weapon into another room.
descriptions.c64:172819: Play detective: question suspects, collect information, and accuse the killer.
descriptions.c64:172820: A talking illustrated text adventure: find Mary before time runs out and she is killed.
descriptions.c64:172821: A text adventure from The Lockerby Collection: track down and kill a dangerous mutant roaming the area.
descriptions.c64:172824: Based on John Astrop's Puffin book, part game and part personal database for storing private secrets about yourself, your friends and your family.
descriptions.c64:172842: A Pac-Man clone: clear every dot while four monsters give chase, using power pills to turn them blue and eat them.
descriptions.c64:172843: As a security guard, run along the roof of the ITA Express from the last carriage to the front, jumping gaps and kicking off the Redmen who have taken over the train.
descriptions.c64:172847: An update of ShareData's Wheel of Fortune with over a thousand fresh phrases to solve.
descriptions.c64:172856: Explore an island for ten hidden treasures and store them in the cave behind the waterfall; only five items can be carried at once.
descriptions.c64:172865: Write a script and combine music, characters and backgrounds to stage your own show.
descriptions.c64:172868: A three-part text adventure: adrift on a raft after abandoning ship in shark-infested waters, find a way home through quests and encounters with monsters.
descriptions.c64:172869: Use the Stack lightpen to sort a shuffled grid of letters into alphabetical order, sliding letters singly into the vacant square.
descriptions.c64:172872: A H.E.R.O.-style game across 12 rooms: collect every gem, swinging between platforms with a grappling hook and occasionally a gun.
descriptions.c64:172873: A platform shooter: find the key, ride teleport lifts and open the door, never touching sprites, mines or death zones.
descriptions.c64:172875: A hack of the Pac-Man clone Munch Mania that plays the game upside down and backwards.
descriptions.c64:172876: Third of the Mojon Twins' Classic Japanese Monster Castle games and the first starring Nanako; a puzzle platformer that started out on the ZX Spectrum.
descriptions.c64:172877: A real-time strategy game of the 1815 Battle of Waterloo: command Napoleon's army on a top-down wargame-style map of terrain and unit symbols.
descriptions.c64:172904: Guide a spacepod through miles of underground caverns without touching the walls; the score rises for every second survived.
descriptions.c64:172905: Text adventure that opens in a hotel room one floor up in present-day Athens, with the Acropolis ruins in view, as you hunt for the legendary wine that grants immortality.
descriptions.c64:172907: Recover four treasures that the banker Mr. Klinkoyn has lost around his nine-room house, and bring a bowl of milk to Nellan, his thirsty cat, helped by a magic map and the household's residents.
descriptions.c64:172909: Trace the lines of a grid to capture its boxes in this Amidar-style game from the Swedish publisher ScandSoft.
descriptions.c64:172910: An unfinished preview of a planned Doom-style shooter that plays more like an exploration game, distributed on the Commodore Scene #31 disk.
descriptions.c64:172911: Repeat the computer's sequences by pointing the Stack Lightpen at the right squares; after eight successes the pace quickens, across up to seven levels.
descriptions.c64:172923: A racing game played against opponents over the internet, with IRC support built in.
descriptions.c64:172928: Head-to-head Pong-style tennis for one or two players, an updated take on the earliest video tennis games, released on Magic Disk 64 in September 1988.
descriptions.c64:172929: Box against a computer-controlled champion or a second player, or watch the computer fight itself; released in Italy as Megabox.
descriptions.c64:172931: A set of 20 new Boulder Dash caves, credited in the game to Prof. Knibble.
descriptions.c64:172937: A rogue Master Control Unit has turned every machine and robot against humanity; as a survivor, gather the pieces of the shutdown code that its programmer spread among others and switch it off.
descriptions.c64:172939: Steer a growing snake around single-screen mazes, eating every dot without boxing yourself in; after sixteen levels the mazes start over.
descriptions.c64:172940: Golf simulation built on Arc's Reality3 3D engine, with two courses plus a hidden low-gravity nine-hole course on Mars, and match or stroke play against eight computer golfers of varying skill.
descriptions.c64:172941: A shooting gallery with a 30-second limit: hit as many targets as possible, and on later levels some of them return fire.
descriptions.c64:172943: Race at night along one of four tracks, scoring by passing checkpoints; hitting the roadside, oncoming cars or obstacles drops your speed to nothing.
descriptions.c64:172946: Ski down Slalom, Giant Slalom or Alps courses as fast as possible without wiping out; best times are kept until the computer is switched off.
descriptions.c64:172966: The mathematical strategy game Nim: players alternately remove one or more objects from a single pile. Part of the Cassette 50 compilation.
descriptions.c64:172970: Steer a runaway sleigh down a steep mountainside, dodging trees, hidden snowmen and moguls as the speed keeps building.
descriptions.c64:172978: Side-view tennis in which players can only move forward and back or jump, with the joystick shaping the height and power of each shot.
descriptions.c64:172979: Catch barrels and throw each back aboard the ship while dodging hazards such as kangaroos and penguins; every screen sets its own quota of barrels.
descriptions.c64:172980: Guide a lengthening snake to apples while avoiding walls and its own body; after ten apples a door opens to the next level.
descriptions.c64:172981: A beginner-level vertical shooter made with the Shoot-'Em-Up Construction Kit: gun down ninjas and spiders and collect weapons, treasure and potions.
descriptions.c64:172982: Horizontally scrolling space shooter in which the Federation sends its best pilot to repel yet another alien invasion of the solar system; released in Italy as Raid.
descriptions.c64:172985: Text adventure loosely based on the Hans Christian Andersen fairy tale, set in a land spoiled by the scattered shards of a mirror that makes everything look ugly.
descriptions.c64:172995: Fly an F-14 'Rapier' against drug traffickers in Colombia, striking labs, refineries and convoys from land bases, or sinking drug ships and enemy carriers from an aircraft carrier.
descriptions.c64:173000: Tile puzzle in which you swap and flip tiles to form matches without leaving other tiles stranded; published on Game On 1992/06.
descriptions.c64:173001: Top-down racing game featuring Porsches, distributed on Tiger-Crew-Disk #020.
descriptions.c64:173002: Bounce a ball across 99 levels of tiles to reach the exit before time expires; each tile type rebounds differently and vanishes once left, and missing a tile costs a life.
descriptions.c64:173003: Text-only fantasy adventure: as an elite Nogard warrior, collect six items for your king, who is hiding under a bed in his storeroom during a war. Later reissued with graphics as Maze of Nogard.
descriptions.c64:173005: Fight through three kinds of combat: on foot with a rifle against waves of troops, then in a tank, then in an attack helicopter.
descriptions.c64:173009: As the space pirate Nomad, weave through the outer galaxy evading those who want your cargo of precious metals; part of the Sky Fighters game pack.
descriptions.c64:173010: Railroad traffic control simulation spanning 325 miles of track from Washington, D.C. up to Wilmington, Delaware.
descriptions.c64:173029: Puzzle game in the vein of Deflektor: place tiles on the board to route light beams to a target, using deflectors, solid blocks and blocks the light destroys.
descriptions.c64:173030: Side-scrolling shooter defending four domed cities from air and ground invaders; each shield absorbs one hit, and the ship fires lasers forward and drops bombs.
descriptions.c64:173031: Vertical space shooter made with the Shoot-'Em-Up Construction Kit: armed with an experimental Nova-Proton weapon, strike back after the Rutilians seize the base holding the defense codes on Deimos.
descriptions.c64:173033: Space Invaders-style shooter where your ship slides left and right firing at seven kinds of attackers descending from above; released in Italy as Stronghold.
descriptions.c64:173034: Adventure in which you must stop the deranged General K.A. Boom, who has set computers in motion to destroy the world and does not welcome intruders.
descriptions.c64:173035: Educational bowling game in which children solve fraction and decimal problems; aimed at ages 11 and up.
descriptions.c64:173036: Math game where the creature Wumblechum hops across numbered and sign cubes, adding or subtracting values to reach target numbers.
descriptions.c64:173038: Puzzle in which colored nuts sit in two square grids; slide whole rows or columns of the left grid to match the layout of the right one. Released in Italy as Snocciolando.
descriptions.c64:173067: Occult detective text adventure: as a private investigator, begin in your office piecing together clues from an envelope on your desk. It became the basis for the author's later Methyhel games.
descriptions.c64:173069: Command the White Fleet to retake a South Pacific island from the Black Fleet, using a carrier, patrol planes, bombers, PT boats, destroyers, battleships and landing ships.
descriptions.c64:173075: Crosshair shooter casting you as Lee Enfield, retaking a space station from invading soldiers by tracking down and shooting each one across a multi-directional scrolling map.
descriptions.c64:173077: As a bounty hunter in a newly colonized star system, track down the source of the attacking alien ships and destroy it.
descriptions.c64:173085: Shoot down enemy ships that appear ever faster using your ship's laser shield; six hits freeze you and end the game.
descriptions.c64:173087: Shareware nuclear power plant simulation: work the control rods and primary and secondary cooling pumps to keep the reaction stable, scored on the power produced in each attempt.
descriptions.c64:173088: Minimalist adventure in which you ignore a warning sign and enter the Tomb of Shalimar in search of its treasures.
descriptions.c64:173094: Viking text adventure in which you must rescue Sif; praying at altars brings random hints, and food keeps hunger away. Shared on Q-Link in 1986.
descriptions.c64:173096: Party game for four based on Warlords: each lord moves a shield to deflect plasma balls away from their own space station at the edge of a spiral nebula.
descriptions.c64:173105: Stranded in the Tessican system, fly a hijacked Star Five gunfighter over varied landscapes while fighting off the local pilots.
descriptions.c64:173107: Release a ball from moving wires so it bounces through a maze collecting treasure; it has limited hit points, so the timing of each release matters.
descriptions.c64:173109: Escaped from a cell beneath planet Morgon, flee through tunnels chased by robots, some destructible and some not, while watching your oxygen supply.
descriptions.c64:173114: Run the Spare Change Arcade, a hall of token machines, jukeboxes, phones and popcorn machines, restocking token machines with money from the register when they run dry.
descriptions.c64:173127: Two arithmetic drill games, Speed Math and Bingo Math, on one release.
descriptions.c64:173132: Word-recognition games for readers six and up: as a diver, uncover words hidden by lettermoss on the sea floor while avoiding flipper-nippers and sharks.
descriptions.c64:173133: Spell words correctly to keep a helicopter in the air; 400 words in 40 categories across beginner, intermediate and advanced levels.
descriptions.c64:173135: Oil's Well-style game: prospect for oil with a drilling rig without touching the enemies underground. Published in 64'er Sonderheft 54.
descriptions.c64:173136: An Oil's Well-style drilling game in which you prospect for oil while avoiding the hazards of the trade; published on Golden Disk 64 in July 1991.
descriptions.c64:173140: Horizontally scrolling shooter: destroy aliens that keep attacking in new formations. Published in 64'er Sonderheft 37.
descriptions.c64:173155: Arcade adventure across 384 screens of a haunted mansion, where touching ghosts knocks your ghost hunter off course, sometimes down a whole screen.
descriptions.c64:173156: MLBPA-licensed baseball featuring stars like George Brett, Ozzie Smith and Roger Clemens, plus the option of a Hall of Fame team; play a friend or the computer, or watch the computer play itself.
descriptions.c64:173157: Quiz game based on the late-1980s British TV show: three human or computer players each pick from 12 sport categories such as soccer, cricket and Pot Luck across seven rounds.
descriptions.c64:173158: 7Up-licensed strategy board game for up to four players: spread your colored spots from your corner by cloning into adjacent squares or jumping further.
descriptions.c64:173166: A 1987 rework of Omega Race with new character sets, sprites, hi-res pictures and selectable speeds; shoot the attacking Droid ships and the mines they drop.
descriptions.c64:173187: Text adventure where you captain a long-range maritime patrol aircraft at 15,000 feet over the Arzelean Sea, hunting enemy boats and submarines.
descriptions.c64:173188: Columns-like puzzle: drop groups of three colored blocks into a 6x18 grid and line up three of the same color.
descriptions.c64:173189: Crosshair military shooter inspired by Operation Wolf.
descriptions.c64:173190: Unfinished 1987 fighting game: kick enemies or attack with a gun, bazooka and grenades across two floors, backed by Rob Hubbard music.
descriptions.c64:173191: As agent Rip Steel, pilot a small submarine to destroy the Yellow Shadow's undersea mining bases while defending your own.
descriptions.c64:173192: Single-screen first-person shooter set at a church: aim at the windows and shoot the priests who appear every few seconds; two difficulty levels.
descriptions.c64:173193: Espionage action game: hunt through the mysterious Antimatter Complex for secret documents, with a two-player mode over modem.
descriptions.c64:173194: Infiltrate the military base that invaders from Zekloke have built on Mars, destroy it, and recover the hidden plans for a defense shield.
descriptions.c64:173195: Snake game for two players at once, published on Magic Disk 64 in June 1991.
descriptions.c64:173196: As a frog, hop between tiles and the blank island to bring all matching pieces together without stranding yourself.
descriptions.c64:173197: Space combat in 3D: hunt enemy saucers, using the scanner to track individual ships and to find your base.
descriptions.c64:173198: Clear colored stones within 99 seconds per level by matching identical ones, guiding an arrow-shaped figure that jumps between them.
descriptions.c64:173199: Push blocks so two or more identical squares meet and vanish; 32 levels on each of four difficulty settings, the last unlocked by beating hard mode.
descriptions.c64:173200: Puzzle game: move the four-ball Orbs into pillars to clear them from each level. Published on Magic Disk 64 in June 1994.
descriptions.c64:173201: As a new Starfleet Academy graduate commanding the training ship U.G.A.S. Republic, defend the Antares III region against the Krellan and Zaldron empires.
descriptions.c64:173219: Adventure set in King Elrad the Second's palace: restore the missing Orb of Light to its empty crystal cage before darkness takes the land.
descriptions.c64:173222: Lander game from Cassette 50: from a decaying orbit, pick a spot on a fissured high-gravity planet and touch down before fuel runs out.
descriptions.c64:173226: Parker Brothers' cartridge version of the Atari arcade game: as Luke Skywalker, Red Five, fly a first-person rail shooter that imitates the arcade's color vector graphics.
descriptions.c64:173231: Tetris variant where blocks of matching color and pattern combine to keep the well from filling; keep stacking until the counter reaches zero.
descriptions.c64:173235: Soccer management sim covering both sport and finances: lead a club from the German fourth division to the top league, reaching a goal chosen before play.
descriptions.c64:173240: 2D RPG set in Beryland in 1227, where the Ormus Cult has seized power; your hero starts on the southwest shore beside the city of Remfield.
descriptions.c64:173245: Single-screen shooter: hit an alien with your laser while dodging its fire, which blasts holes in the ground that restrict your movement and cost a life if touched.
descriptions.c64:173247: Scrolling platformer in which farmer Oskar takes on cow-sized killer wasps and cockroaches mutated by a reactor accident in a small New Arizona town.
descriptions.c64:173249: Humorous parody of sports compilations like California Games, with events such as cow milking and fishing.
descriptions.c64:173254: Arcade conversion: first-person space combat, shooting incoming fighters with a laser sight before fuel runs out; packaged with Fire One.
descriptions.c64:173268: Early party-based RPG: lead one to six fighters, priests, thieves and other classes through a multi-level dungeon, gaining loot and experience while characters age and can die.
descriptions.c64:173274: Flick-screen platformer in the style of Thing on a Spring starring a bouncing red-and-white ball, flipping switches across six themed levels, among them Kitchen, Toys and Plants, to open each exit.
descriptions.c64:173275: Two pink blobs square off beyond the city limits in this two-player-only sequel to Ouch!, each drifting around the screen and trying to drop heavy weights onto the other.
descriptions.c64:173300: Two-player-only space duel viewed from above, with Asteroids-style rotate-and-thrust ships trying to shoot each other down.
descriptions.c64:173319: Vertically scrolling space shooter: blast everything in sight except the diamond-shaped ship, which must be dodged.
descriptions.c64:173325: Shoot-'Em-Up Construction Kit sample game set in the Wild West: two outlaws fight through dangerous territory to escape to Mexico.
descriptions.c64:173326: Galaxian-style shooter with oddball enemies such as umbrellas, slices of toast, fish and snakes and ladders; released at Replay Expo 2011.
descriptions.c64:173329: Boulder Dash-style digger: collect a set number of diamonds before time expires, dropping boulders by clearing the earth beneath them.
descriptions.c64:173332: Collect every dot to advance while avoiding enemies that follow fixed routes.
descriptions.c64:173334: Multi-directional scrolling shooter: fly an advanced starfighter with a particle beam cannon into the Star Bee system to find the Star Queen's hive and destroy her.
descriptions.c64:173335: Collect treats around the stockade while dodging arrows from Native American attackers.
descriptions.c64:173340: Pac-Man clone with four difficulty levels and 25 starting lives.
descriptions.c64:173341: One to six players trade stock in four mining firms as prices rise and fall; whoever first reaches a million pounds wins.
descriptions.c64:173346: Paddington tries out the vanishing ink from his conjuring set while writing a postcard to Aunt Lucy in Peru, in this Collins storybook-and-cassette pack for young children.
descriptions.c64:173347: Pong variant for one or two players, scoring more for catching faster balls, with a flashing energy field at the center of the playfield.
descriptions.c64:173348: Single-player Tron-style trail game from the Crazy Corners and Arcade Action packs.
descriptions.c64:173376: Children type simple sentences like 'The girl jumps over the flower' and watch them animated, building short stories of around 40 words.
descriptions.c64:173377: A terrorist bomb has crashed a shuttle into the Stratton Air Terminal, cutting life support and leaving survivors trapped by active defense units; you are sent into the wreck.
descriptions.c64:173381: Defender-style shooter: protect human prisoners on the ground from aliens that abduct and kill them while firing at your ship.
descriptions.c64:173382: Hop around the world as a runaway pancake, grabbing fruit that birds knock down while avoiding hazards; released in Italy as Urca.
descriptions.c64:173383: Football career game: start as an 18-year-old striker in the English Fourth Division and chase promotion and trophies until retiring at 34, with moves to European and national teams possible.
descriptions.c64:173384: Football management where you are both manager and striker, taking your team from the English Fourth Division to the First, with chances to run a European or national side.
descriptions.c64:173385: Fly a small prop plane through stunts at an airshow, viewed in first-person 3D or a side-scrolling 2D mode.
descriptions.c64:173388: Hulk Hogan movie tie-in mixing space shooting, platform jumping and beat-'em-up action.
descriptions.c64:173413: Aliens have drained Earth's energy and hidden it in a cave at the world's end; with three armed shuttles, fly out to bring it back.
descriptions.c64:173427: Q*bert-style isometric puzzle: hop Pancho onto every square to paint it while avoiding the Mad Mexican Muncher; included in the French compilation 3 Super Jeux.
descriptions.c64:173436: Work a multi-level production line, gathering three kinds of parts that drop from chutes and assembling them in the right order to keep up with orders.
descriptions.c64:173439: Rescue parachutists dropping into the sea by catching them in your boat or throwing a net overboard; they jump in pairs or threes, and any you miss try to swim for it.
descriptions.c64:173477: Comic text adventure: track down the president of Paranoids Anonymous after being invited to its weekly meeting by members who will not reveal its location or the way in.
descriptions.c64:173494: Slide and drop pieces to match and remove them, opening up further combinations without blocking yourself in; published on Game On 1991/05.
descriptions.c64:173495: Interwar spy adventure: as French Secret Service agent Phillip Groucy, wake up penniless in a seedy Paris suburb and recover your stolen credit card.
descriptions.c64:173497: Horizontally scrolling shooter with attack waves, power-ups, mini-bosses and boss fights, published on Game On 1993/10.
descriptions.c64:173502: Based on the TV show in which kids from the four home nations of the UK competed on motorcycles, quad bikes, mini-hovercraft and jet skis.
descriptions.c64:173586: With the Emperor dead and the Parthian Empire splintered, command a king's army, hire mercenaries, form alliances and levy taxes to conquer rival city states and take the throne.
descriptions.c64:173587: Trivia game with 2,500 questions for one to four players or teams, played on four hand-held response controllers; game length and answer time are adjustable.
descriptions.c64:173588: UK driving theory quiz in 40 lessons, each covering a topic likely to come up in the written test.
descriptions.c64:173589: Adventure based on Francois Bourgeon's comic series: direct the heroes' choices through many locations and events, with the story branching on the paths you take.
descriptions.c64:173590: As a tour guide for 12 tourists who wander off and pocket priceless British treasures, search a maze of London streets to recover the missing objects.
descriptions.c64:173591: As a tour guide whose group's flight home has been moved up an hour, round up all 12 wandering tourists around Paris before it leaves.
descriptions.c64:173595: Two-player edition of the game OsWALD of the Ice Floes, which was first designed to be played by push-button telephone on Danish TV2's Eleva2ren show.
descriptions.c64:173614: Spy mission to locate a fighter jet armed with a nuclear warhead that vanished on a training flight, and defuse it; the game opens as a text adventure.
descriptions.c64:173640: Race a truck through nine European cities such as London, Brussels and Paris, beating the time limit on each section despite blind hills and roadworks.
descriptions.c64:173663: Fly an impulse-drive fighter to stop the Syntax assault on Earth by collecting ten radio-deactivation crystals and dropping them down the Syntax ventilation shaft.
descriptions.c64:173728: Table tennis against seven computer opponents for the championship, with exhibition and tournament modes and settings for match length and skill.
descriptions.c64:173729: Two programs for practicing multiplication tables from 1 to 10, for children aged six and up.
descriptions.c64:17373: Mondain and Minax left behind a child, Exodus, who now menaces Sosaria; lead a party of four adventurers across the land to find and destroy it.
descriptions.c64:173741: WWII tactical armor combat: pick a British, American, German or Russian force, build a team of tanks, tank destroyers and assault guns, and hunt the enemy while the computer takes care of technical details.
descriptions.c64:173742: The villain Vincent Ratatoui has stolen the world's cheese, and a martial-arts tortoise sets out across over 100 screens of platforms and ladders to get it back.
descriptions.c64:173747: Two to four players battle in tanks until one remains, across ten maps from deserts and snowfields to arenas, mountains and swamps, with an adjustable number of mines.
descriptions.c64:173750: To win Princess Kelly's hand, a prince must complete seven tasks set by her doubting father King Otto, starting with surviving a night outside the castle.
descriptions.c64:173753: Pac-Man clone with six levels: eat money while dodging the Taxmen trying to bankrupt you; modeled on Taxman for the Apple II.
descriptions.c64:173755: Overhead horizontal shooter against an alien invasion over six levels in three stages, the first modeled on Uridium's runs across a planet or spacecraft surface.
descriptions.c64:173756: Steer a tank through a trap-filled maze to find seven parts of the Hypercom machine; ammunition is limited, depots refill it once, and touching walls is fatal.
descriptions.c64:173757: Mixing strategy, action and crosshair shooting, lead Red Leader's anti-terrorist squad to a town under attack, with four difficulty levels, randomized attacks and 3D battles on over 8,000 maps.
