descriptions.c64:173768: Bookware text adventure based on Colin Kapp's science fiction stories: as Lt. Fritz van Noon, lead the Unorthodox Engineers to learn the purpose of an indestructible pillar of darkness.
descriptions.c64:173772: Sliding-block puzzle: maneuver the large red block out through the gap at the bottom by entering block numbers and directions; three invalid moves lose the puzzle.
descriptions.c64:173778: Vietnam War flight sim as an F-105 Thunderchief pilot, flying strike and defense-suppression missions into North Vietnam's Route Package target zones.
descriptions.c64:173786: Learn Spanish language and culture by exploring Spain, completing tasks such as visiting monuments, eating at restaurants and shopping at grocery and department stores.
descriptions.c64:173796: Battle of the Bulge wargame: as the German commander in December 1944, push division and regiment-sized units through the Ardennes and across the Meuse.
descriptions.c64:173799: Rescue Anacron, who meddled with your time machine, fell in, and is now tumbling through history.
descriptions.c64:173800: As a trans-temporal mercenary, fight through seven time zones from prehistory, the Middle Ages and the Wild West to Prohibition, WWII, the space age and 1980s New York.
descriptions.c64:173804: Text adventure: explore the countryside around your village to locate a time machine before you can use it.
descriptions.c64:173806: Rescue five warriors held in different eras, from the Primitive Age and Rome to the World Wars and Future World, each held by a henchman of Gylend.
descriptions.c64:173810: Seal eight portals that dark forces opened in the space-time continuum by returning objects to the Minds guarding them and forming spells from the runes they give.
descriptions.c64:173824: Five spelling and vocabulary games in which children travel to town with Tuk through four changing places on eight different vehicles, at adjustable difficulty.
descriptions.c64:173827: Text-only boxing sim with more than 600 fighters, including retired boxers at various points in their careers who can face each other across eras; adjust tactics between rounds.
descriptions.c64:173828: Chase a top-ten hit: walk a street visiting homes, a recording studio, a disco and a TV station as you create a song.
descriptions.c64:173832: Tactical wargame of the May-July 1942 battle for Tobruk in Libya, where control of the Allies' six supply points is vital.
descriptions.c64:173841: Early-learning package covering the alphabet and numbers, with memory and matching games.
descriptions.c64:173842: Control both Tomarc and Senta at once: Tomarc searches the caves for his magic sword, then frees Senta from her magical cage, avoiding rats and other dangers.
descriptions.c64:173843: Drag racing with tire and engine setup, shown in split first-person and side views; win four races in a 16-car bracket to take the title.
descriptions.c64:173844: Strategy game for one to ten music producers: starting with 75,000 pounds, fund songs at one of three budgets, naming the title and artist, with bigger spending making bigger hits.
descriptions.c64:173855: A top-hatted policeman searches four floors of rooms linked by corridors and a lift for clues, pinning the crime on one of seven suspects before time runs out.
descriptions.c64:173871: Golf with two 18-hole courses featuring traps and gophers, plus a driving range and putting green for practice.
descriptions.c64:173876: Switch traffic lights to steer cars, buses and motorbikes through the crowded streets of London, getting a set number of vehicles off the screen to advance.
descriptions.c64:173878: Drive a train collecting passengers along the track, scoring one point per carriage, while avoiding the Ghost Train; clear all passengers and enter the tunnel for more.
descriptions.c64:173880: Text-only management game: pick and train England's squad and follow matches through running commentary on the road to the World Cup.
descriptions.c64:173906: Three math games featuring a hungry space invader, a haunted house and a Digitosaurus.
descriptions.c64:173913: As Polly, walk beneath cards and flip them until you find the one requested; up to 52 cards are spread across a chosen number of screens, some hiding jokers.
descriptions.c64:173914: Towers of Hanoi puzzle, published on Game On 1992/12.
descriptions.c64:173915: Shoot-'Em-Up Construction Kit game steering Paul the beetle through a dangerous world where anything that moves is a threat; published on Magic Disk 64 1988/08.
descriptions.c64:173917: Collect green peas around a maze while a giant pea monster hunts you; swinging doors can be broken but the monster repairs them, and at times it can be eaten.
descriptions.c64:173918: For ages 4-8: solve randomly generated mazes to get Peanuts characters to their destinations.
descriptions.c64:173919: Rebuild Peanuts pictures split into four blanked sections by choosing the right piece for each, then watch an animation; timed or untimed.
descriptions.c64:173920: Dizzy-style arcade adventure in a medieval fantasy world: explore a castle and its surroundings to recover the Pearl of Dawn, fighting or avoiding enemies along the way.
descriptions.c64:173921: Frogger-style crossing game: get a pedestrian over a busy highway, past spiders and aliens and across a crocodile-filled stream to reach home.
descriptions.c64:173922: Joust-style action on a single screen of mountains and a glowing volcano, flying a pegasus against enemy riders.
descriptions.c64:173925: Turn-based strategy: move a castle across a checkerboard from bottom to top, with one to four moves per turn set at the start.
descriptions.c64:173926: Horizontally scrolling shooter guiding Peppi the dragon through a hostile cityscape, defeating bosses to reach each new area.
descriptions.c64:173930: Across 64 levels, brown blocks win over grey ones simply by touching them, but each brown block has a limited number of moves, so every step needs planning. No time limit, and passwords record your progress.
descriptions.c64:173932: Roll a ball over coloured tiles without falling off: green is solid ground unless cracked, blue slides you like ice to the next colour, and the flashing violet squares that must be collected vanish once crossed. One life, and an editor for building or changing levels.
descriptions.c64:173933: Checkers against the computer under standard rules, with pieces crowned on reaching the far side.
descriptions.c64:173939: Simulation of the 1905 Battle of Tsushima, where Japan's fleet defeated Russia's Baltic Fleet; one or two players, with strategic and combat-only scenarios.
descriptions.c64:173940: Horse racing program that takes form data for each horse and uses a prediction routine to suggest likely winners.
descriptions.c64:173959: Quiz on UK geography with five modes covering naming and locating towns, regions and mountain ranges.
descriptions.c64:173960: Detailed simulation, played one day at a time, of the WWII daylight strategic bombing campaign against Nazi Europe, tracking every serviceable aircraft before and after each mission.
descriptions.c64:173961: Uhg the hungry caveman climbs down vines through four cave levels to find five dinosaur eggs and bring them to the surface, clubbing small dinosaurs on the way.
descriptions.c64:173962: Casino simulation set in Trump Castle with blackjack, poker, roulette, craps, keno and slots, and an adjustable $10,000 default bet limit.
descriptions.c64:173963: WWII tactical land combat with American, German and Russian troops across nine scenarios, from open firefights to house-to-house battles.
descriptions.c64:173964: Text adventure: a wizard has trapped you in the underworld, and you must find a way out using verb-noun commands.
descriptions.c64:173965: As secret agent Rupert Pettigrew, track down five agents and the Safras sword in four parts; partly combines Shards' Pettigrew's Diary and Operation Safras.
descriptions.c64:173966: Stack falling polygons so their faces fit exactly, clearing complete horizontal lines to keep the tower low; released in Italy as Fadrika.
descriptions.c64:173967: Short adventure with odd puzzles in which you must reach the princess, who will then rescue you.
descriptions.c64:173980: Word game: grab letters off a rotating cube before your opponents and arrange them into words in your playing area.
descriptions.c64:173981: Two learning games on one cartridge: Number Nabber for arithmetic and Shape Grabber for recognizing shapes.
descriptions.c64:173982: One- or two-player space shooter: nearing your galactic outpost, attack an Alderon mothership orbiting above a settlement.
descriptions.c64:173985: Maze game across 250 rooms on four levels joined by elevators, collecting eight treasures as a squid-like character; finishers could enter a $500 prize drawing.
descriptions.c64:173986: Children aged 5-10 build and animate Wild West scenes from a set of critters, characters and shapes.
descriptions.c64:173990: Illustrated text adventure set in a sleepy English village where odd things start happening after Professor Blowitovitz moves in.
descriptions.c64:173992: Medieval fantasy platformer and scrolling shooter inspired by Ghosts'n Goblins, with a hero battling monsters; by Alberto Frabetti, who went on to write Dragon's Kingdom.
descriptions.c64:173993: As a master thief, descend through a Swiss bank's underground vaults to the chairman's chamber nine levels down and steal the OPEC oil deeds.
descriptions.c64:173994: Casino game with video poker, roulette, blackjack and slots, starting with $500; limits are $200 for blackjack and roulette and $5 for poker and slots.
descriptions.c64:174000: Egyptian-themed multi-screen platformer that borrows some sprites from Myth; published on Game On 1992/09.
descriptions.c64:174005: Computer jigsaw puzzles of 25 or 50 pieces, with or without outlines: study the picture, then move pieces into the empty square to rebuild it.
descriptions.c64:174007: One- or two-player shooter: roam a single screen guarding a central core from aliens over nine levels while its energy steadily drains.
descriptions.c64:174016: Fire a phaser at waves of attackers descending the screen; part of Cassette 50.
descriptions.c64:174017: Puzzle with four test tubes holding three colors each: stack them to reproduce the color combination shown by the lamps above the lower box.
descriptions.c64:174018: Crosshair shooter: hit as many Psychoballs as possible within one minute and compare scores with friends.
descriptions.c64:174022: In a future where cats are precious, travel between planets bartering cards and playing a poker-like game to raise the 8,000-cat ransom for your kidnapped cat.
descriptions.c64:174034: Top-down Formula 1 racing with eight cars differing in gearbox, acceleration and top speed, plus tunable tires, spoiler, dampers and steering.
descriptions.c64:174035: Tactical WWII Pacific naval wargame with four historical battles and a scenario builder; Japanese and US sides can both be human-controlled.
descriptions.c64:174036: Elected sheriff of Dodge City after Wyatt Earp was run out of town, you are now the target of the outlaw Cockeyed Frank Loving.
descriptions.c64:174040: Five minigames based on the German comic character Werner, including the bluffing dice game Meiern.
descriptions.c64:174041: Hamurabi with simple graphics: each turn, decide how much land to buy or sell and how much grain to feed your people and to plant, while random events intervene.
descriptions.c64:174045: Text adventure played in real time, set in 1885: as a sheriff, recover the loot a gang of bank robbers hid in town and get away, reacting quickly to random events.
descriptions.c64:174052: Motor trade sim: acquire gearboxes, tyres and engines to build cars, form syndicates, trade parts and buy dealerships while staying clear of bankruptcy.
descriptions.c64:174053: Multi-directional scrolling platformer in which up to four players guide hungry Nurds through 50 levels, each hiding four pieces of food.
descriptions.c64:174058: Transformed into Pegasus, Circe battles dragons, hawk men and skeletons to free Odysseus from a wizard's spell.
descriptions.c64:174059: As an anthropologist invited by your Soviet friend Sergio, investigate the lost civilization he has found in the Himalayas of Tibet.
descriptions.c64:174060: Vocabulary-building game for young children set in an adaptive storytelling environment; part of the Children's Collection pack.
descriptions.c64:174061: Put matching pieces next to each other to remove them, clearing each set completely, since a single leftover shape ends the game.
descriptions.c64:174062: Dr. Mario-style falling-block game: line up pills to wipe out viruses; published in 64'er 1994/12.
descriptions.c64:174064: One-button pinball: hold the space bar to set launch power and land the ball in all nine bins within 15 shots.
descriptions.c64:174067: Oil's Well clone: extend a pipeline from the tunnel entrance through the passages to collect oil, retracting it piece by piece with the fire button.
descriptions.c64:174072: A target word is hidden twice inside a grid of jumbled letters, and you frame it with a movable window. Alone you race a frog or butterfly that nibbles the letters away; two players each get their own window.
descriptions.c64:174078: Players take turns finding anagrams hidden in rows of letters on a grid, earning more for longer words and a bonus for using a whole row.
descriptions.c64:174083: Manage heavyweight boxers' careers from an icon-driven office, planning training around their strengths, weaknesses and injuries from earlier fights.
descriptions.c64:174084: Squash for up to eight players in single matches or tournaments, with an adjustable number of rounds, skill and ball type; only the server can score.
descriptions.c64:174087: Arcade soccer built around the 1990 World Cup in Italy with every competing nation under fictional player names, plus custom teams and two-player matches.
descriptions.c64:174090: Quiz on 166 countries in eight difficulty groups: each is marked on a hi-res world map and you name its capital or population.
descriptions.c64:174104: Rugby management: pick and train a national side, tend to injuries, and lead it from the third division to the first.
descriptions.c64:174108: Platform shooter in which Alberto boards pirate ships to rescue his girlfriend, held in one of the cabins.
descriptions.c64:174110: Deliver pizzas around a grid map by entering the coordinates of each order's address.
descriptions.c64:174113: The planet Nap is still occupied by PAO invaders a century after they arrived; fly an upgraded spaceship to liberate it. Released in Italy as Planet War.
descriptions.c64:174114: 2D fantasy RPG with a party of up to four humans, dwarves or elves, mixing melee and magic and spending gold from slain monsters on new gear.
descriptions.c64:174115: Shoot down attacking mini planets in this blaster by Richard Bayliss, released with Scene World #22.
descriptions.c64:174117: Moon Buggy-style driving game starring a Smurf in space.
descriptions.c64:174118: Yahtzee adaptation: roll five dice, reroll any of them up to twice, and fill categories from ones to sixes through full house, straights, chance and five of a kind.
descriptions.c64:174121: Pac-Man clone: guide Whirly around mazes collecting Alpha Particles while avoiding Zooks, grabbing Power Drain Plugs to make them safe to touch.
descriptions.c64:174122: Space Invaders-style game in which a wizard runs along the ground shooting down the thunderbolts that an angry Zeus hurls at him.
descriptions.c64:174124: Guide missiles into a fleet of UFOs speeding down to bomb your planet, with 20 missiles to down 10 UFOs and a hyperthrust for extra speed.
descriptions.c64:174125: Fly past asteroids and space mines, shooting the sides of plasma bolt barriers to clear a path but never the mines; part of Cassette 50.
descriptions.c64:174126: Pipe-fitting puzzle: add one shaped section at a time, previewed in the corner, to build your pipe network, with goals set by the chosen game type. Also released as Work Pipes.
descriptions.c64:174127: Puzzle for one or two players: bounce across a board whose squares crumble behind you to reach all squares of your color; landing on an empty space costs one of three lives.
descriptions.c64:174129: Lone survivor of an exploration mission, fight your way through a galaxy ruled by Zordian warlords in a constantly upward-scrolling shooter.
descriptions.c64:174139: Clear Alien Cycloids from each zone of a 7x7 grid, moving around the zone's edge and firing up to eight bullets at a time.
descriptions.c64:174140: Shoot the unpredictable Zwarks before they reach the bottom of the screen, where they become deadly; more appear as your score climbs.
descriptions.c64:174141: Top-down vertical shooter over four alien planets with pseudo-3D touches; steer and set forward speed, even stopping, while fighting tanks, turrets and planes.
descriptions.c64:174149: Shoot-'Em-Up Construction Kit game: pushed off course by a solar wind, a lost pilot ends up on the strange planet Sector RCM1972.
descriptions.c64:174152: Tennis against the computer or a friend, released on Magic Disk 64 1993/09.
descriptions.c64:174153: Play through 91 bridge deals devised by Alfred Sheinwold, paired with his book Bridge Puzzles Number 1, with guidance toward the correct play.
descriptions.c64:174164: Shoot-'Em-Up Construction Kit game that is not a shooter: Alain, locked in his countryside hotel room over an unpaid bill while the owner calls the police, makes his escape.
descriptions.c64:174176: Shoot-'Em-Up Construction Kit game: fight enemy mechs to liberate your oppressed world; published in Commodore Free #067.
descriptions.c64:174192: Turn-based tactical American football with 16-player squads, 11 on the field; each turn move any number of players, block, or set up a pass.
descriptions.c64:174193: Arkanoid-style game with 33 levels: break into the fortress of the tyrant Gohd on Gohdinia to free your captured friends.
descriptions.c64:174205: Horizontally scrolling space shooter in the vein of Armalyte, published on Game On 1991/12.
descriptions.c64:174206: Two-player strategy game on a lattice of atomic nuclei that hold two, three or four electrons depending on their position, all starting out neutral.
descriptions.c64:174207: Bounce Poga, a remote-controlled robodroid, through a mechanical world, avoiding spinning nuts and bolts, robot birds and electromagnetic coils; from the Red Ribbon Game Pak.
descriptions.c64:174208: Bounce around mazes on a pogo stick fixing bricks and collecting bonuses, repairing every brick before the hourglass empties.
descriptions.c64:174209: Two-player Pong remake with extra twists; the first to nine points wins.
descriptions.c64:174249: Not a playable game: this prank asks for a police security password but ignores whatever you type. It is believed to have been aimed at crackers who had pirated Crystal Computing releases.
descriptions.c64:17425: Nina, sister of the slain ninja from Saboteur, uses kung-fu moves across 700 screens to avenge him.
descriptions.c64:174250: Snake variant: as the lead wolf, touch party guests to recruit them into a growing polonaise line.
descriptions.c64:174252: Find the hop pattern that guides a frog safely across the pond to the farthest lily pad, choosing how many hops to make and in which direction at each step.
descriptions.c64:174268: Christmas activity collection with the Popples toys, combining simple games, mazes and music.
descriptions.c64:174282: Climb ladders and leap over shooting robots to collect the pots guarded on each floor.
descriptions.c64:174283: Klax-like puzzle as a restaurant pot washer: stack falling pots so five of the same type sit atop one another to clear them.
descriptions.c64:174286: As a German spy working for the Allies, break into an English POW camp, steal a set of plans and deliver them to the resistance within two hours.
descriptions.c64:17429: Compete in winter sports events such as ski jump, hot dog aerials, biathlon, bobsled, free skating and figure skating.
descriptions.c64:174298: Remix of Mega Starforce, a Space Invaders-style shooter subtitled Return to the Great Star.
descriptions.c64:174303: Pilot an outboard powerboat around a hazard-filled course, completing the required laps within a tight time limit; released in Italy as Fuori Bordo.
descriptions.c64:174304: Railway signalling sim: control traffic through the Leicester and Stafford power boxes over two four-hour shifts on a mid-1980s summer day, keeping trains to schedule.
descriptions.c64:174305: Railway signalling simulation of a power signal box on the Highlands routes.
descriptions.c64:174306: Guide an orb through a flashing maze to the exit before time expires; touching the walls sends you back to the start.
descriptions.c64:174307: An explosion has cut the northern polar thermal reactor's power links and contact with its engineers; set out to restore it. Made for RGCD's 2013 16KB cartridge competition.
descriptions.c64:174311: Pilot a lone spaceship down a narrow, heavily defended tunnel toward the core of the enemy's attack system, weaving past meteorites and hostile craft while firing lasers to clear the way.
descriptions.c64:174312: After the comet Blazer 76 swept past Delos V and poisoned it with gas, a handful of survivors in sector 98 must make their way to the central sector's spaceport, their only route off the planet.
descriptions.c64:174313: A falling-block puzzle in the Tetris mould for one or two players, controlled by joystick or keyboard, with high scores saved to disk.
descriptions.c64:174319: A two-player head-to-head contest: guard your own goal while knocking the ball into your rival's. Goals and obstacles move to new spots every round, and whoever leads after 20 rounds wins.
descriptions.c64:174320: Items drop from the top of the screen; catch them, shift them between columns and pair identical shapes to clear them. Two matched bombs also destroy the piece beneath, and a full column ends the game.
descriptions.c64:174321: Gollum of Fairlight's unofficial Arkanoid follow-up, released a year ahead of the real sequel: steer the Vaus to bounce the ball into the blocks, with capsules hidden behind some of them and five lives to spend.
descriptions.c64:174322: Serve as campaign manager in US presidential races from the 1960s up to the 1984 election, or build a custom candidate through a role-playing-style creation process and send them into the contest.
descriptions.c64:174323: An unofficial Arkanoid sequel with a fresh set of brick-breaking stages; after the mothership Arkanoid is destroyed, the escaping Vaus craft is once again trapped in space by an unknown captor.
descriptions.c64:174328: Steer a ball with the joystick to eliminate a set number of coloured pieces on each screen and move up to the next level, a puzzle that leans on quick reactions and dexterity.
descriptions.c64:174330: A Pong-style bat-and-ball game dressed up with bright, colourful graphics.
descriptions.c64:174335: A final unofficial Arkanoid level pack: keep the ball in play with the Vaus paddle until every block is gone, grabbing the helpful power-ups and dodging the harmful ones.
descriptions.c64:174341: A text adventure in which a wager with a millionaire commits you to breaking out of a prison.
descriptions.c64:174364: A short platformer by Steve Skillcorn set on the lunar surface in 1997, where experts from twelve nations have spent seven years perfecting P.R.O.B.E., a programmable robot battle unit.
descriptions.c64:174392: Two casino card games in one package: Banco, a baccarat simulation with its rules built in, and a game of draw poker.
descriptions.c64:174393: Take charge of a speedway motorcycle team, choosing which side to run at the outset, in a blend of racing and management simulation first released in Italy as Speedy in 1993.
descriptions.c64:174396: A tutorial program that teaches magic tricks, presenting them through simple on-screen graphics.
descriptions.c64:174399: A Shoot-'Em-Up Construction Kit game about blasting a path across an alien world, distributed by Binary Zone PD and later included on a Commodore Zone cover disk.
descriptions.c64:174402: In the 22nd century, an ordinary man is captured and rebuilt as the cyborg Argus to fight for the conquering Kansler, then turns on his masters; he and fellow cyborg Venix battle across the solar system for their freedom.
descriptions.c64:174403: Fly the Hell-Storm attack helicopter through an underground cave labyrinth in a horizontal shooter, chasing Lord Rübe, who stole the world's entire beer supply in a single night.
descriptions.c64:174409: As the half-man, half-machine Protectoid, fly low over the Earth destroying mines dropped by an alien mothership, collecting power-ups while a temporary shield wears away.
descriptions.c64:174438: Roll a ball through maze-like screens shooting everything in sight and running over stars for points, while steering clear of spikes that cannot be destroyed. Made with SEUCK.
descriptions.c64:174447: An unusual shooter-puzzle hybrid: move your ship up and down, fire to the right and pick from seven puzzle pieces to throw, only one of which fits. Pieces never run out; contact with enemies is what kills you.
descriptions.c64:174452: Gather every energy pod on each of 24 levels before the timer hits zero and the craft self-destructs, in a mix of arcade action and puzzle solving that won a Loadstar programming contest.
descriptions.c64:174453: A motorbike races up a busy highway, dodging reckless drivers in this Spy Hunter-flavoured Alf Yngve shoot-'em-up built with SEUCK. Planned by Psytronik for 1994 but shelved, it was finished and enhanced by Richard Bayliss in 2008, gaining a two-player option.
descriptions.c64:174456: A Pac-Man variant with no ghost pen and no wraparound tunnels; new ghosts emerge from existing ones or from the middle of the maze.
descriptions.c64:174457: Steer a fairy through the air dodging flying Christmas puddings; each hit drains energy, and the game ends when it runs out.
descriptions.c64:174458: A sparse shooter with a strategic bent, full of ladders and routes for creeping up on enemies, first given away on a Commodore Format cover disk.
descriptions.c64:174460: Dodge tanks and bulldozers while keeping the snakes from spreading out of control.
descriptions.c64:174510: Guide a puppy through 24 house screens of floors and ladders, eating ten pieces of fruit on each while jumping over holes and ducking under four birds that fly back and forth.
descriptions.c64:174511: A horizontal shooter built around a bouncing ball: release it in order to fire, recover it by touching it with the button held, and carry it upward before its limited bounces are used up.
descriptions.c64:174512: A statistics-driven basketball simulation for replaying single games or whole college seasons, past or present, with a Stat Compiler that keeps a permanent record; teams span 1960s UCLA through the 1980s.
descriptions.c64:174583: A box-pushing puzzle in the Sokoban style: shove crates onto their marked spots, taking care not to trap yourself, since a box can only move when there is free space beside it.
descriptions.c64:174587: Two players race each other to solve a 5x5 sliding-tile puzzle first.
descriptions.c64:174621: A SEUCK shooter designed for two players working together, as a heroic duo storms a giant floating prison fortress where aliens are holding hostages.
descriptions.c64:174623: A picture puzzle with eight images to choose from plus adjustable difficulty and timer; the screen is split into the scrambled pieces, a clock and the frame to fill.
descriptions.c64:174624: Each Incan gate is split into nine sections, one of which breaks the pattern; spot the odd one out before time expires to continue the journey.
descriptions.c64:174625: A 25-piece sliding puzzle: return the numbered tiles to their proper order to reassemble a larger picture.
descriptions.c64:174626: A timed tile puzzle: the computer scrambles the blocks of a picture shown in the top right corner, and the player must restore them against the clock.
descriptions.c64:174643: A jigsaw-style game in which every piece is supplied and must be locked into its correct place to score points and complete the picture.
descriptions.c64:174648: An isometric puzzle-platformer modelled on Q*bert, later reissued in Italy on the Go Games tape series.
descriptions.c64:174649: One or two players climb a pyramid by answering multiplication questions, moving up a step for each correct answer given within ten seconds, with three levels of question difficulty.
descriptions.c64:174650: A maze-like platformer with many branching paths but only one exit, populated by enemies that move entirely at random.
descriptions.c64:174651: Explore the ten-level Pyramid of Pyro in the desert of Lost Sands, gaining experience and seeking the Eternal Flame, in a simple adventure with role-playing elements; you may leave at any point.
descriptions.c64:174656: A fan-made Lode Runner edition with 104 new levels from 4711-Soft and blue bricks instead of red; a damaged copy in circulation has only 21 working levels.
descriptions.c64:174659: Another fan edit of Lode Runner, with bright green bricks and 127 levels, 32 of them new and the rest reused from Lode Runner II; its story concerns Egyptian statues from Giza stolen by the collector Goldstar.
descriptions.c64:174660: A fan edit of Lode Runner with blue bricks and 107 levels, only 14 of them new; the rest are borrowed from the second and fourth fan editions.
descriptions.c64:174661: A remixed Lode Runner by DrHonz of Reengine & Mod, also called Hansmanns Lode Runner, updated in 2010 and reworked in 2016 as the cleaned-up Tricky Mix.
descriptions.c64:174732: Four-sided Arkanoid: each player handles a pair of paddles on the screen edges to clear the stones, catching bonus items released by some of them but avoiding the skulls.
descriptions.c64:174733: Four-in-a-row across four stacked levels, a four-dimensional take on noughts and crosses for one or two players against a human or the computer.
descriptions.c64:174734: Arkanoid-style brick breaking for two players cooperating on the same screen.
descriptions.c64:174735: Drop silver spheres from above to form lines of four in any direction, which then vanish; the computer opponent drops two pieces per turn, and some pieces recolour ones already placed.
descriptions.c64:174736: A tricky isometric collecting game starring a Pac-Man-like character, blending ideas from Pac-Man, Marble Madness and several other games.
descriptions.c64:17475: In Sosaria, ravaged for a thousand years by the sorcerer Mondain, a lone hero must assemble a time machine and travel back to defeat him before he becomes invulnerable.
descriptions.c64:17476: Minax, Mondain's apprentice, seeks vengeance on the hero who slew her master and throws history into chaos; travel through different eras of time to track down and stop the enchantress.
descriptions.c64:174901: A re-release of the Apple II adventure Dondra: A New Beginning, with cartoon-style graphics and typed commands; the hero is pulled into another dimension to face and overthrow the villain Colnar.
descriptions.c64:174909: Up to four players drive trucks, hauling building materials from supply depots to construction sites and using map scales to measure distances across two maps.
descriptions.c64:174910: Play the ghost of someone who once died in quicksand, throwing ropes to a man and his dog so they can climb out, with devils and pebbles appearing on later levels.
descriptions.c64:174933: A trivia board game on 26 hexagons: move to a neighbouring space each turn and claim it by answering a question; players speak their answer aloud, then report whether they got it right.
descriptions.c64:174937: A trivia game for one to eight players: tackle odd questions generated by eight malfunctioning satellites orbiting Earth, combining knowledge with strategy to get aboard and destroy them.
descriptions.c64:174945: Gather the green Moonunits and the blue energy pills, lift off from the pad when fuelled, shoot aliens in flight and land again to refuel; clear all Moonunits and aliens to leave through the exit hole.
descriptions.c64:174964: A racing game for up to eight players via the poly.play adapter, with countryside, desert and city tracks and new courses unlocked by collecting stars.
descriptions.c64:174988: Drive around a maze collecting gas while avoiding other cars and potholes.
descriptions.c64:174989: A quiz of facts and trivia about the US states.
descriptions.c64:174991: Run a racing team: budget for maintenance, sign sponsors and follow championship points in pursuit of the overall title.
descriptions.c64:174992: Help Barry the Bear, stranded on an alien planet, gather food from colourful gardens for a feast while avoiding the angry alien bugs that guard them.
descriptions.c64:174994: A vertical shooter in which you battle your way back to your mothership.
descriptions.c64:174997: A cooperative educational game for two to six players stranded on a riverbank after a rafting accident, who must work together to build a new raft and escape downriver.
descriptions.c64:174998: A two-player duel shooter: since neither the Omega nor the Theta galaxy can win their war, each side sends its best pilot into a fight to the death.
descriptions.c64:175097: Losing altitude after being hit at Pearl Harbor, a kamikaze pilot must bomb New York's skyscrapers flat to land, repair the plane and take off again to attack new areas.
descriptions.c64:175098: Grab all the treasure while dodging flapping monsters that speed up and grow more aggressive with each cleared level.
descriptions.c64:175106: Control the signals and points around Penzance, routing every kind of train so passenger services run to time and contracted schedules are met.
descriptions.c64:175109: Rail traffic control at Birmingham: set routes for passenger and freight movements, keeping services punctual and honouring timetable contracts.
descriptions.c64:175111: Direct the train movements around Buxton, juggling passenger services and other traffic so everything keeps to the timetable and contracts are fulfilled.
descriptions.c64:175173: Run the signalling at Doncaster, threading passenger and freight trains through the junctions on schedule to meet contracted timings.
descriptions.c64:175175: Manage train movements into and out of Liverpool Lime Street, setting routes so passenger services stay punctual and timetable contracts are met.
descriptions.c64:175177: Take over rail traffic control at Reading, steering trains of all types through the area on time to satisfy the contracted schedule.
descriptions.c64:175178: Signal trains through Leeds City, keeping passenger services punctual and every scheduled movement on track to meet the contracts.
descriptions.c64:175179: Handle the rail traffic at Carlisle, routing passenger and freight trains through the station area in line with the timetable and its contracts.
descriptions.c64:175180: Control the busy rail network at Manchester Piccadilly, setting routes for every train so services run punctually and contracted timings are met.
descriptions.c64:175181: Route trains around Bristol Temple Meads, keeping passenger services to time and meeting the contracted schedule for every movement.
descriptions.c64:175183: Oversee rail traffic at Peterborough, guiding passenger and freight trains through the area on schedule to fulfil the timetable contracts.
descriptions.c64:175221: An environmental game named after the sunk Greenpeace ship, with seven campaigns in different game styles based on real Greenpeace actions, such as blocking pipes to stop nuclear waste escaping while dodging mutated wildlife.
descriptions.c64:175222: A set of ten games, puzzles and activities, with results that can be printed out and shared.
descriptions.c64:175223: A motorcycle rally through the African desert across four stages, each unlocked only by finishing the previous one inside the time limit.
descriptions.c64:175244: A sample adventure supplied with The Graphic Adventure Creator: find enough gold to pay the ransom for a kidnapped king.
descriptions.c64:175245: A polished falling-block puzzle in the Tetris style, with side-by-side play for two.
descriptions.c64:175344: Fly through space dodging everything that comes at you.
descriptions.c64:175347: Steer a nimble radio-controlled racing car along a course full of computer-driven vehicles that swerve and feint as they try to ram it head-on.
descriptions.c64:175560: A multi-genre game of separate sections modelled on Space Invaders, Tetris, Frogger and other well-known titles, mixing puzzles, shooting and action.
descriptions.c64:175600: The sequel to Reactor, this time a horizontally scrolling space shooter crowded with skulls.
descriptions.c64:175601: In the year 2990, the cooling system at the nuclear station beside the town of Barninghum overheats, setting off an emergency evacuation.
descriptions.c64:175603: Four word games for children aged three to seven that build reading and spelling: a word sorter, picture labelling, the Word Train and a memory-style matching game.
descriptions.c64:175643: A text-only adventure: starting on a beach, search a small island kingdom for the King's stolen Crown Jewels and any other treasure to bring back.
descriptions.c64:175644: A maze collecting game in the Pac-Man mould.
descriptions.c64:175645: As a galleon, defend the city in each realm by firing cannonballs at invaders while friendly farm carts try to reach it and bad weather hampers you. Made with SEUCK.
descriptions.c64:175646: A tile-flipping logic puzzle with over 100 levels: each move inverts the chosen square and its neighbours, and the grid must be turned one colour before time runs out to purge a virus from a nuclear plant's computer.
descriptions.c64:175683: Kick enemies from just the right distance to defeat enough of them to earn a key, use each key to close one gate, then finish off the rest to move on to the next level.
descriptions.c64:175691: A word memory test: as words flash up, use the joystick to mark each one as new or already seen, with repeats arriving quickly.
descriptions.c64:175692: A Robbo-like puzzle: guide a robot to gather every screw on the board while avoiding magnets, nuclear signs and other hazards, covering magnets with boxes so they cannot pull it in.
descriptions.c64:175732: A Lunar Lander-style game: get past the asteroid belt, land to pick up stranded scientists, then fight back up to dock with the mothership.
descriptions.c64:175733: A word with letters missing drifts slowly down the screen; fill the gaps by choosing letters from the alphabet along the bottom before it lands.
descriptions.c64:175736: A six-level platformer by Jason Kelk printed as a type-in listing in Retro Gamer issue 100, squeezed into under 4 KB of code and data.
descriptions.c64:175745: A boxing simulation in which you manage fighters from a roster of more than 45 greats across eight weight classes; one or two players, or let the computer run both corners.
descriptions.c64:175746: An Electric Company educational game for practising spelling, rhyming and word recognition on a spinning word machine.
descriptions.c64:175747: A two-player business game: bizlings stranded on Planet Simian must earn enough money to buy paint and repair their ship's damaged shield.
descriptions.c64:175748: Space hero Brad Stallion is sent by the Federated Government to stop The Tribe, a band of Amazon raiders terrorising the galaxy, helped by the ship's computer Sandie in an illustrated adventure across two planets.
descriptions.c64:175749: Two text adventures: a clock-seller mystery in which Holmes and Watson look into the death of antique clock dealer Otto Meinwold, and a second case involving the Rosetta Stone.
descriptions.c64:175750: The King of Averon sends his son to slay Skariten, a dragon that has ravaged the land for two hundred years and cannot be harmed by any spell or weapon.
descriptions.c64:175751: An illustrated text adventure: with a map from an old sea chest left by your great-grandfather, search Skull Island for its buried treasure.
descriptions.c64:175752: Leap from a plane over a gorge and parachute down while avoiding the protected condors.
descriptions.c64:175757: A stress-reduction program designed by Timothy Leary, with a few game-like elements.
descriptions.c64:175767: Play a single one-armed bandit, stopping whenever you like, while the program tracks the money paid in and won.
descriptions.c64:175774: An updated one-armed bandit simulation with brighter colours and fruit images that tracks stakes and winnings; included in Timeworks' second Programming Kit.
descriptions.c64:175775: Race a futuristic hoverbike against computer-controlled rivals across alien planet surfaces, avoiding collisions to reach the finish first.
descriptions.c64:175805: A text-based strategy game about a rogue F-16 pilot carrying a nuclear weapon toward an American city, built around a list of possible targets and fail-safe codes.
descriptions.c64:175889: A text adventure: track down your enemy Dave by following clues and talking to everyone, then take your revenge before getting the band back together at The Nip club to land a recording contract.
descriptions.c64:175897: Dock manually with the deserted Earth Orbital Station 1, then explore the damaged station, which shows signs of alien intrusion, to find a way to contact Earth.
descriptions.c64:175942: A drawing program for doodling, sketching and painting on screen.
descriptions.c64:175945: Stickybear lands in sticky situations, such as needing enough balloons to get over a small wall, and children aged six to nine solve arithmetic problems to rescue him.
descriptions.c64:175946: Numbered ducks swim around a pool; toss rings around them so their numbers add up to the target shown on the scoreboard. Aimed at ages 8 to 12.
descriptions.c64:175947: Drive a truck around an overhead map collecting produce from farms and delivering it to a depot while practising time skills; one of the three maps is printed in the manual and the other two are secret.
descriptions.c64:175960: Three text adventures in one package: History's Twist, A Place of Safety and, finally, Challenge of the Pirate King.
descriptions.c64:175962: A Trivial Pursuit-style quiz board game for two to four players, with colour-coded questions on Geography, History, Science & Nature, Sport & Leisure, Arts & Literature and Entertainment.
descriptions.c64:175966: Trapped in a chamber crossed by seven tunnels, your ship slides up and down a central vertical corridor, darting into the tunnels to blast the enemies that stream along them.
descriptions.c64:175969: A Hungarian joystick-driven adventure in which you travel through time to save the Earth, and the four items chosen at the start decide your chances; English text was added unofficially in 2019.
descriptions.c64:175970: The Muppets teach computer literacy through five activities, including steering the ship with Kermit through a Logo-style programming language, an arcade game played over Sam the Eagle's objections, and a joke library.
descriptions.c64:176012: A children's edition of the TV game show for ages 8 to 15: one team member draws on the big board and the other guesses what it shows, often a common phrase pictured literally.
descriptions.c64:176015: Two birds perch on letter towers at either side of the screen as letters and words of up to four letters grow and drift toward the players, who race to pick the right match with the joystick.
descriptions.c64:176016: A Yahtzee-style dice game for up to four players: roll, re-roll a limited number of times and aim for straights, full houses and multiples of a kind.
descriptions.c64:176017: A Quill-made text adventure with a verb-noun parser: in 3065, with Earth's fuel reserves nearly exhausted, you must find two Zacaron crystals to save the planet.
descriptions.c64:176027: As Cedric, a vampire without teeth, fetch your dentures from the dentist so you can feed again, then escape town while steering clear of garlic and crucifixes.
descriptions.c64:176093: A version of Reversi with distinctive graphics: place discs to outflank the opponent's pieces and flip them to your colour.
descriptions.c64:176094: The board game Reversi on screen: trap the opponent's discs between your own to turn them over, aiming to own most of the board.
descriptions.c64:176095: Your ship stays fixed while the joystick rotates everything around it; collect power-ups, destroy asteroids and destroy or avoid aliens, building firepower and guarding your shields.
descriptions.c64:176098: An electronic picture word book for children aged five to eight, with scenes such as an airport and a grocery store and hundreds of labelled objects to build vocabulary.
descriptions.c64:176116: Move a turret along the bottom of the screen and fire upward at a small character bouncing around, hitting it before the timer at the top runs out.
descriptions.c64:176118: To decide which charity inherits his estate, the dying Mr. Dillworth sets riddles; as the last candidate, armed with three hints, search his premises in an adventure that plays much like a choose-your-own-adventure book.
descriptions.c64:176127: A circus game: tap fire to make a man bounce higher, then launch a woman into the air off a see-saw and position her so the catchers can grab her. Released in Italy as Circus.
descriptions.c64:176139: Run left and right through side-scrolling levels, climbing ladders and riding lifts between floors, switching between melee and a laser gun to kill flying aliens; F3 opens a bat-and-ball sub-game.
descriptions.c64:176144: Defend a castle tower by dropping balls on the invaders as they climb its wall.
descriptions.c64:176145: Flee pursuers in a speedboat, dropping mines and trying to steer them into obstacles in the water. Released in Italy as Boats.
descriptions.c64:176148: A two-player speedboat race on one of eight courses, collecting a set number of flags while avoiding walls that slow you down.
descriptions.c64:176154: A stock-trading game for one to four players, who alternate buying and selling shares and putting money into real estate and money markets, with play divided into quarters.
descriptions.c64:176155: Drive a Corvette down the road using its built-in weapons to destroy the vehicles trying to stop you reaching the end.
descriptions.c64:176157: An illustrated text adventure in which the secret of life is hidden inside the walls of two houses, and you know the address of only one of them.
descriptions.c64:176158: A geography game: drive a top-down road trip through one of six real US regions, following the roads and avoiding thunderstorms, mailboxes and falling rocks.
descriptions.c64:176162: A horizontally scrolling shooter in which you blast any car that tries to force you off the road. Released in Italy as Speedy.
descriptions.c64:176171: Search the rooms of a lost tomb for four Sacred Tablets from a first-person view, choosing between three numbered doors in each room while avoiding mummies, snakes and ghosts.
descriptions.c64:176214: A scrolling platformer in which you guide a bouncing ball safely through each level to the exit.
descriptions.c64:176218: As a robot, blast other robots to pieces across eight levels.
descriptions.c64:176219: A Berzerk-style shooter: destroy robots and flee an invincible pursuer, with enemies that can also fire diagonally.
descriptions.c64:176223: Race through an asteroid belt without hitting the deadly rocks, where speed is essential.
descriptions.c64:176224: Command four squadrons of Tornado jets against Soviet arms factories at Helsinki, Magdeburg, Kiev and Belgrade, which are defended by surface-to-air missiles.
descriptions.c64:176251: A Boulder Dash clone using only four on-screen colours: rocks never roll diagonally and crush you if you linger beneath them, gems do not fall, and there is no timer.
descriptions.c64:176252: The second Boulder Dash-style game in the Rockfall series, about mining the energy-producing gems of Rockfall as supplies run low. Released in Italy as Crokko.
descriptions.c64:176262: In this flick-screen platformer you gather the required disks and keys on each level, then head for the far right edge. Punching blocks reveals bonuses, umbrellas give brief invulnerability and boots add speed. A 1993 64'er contest entry written mostly in BASIC.
descriptions.c64:176304: Learn logic circuits by moving a square through rooms stocked with logic gates (AND, OR, NOT), flip-flops, clocks and delays, picking them up and wiring them into circuits after a tutorial.
descriptions.c64:176306: Two players at once travel through many countries, navigating a shifting maze on each screen to collect objects like smiley faces and light bulbs, with the terrain growing trickier as they go.
descriptions.c64:176350: Collect a required number of cells in this rolling-ball game by Gábor Gaspar, who billed it as a legend of rolling balls.
descriptions.c64:176352: Rule the Roman Empire in the 5th century AD as barbarian threats mount, on a top-down map of Europe with abstract unit symbols, where most of the play centres on the economy.
descriptions.c64:176427: Space Invaders with boss fights added, by Gábor Csendes.
descriptions.c64:176429: Row downstream while avoiding sandbars, islands and other obstacles. Released in Italy as Canoa.
descriptions.c64:176430: Against the clock and with limited jumps, knock tiles out of the bottom row to create matches among the rest, clearing every tile to reach the next level.
descriptions.c64:176431: Answer questions correctly to make your way through a party.
descriptions.c64:176432: As a thief working through a string of banks, you hunt for the combinations to three safes in each while dodging electric clouds, laser beams and other hazards. Ivan Venturi's early game was meant for Simulmondo in 1986 but stayed unreleased until Ready64 recovered it in 2011.
descriptions.c64:176433: A carefully balanced Pac-Man clone whose joystick control demands precise directions at corners.
descriptions.c64:176434: A 3x3x3 Rubik's Cube on screen, twisted face by face with animated rotations, with the option of letting the computer work out the solution for you.
descriptions.c64:176435: Manage one of 16 Rugby League clubs, aiming to climb from Division 2 to win the Division 1 title and several cups.
descriptions.c64:176439: Escape a demon dungeon by reaching the top of the screen while two monster guards chase you and try to cut you off.
descriptions.c64:176514: A Hansel and Gretel-inspired platformer: search for two children lost in a faraway land across 32 levels of desert sand, rain and snow.
descriptions.c64:176516: A single-screen platformer based on the story of Samson from the Book of Judges, offering many play options.
descriptions.c64:176520: Govern a city-state in 15th-century Italy as a merchant prince, battling nature and up to five other hot-seat players to rise through titles from Count and Marquis to Grand Duke and beyond.
descriptions.c64:176527: Fly around a space station collecting items while avoiding enemies.
descriptions.c64:176528: A lander game written in BASIC, with 24 phases to get through and an ending sequence.
descriptions.c64:176529: Forced to land with drained energy near a deserted mining base, search its maze of puzzles for Dilithium crystals to refuel your ship.
descriptions.c64:176609: Shoot down the plaque saucers and sweets before they reach your teeth.
descriptions.c64:176610: A Simon Says-style memory game: repeat a pattern of signals that grows longer each round.
descriptions.c64:176612: Run a motel for ten days, setting prices to fill rooms and earn as much as possible, a simple lesson in supply and demand with the best price changing each game.
descriptions.c64:176613: An adventure in which you recover 20 treasures, each marked with an asterisk in its name, and return them to their proper place.
descriptions.c64:176615: As Caliph, ruler of Iraq, recover the sacred Sceptre stolen by an evil wizard who turned your palace into a labyrinth of traps and puzzles, dodging enemies and making platform jumps.
descriptions.c64:176617: Guide an Indiana Jones-like explorer through a house collecting bags of gold before time runs out, while a ghost gives chase. Five levels and four speed settings, all from a 20-line program.
descriptions.c64:176618: A falling-block game built on rock-paper-scissors: stack scissors on paper, paper on rock and rock on scissors to clear both pieces.
descriptions.c64:176620: A SEUCK vertical shooter across five levels, where wiping out a whole enemy formation leaves a capsule granting a power-up such as weapon upgrades or a satellite.
descriptions.c64:176638: An Arkanoid clone with its own music and intro; the original release crashes on NTSC machines, a problem fixed in later updated versions.
descriptions.c64:176678: Scrambit: answer trivia questions on four topics by unscrambling the letters of the answer, for one to four players, with five to ten questions and 10 to 60 seconds for each.
descriptions.c64:176746: Shrunk to thumbtack size by a newly discovered magic dust and planted inside a small saltwater fish with a homing device, reach a foreign shore undetected while avoiding killer sharks.
descriptions.c64:176752: Survive a night in Windward House above Smuggler's Cove, then board a ghost ship to break Captain Thorne's curse and find pirate treasure.
descriptions.c64:176757: A mostly text-based history program about early European explorers, with four game modes for learning about them or testing your knowledge.
descriptions.c64:176801: A Defender-inspired shoot-'em-up made for the 2011 SEUCK competition, without the radar window.
descriptions.c64:176842: Sequel to Dungeons of Magdarr: Magdarr has escaped and must be hunted down again, using your existing party or a new one, with new monsters, magic and combat routines.
descriptions.c64:176862: Sent by King Scott into Adventure Land, recover REAPER, the Golden Sword that alone protects the kingdom from attack.
descriptions.c64:176891: The miser Mr. Stone has died, reportedly leaving his estate to whoever opens his safe; explore his property with two-word commands to find it.
descriptions.c64:176892: Explore a house for five jewels, then set them in a sword and use it to escape.
descriptions.c64:176893: Collect diamonds in a maze full of invisible traps and walls, using shields that each disable one trap and dodging wandering smiling monsters.
descriptions.c64:176905: A Simon-style memory game meant for parties.
descriptions.c64:176906: Two games in one: a run-and-avoid section and a beat-'em-up.
descriptions.c64:176941: A tile-matching logic puzzle in the vein of Sarakon: pick pairs of matching symbols, subject to rules on the line that connects them.
descriptions.c64:177031: A naval strategy simulation of a hypothetical 1996 Pacific war between Soviet and US forces; one or two players command each side's main naval and naval air forces as theatre commander.
descriptions.c64:177032: A horizontally scrolling space shooter pieced together by Happy Hacker from graphics borrowed from Armalyte, Into Oblivion and Shadow Skimmer, credited to Magic Soft in 1989.
descriptions.c64:177136: A Scramble-style horizontal shooter: fire at or bomb fuel dumps to top up reserves and push as far as possible into a twisting shaft.
descriptions.c64:177137: Hired by Alonzo Erastus Horton to recover the stolen golden key to San Diego, the city he is founding, track it down for a big reward.
descriptions.c64:177138: Caught in an earthquake, rescue the other survivors and escape, using a simple verb-noun parser that only reads two letters per word.
descriptions.c64:177139: A side-scrolling platformer: collect the required number of bottles in each level before the time runs out to progress.
descriptions.c64:177214: Help Robo-Bird match toy parts by shape, colour and size, an early-learning exercise in comparing characteristics.
descriptions.c64:177218: An undersea shooter: fire a spear gun at sharks.
descriptions.c64:177219: A two-player contest in which each shark races to eat its quota of fish and divers; the first to reach it wins.
descriptions.c64:177224: A horizontally scrolling two-player sequel: eat as many divers and fish as possible before time runs out, with some food hiding behind the scenery.
descriptions.c64:177226: A Breakout variant with a sheep theme.
descriptions.c64:177227: Sheep battle foxes once more in this deluxe sequel to Sheep vs Fox, a Shoot-'Em-Up Construction Kit game by Alf Yngve with fresh obstacles, comic touches and a country-style tune. Psytronik included it as a bonus alongside Sheepoid DX and Woolly Jumper.
descriptions.c64:177228: A two-player strategy game on an 18-by-11 grid: each player moves a black or white sheepdog among six black and six white sheep, with black's pen in the top left and white's in the bottom right.
descriptions.c64:177231: Push all the red hearts into the dark squares to advance, in a puzzle with small font-like graphics, varied opponents and objects, and an editor.
descriptions.c64:177232: A Columns-like falling-block game with balls instead of blocks, which can also be rotated diagonally.
descriptions.c64:177234: A run-and-gun shooter with vertical scrolling, in the vein of Commando and the Rambo: First Blood Part II tie-in.
descriptions.c64:177415: Arrange all the pieces on screen so their colours and positions match the target pattern shown at the bottom.
descriptions.c64:17748: Roll a face around a maze and rotate its sections to link each one to the source at the centre, turning the whole maze green to move on.
descriptions.c64:177493: Fly a helicopter through a maze without touching the walls, dodging falling rocks to reach the exit.
descriptions.c64:177506: A Guitar Hero-style rhythm game played with a guitar controller: hit notes in five coloured columns in time with the music to keep the applause meter up.
descriptions.c64:177507: A tactical wargame of the World War II North African campaign between Axis and Allied forces, starting from Italy's 1940 advance from Libya into Egypt.
descriptions.c64:177512: Steer a droid vertically past security bots, collecting disks to defeat a computer virus threatening every machine in the world.
descriptions.c64:177513: A text adventure set in a dark future on a dying Earth, beginning at a deserted metro station and leading to the enigmatic sign of the Sphinx.
descriptions.c64:177530: A collection of joke programs: an annoying repeating message, Sillydata, a Sillypoem and a Sillycrisis to react to.
descriptions.c64:177531: A psychedelic twist on Breakout, best played with a second player.
descriptions.c64:177535: A top-down minigolf game over an 18-hole course, each hole a single screen with its own shape and obstacles or gates.
descriptions.c64:177536: A turn-based two-player strategy game mixing action and interactive fiction, with the kings of Soregno and Saratosa at war on a divided, scrolling screen.
descriptions.c64:177537: A one-player shootout from the Cassette 50 collection: hit the robot before it hits you.
descriptions.c64:177538: An 11th-century crusader from Manchester, swept down the Alcoraz River into the Monegros Desert after tripping over a rock, has lost his sword in this 2D platformer.
descriptions.c64:177539: Place each stone the computer hands you so that it matches every neighbour in pattern, colour or both, racing a timer. Filling a row or column scores a bonus, largest for a single colour, and clears it. Played solo or by two.
descriptions.c64:177546: Skate the bowl, dodge obstacles and pull tricks to beat an opponent or your own best score.
descriptions.c64:177547: A scrolling platformer entered in the 4K category of the 2003 Minigame Competition.
descriptions.c64:177604: Four skill-building programs: Typing Tutor, Speed Reader, Memory Builder and Decision Maker.
descriptions.c64:177605: A timed slalom: ski through the gates as quickly as possible.
descriptions.c64:177608: A single-screen racer for up to two players where the first car to complete the set number of laps wins, with several car types and adjustable vehicle colours.
descriptions.c64:177618: A home planetarium program that models the night sky for studying the stars.
descriptions.c64:177633: Fly through ten levels of space hazards, avoiding rocks, comets, shields, platforms and space stations; a crash sends you back to the start of the level.
descriptions.c64:177635: A low-altitude run over an unknown spaceship as the final test of pilot training: race along the safe path, avoiding the black blocks, to join the galactic elite.
descriptions.c64:177637: Start with $10,000 and grow it by trading commodities, each turn representing a week of market activity, in a follow-up to Millionaire.
descriptions.c64:177664: Collect the stars the hero scattered on his reckless trip across the galaxy, over 40 side-scrolling levels, gathering enough on each planet and reaching the exit before time runs out.
descriptions.c64:177665: Sled downhill as fast as possible while avoiding the berms that would tip you over.
descriptions.c64:177666: Push blocks around to form images.
descriptions.c64:177669: As a hungry ghost, open your mouth to catch food and keep it shut to avoid the bombs.
descriptions.c64:177671: Sliding block puzzles with four images to choose from and a difficulty set by the number of rows and columns.
descriptions.c64:177675: A simple boxing game against a range of opponents.
descriptions.c64:177676: Slynky the thief finds a map to a golden statuette buried near his home and sets off with a pick-axe and shovel to dig it up in this platformer.
descriptions.c64:177710: A Pac-Man-style maze collecting game for one to four players.
descriptions.c64:177711: A Pong and air hockey hybrid: knock the ball into the opponent's goal past deflecting objects, using limited energy to speed up and hitting the creatures that wander the field.
descriptions.c64:177713: After the wealthy planet Bankonia explodes, collect the money bags flying through space while avoiding the meteorite fragments.
descriptions.c64:177715: A basic Breakout game written in BASIC with PETSCII graphics.
descriptions.c64:177718: Eight snakes are imprisoned behind biscuits, and your smiley must eat them all in this Snake-style game.
descriptions.c64:177720: Whack moles on the head by pressing the right key as they pop up in your yard.
descriptions.c64:177721: Guide a Smurf across the screen, jumping obstacles and avoiding spiders, to rescue Smurfette from a platform in Gargamel's castle; each rescue restarts the game faster with more scenes.
descriptions.c64:177723: Steer a large snake around the field to gather up all the small snakes lying there, then slip through the exit that opens to the next screen, racing an hourglass and never running into your own tail.
descriptions.c64:177725: Guide a fast-moving snake to grab objects that pop up briefly at random spots; reach the target count to advance, and touching a building or the enclosure wall costs a life.
descriptions.c64:177756: A maze chase in the Pac-Man mould: green tokens are worth 5 points and red ones 25, and taking a red token turns the four gremlins white so they can be caught for a short while.
descriptions.c64:177760: An English-teaching program from Hungary's Novotrade for one to four players, drilling grammar with a focus on irregular verbs.
descriptions.c64:177762: A Breakout variant whose brick wall has gaps between the bricks, letting the ball slip through and rack up combination hits.
descriptions.c64:177832: Rather than playing snooker, take charge of the careers of young players and steer them toward the world championships.
descriptions.c64:177834: Help Snoopy rescue Woodstock from a castle in this one- or two-player side-scroller, running and jumping through stages with the aim of reaching the top-left corner of each screen.
descriptions.c64:177835: A 1K entry in the 2007 Minigame Competition: race down a snowy hill, avoiding the trees as the pace climbs toward the bottom.
descriptions.c64:177837: Two players race to catch the presents Santa drops while flying overhead; the first to meet the quota wins, and anyone struck by a falling giant snowball is frozen for a moment.
descriptions.c64:177838: Snowboard down the slope against rival racers; missing a gate brings a 20-second time penalty instead of disqualification.
descriptions.c64:177839: As Tom, orphaned when the Abominable Snowman killed his family, aim a crosshair at the creature's grinning snowmen henchmen before their smiles twist into a horrible grimace.
descriptions.c64:177840: An Italian-language public domain game where the player dodges flying saucers and steers clear of aliens inside tunnels.
descriptions.c64:177841: Football management: train and trade players, deal with injuries, and try to finish as the league's strongest and most profitable club.
descriptions.c64:177842: A European football management game in which the matches themselves are also played, not only managed.
descriptions.c64:177843: A football quiz where every result depends on trivia: correct answers train the squad up and wrong ones weaken it, and matches are decided by answering questions while attacking or defending.
descriptions.c64:177844: Start as a new manager with a bottom-division side, buy better players over the seasons, and push for promotion, the division titles and the cup.
descriptions.c64:177846: A Sokoban puzzle game: push crates around a warehouse until every one sits on a storage spot.
descriptions.c64:177861: Text adventure casting the player as Captain Kirk of the Starship Enterprise.
descriptions.c64:177862: Strategic simulation of the May 1942 to March 1943 land, sea and air struggle between the US and Japan in the South Pacific, with 79 ship types, 17 aircraft types and three mini campaigns.
descriptions.c64:178321: As Xain, travel to invaded planets and destroy the forces menacing their people, mostly in side-scrolling run-and-gun stages where he jumps and ducks, broken up by horizontal shoot-'em-up sections.
descriptions.c64:178391: Recreates three American War of Independence battles, from small Bunker Hill to Monmouth, with either side played by a human or the computer at three skill levels and adjustable reinforcement and ammunition levels.
descriptions.c64:178392: A troll has hidden 15 treasures belonging to Mark, King of the Dwarves; hunt them down with little typing needed, coming back later for any that the troll is guarding until he can be made to leave.
descriptions.c64:178412: Adaptation of the 1980s TV game show: players trade clues to guess five passwords, which together point to the Super Password, over three or four rounds.
descriptions.c64:178452: Vertically scrolling space shooter packed with enemy ships and UFOs, first released on Magic Disk 64 in July 1988.
descriptions.c64:178585: A stock market game: begin with $5000, choose among ten securities, buy while prices are low and sell after they climb.
descriptions.c64:178939: Command a destroyer hunting a submarine, reading sonar returns, dodging incoming torpedoes and closing in to attack when the sub is directly beneath.
descriptions.c64:179004: Sonny the Snail sets out to rescue Snail Meadow, his home, in the first entry of a series that concluded with Magical Formula.
descriptions.c64:179009: Part arcade game, part text adventure, set in olden times when a young lad is offered an apprenticeship to a sorcerer.
descriptions.c64:179011: Licensed adaptation of the Parker Brothers game Sorry!: four players draw cards to move their four pawns from start around the board and home, and only a drawn one or two lets a pawn leave the start.
descriptions.c64:179013: Lead an anti-terrorist squad with a range of vehicles and weapons to keep terrorists from taking over a city generated at random, mixing action, strategy and shooting.
descriptions.c64:179014: Dungeon-crawling role-playing game in first-person 3D: assemble a party of adventurers and descend through deep dungeons, with 1351 mouse support; a fan project published in 64'er in December 1993.
descriptions.c64:179108: Vertically scrolling SEUCK shooter for one or two simultaneous players, flying over enemy bases whose gun emplacements along the pipes and corridors fire in all directions, diagonals included.
descriptions.c64:179111: Up to four players, plus an optional computer rival called Deep Jones, each command a fleet of spaceships and try to conquer a randomly generated galaxy whose planets are often held by neutral natives.
descriptions.c64:179113: Missile Command reversed: drop bombs on the cities while avoiding the fire coming up from them. Part of the War Games pack.
descriptions.c64:179115: A two-player duel between spaceships, in the spirit of the old tank-versus-tank games; published in COMPUTE!'s Gazette in January 1986.
descriptions.c64:179117: Starts with the player as an Indiana Jones lookalike, then moves on to two shoot-'em-up levels and a stage of dodging falling blocks.
descriptions.c64:179266: Guide Tonk through a spooky garden and into Gork's castle to recover a stolen toy chest, collecting keys to unlock doors and keeping out of sight of Gork's evil eye.
descriptions.c64:179269: Children aged 4 to 8 practise basic subtraction across five activities with Mercer Mayer's Tink Tonk characters.
descriptions.c64:179270: A budget follow-up to Vegas Casino from Tarheel Technologies and Mastertronic, offering just two table games, roulette and craps, for up to four players. It came on a dual-format disk for the C64 and PC and was sold only in America.
descriptions.c64:17933: Vertically scrolling shooter in which the descendants of humans who stayed on Earth fight the Xevious forces, whose ancestors left the planet during the Ice Age, along with their GAMP technology.
descriptions.c64:179330: Compilation of three games starring the sailor: Popeye, Popeye 2 and Popeye 3: WrestleCrazy.
descriptions.c64:179384: Aliens are attacking Earth for its natural resources; as the top pilot, battle through every line of defence to reach and destroy their headquarters, with three ships per mission.
descriptions.c64:179385: Children aged four and up compare two groups of objects and decide whether one has more, fewer or the same number; one of the Let's Count programs covering numerals zero to nine.
descriptions.c64:179388: Children practise percentages, solving problems within two minutes to intercept meteors or land on planets.
descriptions.c64:179389: Vertically scrolling shooter set in Sector 93D in 2073, after the Rovolians overran the Alpha-Pluto base and survivors hid behind lead walls in radioactive deposits.
descriptions.c64:179393: As the last survivor of lunar base GERXI 21, fire a laser cannon from the ground at waves of attacking aliens in Galaga-style single-screen action.
descriptions.c64:179394: Two players team up at the same time to shoot down the enemies before they reach the shield generators and attack the base.
descriptions.c64:179395: Lunar Lander combined with mental arithmetic, with three difficulty levels and problem sets for addition, subtraction, multiplication, division or a random mix.
descriptions.c64:179397: Two players compete simultaneously to be first to 10 points, scoring by making a rendezvous, which can only happen once landed or crashed.
descriptions.c64:179401: Pilot a ship through space and avoid the drifting rocks; a 1995 public domain release by Jason Kelk with Tomas Danko of Bigtime Software.
descriptions.c64:179402: Fly through space looking for a planet that can support life; colliding with a planet ends the game, but flying alongside one refuels the ship and checks whether it is the right world. Part of Cassette 50.
descriptions.c64:179403: The planet's robot inhabitants have stolen your spacecraft and plan to attack Earth; search the rooms of their base for the ship and escape to warn Earth, avoiding robots that electrocute anyone they catch. Part of Cassette 50.
descriptions.c64:179418: Two maths games: in Frenzy, solve 20 subtraction or division problems before an alligator eats 10 fish, earning a bonus round chasing numbers with a smiling face if any fish survive; Flip Flop is the second game.
descriptions.c64:179429: Young children match quantities to the numerals 0 to 9 while captaining a rocket that is setting up a space station; part of the Let's Count collection.
descriptions.c64:179430: An early, quite different version of the game later released as Hero of the Golden Talisman, with its own music, screens, enemies and an odd swimming animation; it leaked to the scene under names such as Labyrinth and Progfine.
descriptions.c64:179435: Blast the Space Train in this Centipede-style shooter before it winds its way down to the player's position.
descriptions.c64:179462: A maintenance engineer sent by mistake to a bleak planet at the edge of the universe in 2040, when humanity is turning worlds into vast hydroponic greenhouses, has to earn enough to pay his fare home.
descriptions.c64:179468: One or two players fall through a dimensional hole by the wall of time and must race in the Space Ball to get back from the far side of the universe; published in 64'er Sonderheft 61.
descriptions.c64:179470: Navigate a maze without touching its walls; one of the games in The Big 100 collection.
descriptions.c64:179474: Text adventure made with GAC: an international superspy bails out after the pilot is shot by another plane, and finds the killer coming for him as soon as he lands. A revised version followed in 1993.
descriptions.c64:179476: Rather than a shooter, this Shoot-'Em-Up Construction Kit creation is a driving game for one or two players at once, with music by Thomas Mogensen. It was given away on the cover disk of Commodore Zone issue 9.
descriptions.c64:179477: In 21st-century America, the terrorist group Zapper is kidnapping people from small towns to help build a secret weapon, and the hero's own family and friends are among those taken.
descriptions.c64:179478: A Light Cycle duel for two players over 10 rounds: each rider leaves a solid trail, crashing into a trail or the board edge loses the round, and whoever takes more rounds wins.
descriptions.c64:179479: Training software for reading faster while still remembering what was read.
descriptions.c64:179481: Vertically scrolling shooter: fly a cutting-edge spacecraft against alien hordes threatening the space federation, protected by a shield with limited energy.
descriptions.c64:17949: Simulation of the Navy's F-14 carrier fighter, with a quick mode of 80 random missions and a career mode that begins with training in basic flight, combat manoeuvres and mock dogfights.
descriptions.c64:179494: Tron-style Light Cycles for two players at once.
descriptions.c64:179506: Platformer set in a tiny world of insects and snails, the same setting later used in Sonny the Snail and Bobix.
descriptions.c64:179531: Spelling tutor with 168 lessons, letting learners go back over the ones that gave them trouble until their weak spots are mastered.
descriptions.c64:179538: Line up three matching pieces quickly to clear them from the field and build a high score. Published in Game On in May 1994.
descriptions.c64:179540: Logic game: steer a sphere that can push certain blocks, choosing which ones to shift so that every dot on the field can be reached, with other block types granting boosts.
descriptions.c64:179707: As a spider, eat as many flies trapped in the web as possible within one minute, while bees swoop low and drop things, and on later levels some flies fire back.
descriptions.c64:179816: Ikari Warriors-themed game built with SEUCK, released on the Commodore Format 43 cover tape within its Shrewd Software Collection.
descriptions.c64:17997: As Quasimodo, cross the castle wall from left to right to ring the bell, swinging on ropes over pits and dodging the other hazards along the way.
descriptions.c64:180003: Move Splidge left and right to catch falling presents while avoiding the biblets that try to bury him in snow.
descriptions.c64:180004: Complete a picture against the clock from randomly chosen pieces, shown one at a time, cycling through alternatives with the arrow keys before placing one.
descriptions.c64:180007: On a bet, explore a haunted house at twenty to midnight on Halloween and get out before Dracula arrives; a conversion of Radio Shack's 1979 Haunted House with a different map.
descriptions.c64:180008: Stab wandering baddies with a spork in a game that resembles Whack-a-Mole; published in GO64! in 2005.
descriptions.c64:180034: Guide your horse around a show-jumping course and clear the fences in this German equestrian game from the Golden Disk 64 disk magazine.
descriptions.c64:180036: Platformer for one to four players about avoiding ghosts, where difficulty can be set separately for each player as a handicap.
descriptions.c64:180079: Logic game starring Bruno, a CP-Verlag warehouse worker who has to haul heavy pallets of freshly recorded Magic Disks over to the goods lift.
descriptions.c64:180081: Educational detective game similar to Carmen Sandiego: track down the jewels stolen by thief and smuggler Dr. Xavier Tortion and find Dr. X himself somewhere in North America.
descriptions.c64:180082: Move a square around a pit gathering small white squares while avoiding those of other colours; a 2K entry in the 2009 Minigame Competition.
descriptions.c64:180083: A memory game: pick two numbered squares to reveal hidden words and find pairs that belong together, such as night and day or horse and carriage; mismatches are covered again.
descriptions.c64:180084: Move a white square around the pit collecting small white squares for points, and avoid the coloured ones, which take lives.
descriptions.c64:180087: Shooter in the vein of Astro Blaster, piloting the Omega 4, a ship built for exploring the alien-infested Zone 8, against an unexpected threat.
descriptions.c64:180092: A two-player thinking game along the lines of Connect Four, published in 64'er in August 1997.
descriptions.c64:180093: Get to each level's exit using no more moves than the move counter allows; a puzzle game by Paul and Mark Kubiszyn.
descriptions.c64:180096: Two-part text adventure: escape the squeaky roundabout and head deep into the universe, then return from a space station bringing back the answer everyone needs.
descriptions.c64:180097: Pong in 3D, seen from behind the player's black paddle at the far end; place the paddle where the ball is heading to deflect it and keep the rally going.
descriptions.c64:180118: Shoot down advancing aliens while dodging their bombs, as they edge ever closer the fewer remain; clearing a wave leads to a section of dodging boulders falling from above.
descriptions.c64:180119: A Concentration memory game designed for Stack Computer Services' light pen.
descriptions.c64:180120: Build the highest tower possible by freezing each sliding three-square block in place with the space bar, lining it up with the block beneath.
descriptions.c64:180121: Lord Foul has ravaged the Land for a century; collect the seven symbols of power, among them a cross, a ruby, a dagger and the Staff of Law itself, in this text adventure.
descriptions.c64:180125: Fend off aliens that bounce and dive from every angle instead of marching side to side like Space Invaders; published in 64'er in February 1991.
descriptions.c64:180127: Alien life forms have destroyed the Alpha Centauri B system, and as a B-class pilot you are teleported into the danger zone to confront them. Made by the Ultraforce Software Team and published on a 64'er games disk.
