descriptions.c64:180140: An alien who hoped to colonise an empty planet finds it full of hostile natives and has to fight them off and get away as fast as possible.
descriptions.c64:18015: Sir Arthur Pendragon must find his way out of an ancient Egyptian tomb in the second Pendragon adventure from Ultimate, following The Staff of Karnath.
descriptions.c64:180208: Klingons are assaulting the Federation's home base; wipe them out before they take over the known systems, earning rewards for each kill while racing the clock.
descriptions.c64:180258: Mr. Universum, once the unbeatable hero of the galaxy, has been slimmed down by a few kilos courtesy of an evil alien in this single-screen platformer by Stefan Gutsch, released by Protovision and on the GO64! disk.
descriptions.c64:180313: A sliding picture puzzle on a 5x5 board: memorise the image before it is shuffled, then slide pieces into the empty black square to restore it before time runs out.
descriptions.c64:180370: Text adventure: waking from ten years of suspended sleep as sole crew of the Starship Ganymede, receive orders to find the Megaship Armstrong, silent and missing for a decade.
descriptions.c64:180487: An 8K cartridge recreating the light cycle sequence from the film Tron, with a two-player mode.
descriptions.c64:180513: A spoof in which the captain has abandoned ship, leaving Leonardo DeCappucinno to steer the whole length of the huge Titanic through a field of icebergs.
descriptions.c64:180539: An Australian role-playing game finished by Jeff and Ann Pritchard but never released: move around the StarSat with keys 1 to 8, aiming to reach the final door and transfer data.
descriptions.c64:180575: Fly a fighter plane over the ocean, shooting targets in the way and avoiding collisions with enemy craft.
descriptions.c64:180576: A tank duel strictly for two human players, fought on a battlefield filling about two thirds of the screen; published on Magic Disk 64 in August 1994.
descriptions.c64:180577: An unreleased game in the style of Transbot, where clearing challenges and building up energy upgrades the weapon into several forms, including a giant robot.
descriptions.c64:180579: Gather falling star coins worth 10, 50 or 100 points by colour while dodging asteroids; at 5000 points comes a bonus round of invulnerability.
descriptions.c64:180580: A sample game made with Garry Kitchen's GameMaker, loosely based on the Atari 2600 shooter: a ship at the screen bottom faces waves of strange, comical attackers.
descriptions.c64:180581: Sink an enemy surface fleet with torpedoes, leading each target to allow for its speed; ships score 100, carriers double but need two hits, and some vessels drop depth charges while the torpedo supply runs down.
descriptions.c64:180582: Children aged 3 to 7 learn their letters with the help of Stickybear, the bear from the 1980s children's book series.
descriptions.c64:180583: As Stickybear, move side to side and jump to catch objects in a basket while they drop and bounce around the stage, keeping clear of hazards.
descriptions.c64:180584: Sequel to Stickybear Math: solve maths problems to rescue Stickybear from sticky predicaments, such as gathering enough balloons to get over a small wall.
descriptions.c64:180585: Young children pick a number from 0 to 9 and see that many animated objects, such as balls, rockets and trucks, appear on screen.
descriptions.c64:180591: An early Lode Runner update with a menu of level sets: the original 1-75, Professional Lode Runner 2's levels 76-150, Championship Lode Runner, Lode Runner 5 and Loadrunner Classic.
descriptions.c64:180622: Young children explore opposites like far and near, shut and open, or short and tall through animated Stickybear scenes, switching between each pair.
descriptions.c64:180624: Three reading activities for ages four to eight with Stickybear, including a Sentence Builder in which players combine nouns and verbs into sentences that are then acted out.
descriptions.c64:180625: Children aged three to six learn to recognise five common shapes, including the circle, square and triangle, through three activities.
descriptions.c64:180626: Lay out a town on an empty green plot by choosing buildings, which are connected by roads automatically, then drive a small car around the streets in two play modes.
descriptions.c64:180627: Text adventure: an evil sorcerer banished from court has cursed the land, and an old hermit tells of four magic tokens in a faraway land that together can bring back peace.
descriptions.c64:180628: Clear the stones from 30 puzzle levels, all fitted into just 5 KB; published in 64'er in November 1993.
descriptions.c64:180629: Clear every blue stone from each level, using teleports, sliding over ice and stopping at the evil-faced stoppers; a 4K entry in the 2011 Minigame Competition.
descriptions.c64:180707: Text adventure: escape the reeking hold of a ship and make it to New York.
descriptions.c64:180710: On an 8x8 grid of coloured blocks, place pieces into one area so it matches the pattern in the other before a fast-shrinking timer expires.
descriptions.c64:180712: Text adventure: wake with amnesia, an aching head and a bruised left arm in a dark, damp alley lit by one flickering street lamp, and work out who you are.
descriptions.c64:180781: Darts against the computer in a pub, with a choice of 301 or 501, after a few too many drinks lead to a challenge with a twist.
descriptions.c64:180826: A one-joke novelty game played by switching the joystick back and forth in a steady rhythm, where overdoing it brings a warning colour change.
descriptions.c64:180827: Text adventure set on Earth rather than in space: track down your partner and work out what pleases them.
descriptions.c64:180828: Steer the hero past energy barriers, sharp corners and other traps to the goal, where any slip is punished; published on Magic Disk 64 in July 1990.
descriptions.c64:180832: Columns-style game for one or two players: stack falling gems so three of a colour line up and vanish, with each completed section revealing more of the game's artwork.
descriptions.c64:180836: A quick free remake of the VIC-20 Sub Hunt, made as a stopgap before the much expanded Sub Hunter.
descriptions.c64:180842: Rescue the divers trapped in an underwater cave; collecting three opens the way onward, while sea creatures, rocks and plants must be avoided.
descriptions.c64:180843: Command a submarine through hostile waters, firing missiles at destroyers and cruisers above while dodging their depth charges, with three subs to sink the fleet.
descriptions.c64:180844: Real-time simulation of a nuclear-powered submarine: leave port, dive, hunt and sink surface ships with the help of sonar, and survive counterattacks.
descriptions.c64:180845: From a ship sailing above, drop depth charges with any key on the pack of submarines below, scoring for every hit. Part of Cassette 50.
descriptions.c64:180852: Practice in adding and subtracting mixed fractions for grades 6 to 8, focusing on lowest common denominators, reduction and cancellation.
descriptions.c64:180897: Sudoku with four difficulty settings and a level editor included.
descriptions.c64:180901: Typing tutor: type the right letters as fast as possible to push a sumo wrestler forward.
descriptions.c64:180994: A two-player version of Tamer, letting a second fighter join the battle against the aliens at the same time, with otherwise unchanged gameplay and slightly rearranged levels.
descriptions.c64:181120: Not a real Mario game: a hack of a cracked Game Over II with altered sprites and title screen, trainer enabled and password entered.
descriptions.c64:181121: Fly Mario on a jetpack, avoiding the waves of oncoming obstacles and keeping his power from running out.
descriptions.c64:181140: Trivia quiz with question sets at Freshman and Graduate levels.
descriptions.c64:181153: Slot machine simulator that blends fruit machine reels with a card game; released in Italy as One-Arm Bandit.
descriptions.c64:181154: Railway CTC dispatching simulation with three territories, floating and train reversing, adjustable clock speed and fully randomised traffic; the follow-up to Train Dispatcher.
descriptions.c64:181155: Pass five tests to rescue brother Jack.
descriptions.c64:181156: Help E.T. phone home by opening garbage cans to find parts for his transmitter, but some cans hide a hunter who will chase E.T. down.
descriptions.c64:181157: Pinball table that seems to have been made with Pinball Construction Set.
descriptions.c64:181516: Bounce a pogo stick around mazes repairing bricks and grabbing bonuses while avoiding obstacles; fix every brick before the hourglass empties. New levels over the original, from Loadstar 139.
descriptions.c64:181517: Minesweeper clone with plain grey graphics and a selectable number of bombs.
descriptions.c64:181519: Rebels have attacked the Pennysland nuclear power plant and sabotaged its power lines; travel in a vehicle hanging from the lines to collect items and restore the region's power.
descriptions.c64:181521: A falling-block puzzle with dice: drop a die onto one of those lying in the container, matching its ever-changing value, and lose a life on a mismatch.
descriptions.c64:181663: Climb a triangle of 21 squares by answering timed multiple-choice trivia with F1, F3 and F5, from six five-point squares on the bottom row up to a single 500-point square at the top.
descriptions.c64:181668: A shootout at the climax of an action film, where enemy bullets and even brushing against the scenery cost a life.
descriptions.c64:181679: Truck racing on a split screen with side and overhead views, published on Magic Disk 64 in November 1991.
descriptions.c64:181689: Up to four players type in their answers to more than 2000 questions across show business, sports, science, history, the arts and a grab bag, competing over who will be the Monster's lunch.
descriptions.c64:181737: Based on a game from the Sat-1 TV show Superball: roll a ball onward while watching out for the deadly disklets ahead.
descriptions.c64:181738: Timed motorcycle racing across Motocross, Supercross, Enduro and Trials events, taking jumps and bumps while avoiding obstacles such as logs, trees and walls as well as other riders.
descriptions.c64:181740: A version of the code-breaking board game Mastermind.
descriptions.c64:181751: Wait near the top of the screen for a wave, then ride it past the marker buoys, threading between pairs of buoys while avoiding sharks and staying on as the wave crests.
descriptions.c64:181752: Windsurf for a high score while avoiding whirlpools, Neptune, surf mines, surfcatchers and even the Titanic.
descriptions.c64:181815: A Mr. Do!-inspired game from the 2014 RGCD 16KB cartridge competition: as Super Strawberry, King of the Orchard, gather the ripe cherries while the Acid Apple Gang roams the orchard.
descriptions.c64:181857: Text adventure at the Kenwood Academy high school, where the school's ladies' man takes up his friends' $500 bet that he cannot win over a beautiful new transfer student, a high-school girl, and follows her home.
descriptions.c64:181858: A reworked and improved Super Seven, the dice-matching falling-block puzzle, released on the Commodore Scene cover disk.
descriptions.c64:181860: A Commodore text adventure known for a flaw in its object handling: item names get shuffled, so opening the chest might call for the book, the key might need reading, and the lion's pit could not be escaped. Patched versions were later circulated.
descriptions.c64:181861: Text adventure: claim the mystic sword by killing the demon that guards it, figuring out some unusual verbs and solving three hard riddles along the way.
descriptions.c64:181862: Text-based role-playing game: raise armies and gather special equipment while exploring a grid above and below ground, then reach Ra, the Master of Evil, in his throne room and defeat him within 55 turns.
descriptions.c64:181876: A football pools forecasting program with a touch of management simulation, intended to help predict real results and win money.
descriptions.c64:181877: Q*bert-style platformer on a flat isometric surface for two simultaneous players, created entirely by Christian Scholz, from code to music.
descriptions.c64:18191: General Zoff holds Ambassador Kryxix aboard his ship, with plans for a new spacecraft hidden in a micro-disc in the Ambassador's spine; command the Emperor's six-strong Enigma Team to free him before the plans are found.
descriptions.c64:181952: Educational text quiz about Britain, covering history, correcting grammatical mistakes and general knowledge.
descriptions.c64:181969: Scrolling jump-and-run platformer, similar in places to Hawkeye: pass the trials to win approval and save the hero's family, all under the gaze of watching eyes above.
descriptions.c64:181980: A Pac-Man variant in which the hero drives a tank.
descriptions.c64:181981: A joystick duel for two players only, framed as a future where heads of state settle wars over a beer and a computer game instead of on the battlefield.
descriptions.c64:182005: Futuristic football for two players at once, each a goalkeeper driving a tank to defend their goal; the match ends when time runs out or both players have used up their shots.
descriptions.c64:182006: Two tanks battle on a single screen in the manner of Atari's Combat; each kill scores a point, first to ten wins, and protective barriers can be switched on or off.
descriptions.c64:182007: Rescue workers from a burning oil rig and ferry them to a nearby tanker, keeping clear of clouds of poison gas. Part of Cassette 50.
descriptions.c64:182105: Shoot moving targets as a warrior of Targon defending the planet from invading mutants, in a game modelled on the 1974 PLATO game Targon.
descriptions.c64:182137: Updated 1991 sequel to Wildfire, a horizontally scrolling space shooter modelled on Delta.
descriptions.c64:182144: Seventeen unreleased Wizard levels, the last a joke never meant to be beaten, plus a level editor; casting levitate or feather fall while falling can save a life.
descriptions.c64:182157: A 1998 remake of Wizard II with 33 new levels.
descriptions.c64:182162: A set of 50 Boulder Dash levels built with Boulder Dash Construction Kit on the original engine, getting very hard from level 20 onward.
descriptions.c64:182186: Gathers 340 caves from No One's compilations of Boulder Dash levels, running on a standard machine but also supporting enhanced graphics on the DTV.
descriptions.c64:182248: Head-to-head Breakout duel for two players, combining Breakout with ping-pong; published on Magic Disk 64 in April 1993.
descriptions.c64:182264: Maze game in the Pac-Man vein where the chasing skulls can be shot, some maze sections may only be crossed in the marked direction, and special symbols do things such as freezing the monsters.
descriptions.c64:182265: Light cycle duel for two players in which each tries to trap the other with a growing trail.
descriptions.c64:182316: Manage the trains and cargo of the Tees-Tyne Pullman, the British East Coast Main Line service linking London and Newcastle from 1948.
descriptions.c64:182319: Second part of Peter R. Boothman's Telnyr role-playing trilogy, opening with news that Telnyr has been overrun by monsters and footpads.
descriptions.c64:182369: A ten-finger typing course in seven lessons, from the home row up to whole texts, plus a game where words must be typed before a laser beam wipes them out, costing energy, across nine levels.
descriptions.c64:182375: Multidirectional scrolling shooter in the style of Netherworld, exploring dark corridors full of monsters and treasure with lives and smart bombs; music by Thomas Detert.
descriptions.c64:182379: Bombing shooter: knock out the anti-aircraft guns on the ground before they bring the plane down.
descriptions.c64:182382: An almost unbeatable alien force is attacking; as the chosen fighter pilot, strike the aliens' own planets and destroy a set number of their ships to force them to surrender.
descriptions.c64:182463: Brave a South American jungle of tribes and piranha-filled rivers to enter an overgrown temple, live through its traps and get out with its three treasures.
descriptions.c64:182465: Amidar clone: move the yellow piece around the grid to score by passing over squares, before the blue enemy catches and atomizes it.
descriptions.c64:182466: Tic-tac-toe in three dimensions on a 4x4x4 board, aiming for four in a row, for two players or one against the computer at three difficulty levels.
descriptions.c64:182507: Tetris for one player or two going head to head, set against varied backgrounds.
descriptions.c64:182508: Text adventure set in 2050 at a theme park with no gentle rides: visitors are dropped into lifelike scenarios and must rely on their wits to survive the day.
descriptions.c64:182513: As the Athenian prince Theseus, roam a randomly generated 3D labyrinth built to chosen settings, hunting the half-man, half-bull Minotaur past secret doors and mirror-maze sections.
descriptions.c64:182522: Cross a series of bridges without dropping through the gaps by forming ice bridges over them, scoring for distance covered. Part of Cassette 50.
descriptions.c64:182530: Adventure featuring the 1980s pop trio, given away on a flexi-disc attached to Computer & Video Games issue 36 together with a recorded message from the band.
descriptions.c64:182580: As a storm cloud moving up and down the middle of the screen, fire lightning bolts left and right at the rows of bombs on either side, which shoot back; a stage ends when every bomb is gone.
descriptions.c64:182595: Science fiction platformer starring Thunderboy, a hard-working exterminator who has to wipe out a set number of rodents and insects on each level.
descriptions.c64:182623: A tough vertically scrolling shooter, probably never released, that was due from Atlantis Software in 1988; passwords let players return to levels already reached.
descriptions.c64:182624: Tibo of Choria sets out across Illussia to fetch sea sand from the beaches of Zabria, the magician Phobias's hope for curing his blacksmith father, in a side-view shooter played over single screens.
descriptions.c64:182625: A trivia game show on a tic-tac-toe board for two players, or one against the computer: answer correctly to claim the chosen square, while a wrong answer hands it to the opponent.
descriptions.c64:182626: Up to four players take turns buying and selling on a simulated stock market in this early keyboard-driven trading game by John D. Price.
descriptions.c64:182627: Educational trivia about Hollywood movies, stars and directors from the 1910s to the 1980s: explore famous locations across six top-down maps and travel between eight decades.
descriptions.c64:182628: Arrive at Victoria Station with a few hundred American dollars, explore London sights such as Trafalgar Square while learning about British culture and geography, and work out who the mystery person is.
descriptions.c64:182629: Fly into Paris with a few hundred American dollars and tour the city, from the Eiffel Tower to the Louvre, picking up French language and culture.
descriptions.c64:182630: Arrive in Washington, DC with a few hundred dollars, visit the city's landmarks to learn about American culture and geography, and work out who the mystery person is.
descriptions.c64:182632: SEUCK helicopter gunship shooter: fly a special mission over enemy territory in a powerful helicopter and make it back to base.
descriptions.c64:182635: Two-player tank duel in the style of Atari's Combat, one driving the green tank and the other the beige.
descriptions.c64:182647: Text adventure: with a gang of Krells armed with knives and stunners pounding on the kitchen door, escape and find the terrorist bomb hidden somewhere in the city before it goes off.
descriptions.c64:182649: Dodging game modelled on the spaceship stages of Turrican II, with a short closing sequence set to music.
descriptions.c64:182650: Single-screen platformer whose story begins with a brilliant 14th-century inventor building a futuristic machine, the Robot.
descriptions.c64:182651: Scramble-style side-scrolling shooter: fly back to base past launch ramps, narrow passages and mines, with difficulty that adapts to the player's skill and a continue option.
descriptions.c64:182655: Two-part Quill text adventure, Shadows and Light and Ironhand, about finding out who steals people's time and so their lives; heavy text compression allows a large vocabulary and a capable parser.
descriptions.c64:182742: Educational journey through five eras of English history for ages seven and up: answer questions about each period, then flee its pursuers, from wild animals in Bronze Age Britain to Roman legionaries and medieval clergy.
descriptions.c64:182876: A Boulder Dash release with 16 caves and 4 intermissions of mixed difficulty in classic style, several of them using open borders.
descriptions.c64:182966: Text adventure that begins on a chilly, windy night outside a huge house, with a wolf howling on a nearby hill and a foggy graveyard to the east.
descriptions.c64:182967: Ralf Kober's timed puzzle from Game On makes you dodge bombs, keep an eye on the clock and decide on the spot whether each special that pops up will help or hurt you.
descriptions.c64:182970: Tetris clone scoring a point per completed line, from the Polish Triada game pack.
descriptions.c64:182971: Addition practice with Mercer Mayer's Tink Tonks, following Tinka on her way to school through mazes with things to see and do, over three levels.
descriptions.c64:182972: Single-screen platformer: gather the required items while dodging floating enemies to open the door to the next level, as the enemies speed up over time.
descriptions.c64:182973: Sequel published in Game On in 1994: on each single screen, pick up the items that unlock the exit door while avoiding drifting enemies that get quicker as levels go by.
descriptions.c64:182975: Two-player boxing with 1983 professionals or historical greats such as Muhammad Ali and Joe Louis, each rated for accuracy, defence, endurance, power and control, with fight strategies shaping the outcome.
descriptions.c64:182990: Unusual split-screen game in which a rugby ball is moved around a pyramid.
descriptions.c64:18317: Action adventure as an astronaut aboard an abandoned space factory, working through 200 screens of puzzles, traps and killer robots to solve its mystery; a separate conversion of the Spectrum game.
descriptions.c64:183237: Arcade adventure through levels of vaults in Dracula's Tomb in search of a half-million-pound treasure; a map of the first level's 300 vaults, showing obstacles, monsters and stakes, is shown briefly to memorise beforehand.
descriptions.c64:183239: Tombola, the bingo-like lottery board game from Southern Italy.
descriptions.c64:183298: Compilation of four shooters designed by Alf Yngve, including the side-scrolling Silverfish and a cargo plane mission carrying medical supplies, with Zap Fight 2: SE as a bonus.
descriptions.c64:183315: Win by guiding the ball through each of the 12 rooms.
descriptions.c64:183523: Steer a balloon to the bomb and back to the exit that appears once it is armed, avoiding moving and fixed objects and lasers against the clock; arming the bomb turns all enemies into collectable points.
descriptions.c64:183527: Text adventure as Maithros, saved from death weeks earlier by the mystic Mitherful, who asks him to join the monks in return.
descriptions.c64:183670: Freescape reworking of Total Eclipse: recover the 12 fragments of the sphinx hidden in the passages under the pyramid within two hours to break an ancient curse.
descriptions.c64:183671: A mercenary fights through a series of checkpoints, crossing rivers, forests and villages and shooting all who stand in the way, collecting items for extra points.
descriptions.c64:183673: SEUCK shooter in which the goal is to fight a way up to the tower's summit.
descriptions.c64:183674: Platformer in which the player battles knights and monsters across four levels of a tower.
descriptions.c64:183691: Firemen holding a net under a burning building catch falling residents, often several times as they bounce, while heavy residents cannot be caught safely and have to be left to fall.
descriptions.c64:183692: Side-scrolling platformer like Bobix set in an alien-infested city and its sewers, where all 180 sacks must be gathered before the exit chamber allows escape.
descriptions.c64:183737: Software for printing out parts of 20 working mechanical models, such as cars and trucks with turning wheels, a crane, an oil pump and a balloon-powered vehicle, to be assembled following the instructions.
descriptions.c64:183739: Tidy up the toys by kicking them around the garden in this puzzle game, made single-handedly by Jan Schulze, that plays like a blend of Puzznic and Sokoban. It was entered in the 2014 RGCD 16KB cartridge competition.
descriptions.c64:183798: Lead a wagon 2000 miles west during the Gold Rush, managing food, ammunition, clothing and supplies, with mini-games such as hunting each turn; included in the Micro-Dozen One compilation.
descriptions.c64:183799: Run a railroad traffic control center through a sped-up eight-hour shift, routing as many as 12 trains each way across 150 miles of track by setting switches and signals to keep them on time.
descriptions.c64:183803: Run a shipping company over 100 days with five vessels starting from London, buying eight kinds of goods cheaply in one port and selling them dearer in another, and taking on time-limited contracts.
descriptions.c64:183804: A logic puzzle that also calls for fast joystick work under tight time limits, as the player restores order to a completely scrambled arrangement.
descriptions.c64:183806: In this sequel to Slap N Tickle, the mutant Matthew Slim has recovered a lost circuit board and now hunts for the Transputer of Learning, the only thing that can cure him. It was one of the sample games bundled with the 1988 Shoot 'Em-Up Construction Kit.
descriptions.c64:183810: Aim a crosshair and shoot flying clay targets in a simulation of shotgun trap shooting.
descriptions.c64:183824: A horizontally scrolling shooter set on the space platform Traxxion, which is breaking apart after a comet strike while its robot cars race around out of control.
descriptions.c64:183938: A text adventure played by picking from offered answers to the computer's questions while exploring an imaginary world; part of The Big 100 collection.
descriptions.c64:183939: Lead Frank through maze-like tombs viewed from above, hurling swords at swarms of monsters while hunting for treasure.
descriptions.c64:183947: A text adventure aboard the starship from the original Star Trek series, which is stuck in a decaying orbit with its engines dead.
descriptions.c64:184108: An Italian side-scrolling shooter mixing ideas from Gyruss and Defender, where a quota of enemy ships must be destroyed to reach the next stage.
descriptions.c64:184236: Three arcade tests in one package: a shooting duel, a dodging game and a crosshair shooting gallery.
descriptions.c64:184239: Unarmed, Triss explores Hephyr's mansion to recover 20 magic stones of Thefrog and stop Hephyr's bid for world domination, carrying up to eight useful items at once past hostile creatures and traps.
descriptions.c64:184246: Trivia for one or two players across 50 categories of 10 multiple-choice questions each, 500 in all, plus the option to write and save new questions.
descriptions.c64:184257: An adventure from the tenth issue of Compute!'s Gazette, written for an article on teaching a computer English, in which the player collects magic items and defeats a troll.
descriptions.c64:184265: A logic puzzle where stones must be arranged to match a pattern shown by the computer, though they can only be shifted by moving whole rows and columns according to set rules.
descriptions.c64:184266: In the year 2525, an expedition leader raids six temples on planet Tronix for ancient treasures, using one lever to open the treasure hatch and another to beam the loot away while avoiding snakes.
descriptions.c64:184267: A text adventure in which the stand-in manager of Bridgeton Asylum left the front door unlocked and must track down every escaped patient before the real manager returns.
descriptions.c64:184268: A Marble Madness-like platformer for one or two simultaneous players, born from a nightmare in which colored bubbles turn into sticky globes that swallow Andrea's toys.
descriptions.c64:184355: A Pipe Mania-style puzzle: lay the longest possible pipeline in 90 seconds before liquid starts flowing from the start square, with more pipe pieces required on each successive level.
descriptions.c64:184356: An adventure built around an intricate tunnel maze that has to be mapped on paper to survive.
descriptions.c64:184357: A Shanghai-style tile game where matching tiles can be removed only when they line up with no other tile between them, with the goal of clearing the whole board.
descriptions.c64:184366: A two-player duel between a blue wizard and a red wizard, each trying to destroy the other first.
descriptions.c64:18448: A Defender-style shooter: a jet-pack spaceman flies fast over a barren scrolling landscape, fighting aliens ranging from simple Planters to the creeping Blunder Storm.
descriptions.c64:18449: A fast side-scrolling shooter crowded with enemies, where the ship has an energy bar rather than dying on one collision, and certain targets release power-ups.
descriptions.c64:184497: A holiday program with four options: an illustrated rhyming story, a greeting card printer, a letter writer for printing notes to Santa, and a puzzle of reassembling a scattered picture.
descriptions.c64:18450: Flimbo sets out to rescue his girlfriend Pearly from Fransz Dandruff across platform levels where he can drop down through platforms as well as jump up to higher ones.
descriptions.c64:184501: A multi-directional scrolling shooter where the real danger is the scenery: touching any wall is deadly, as in Berzerk, so careful steering matters more than firing.
descriptions.c64:184504: A Shoot 'Em-Up Construction Kit shooter with Mario-like sprites, playable by one or two players together.
descriptions.c64:184507: A single-screen platformer set in 2010, after the underworld's evil emperor has cursed the Earth and the forces of darkness have seized the world.
descriptions.c64:18451: A little robot dashes through five sideways-scrolling worlds in Mario fashion, fighting enemies with upgradable bouncing-ball shots and a flamethrower and breaking rocks and walls to uncover diamonds and extras.
descriptions.c64:184518: A head-to-head falling-block game where lining up three identical blocks in a row, column or diagonal clears them; three jokers help in emergencies, and blocks reaching the top end the game.
descriptions.c64:18453: Ride a trials motorbike across side-view courses inspired by the Kickstart TV show, leaping steps, crashing through tyres and hedges and slogging through mud; 24 courses come with a designer for building new ones.
descriptions.c64:18454: A reworked edition of Last Ninja 2: the evil Shogun Kunitoki has escaped through time to set up a new tyranny in modern Manhattan, and the gods bring the Last Ninja across the ages to face him again.
descriptions.c64:18455: A forerunner of The Sims: after being personalized with the owner's name, a cutaway house with kitchen, living room and bedroom gets a small resident who inspects it and, if satisfied, settles in to live his daily life.
descriptions.c64:18456: Mayhem the dinosaur sets out, with help from apprentice Theo Saurus, to undo the gloom that fell on Monsterland after Theo, drunk on cactus juice, tried his master's spells.
descriptions.c64:18457: Soccer with a choice of full 11-a-side games on grass or 6-a-side indoor matches modeled on the American indoor league, plus World Cup and indoor tournaments, a ladder of tougher computer teams, and two-player friendlies.
descriptions.c64:18458: A top-down budget shooter in the vein of Gridrunner with 25 levels, where the goal is to survive until a timer expires; finishing a level grants an extra life, up to five.
descriptions.c64:184580: A puzzle game in which stones scattered randomly across each level must be rearranged into an orderly layout, controlled through an unusual interface.
descriptions.c64:184583: A two-player-only take on Pac-Man where both players move through the maze at once, made for the 2009 MiniGame Compo.
descriptions.c64:184584: Steer a rotating magic wand through 20 mazes, collecting clocks attached to a time bomb before time expires without bumping into obstacles; with two players, each one steers an end of the wand.
descriptions.c64:184585: A new version of the arcade shooter Phoenix, published on Magic Disk 64 in 1990.
descriptions.c64:184586: An Australian strategy game that simulates the international shipping trade, with the aim of making the most money.
descriptions.c64:184587: A typing tutor in the style of Space Invaders: letters drop down in columns and are destroyed by typing them, with wrong keys draining energy; offers 99 speeds and 39 lessons.
descriptions.c64:18459: After a Soviet attack on the United States, lead a US fighter squadron through a series of action stages to destroy defense bases before a bomb's timer runs out; from the makers of Beach Head.
descriptions.c64:184592: A Battleship-style game of hunting down and sinking the opponent's hidden ships, based on the pencil-and-paper game played in classrooms.
descriptions.c64:18460: In 17th-century Japan, torn by civil war among warlords fighting over the Shogunate, play Usagi Yojimbo, a ronin rabbit warrior standing against the dark forces.
descriptions.c64:18461: Fly a hovering taxi through 25 screens of obstacles, picking up passengers from landing pads and delivering them to the pads they ask for; slow trips shrink the fare.
descriptions.c64:18462: Fly a ship governed by inertia and gravity through vector-drawn side-view caverns as a Resistance fighter, towing away a Klystron pod on a swinging line.
descriptions.c64:184627: Ride a gun-mounted hover-board along a beach boardwalk and shoot down as many of the colored balloons streaming past as possible.
descriptions.c64:184628: A word-guessing gambling game similar to Wheel of Fortune but without the wheel.
descriptions.c64:184629: An RPG begun in 1989 and finished in 2013, with a dungeon, wilderness regions and a town map to explore; the original slow BASIC code was replaced with machine language.
descriptions.c64:18463: Guide a rolling ball along patchwork tracks of colored squares that speed it up, slow it down, warp it or reverse its controls, jumping over holes along the way.
descriptions.c64:184632: Table football transplanted into outer space.
descriptions.c64:184633: Steer a large, angry yellow snake as it gathers blue balls while staying clear of a thin blue line.
descriptions.c64:184635: An adventure that opens with a Secret Service spy waking in a cellar with no memory, apparently on the brink of the biggest case of his career.
descriptions.c64:184647: Dodge meteors and other flying objects while keeping the starship Enterprise from touching the top or bottom of the screen.
descriptions.c64:184651: As a wagon operator moving left and right, catch every lump of coal falling from above on a single screen; each one missed costs a life.
descriptions.c64:184744: An educational program that teaches U.S. states and their capitals and then quizzes the player on them.
descriptions.c64:184745: A learning game on U.S. states and their capitals, part of the Fun in Learning pack.
descriptions.c64:184746: A Manic Miner-style platformer with extra sub-games, programmed by Jason Fox with graphics and music by Adam Gilmore and left unreleased for over 20 years.
descriptions.c64:184747: A BASIC supertanker simulation in which the helmsman must reach the Alaskan port of Valdez from the northern Pacific, a demanding trip of about 62 miles.
descriptions.c64:184838: An adventure pitting the player against Dracula as night falls, based on a 1980s BASIC game for Tandy computers.
descriptions.c64:184866: A computer version of Kalaha, the board game of sowing stones from pit to pit.
descriptions.c64:184867: A Lode Runner-style game: grab all the gold bars on each level and reach the exit within the time limit while avoiding monsters.
descriptions.c64:184878: Fearless Bill explores a dungeon in this 2D arcade adventure, battling monsters and gathering treasure, weapons, armor and spells.
descriptions.c64:184880: A fixed-screen Space Invaders-style shooter in which holding the fire button speeds up the whole game.
descriptions.c64:184881: An educational game about map reading and traffic rules: drive through a large, unfamiliar city to find six transmitters within an hour, each running on a battery that lasts only ten minutes.
descriptions.c64:184882: Steer a tank through tight passages collecting yellow bombs, blasting tank traps and avoiding lava, with only one life and limited damage to absorb.
descriptions.c64:184884: Control a bouncing ball armed with lasers and infiltrate an enemy stronghold, wiping out its defenders; a 1988 public domain release.
descriptions.c64:184885: A text-based casino with three games: Even-Odd, Dice and High Numbers.
descriptions.c64:184954: Pub darts for two players over three rounds against the character Jimmy Riddle, centering the aim with the joystick before firing each throw.
descriptions.c64:184959: A trading and strategy simulation for one to four players, each a landowner who farms, buys and sells land, expands a fishing fleet, builds up a manufactory, grows the population and trains soldiers.
descriptions.c64:185049: A peg solitaire puzzle on a cross-shaped board, with water drops in place of pegs.
descriptions.c64:185050: An action game in which the antiserum Vitamin is used to destroy colonies of computer viruses that a virus mafia planted in the vital systems of many planets.
descriptions.c64:185051: An adventure in Raka-Tua National Park, where five treasures must be found and brought back to the Jail; followed by Escape from Raka-Tua.
descriptions.c64:185052: A Breakout and Pong hybrid for exactly two players.
descriptions.c64:185053: Oregon Trail on the ocean: pick the right provisions and sail across the Atlantic, relying on good winds and luck to reach the New World alive.
descriptions.c64:185073: A lander game: with fuel nearly gone, descend through dangerous caverns to an abandoned refueling depot and help underground aliens fight mutant surface dwellers.
descriptions.c64:185077: A fast scrolling shooter with parallax scrolling across ten levels; the Walker moves forward or back, jumps and fires a laser cannon.
descriptions.c64:185114: A fantasy text adventure as helper to Menra the Magician, whose wand and gold were stolen by the evil wizard Dran; recover the wand for him and the people of Ghopasia.
descriptions.c64:185116: A scuba diver moves continuously from the left and fires straight ahead at enemy divers who shoot back; hits score points but the enemies stay on screen, and three hits end the game.
descriptions.c64:185122: A Breakout-style bat-and-ball game featuring speech synthesis.
descriptions.c64:185124: Cosine's horizontally scrolling space shoot 'em up, first given away on the cover disk of Commodore Zone issue 4 in 1996. Typing "the magic roundabout" on the title screen switches on invincibility.
descriptions.c64:185125: Cosine's 2006 remix of its 1996 shooter Warflame, rebuilt for release through Cronosoft with new background colours, a more detailed loading picture and reworked collision detection that makes it noticeably easier.
descriptions.c64:185130: A domination strategy board game fought over the Ancient Continent, released in shareware and registered versions.
descriptions.c64:185143: The second Warriors of Ras game, an early graphical roguelike: explore the monster-filled dungeon Kaiv turn by turn with typed commands such as MOVE NORTH, killing monsters and taking treasure.
descriptions.c64:185272: Third in the Warriors of Ras series: Grimsweord came back from the Kaiv crippled, the wizard's magic failed to heal him, and a new quest must find the one thing that can cure him.
descriptions.c64:185278: The fourth Warrior of Ras role-playing game takes you into the Ziggurat of Ras, tomb of a tyrant king, in search of the Sapient Scepter of Sirocco. You climb randomly built levels using typed commands, defeat the guardian mummy at the top and then make your way back out.
descriptions.c64:185290: A typing game where attacking words descend toward a city and are destroyed by typing them and pressing space; blinking words give bonuses, with blitz attacks and six difficulty levels.
descriptions.c64:185294: On planet Zypar, 18-year-olds must face their peers in a special arena to decide their future, battling each other while riding inertial platforms.
descriptions.c64:185298: Over 15 levels, gather falling gems while dodging boulders and bricks; one boulder hit can be survived, but a brick is fatal.
descriptions.c64:185317: Similar to Air-Sea Battle on the Atari 2600: sink an endless convoy of ships while avoiding depth charges dropped from a plane.
descriptions.c64:185319: Alfredo the Idiot ferries water back and forth to fill a bucket before time runs out, dodging falling objects, to the tune of Morning Has Broken.
descriptions.c64:185329: Beneath Annapurna in Nepal, Micro digs tunnels through cold rock and sets detonators to blast open waterfalls that carry lake water down to an accumulator for the people of the Rajistan Valley.
descriptions.c64:185385: An educational game that teaches U.S. geography through weather.
descriptions.c64:185386: An artillery game for two players, enhanced from Ouranos!, in which rivals at either side of the screen attack each other's castles with hail, rain, lightning or tornadoes from a drifting cloud.
descriptions.c64:185390: Teleported to the moon, uncover the secret work at the Mad Scientists Association's lunar lab, codenamed Wega, and find a way back to Earth.
descriptions.c64:185393: An interactive fiction story where the player becomes the main character, shaping the tale through decisions and interaction with its world.
descriptions.c64:185505: An adventure with an animated hero: break out of captivity, gather supplies at the saloon, keep a canteen filled while crossing the desert in search of an outlaw, and win the final shootout.
descriptions.c64:185507: A crosshair shooting game with five Wild West events, including bottle shooting, calf roping and a sheriff challenge.
descriptions.c64:185662: Stop enemy helicopters from escaping off either side of the screen using a machine gun and five nuclear missiles; one getting through ends the game.
descriptions.c64:185664: A platformer set in trap-filled areas around and beneath the White House, scoring by surviving and collecting treasure.
descriptions.c64:185669: Jump from a plane and open the parachute to steer the jumper onto a base at the foot of the screen, watching the wind indicator, since the chute can only be steered when open.
descriptions.c64:185762: A detective text adventure: search the Carr estate for a necklace that vanished during a party when the lights went out.
descriptions.c64:185778: In 2025, play a self-delivering Burger King Whopper making its way to a hungry customer while others try to grab it and stray ingredients try to pile on.
descriptions.c64:185780: An educational quiz on U.S. presidents through Ronald Reagan, covering birthplaces and birth and death years.
descriptions.c64:185793: A bonus game on the Quedex disk in which Willy returns with inertia-based movement.
descriptions.c64:186627: A Mastermind-style code-breaking game that allows up to 999 players.
descriptions.c64:186865: A modified set of levels for Wizard, based on 33 New Levels and including the Wizard Game Construction editor.
descriptions.c64:186867: A new collection of hard levels for Wizard, built with Wizard Game Construction.
descriptions.c64:186868: A follow-up to Wizard Expert I with more expert levels made in Wizard Game Construction.
descriptions.c64:186876: An educational grammar and spelling program built from word subgames such as Word Spinning, Dragon's Spell, King Author, Herald's Hark and Jester's Jumble.
descriptions.c64:186880: A 2D RPG drawn in PETSCII graphics with Dungeons & Dragons flavor, whose world is randomly generated at the start of every game.
descriptions.c64:186888: Guide a ball through a dangerous maze without touching its walls or obstacles.
descriptions.c64:186898: The wizard Nerkus has abducted Sherlie and transformed her sweetheart Dave into a ball of iron; as the constantly bouncing Dave, clear the zones guarding a magic door to reach Nerkus' castle, steering over water and spikes.
descriptions.c64:186910: A snake game for up to four players, with three- and four-player matches requiring two linked computers and a special cable.
descriptions.c64:186913: As a woodpecker guarding the Sacred Tree, use its holes to catch prey and keep the tree healthy.
descriptions.c64:186916: Guide Pepito the sheep out of Mindspace across 16 levels, past Space Chickens, Wiggly Worms and Green Martians; an expanded 64K version of an RGCD 16K cartridge competition entry with better graphics and jump physics.
descriptions.c64:186918: A Boggle-like solo word game: find as many words of three or more letters as possible in a 4x4 grid of random letters before time runs out, chaining adjacent letters and using each only once.
descriptions.c64:186941: Reading games for children aged 5 to 8 starring Roger Hargreaves' Mr. Men, such as Mr Noisy's Word Game, which teaches opposites, comparatives and superlatives.
descriptions.c64:186943: A word search puzzle that comes out on a printer; after solving it on paper, the player is quizzed on the answers.
descriptions.c64:186944: A vocabulary and spelling trainer for ages 11 and up, with more than 1,200 words in sections on synonyms, similes, collective nouns, and nouns with their adjectives.
descriptions.c64:186945: Collect diamonds and items in shifting platform levels, using the items to reshape the level so it can be cleared within the time limit; three difficulty settings let players start at harder levels.
descriptions.c64:186947: Ice hockey with practice matches or a world cup for up to nine players; games last 90 seconds plus possible overtime, controlling one skater at a time.
descriptions.c64:186948: International soccer with tournaments for up to eight human players or single friendlies, three skill levels and adjustable match length, viewed from the side.
descriptions.c64:187058: Restore a scrambled field to match the pattern shown beside it by rotating its pieces; turning one piece also turns every piece connected to it.
descriptions.c64:187065: Drive against oncoming traffic starting on the screen's right side, dodging vehicles and pit crews trying to box the car in, and last as long as possible; four difficulty levels.
descriptions.c64:187338: Fly a glider through tight underground mazes shooting the 75 energy blocks on each level. Moving and firing burn energy, which hitting energy blocks restores; barriers fall only when hit at their ends, and landing on a base sets a restart point. Seven gliders.
descriptions.c64:187579: A Drelbs-like maze puzzle: flip revolving doors to form as many squares as possible while guardians give chase; some completed squares reveal a door to the next phase.
descriptions.c64:187586: A four-in-a-row strategy game where stones are pushed onto the board from the bottom and from the right, shoving other stones off the opposite side.
descriptions.c64:187597: Fuzzle works in Santa's present factory, dropping gifts into boxes of the matching colour as they roll along a conveyor belt, while a cheeky character pelts him with snowballs to slow him down.
descriptions.c64:187598: Blast Christmas-themed asteroids with a ship shaped like a tree in this bonus game from the European disk of Delta.
descriptions.c64:187610: A Scramble-style shooter set at the dawn of the 22nd century, when interplanetary wars make skilled pilots of advanced attack craft constantly in demand.
descriptions.c64:187617: Blast the force field guarding the Star Fortress to weaken it while avoiding the field and falling planets; made for the 2007 Minigame Competition's 2K category.
descriptions.c64:187660: A falling-block game for one player or two at once, where clearing several lines adds rows to the opponent's stack: two for a double, four for a four-line clear.
descriptions.c64:187664: Rebuild a picture cut into pieces, some of them interchangeable, on grids of 2x4, 4x3 or 8x6 depending on difficulty.
descriptions.c64:187670: A dice game in the Yahtzee mold: roll for scoring combinations, clicking dice to keep them between rolls.
descriptions.c64:187795: An exploration platformer through linked underground rooms full of deadly pits, spikes, water, moving platforms and strange plants, with tricky puzzles barring the way.
descriptions.c64:187796: A quest to obtain the sword and become King of Britain, ported from the VIC-20 and requiring a 22-column formatter from the same disk to be run first.
descriptions.c64:187798: A stock market simulation in which the player trades on Wall Street to build wealth and power.
descriptions.c64:188101: Explore a haunted castle for five diamonds amid traps and hostile creatures; every touch drains energy that cannot be restored, locked doors need keys, and falls cost nothing.
descriptions.c64:188103: Space Invaders-like shooting with triple shots, where a new volley comes only after the last one hits or leaves the screen; stop the alien ships before they get across.
descriptions.c64:188106: As Fax McSheen with three attack drones, investigate a zone of space that defies the laws of physics, blasting every planet and alien in the way over 15 levels.
descriptions.c64:188112: A logic puzzle where clicking blocks changes their color, with the goal of turning every yellow block white.
descriptions.c64:188761: Pilot a spacecraft with twin lasers through waves of enemy fire, beating a mothership to end each wave; some waves demand threading a set path without touching walls.
descriptions.c64:188856: Pilot a zeppelin through a trap-filled maze around a sunken city, avoiding walls and managing fuel while searching for the wreckage of seven earlier zeppelin expeditions.
descriptions.c64:188858: A text-only American football game set in the fictional ZFL league.
descriptions.c64:188950: A slot machine simulation from the Magic Disk 64 disk magazine that lets you gamble on the reels without spending real money.
descriptions.c64:188954: A 2D arcade adventure that begins in 1993, when a satellite spots unusual heat in the Arizona desert above hot-water caves and a government science team finds something huge underground.
descriptions.c64:188960: A Scramble-style scrolling shooter: destroy everything possible and hit fuel targets to keep flying.
descriptions.c64:188964: A blend of Centipede and a wild variant of Space Invaders with cute-style graphics.
descriptions.c64:188965: An Asteroids-like shooter starting at the screen's center, where shots bounce off the edges of the play area instead of wrapping around and keep flying until they hit something.
descriptions.c64:188966: The last of the Zone 7 trilogy, a diagonally scrolling shooter where, as in Asteroids, play starts mid-screen, but shots ricochet off the arena borders.
descriptions.c64:188967: Defend a city from a huge enemy assault across several zones, driving various vehicles against tanks, with the main goal of reaching zone six to defuse a bomb that could level the city.
descriptions.c64:188968: A vertical shooter over a smooth-scrolling landscape, with limited forward and back movement, a miniboss and an end boss on each level, followed by a bonus stage for extra points.
descriptions.c64:188969: A match-three puzzle about capturing animals for a zoo: line up three or more of the same kind vertically or horizontally, and new animals drop in from above.
descriptions.c64:188973: A primal duel for two players only, fought over who gets to eat meat tonight.
descriptions.c64:188974: A vertically scrolling SEUCK shooter with two stages of enemy ships to destroy using built-in lasers; a crash or a hit costs a life.
descriptions.c64:188977: A horizontally scrolling shooter: the Interplanetary Federation drops the player onto the Zynon-Lotec platform, a rebel base for revenge attacks, to fight through enemy territory.
descriptions.c64:188980: A puzzle in which arrows creep onto the board from each side and must be turned and slid so they stop on board squares, arranging them into the correct formation around two fixed points.
descriptions.c64:19022: As Inspector Snide of Scotland Yard, investigate the death of Angus MacFungus at his mansion, gathering clues around the house to name the murderer; the screen border flashes near anything worth examining.
descriptions.c64:19024: Crockett and Tubbs work up a drug ring run by Mr. J, from street dealers to suppliers to the bosses at the casino, through overhead driving and shooting.
descriptions.c64:192157: A public domain clone of the Atari 2600 game Haunted House.
descriptions.c64:192636: Accept a challenge from a friend of the hero's father to escape his labyrinth alive, seeing only the rooms adjoining the current one, so drawing a map is advised.
descriptions.c64:194987: A reading program aimed at understanding and remembering what has been read.
descriptions.c64:195025: A shoot-'em-up closely resembling Sea Ranger, but with a far bigger play area and reworked graphics.
descriptions.c64:195671: A Shoot 'Em-Up Construction Kit shooter for two cooperating players: the Federation strikes back at the Xenians, whose border raids keep hitting its convoys.
descriptions.c64:195693: A Spanish-language shooter about defending a city from alien ships.
descriptions.c64:195705: A solo or two-player board game resembling an enlarged tic-tac-toe.
descriptions.c64:195749: A Swedish-language first-person adventure with monochrome pictures and a menu of five commands: go, take, use, give and hit.
descriptions.c64:195750: A wargame of the clash at the Shevardino Redoubt, fought the day before Borodino, serving as a prequel to Krentek's Borodino: 1812 game.
descriptions.c64:195752: Steer a spaceship through a series of mazes while avoiding very strange enemies.
descriptions.c64:195756: A Bubble Bobble parody in which enemies are knocked about by shouting Swedish into their ears.
descriptions.c64:195785: A single-screen platformer about collecting every diamond while avoiding crawling aliens.
descriptions.c64:195859: As Special Inspector Francis, find the murder weapon in the English market town of Harboro so an arrested suspect can be convicted; also part of a trilogy alongside St. Jives and Lost in the Amazon.
descriptions.c64:195862: The only survivor of a plane crash on an expedition seeking the Golden Condor must find a way out of the South American jungle.
descriptions.c64:195863: The village of St. Jives is terrorized by a mad scientist, and only casting a spell can stop his takeover.
descriptions.c64:195865: A multiplayer RPG drawing on Chaos: The Battle of Wizards, Magic: The Gathering and Dark Legions.
descriptions.c64:195886: Control the Super Ball to destroy asteroids among other threats in this Shoot 'Em-Up Construction Kit game for one or two cooperating players.
descriptions.c64:195926: Never officially released, this unfinished side-scrolling shoot 'em up supports one or two players and was coded by Duncan MacDonald with graphics by Dave Edwardson. It offers only a handful of attack waves, and its Rob Hubbard music is borrowed from Deep Strike.
descriptions.c64:195927: The Grixlons have taken the universe, and a house down the road, to wage eternal war; destroy every power orb to defeat them in this space shooter.
descriptions.c64:195928: Push through enemy lines to find and destroy the enemy's secret headquarters.
descriptions.c64:196037: A one-player cute-'em-up built with the Shoot 'Em-Up Construction Kit, featuring unusual bosses and a road-crossing section in the style of Frogger.
descriptions.c64:196057: Wicked Dr. Dactor has abducted the king and seized a once-peaceful land, and the hero Bogue emerges to save it.
descriptions.c64:196060: Bogue, a grape, returns to rescue all his friends from the evil Dactor, who plans to turn them into robots.
descriptions.c64:196061: Explore a tomb full of traps, beetles, snakes and bats, the last of which shove the explorer around.
descriptions.c64:196125: An early Bomberman-style game made with the Shoot 'Em-Up Construction Kit, for one player or two at once.
descriptions.c64:196167: A follow-up to Border War that frees movement across the whole screen, with eight-way shooting and a weapon that sends walls of fire in from the left and right.
descriptions.c64:196213: Fight through a heavily defended fortress, destroying guard troops and robots to claim a bounty.
descriptions.c64:196219: A bounty hunter shoots his way in all directions through an enemy stronghold, battling many defenders and bosses.
descriptions.c64:196241: Another Bounty Hunter fortress assault, with improved graphics, more enemy types and a tougher challenge.
descriptions.c64:196247: Storm a fortress whose defenses grow ever stronger, facing threats drawn from the distant past to the far future.
descriptions.c64:196248: A bounty hunter battles through a fortress guarded by warriors from many different eras.
descriptions.c64:196795: A hacked version of Championship Sprint, the overhead racer for one to three players, with added tracks.
descriptions.c64:198078: Dizzy hunts down all his friends to invite them to his rave.
descriptions.c64:19858: As Louie the construction worker, bolt down girders that slide back and forth, then return to the starting point; across 100 levels, some also require placing girders in specific spots.
descriptions.c64:199389: As a big fish in a small pond, dodge fishing hooks while grabbing worms when possible; two players can compete simultaneously.
descriptions.c64:199556: A compilation of The Great Giana Sisters, Power-Sisters I, and both Gitty's Dreams games (Gitty's Land and Gitty's Revenge), each with a trainer and saved high scores.
descriptions.c64:199607: Five original Boulder Dash caves by Lars Bernhofen, mostly built in the late 1980s and released decades later.
descriptions.c64:199608: Twenty-five new Boulder Dash caves by Lars Bernhofen: 20 regular caves and five intermissions.
descriptions.c64:199610: Another 25 Boulder Dash caves from Lars Bernhofen, built with the Crazy Light Construction Kit 3.0 and including hidden-cave code.
descriptions.c64:199611: A further 25 Boulder Dash puzzle caves by Lars Bernhofen, created with Crazy Light Construction Kit 3.0.
descriptions.c64:199612: Twenty-one new Boulder Dash caves from Lars Bernhofen.
descriptions.c64:199621: A set of 24 new Boulder Dash caves by Lars Bernhofen.
descriptions.c64:199622: Thirty levels of Boulder Dash from Lars Bernhofen: 24 caves plus intermissions.
descriptions.c64:199623: The final Lost Caves set: more than 30 new Boulder Dash caves from Lars Bernhofen, released at the Doreco party in 2013.
descriptions.c64:199624: A space shooter where the enemies are planets that rush in from the distance and hurl their orbiting moons at the player's ship.
descriptions.c64:199633: An unofficial conversion of the 1983 Spectrum Manic Miner: Miner Willy explores underground caverns of a long-gone advanced civilization, rich in valuable ores.
descriptions.c64:200004: A hacked Petch, a Pengo clone, running at double speed.
descriptions.c64:200369: A two-player shuffleboard game with four counters each: pick a row, then hold F7 longer to slide the counter farther, varying rows as the rules require.
descriptions.c64:200641: An unreleased side-scrolling space shooter by Steve Collins in the vein of Defender and Uridium: blast enemy craft with upgradable weapons and gather orbs, which once enough are collected allow a landing where a man can be controlled.
descriptions.c64:200644: Guide a craft through 32 levels of a deadly nuclear reactor built by the alien Cygma Elite, gathering radioactive pods while avoiding obstacles and seekers; this edition is harder with fewer lives.
descriptions.c64:200687: Navigate corridors with deadly floors and ceilings, lethal spaceships and destructive beam barriers, where any contact means instant death.
descriptions.c64:200701: Find the object shown in the top-right corner somewhere in a crowded playfield; later remade as Needle in the Haystack.
descriptions.c64:200715: A wrestling game for one to four players, including a tag team mode for two to four.
descriptions.c64:201453: A public domain Tetris clone controlled by keyboard only.
descriptions.c64:202086: A simple version of the Wheel of Fortune game show: guess letters to solve phrases across three rounds and a bonus round, against two computer opponents or up to three people.
descriptions.c64:202197: A hack of Cosmic Causeway: Trailblazer II that reworks physics and levels to match the C16/Plus4 original more closely than the buggy C64 port, and adds 24 levels.
descriptions.c64:207339: A German role-playing adventure about freeing the land of Dreistromland from evil's reign of terror.
descriptions.c64:208414: A two-player Pong written in C++17.
descriptions.c64:20843: A young shepherd loots a dead body on his first visit to the city, taking a bracelet, a black disk and a scroll, and is drawn by the mysterious Galactic Museum into a line of adventurers.
descriptions.c64:21010: Kid Niki wields the Spinning Sword, collecting bells for extra power, such as the Golden Bell that fires a projectile with each spin.
descriptions.c64:210284: A personal take on the 1983 Panorama Game & Watch Kong game, with richer, more colorful scenery than the original.
descriptions.c64:210661: Fly a battle-armored jet suit over a planet's surface through more than 20 levels, fighting enemy aircraft and guided missiles and avoiding lethal terrain, with a bonus section linking the levels.
descriptions.c64:21195: Ambushed outside Tilverton, a party of heroes is marked with five azure bonds that can seize control of them, and must find their source to break the curse; the second Gold Box Forgotten Realms game.
descriptions.c64:21315: Ten-pin bowling for up to eight players in open play or tournaments, with Kids, Amateur and Professional difficulty; from the makers of Leader Board.
descriptions.c64:215111: A one-player Finnish boxing game in which the aim is to floor the opponent, and pacing your stamina wisely through the bout matters as much as landing punches.
descriptions.c64:216838: Three sports in one package: two-player side-view Baseball with alternating pitching and batting, text-based Football against the computer with plays picked from a menu, and two-player one-on-one Hockey.
descriptions.c64:216869: Standalone companion to Avalon Hill's Super Sunday that moves the focus from play-calling to running an American football team as its general manager.
descriptions.c64:218263: Quirky Danish arcade adventure about tracking down Bubber's stolen bathtub; an unofficial English translation circulates as Hunt for Bubber's Bathtub.
descriptions.c64:22536: Home version of Sega's arcade racer: steer a Baja buggy along a hilly scrolling course packed with rival vehicles, killer pickup trucks and boulders to dodge or leap onto.
descriptions.c64:24110: Bounce a ball through timed levels, gathering the required number of diamonds while getting past enemies and hazards like water and storms; power-ups grant extra time or energy.
descriptions.c64:24322: Storm the island fortress of Kuhn-Lin, seized by a dictator, over six sequences that open with an aerial reconnaissance where the fleet sneaks past the enemy or through a hidden passage.
descriptions.c64:24323: The dictator from the first game returns as The Dragon to take revenge on the Allies; one player commands the Allied side and another can play The Dragon through four sequences, starting with an attack on his machine-gun-defended base.
descriptions.c64:24324: Fly a helicopter on bombing runs against the Bungeling empire's factories, flying back to the home aircraft carrier for repairs and fresh bombs while keeping it from being sunk.
descriptions.c64:24325: Pilot a lone rocket copter down through the Draconis and Crystaline caves to free prisoners held by the Kralthans and then strike their command center, Fort Apocalypse.
descriptions.c64:24326: Jumpman must defuse bombs that terrorists planted on Jupiter by touching each one, climbing ladders and one-way ropes and jumping between platforms without falling.
descriptions.c64:24599: Blast an alien formation hovering high above while ships break away from its edges to dive and fire; each of the four enemy types attacks in its own way.
descriptions.c64:24601: Illustrated text adventure retelling Tolkien's novel with the player as Bilbo Baggins, starting with Gandalf and Thorin; other characters act independently and can change how events play out.
descriptions.c64:24602: Junior eats every dot in mazes too big for one screen, which scroll to follow him as four ghosts give chase and bonus treats wander through.
descriptions.c64:24603: The yellow dot-eater clears mazes of dots and fruit while four ghosts, Blinky, Pinky, Inky and Clyde, hunt him; power pellets briefly let him eat them.
descriptions.c64:25431: Run, jump and fight through stages built on myths and legends, such as Hades, ancient Greece and a pyramid in Egypt, collecting weapons and solving puzzles to win each level's magic orb.
descriptions.c64:25470: Horizontally scrolling shooter starring St. Dragon, a cyborg warrior who rebels against the cyborg monsters that have enslaved race after race across the galaxy.
descriptions.c64:25476: Arcade brawler across six levels: punch and kick through waves of thugs on upper and lower screen tiers, joined by jumps and ladders, to reach each boss and rescue the kidnapped President.
descriptions.c64:25489: The warrior Amul becomes a blue dragon to save Princess Alicia from the monster Zawell, flying through nine vertically scrolling stages and attacking targets in the air and on the ground.
descriptions.c64:25490: Jason Voorhees lurks around the Crystal Lake holiday camp in his hockey mask while ten friends wander the grounds; the player tries to keep them alive and put an end to the killer.
descriptions.c64:25491: Vertical arcade shooter set after a tabloid journalist's campaign of hatred drives once-peaceful aliens to invade; collected gunballs trail behind the ship and can be launched as special weapons.
descriptions.c64:25504: Shoot through 16 maze-like levels inside a huge alien orbiting Earth, picking up maps of each level and weapons suited to different creatures in order to kill it from within.
descriptions.c64:25505: Batman pieces together clues in two cases: the Penguin's umbrella factory hiding a robot-penguin plan for world rule, and a separate showdown with the Joker.
descriptions.c64:25515: After the Demon King kills his master and escapes into the future, a samurai pursues him through time with the help of the Wizard Mage.
descriptions.c64:25516: One or two players guide robot ninjas through a side-scrolling brawl with shuriken and knives; damage rips their clothing away to reveal machinery until they finally blow apart.
descriptions.c64:25517: Drive an armour-plated, weapon-laden car through a post-apocalyptic land, carrying cargo for big money while the established Overlander gangs try to run newcomers off the road.
descriptions.c64:25518: Side-scrolling platform action in which Aarbron, transformed into a beast-like slave by the Beast Lord Maletoth, sets out to take revenge.
descriptions.c64:25519: Horizontal shooter that fights on land and in the air: one player flies a helicopter while a second can join in a jeep, each covering the other.
descriptions.c64:25520: A secret agent in a Bond-like story set in 199X chases terrorists who strike at the President outside the White House, fighting on foot and in action set pieces across the US.
descriptions.c64:25521: Motorbike racing against 19 riders on ten famous circuits such as Silverstone, Monza and Daytona, viewed from behind the bike, with two, four or six laps and Novice, Champion or Pro skill.
descriptions.c64:25522: Maximus Mouse hunts for the lost American flag needed for Summer Camp's grand opening day, crossing screen after screen of cartoon platform action.
descriptions.c64:25523: Vertical shooter and unofficial follow-up to Silkworm: one player flies a helicopter while the other drives a jeep that becomes a boat on water, with mid-level boss enemies to destroy.
descriptions.c64:25524: In 2039 deep-space explorers discover hostile alien life; a first-person shooter in which the player blasts aliens while rescuing captive crew.
descriptions.c64:25526: One or two players choose a turtle and take on Shredder's forces, first rescuing April from a burning building and then going after the kidnapped Splinter.
descriptions.c64:25527: Hack through Ghosts 'n Goblins-style levels against Mumm-Ra's minions, from dwarves to bats, smashing containers to find weapons stronger than the starting sword.
descriptions.c64:25528: The Autobots battle the Decepticons on Earth to gather all four parts of the Energon Cube and deliver them to their own base.
descriptions.c64:25529: In 2019 water-dwelling aliens have conquered Earth from the oceans; fight back in underwater shooting stages with a craft whose ships and weapons are bought between levels.
descriptions.c64:25730: Escape from thirteen castles, each a puzzle of force fields, trapdoors, lightning machines and prowling monsters; two players can work together.
descriptions.c64:25757: Based on the 1986 Disney film: Basil, the mouse living beneath 221B Baker Street, follows clues across London to save Dr. Dawson from Professor Ratigan.
descriptions.c64:26127: Crow-Ther, protector of the city of Wizening, drives his armoured car with cannons and missiles out along the freeways against the forces of the tyrant known as The Wizard.
descriptions.c64:26679: Armed with a machine gun and dynamite, rescue a POW from an enemy camp within a 24-hour limit (five real minutes), avoiding gunfire, land mines, tanks and deep water.
descriptions.c64:26832: Two-player tennis seen from an elevated angle behind one baseline, with difficulty levels 0-3, one to three sets, slow or fast ball, and forehand and backhand shots.
descriptions.c64:26834: A work-shy janitor roams the floors of a building and sneaks into back rooms to play old computer games, dodging the security guards.
descriptions.c64:27054: Vertical shooter off Midway Atoll: fly through 16 levels hitting Japanese air and naval forces on the way to sinking the battleship Yamato.
descriptions.c64:27056: Alice tumbles into Videoland after the White Rabbit and needs four games to get home; the first has her collecting potions, cake slices and keys in a strange room.
descriptions.c64:27057: Sequel to Forbidden Forest: an archer with unlimited arrows hunts monsters to earn golden arrows, moving into and out of the screen as the scene shifts from daylight to starry night.
descriptions.c64:27058: Jack runs, jumps, climbs and shoots through the kingdom of Allegoria searching for nine coloured lamps while creatures attack nonstop.
descriptions.c64:27059: Fly four missions shooting enemies for the money they leave, then upgrade the craft in shop rooms; touching foes or walls drains energy.
descriptions.c64:27060: Bump 'n' Jump clone: race up a futuristic, curve-free top-down road that narrows and widens, swerving or jumping over potholes, breaks and islands and ramming rival cars away.
descriptions.c64:27061: Track down five clones of Captain Blood and disintegrate them, earning aliens' trust through UPCOM, a conversation interface of around 150 icons.
descriptions.c64:27062: A captive breaks out of his cell in a Nazi-held castle, takes weapons from guards, and must steal the war plans and escape alive.
descriptions.c64:27063: Pursue five vehicles linked to the kidnapping of three girls, the mayor's daughter among them, in a twin-turbo car with five nitro boosts and a mounted gun.
descriptions.c64:27064: World War II flight simulation of the bombing raids on dams, crossing heavily defended territory with machine guns to fight back before the run on the target.
descriptions.c64:27065: Up to four players compete in all ten events of a real decathlon, either in order or one at a time, including the sprint, long jump, pole vault, shot put and javelin.
descriptions.c64:27067: Shooting gallery based on the 1990 film, with John McClane gunning down terrorists who have taken over an airport.
descriptions.c64:27068: A martial artist crosses a hostile land of swamps, forests, mountains and caves, fighting ninja, shoguns, soldiers and wild animals who ignore the rules of temple tournaments.
descriptions.c64:27069: Archaeologist Fred explores the pyramid of Tootiecarmoon over six levels, grabbing treasures and the map he needs to get out while avoiding acid drops.
descriptions.c64:27070: The Goonies hunt for treasure to save their homes from a property shark, with the player switching between two of the kids to solve each screen's puzzles.
descriptions.c64:27071: A lone gunman fights up vertically scrolling streets to rid Hicksville, a gold rush settlement, of the Wingate gang, taking down each level's chief outlaw and his henchmen.
descriptions.c64:27075: Play a wicked toddler causing as much trouble as possible over 50 screens, jumping on things and grabbing and dropping objects to fill the naughtyometer without being punished.
descriptions.c64:27076: Michael Knight and his computerised car KITT race to stop a terrorist group set on sabotaging important East-West summit meetings.
descriptions.c64:27078: Bio-war has reached Europe; lead a road gang across the continent to find and disarm terrorist bio-bombs and then destroy the terrorists' headquarters and leadership.
descriptions.c64:27079: Race one rival at a time on elevated tracks with jumps and chasms, viewed from the cockpit, and win each three-man division of a four-tier league to climb.
descriptions.c64:27080: The android Scih-Berg drives a nuclear train along the monorail network of planet Nilmerg, blasting hostile life forms until reaching 100,000 points.
descriptions.c64:27081: Barbarian-style one-on-one duels moved to the future, with fighters wielding laser swords and using jumps, rolls, kicks and sweeps that score different points.
descriptions.c64:27107: Steer Buck Rogers' ship between pairs of pylons, accelerating, braking and sliding left or right along a science fiction obstacle course.
descriptions.c64:27110: Jeff Minter's third camel shooter: 90-foot mutant camels defend a planet long unused to war from the returning Zzyaxians across 100 horizontally scrolling levels.
descriptions.c64:27112: Wizard, warrior, elf and valkyrie heroes explore mazes, gathering treasure and magic potions while fighting off creatures and ghosts.
descriptions.c64:27114: Gauntlet-style World War II raid on the Eagle's Nest command HQ: free three captured Allied soldiers, recover stolen art treasures and blow the building up.
descriptions.c64:27115: Monty Mole, freed from prison, flees Britain through flick-screen platform rooms, learning enemy paths and the timing of crushers to plot a route out.
descriptions.c64:27118: Rick tries to stop the Fat Guy helping aliens seize the world, crossing Hyde Park, ice caverns, a forest and atomic mines full of booby traps, laser bolts, robots and penguins.
descriptions.c64:27119: Based on the Schwarzenegger film: an ex-cop framed for mass murder is forced into a hugely popular deadly TV show and has to survive it.
descriptions.c64:27121: Qualify for pole and then race Richard Petty and 18 other pros on the superspeedway, planning pit stops, drafting to gain time and fuel, and handling yellow caution flags.
descriptions.c64:27122: A journalist from The Clarion infiltrates a drug ring's headquarters in Colombia to free a friend whom the Drug Baron is holding hostage.
descriptions.c64:27475: Stranded on a strange planet without fuel, Rocket Roger has to gather 99 fuel crystals scattered across its surface while hostile locals try to kill him.
descriptions.c64:28688: A huge asteroid is heading for Earth; fly a jet-pack around it to bring 36 uranium cubes together to destroy it, refuelling at depots and watching the oxygen supply.
descriptions.c64:29700: Wally assembles ten cars, each from six parts scattered around the stock room, placing them correctly at the assembly area while dodging robots, bouncing tyres and air hazards.
descriptions.c64:29702: Caveman B.C. Bill swings his club to stun or kill roaming creatures and drags cavewomen home to his cave to start a family.
descriptions.c64:29703: On each single-screen level the burglar Blagger must pick up every key and open the safe before time runs out, walking and jumping in fixed arcs.
descriptions.c64:29704: Cabin boy Jim searches the 20 holds of the Black Galleon for loot, and after clearing a hoard has 45 seconds to find the Bronze key that leads to the next.
descriptions.c64:29705: Based on the 1985 film: vigilante Paul Kersey takes to the New York streets after a friend is killed, helping the police wipe out the gangs.
descriptions.c64:29706: Ocean turns its hunchback hero into a text adventure: Quasimodo seeks to help Esmeralda by exploring Notre Dame and places in, around and beneath Paris, gathering items to solve puzzles and get past the Bishop's and Cardinal's servants.
descriptions.c64:29707: Sequel to Jammin': the musician Rockin' Rodney, or alternatively his girlfriend Rachel, collects notes for a new song across 60 screens of vertical alleys in three colours that cannot be crossed directly.
descriptions.c64:29708: Kokotoni Wilf travels across six time zones and 63 side-view screens to gather all seven fragments of the Dragon Amulet, flying and hovering with precision.
descriptions.c64:29709: Bounce a tennis ball across courses of tiles hanging high above the ground, getting past walls and enemies without plunging over the edge.
descriptions.c64:29710: Wally Week is stuck in his own nightmare and must find the key to wake his alarm clock before he is late for work, using escalators, lifts and locked doors to get around.
descriptions.c64:29712: Time Pilot-inspired multi-directional shooter: a time-travelling fighter crosses five eras, battling aircraft of each period; downing 56 enemies moves on to the next.
descriptions.c64:29715: Recreate the stunts of British daredevil Eddie Kidd, beginning with bicycle jumps over oil barrels.
descriptions.c64:29824: Three-on-three basketball with time limits, free throws, a three-point line and realistic backboard rebounds, played in three 200-second periods.
descriptions.c64:29825: Life simulation from the female perspective: shape a character's personality through questions or at random, then make choices across seven stages from infancy to old age.
descriptions.c64:29826: Life simulation from the male perspective: a character's personality is set by answering questions or at random, then guided through decisions in seven stages of life, from infancy through old age.
descriptions.c64:29827: Still trapped by aliens in an alternate reality, the player leaves the City and descends into the dungeon below, following a largely linear route where survival is the goal.
