descriptions.c64:90295: Two-on-two beach volleyball playing Randy Stoklos and Sinjin Smith, with practice, match play and a tournament across Waikiki, Rio de Janeiro, San Diego, Chicago and Australia.
descriptions.c64:90296: Race BMX bikes around seven overhead tracks against a second player or the computer, beating a time limit, with slow-motion replays after each race.
descriptions.c64:90298: As sheriff of the frontier town Gold Gulch, talk with townsfolk and gunslingers by choosing dialogue responses, deciding when words fail and it is time to draw.
descriptions.c64:90299: Returning home to find the family castle in ruins and an evil uncle raising an army, rally the people, enter archery contests, visit taverns and duel knights to build a force of your own.
descriptions.c64:90300: Lone Rider never leaves the saddle in this side-scrolling western, riding both ways across prairie and towns, shooting bandits, jumping obstacles and ducking incoming fire, and losing points for hitting townsfolk.
descriptions.c64:90326: A sequel to Velnor's Lair: Grako has slipped back from the Abyss and seized a source of power, and the hero must defeat him in this text adventure with graphics.
descriptions.c64:90334: Tend four bars, sliding drinks to advancing customers and catching empty mugs; anyone who reaches the bartender throws him out.
descriptions.c64:90382: Ride Gandalf on his white horse against an endless stream of Nazgul, blasting the black riders with lightning bolts while avoiding contact.
descriptions.c64:90383: Smiffy, trapped in an Orwellian world run by a Central Computer, sets out to switch it off.
descriptions.c64:90384: Guide an aardvark's tongue through an underground maze to eat food, dodging worms, stinging ants and spiders.
descriptions.c64:90392: Text adventure: explore the land to rescue a maiden abducted by the Demon Knight, collecting objects, defeating foes and solving puzzles.
descriptions.c64:90402: Choose Buzz, Ty or Kato and brawl against digitized fighters for bonuses and prize purses, with a grudge match every third bout.
descriptions.c64:90420: Centipede-style shooter on a grid: blast zigzagging chains of pods, whose dead segments become obstacles and split the chain in two.
descriptions.c64:90422: Steer a motorboat through hazards while the water-skier behind it swings on a different line, making narrow gaps treacherous.
descriptions.c64:90425: Avalon Hill's American football board game on computer: pick teams from the 1966 Packers to the 1982 Redskins and call offensive and defensive formations each down.
descriptions.c64:90426: NFL strategy simulation with semi-pro and pro playbooks (18 or 36 offensive and 14 or 24 defensive plays) and a mode against the computer team, The Robots.
descriptions.c64:90431: Text adventure closing Level 9's Middle Earth trilogy: hunt for magical treasures in the defeated Demon Lord's fortress across over 200 locations.
descriptions.c64:90441: Australian-themed events including boomerang throwing, a bellywack contest, Aussie Rules punting, a dry boat race and a skeet shoot at beer cans tossed from a moving ute.
descriptions.c64:90459: Text adventure with graphics where an explorer treks through the Amazon jungle in search of a lost Aztec tomb; finding it ends the game.
descriptions.c64:90460: Defend Earth from invaders in a first-person 3D tank, hunting enemy tanks and planes across a wireframe battlefield.
descriptions.c64:90462: Based on the original mainframe adventure: rescue the elves and gather fifteen treasures, managing lamp batteries in dark caves and fighting dwarves with axes while carrying only four items.
descriptions.c64:90463: To break an energy embargo, steer a ship against gravity past falling meteors into one of four cosmic tunnels, fly through in a third-person view, then land on each asteroid to gather its energy bars, with every move draining fuel.
descriptions.c64:90469: Trapped inside a computer by a rogue 6502 processor, run through mazes collecting the exit key and the program disk while the MCP pursues.
descriptions.c64:90477: Hunt the Shadow through more than 120 rooms of his lair, shooting robot minions in a blend of Berzerk-style maze action and exploration.
descriptions.c64:90503: Drive a racing car up a vertically scrolling road for as many miles as possible, controlling speed up to 80mph and dodging other drivers and obstacles on three road types.
descriptions.c64:90504: Pinball simulation for one to four players with adjustable physics, including ball count, ball speed, table incline and bumper kick.
descriptions.c64:90505: As Plaqueman, protect teeth from the plaque germ D.K. using a toothbrush loaded with fluoride toothpaste and dental floss, without touching the germ.
descriptions.c64:90506: A survivor of pirate-raided Corillian hunts the pirates across a galaxy map in a powerful starship.
descriptions.c64:90510: Tactical tank and mechanized infantry battles, played as strategy or arcade, commanding at company, platoon or squad level with over 70 historical tanks.
descriptions.c64:90511: Defuse terrorist bombs in caverns beneath an erupting volcano across nine platform levels before they detonate.
descriptions.c64:90521: A flying, shooting robot rescues children wandering each level of platforms, dropping through gaps between floors while dodging hopping aliens, demons and snakes.
descriptions.c64:90528: Help New Phlan reclaim its monster-overrun districts on the Moonsea, leading a party through AD&D rules-based exploration and turn-based combat.
descriptions.c64:90553: Command a submarine sinking ships above and below the surface with forward and upward torpedoes, restocking from a dolphin sent by the green supply ship.
descriptions.c64:90554: Defend Federation space in the starship FSS Demona, using shields, hyperspace and lasers against a horde of barbarian ships.
descriptions.c64:90555: Climb a mountain past snakes, porcupines, an archer and falling eggs to grab a spear and hit the condor before it reaches the child below.
descriptions.c64:90556: Illustrated text adventure: starting with a pocket of gold coins, recover the magic sword Myraglym through forests, swamps, a maze and cliffs.
descriptions.c64:90557: Caesar guards the pantry, catching mice in his mouth and taking them over to the larder door before they eat the food.
descriptions.c64:90558: Statistical baseball strategy: manage pinch hitters, fielding positions, relievers and base runners for 28 major league teams, with custom team entry.
descriptions.c64:90560: Space shooter with configurable rules, including terrain on or off, shots that ricochet off screen edges and four difficulty levels.
descriptions.c64:90567: Pinball for one to four players modeled on the Black Knight table, with dual flippers, upper and lower playfields, multiball and a tilt mechanism.
descriptions.c64:90619: Shoot Droid ships and their mines in an endless arena, as the last ship of each wave spirals in.
descriptions.c64:90620: An underwater Pac-Man variant: the pakacuda fish eats smaller fish through a maze while fleeing octopuses.
descriptions.c64:90622: Sink enemy ships, especially fast PT boats, with four reloading torpedoes over a chosen game length of 1 to 9 minutes.
descriptions.c64:90623: Guard a bridge against tank after tank, moving left and right and adjusting gun elevation to time shells as they cross.
descriptions.c64:90624: Sequel to Colossal Adventure: a two-word text adventure in a Tolkien-flavored Middle Earth struck by crop failure, violent animals and a mysterious enemy.
descriptions.c64:90625: Galaxians-style shooter where enemy ships scroll across the screen in waves over eight looping levels.
descriptions.c64:90627: The Golden Baton has turned evil, bringing crop failure and sickness to the land, and the cure is to gather the scattered parts of the Arrow of Death. An illustrated text adventure.
descriptions.c64:90628: Holding every fragment of the Arrow of Death, the hero must locate the Fletcher who can put it together, in this illustrated text adventure.
descriptions.c64:90630: Type commands for altitude, course, radar and weapons to guide a B-1 bomber to its Soviet target past MiGs and SAMs.
descriptions.c64:90631: Guard lunar base supplies from waves of bandits with a mobile laser and shields across 28 levels, earning a bonus ship every 5,000 points.
descriptions.c64:90632: Galaxian clone: move left and right shooting swooping bats while avoiding their shots and collisions.
descriptions.c64:90633: D-Day wargame: as Allied commander, secure Sword, Gold, Juno, Omaha and Utah beaches and push toward Cherbourg, Caen and St. Lo, or defend as the Germans.
descriptions.c64:90634: Find machine parts hidden in a maze of houses and assemble them per the blueprint to stop Ollie Org from catching Daisy.
descriptions.c64:90635: Space Panic clone: dig holes for electrocuting Meanies, then bash them through before oxygen runs out.
descriptions.c64:90636: Regimental and brigade level Battle of the Bulge wargame, scoring victory points as the Germans by taking towns, exiting units and destroying American forces.
descriptions.c64:90637: Paint every room of a building before time runs out without losing your brushes, choosing from eight painters for up to four players across six skill levels.
descriptions.c64:90639: Operational carrier warfare in 1942 between US and Japanese fleets, with scenarios for Midway, Coral Sea, the Eastern Solomons and Santa Cruz Islands.
descriptions.c64:90642: Donkey Kong-style climber: scale ladders to the top past barrels rolled by a giant ape to rescue a girlfriend.
descriptions.c64:90643: Play a movie monster, crawling, swimming or flying, managing health and appetite while destroying cities.
descriptions.c64:90662: Defender clone: fly a starcruiser over a side-scrolling alien world protecting ten colonists from a hostile neighbor planet.
descriptions.c64:90752: Escape the dungeon within 60 minutes, past traps and guards, defeat the vizier and reach the princess.
descriptions.c64:90753: As schoolboy Eric, steal his report card from the staff room safe by completing tasks around a school full of computer-controlled teachers and pupils.
descriptions.c64:90809: Follow-up to the Super Sprint coin-op: one or two drivers race top-down around eight fresh circuits, dodging hazards such as whirlwinds and oil slicks along the way.
descriptions.c64:90927: As mayor of a brand-new town, zone land and lay down housing, roads, schools, factories and shops so citizens move in, find work and stay content.
descriptions.c64:90966: Pilot the Q10 Tankbuster across several war zones, strafing with a forward gun and dropping bombs on enemy aircraft, vehicles and installations; shooting a blue helicopter leaves behind a pickup icon.
descriptions.c64:91679: A pub darts simulation using traditional 501 rules over a best-of-three-sets match, either head to head or through a championship knockout against computer players drawn from a field of eight.
descriptions.c64:91746: Taking cues from Rampage, play an ogre or a dragon smashing buildings across an island in search of an egg that grants super powers, wrecking each structure with horn or fiery attacks to find the right one.
descriptions.c64:91931: Three karate fighters share a beach arena, each racing to be first to six points; every two rounds a bonus stage has a fighter deflecting bouncing balls. Sold in Europe as IK+.
descriptions.c64:95420: Steer Gogo, a small friendly ghost, through 150 rooms of a haunted castle, gathering objects and keeping clear of evil forces on the way to rescuing a princess. Level codes let a later session resume where the last one ended.
descriptions.c64:95670: Bugaboo, a tiny yellow flea with very long legs, has tumbled through a crack into a deep cavern; time his jumps to bounce back up the cave walls and escape to the surface.
descriptions.c64:95676: An arcade adventure in which control switches between Wally the handyman, his wife Wilma, and friends Tom the mechanic, Dick the plumber and Harry the electrician, each needed for different jobs around town.
descriptions.c64:95710: Captain a merchant frigate trading between Barbary Coast ports to raise ransom money for Katherine, a daughter kidnapped by the pirate Bloodthroat.
descriptions.c64:99113: Cactus Pete, outlaw with a $4000 bounty, rides his horse alongside moving trains, matching speed to grab the ladder and climb aboard for another robbery, all seen from an elevated side view.
descriptions.c64:99114: Fire the button to push puzzle pieces one at a time onto an empty board, then slide each into place to rebuild a hidden picture, guided by a small preview image.
descriptions.c64:99115: Careless tourists have littered Poconose National Park with cans, bottles and rubber balls, and a park ranger must patrol the grounds clearing up the mess.
descriptions.c64:local-015ed4a7ad: Barnaby picks blocks from five chutes and arranges them on a springboard before sending them to the building site, stacking a stable tower tall enough to climb to the exit ladder; time per level shrinks, though an instructor mode removes the clock.
descriptions.c64:local-01a9c01bb0: Illustrated Level 9 text adventure in three parts that retells Malory's Lancelot: beat the Black Knight, join the Round Table, and finally seek the Holy Grail, with companions such as Sir Bors who can be given orders through the parser.
descriptions.c64:local-020700179f: Defuse every bomb the Alienators planted across 30 levels of Jupiter Headquarters, running girders and climbing ladders and ropes; each stage has its own hazards, and some bombs reshape the level when collected, so their order matters.
descriptions.c64:local-02ca667774: Domark's conversion of Atari's isometric Return of the Jedi coin-op. Leia races a speeder bike through Endor's forests, Chewbacca pilots a stolen AT-ST, and the Millennium Falcon flies against TIE fighters and into the second Death Star.
descriptions.c64:local-02e64d6e47: A hidden passage in a London flat leads to Pirate's Isle in this Scott Adams two-word text adventure, where you build a seaworthy ship and win over a pirate and his parrot to recover Long John Silver's two lost treasures.
descriptions.c64:local-030d46acce: Pilot an attack shuttle through an isometric scrolling enemy fortress, judging altitude by its shadow and an altimeter to slip through wall gaps and force fields, shooting fuel tanks to stay airborne before dogfighting in open space.
descriptions.c64:local-0440b29510: Guide a crosshair to shield a baby from eagles, spiders and worms while popping the balloons drifting across the screen; every creature that reaches the infant drains milk, and the game ends when milk or ammunition runs out.
descriptions.c64:local-044f6f7ffc: To lift a plague from your village, descend into the catacombs to find a sorcerer's potion formula and its ingredients, playing as the fighter Duke or the cunning Witch in an illustrated text adventure where some creatures talk and others must be fought.
descriptions.c64:local-04e1267800: Moonboots the Lunar Explorer, stranded in Metropolis, must find and refuel his spaceship in this flick-screen platformer, turning into Zoid the Droid, Super Spy or the Mad Monk when carrying the right objects to reach areas closed to him.
descriptions.c64:local-05ff96f565: Ralph the dog watches over his sleepwalking master Lee, bridging gaps, fending off enemies and keeping him from falling into water so that he never wakes up, with dream bonus stages between the main levels.
descriptions.c64:local-061b4c3d24: A grounded alien cruiser disguised as public toilets on Cleethorpes pier needs protecting: hover overhead stunning the people and dogs who come for the fleet's battle plans, now resembling toilet paper, while avoiding jets and an RSPCA helicopter.
descriptions.c64:local-064206b5ed: Drug captured scientists and deliver them to the supercomputer The Big One, each unlocking one letter of its code, in a multi-directional scrolling overhead shooter where you can dive beneath surface layers or leave the ship on foot.
descriptions.c64:local-065e2282e8: Level 9's final text adventure, with pictures. Detective Alan Chance, killed when an undercover drugs operation was betrayed, returns as a ghost at his own funeral and has three nights to expose the traitor, clear his name and save his partner Sarah.
descriptions.c64:local-06a79d8f37: Roll up a character at the innkeeper's, buy weapons and armor, then explore the temple's monster-filled dungeon levels room by room in a top-down view, with the manual's room descriptions filling in what the sparse graphics show.
descriptions.c64:local-077c9ed1c2: Illustrated and scored with music, this text adventure begins after Ereth, the evil Lord Death, has turned Carus's beloved royal family to stone, and a wandering traveler vows to find five scattered magic gems that will break the spell.
descriptions.c64:local-07fe2926b5: Rule a barony in feudal England from 1156 in yearly turns, setting taxes and tolls, paying scutage to the king and managing your army, with a joust where you aim your lance before the year's battles, revolts and harvest are shown.
descriptions.c64:local-09258c21ed: International Rescue takes on four missions with two-member teams you switch between: freeing miners from a flooding mine, saving a crippled nuclear submarine, breaking into a bank for documents, and stopping a madman in his lair.
descriptions.c64:local-09d8a927d7: As a policeman, fight through city streets, a park and a bridge to the prison itself to free a warden held by escaped convicts; rescuing hostages earns weapons like a tear gas gun, but shooting one costs every weapon you hold.
descriptions.c64:local-0ac01f8ce1: Chasing the ape Bongo, who set his tent alight, a safari hunter climbs four isometric single-screen stages in the manner of Donkey Kong, dodging coconuts and other animal attacks with no weapon but his jumps.
descriptions.c64:local-0b1dba078d: Domark's James Bond racing game, which began as Elite's Aquablast: Bond drives an armed speedboat along hazard-filled waterways, recalling the boat chase of the 1973 film.
descriptions.c64:local-0be9243bbd: Home version of Irem's Moon Patrol: a Luna City patrol buggy rolls across the scrolling lunar surface, jumping craters and mines, blasting boulders ahead and shooting down attacking UFOs, checkpoint by checkpoint.
descriptions.c64:local-0c4b0ba7b4: Crash-landed on the hostile planet Zarp in 2554, Earth's last agent must find the data to defuse a planet-killing bomb in this illustrated text adventure, with no obvious way off the planet afterward.
descriptions.c64:local-0c6e9660a1: Sequel to The Dungeons: roll attributes, choose fighter or magician, buy gear from a dwarf, then grope through unlit rooms past a fire-breathing dragon and other monsters to find a scroll whose riddle is the way out, entering one-letter commands.
descriptions.c64:local-0cccd8d781: Chameleon restores balance across five side-scrolling levels themed on fire, water, earth and air, finding hidden exits and triggering power points at the right time of day while switching among four missile types against elemental demons.
descriptions.c64:local-0cce559a30: Xain, the Soldier of Light, frees five invaded planets in any order, from desert to frozen worlds, running and gunning through each with collectable weapons before a short space shooter stage, then assaults a final fortress planet.
descriptions.c64:local-0cda2f49eb: A behind-the-skier 3D winter game with Downhill, Slalom, Giant Slalom and Ski Jump events, played in training or competition for up to five players, with penalty points for missed gates, leaving the course or hitting trees and spectators.
descriptions.c64:local-0e2ea99ac1: Rod Pike's three-part illustrated text adventure: as Dr Frankenstein you hunt the creature that killed your sister, and in the final part you become the monster itself, waking without memory and slowly learning.
descriptions.c64:local-0fa34d4492: In a city wrecked by nuclear disaster, Geitor battles with sword and shield through a Trojan-style fighting game toward the Townsman headquarters, facing sword warriors, fireball-throwing mutants and a fierce female gang while hunting five nuclear tanks.
descriptions.c64:local-0fc8ce7b4f: Fanatics have armed the Doomsday device, leaving 25 minutes to fly to its building and destroy it in this cockpit-view 3D shooter, dodging laser beams and flak, refuelling midway and watching the scanner and damage gauges.
descriptions.c64:local-0fe05aba9c: A single-table pinball game with two sets of flippers at the bottom and four bumpers on each side; hitting the gap bumpers that spell SAGITTARIAN across the top turns them into bonus lights, while a running bonus grows by 50 at a time.
descriptions.c64:local-10734fe40e: The first half of Scott Adams's two-part adventure: stranded on a tropical island menaced by storms and a volcano, explore beaches, jungle and caves with two-word commands; finishing reveals the password for Part II.
descriptions.c64:local-1173808de8: Scott Adams's notoriously hard island adventure: washed up on a remote shore under threat of a volcano and violent weather, you dig, build equipment and cross water with terse verb-noun commands to learn why you are there.
descriptions.c64:local-125ece37db: Hover an inertia-heavy craft over an isometric grid of rising squares, boosting upward to line up precisely on energy spheres and ferrying them to a transformer that beams the power back to an energy-starved Earth.
descriptions.c64:local-127ffb2ff3: Stuart Smith's role-playing adventure from the Age of Adventure pack. Ali Baba crosses a maze-like city and wilderness of Arabian tales to rescue a princess; up to 17 players can join in hot-seat co-operative play, and the quest can even be finished peacefully.
descriptions.c64:local-131bf2c088: Pac-Man seen from inside the maze: wander first-person 3D corridors eating pills while ghosts may wait around any corner, with an overhead map of the layout beside the view.
descriptions.c64:local-1328790d2c: A Centipede-style shooter: a droid near the bottom fires upward at a segmented creature that winds down through the barriers, while spiders and other pests roam in for bonus points.
descriptions.c64:local-132e848abb: International Rescue answers a call from Egyptologists trapped in a tomb: load up to 40 tons of equipment into Thunderbird 2, then steer through block-filled mazes where Thunderbird 1 and 2 can each shift only certain colored blocks, minding fuel.
descriptions.c64:local-1423853ebe: Checkers played with a light pen: move pieces diagonally on the 8x8 board, capture by jumping, and crown pieces that reach the far side as kings able to move in both directions.
descriptions.c64:local-148d0e6e5e: An early real-time strategy game: direct your landed army with a cursor across an alien planet, protect your vital bombs, detonate at least two beside the enemy weather control station, then evacuate fast.
descriptions.c64:local-15061767ca: Patrol a fast 3D arena in a probe vehicle shooting saucers and homing missiles; after enough kills, run a stargate barrage of oncoming spheres to warp to the next of eight planets.
descriptions.c64:local-152a6e0371: As Amity's Chief Brody, explore 150-plus underwater screens shooting fish and recovering the four pieces of the weapon that can kill the shark, while deciding when to close beaches against the wishes of a cost-conscious Mayor.
descriptions.c64:local-15b912cc00: An overhead racer: hold fire to accelerate up the scrolling road, weaving through traffic to score 20,000 inside the minute and earn more time; a crash leaves the car smoking until you pull into the pit lane for repairs.
descriptions.c64:local-15cece03dc: A sheriff defends his town over five waves of outlaws raiding the saloon and bank, shooting in eight directions as they ride in, throw dynamite and fire from windows, with an undertaker clearing bodies and a quick-draw duel after each wave.
descriptions.c64:local-163fac93d6: Darrian defends human colonies from the Xenites in a vertically scrolling shooter where his craft switches between ground tank and jet, each needed for different targets, collecting upgrades from destroyed enemies.
descriptions.c64:local-16d89c6966: Recover the twelve Signs of the Zodiac from demon-guarded corridors lined with a lethal force field, 400 of them in all, shooting only while on the move, before a final battle with the demon Jemon.
descriptions.c64:local-182f31545f: Concluding Level 9's Silicon Dreams trilogy, this text adventure explores the domed cities of Eden, a society run on fines and robots, where you must get home before dark on a decimal clock and note building coordinates that change each game.
descriptions.c64:local-187df6c23b: Concluding half of Scott Adams' Savage Island text adventure, unlocked with the password earned in Part I. The player wakes in a small metal room behind a force field and must search glowing corridors for the clue that finally explains the island's secret.
descriptions.c64:local-189becdd87: A Donkey Kong-style single-screen climber: run up diagonal stepped platforms, jumping the barrels hurled by a giant ape, to rescue the maidens held at the top, one per screen.
descriptions.c64:local-18d42307f8: Defend an outpost's last Neutronium deposits by driving a combat vehicle along the surface, weaving between rows of rocks while shooting alien craft overhead and the automated mining vehicles still prowling for ore.
descriptions.c64:local-195248a7d7: A version of Defender: fly a fast ship back and forth above a planet surface, destroying waves of alien raiders.
descriptions.c64:local-1979a36b36: Mario and Luigi clear the sewer pipes of crabs, turtles and fighter flies by bumping the platform beneath each one to flip it, then kicking it away, with coins to collect and a competitive two-player mode.
descriptions.c64:local-1a241df178: Infocom's science fiction text adventure: a lowly deck-scrubbing ensign escapes his exploding ship to the deserted planet Resida, explores its abandoned research complex with the robot Floyd, and works out what happened to its people.
descriptions.c64:local-1a438531aa: Based on the TV game show, this trivia contest lets you answer questions or take a dare, with toss-up and physical challenges and a final obstacle course.
descriptions.c64:local-1acd492f7a: Hunt the battleship Bismarck in a torpedo plane, working separate pilot, engineer, navigator and gunner panels to take off, plan patrol areas and line up the decisive torpedo run.
descriptions.c64:local-1b1410d899: A side-view boxing game: win three bouts for the European title, then three more for the world crown, with adjustable stamina, a two-player fight and an opponent editor; one knockdown, when the head-hit gauge fills, decides each bout.
descriptions.c64:local-1d349ee7b7: Second part of Mike Doran's Ormus Saga role-playing trilogy, Guild of Death. In January 1228, two years after Lord Marox and the Ormus Cult were defeated, Beryland faces Armageddon unless the hero completes nine tasks set by the God Servants within about a year.
descriptions.c64:local-1d541f6e52: The final Time and Magik adventure from Level 9: Myglar, keeper of the Red Moon crystal, has turned its power on the magicians of Baskalos and must be stopped, using 18 spells cast with three-letter codes found along the way.
descriptions.c64:local-1db7bbf57d: Take one of 32 European national sides through qualifying and on to the European Championship finals, picking the squad, formation and style of play, then watching matches unfold on a full-pitch view with key events reported in text.
descriptions.c64:local-1e33e0ddb5: Activision's jungle platformer: Pitfall Harry has 20 minutes to grab treasure, swinging on vines over tar pits and quicksand, leaping crocodiles and rolling logs, and taking underground tunnels to cover ground faster.
descriptions.c64:local-1ec7185690: A circus event game: put tigers through their routine, turn somersaults and corkscrews on the trapeze, cross the tightrope with handstands, and do stunts on horseback, separately or in an international competition.
descriptions.c64:local-1ef1873b36: Tennis for up to four players on grass, clay and hard courts with their own bounce, offering men's five-set and women's three-set singles, mixed doubles, and computer-only matches.
descriptions.c64:local-1f14614217: Simon Pick's budget drum machine for Firebird, built on sampled kick, snare, tom, hi-hat and cymbal sounds. Beats are built as bar patterns, chained into songs, or tapped out live on the keyboard.
descriptions.c64:local-1f39ce9eb1: An arcade adventure from Stevenson's novel: Jim Hawkins boards ship and reaches Treasure Island, then explores a maze of flick screens, using a limited stock of cutlasses on pirates in his way as he hunts down Long John Silver.
descriptions.c64:local-1f5c45b469: A hex-based turn-based wargame refighting Gettysburg, Gaines Mill, Stones River, Chickamauga and Chattanooga for either side, modeling limited command and fog of war, with a scenario editor.
descriptions.c64:local-2077571128: Steer a creature around two mazes, switching between them with the fire button, to carry eight bone-shaped treasures to the maze centres while avoiding roaming creatures; yellow bones let you kill most of them, though survivors may carry treasure off again.
descriptions.c64:local-20ff80492c: A fixed-screen shooter where your ship travels around all four edges of the screen, firing inward at swarms of abstract shapes that circle in patterns, over 24 levels.
descriptions.c64:local-21890e5877: Statistics-driven baseball simulation from Sublogic in which the player manages a club: set lineups, choose pitchers, make substitutions and call plays, against a friend or the computer, or let the computer handle both sides. Rosters cover the 1985 major-league season plus classic teams.
descriptions.c64:local-23a1260dd7: A tank battle for up to three players, two on joysticks and one on the keyboard, fought round by round with random power-ups and coins to spend on lasting upgrades in a shop; a lone player gets target practice rounds instead.
descriptions.c64:local-242338024a: Sador the reptile man searches nine regions of Haven for magic left by the defeated sorcerer High Vanish, each find giving a cryptic clue to the next, while shooting monsters in a flick-screen overhead maze.
descriptions.c64:local-246ed196db: Scarab must escape a pyramid by pushing pairs of matching stones into line so they vanish, around teleporters, ice and traps, in a 100-level logic mode or a timed arcade mode with random boards; a level editor is included.
descriptions.c64:local-24cf03afb7: Guard six cities on the planet Eetalamer from falling missiles by placing a crosshair where your limited shots will explode into expanding fireballs, picking off planes and satellites for bonus points.
descriptions.c64:local-256de4d34d: An astronaut floats out to catch a stray satellite, shooting or avoiding asteroids and rival spacemen, then holds fire to tow it back into the ship; each level brings faster hazards.
descriptions.c64:local-25c8c29665: A madman threatens to wipe out the five biggest cities on Earth with nuclear weapons, and you have until June 9th to stop him: a verb-noun adventure that hops between London, Paris, Rome, San Juan and Miami, with a water-skiing contest and a missile-shooting sequence.
descriptions.c64:local-260315777b: Set to the High Noon film theme, this western shooter has a lone lawman holding off gangs who ride into town, hurl dynamite and hide in windows, ending at the outlaws' cave; every wave closes with a showdown to see who draws first.
descriptions.c64:local-27e9bcbf37: Orion's stars are breaking formation, and only chemicals from alien-held mining colonies can restore their balance; walk across the colonies in side view, blasting the occupiers.
descriptions.c64:local-27efb98f6d: A Bomberman-style maze battle for up to four players using a four-joystick adapter, with range, bomb count, speed, kicking and remote-detonation power-ups across eight arenas such as a dark Night Shift and a closing-in Under Pressure.
descriptions.c64:local-284274b4ba: A Missile Command clone: move a crosshair to burst your limited missiles in front of falling nuclear tracers to protect six cities, shooting passing planes for bonuses, with a selectable wind speed.
descriptions.c64:local-2944039f7a: Cosmi baseball game in which Steve Garvey and Jose Canseco, the only real players, always lead opposing sides. Teams win on points rather than runs: grand slams and homers score big, conceding a run costs 300, and with the bases loaded one of the stars bats with seven strikes.
descriptions.c64:local-29e21c7cbd: Guide a lander down onto Jupiter's surface with vertical and side thrusters, keeping descent speed low and fuel in reserve; narrower pads score x5 or x10 and each safe landing tops up fuel for another try.
descriptions.c64:local-2acd05c76a: Rebuild a given shape, such as a giant letter A, from a limited stock of eight block types that can be rotated and placed, racing a time limit; two players can cooperate, taking turns on one puzzle.
descriptions.c64:local-2adefa7e17: A side-scrolling martial arts game in which a ninja fights his way through guards with fists, a dagger and shuriken, gathering scattered idols that restore strength; collecting all of them wins.
descriptions.c64:local-2ae44a71fb: Steer a craft through the 20 deadly levels of André Thelman's maze, jumping holes, shooting robots and solving switch puzzles to find the right teleporter; turning around flips the entire level.
descriptions.c64:local-2aeaac8114: Fly a small plane leftward over enemy planes, troops and missile launchers, shoot down the plane carrying dynamite, then crash into a castle gate to free hostages and ferry them home two at a time in a replacement plane.
descriptions.c64:local-2bdeb5c92d: Victorious after Troy's fall, Odysseus heads home to Ithaca, where rumours say his throne, wife Penelope and son Telemachus are in danger, in a two-part text adventure of surviving the voyage and then reclaiming the kingdom.
descriptions.c64:local-2c6f8ad5fa: The villain Phobos has built 15 planets based on common fears such as spiders, snakes and dentists; fly to each, blast across its surface and through its caverns to rescue the Galactic Emperor, alone or with two players at once.
descriptions.c64:local-2c85432374: Based on the darts quiz show for two players: throw at category segments to earn questions, compete on a standard board for the right to answer, then try the red-and-black bonus board without hitting the same red twice.
descriptions.c64:local-2ce2dcfbc0: Manage an English county cricket side through the championship, choosing the team, bowlers and field placings and buying players from scouts, with matches followed on a running scorecard rather than played.
descriptions.c64:local-2dda3dcc4c: River Software text adventure: a bounty hunter armed with a pulsar is beamed to Bodholm Downs on the planet Karakata and must kill a set number of Viroids before he can return home and collect his fee.
descriptions.c64:local-2e1b9f6b61: Judge Dredd takes on six crime missions in Mega-City One in a scrolling side-view game, switching between walking, which lets him shoot and arrest, and the faster Lawmaster bike, before the crime rate climbs too high.
descriptions.c64:local-2ea9948c72: Text-only edition of Level 9's revised trilogy: Lords of Time sends the player through history for nine treasures, Red Moon hunts a stolen magic crystal, and The Price of Magik confronts the mad magician Myglar.
descriptions.c64:local-2eab9efd1f: Sublogic's combat flight simulator: fly an F-16 from land or an F/A-18 off a carrier, practise in free flight, dogfight MiGs or strike land and sea targets with a chosen load of missiles and bombs.
descriptions.c64:local-2f0c8504b2: Recover seven pieces of your father's crown from the Ice Queen's palace by rotating hexagonal rooms to link their exits, burning creatures with a firestick and solving object puzzles on a text screen as a candle burns down.
descriptions.c64:local-2fa6aba6e9: Potsworth the dog and his Midnight Patrol friends cross five platform levels of the Dream Zone to recover the sleep potion stolen by the Nightmare Prince, pushing crates onto switches and using each character's own ability.
descriptions.c64:local-3015efeffc: A former soldier clears his name and rescues his kidnapped brother and niece from terrorists by gathering evidence in Last Ninja-style isometric screens, then racing an armed car between stages past bombers and police.
descriptions.c64:local-30ce345cf1: Play three pawns against three on a 3x3 board, aiming to reach the far row or leave the computer without a move; the program learns from every loss and soon becomes very hard to beat.
descriptions.c64:local-31727797a7: A soldier with an extending bionic arm swings from fixed points and climbs between levels instead of jumping, pulling enemies in as he storms a fortress to destroy the launch computer of a doomsday weapon.
descriptions.c64:local-32f8b76d19: A text-based bridge game for one player, who handles both the north and south hands through the bidding and then tries to take the contracted tricks.
descriptions.c64:local-33dec97c33: Treasure hunters vanish in the desert searching for the buried tomb of the pharaoh Rak-Tuman. In this typed-command text adventure you follow a map across the sands to the pyramid, then face its puzzles, traps and creatures.
descriptions.c64:local-343d3570bd: Sequel to Barbarian in which either the barbarian or the princess he rescued hunts the sorcerer Drax through four dungeon levels, using one-on-one sword combat against monsters that each call for different attacks.
descriptions.c64:local-34b014916f: Version of the classic BASIC Super Star Trek: command the Enterprise across a galaxy of quadrants, hunting Klingon warships with phasers and photon torpedoes before the stardates run out, docking at starbases to repair and resupply.
descriptions.c64:local-3505588e3a: A version of Joseph Weizenbaum's ELIZA conversation program: the computer plays a psychotherapist, picking out key words in whatever the user types and turning statements back into questions.
descriptions.c64:local-3572d4ced7: Audiogenic's cricket game endorsed by Graham Gooch. In simulation mode the player makes the captain's decisions while the computer plays the match; in arcade mode one or two players bat and bowl directly, over limited-overs or two-innings games.
descriptions.c64:local-36b6d2c052: Konami's table tennis conversion: rally against the computer across nine skill levels, playing to 10 points with a two-point lead. Scoring rewards long rallies and wide winning margins.
descriptions.c64:local-36dd89aa54: Educational detective game for kids. Ghostly happenings at the Cable family's old mansion in Granite Point and a missing Siamese cat must be explained by driving the SnoopMobile around town, questioning eight suspects and gathering clues.
descriptions.c64:local-37142b7c02: Ultima-style fantasy role-playing game set in Beryland in 1227, where the Ormus Cult and its leader Lord Marox have taken power. The hero roams a scrolling overland map, visits cities and hires troops, who are needed to capture or defend a city.
descriptions.c64:local-379d50a6f0: Text adventure that starts by an abandoned cottage in an old forest; find the castle said to house goblins guarding a hoard, recover the treasure and escape, scoring up to 160 points. The parser handles full sentences.
descriptions.c64:local-39a7dfa194: Capcom's action platformer where the soldier cannot jump: instead his extendable bionic arm latches onto ledges to swing and climb, and also drags enemies in, on the way to the enemy fortress and its doomsday launch computer.
descriptions.c64:local-3ada3562b0: Alligata's vertically flick-screen commando shooter across eight occupied zones. A rifle and a handful of grenades share one fire button (tap or hold), and captured comrades being marched away can be freed.
descriptions.c64:local-3ca68baa62: Ozark Softscape's exploration game: sail from Spain to the New World in 1492 (or to a randomly generated continent), meet native peoples, found missions and forts, and bring back gold to win promotions from the Queen.
descriptions.c64:local-3d2ba777f2: Melbourne House's Judge Dredd: pick crime reports such as arson or murder off the Mega-City map, then enter each location for a platform shoot-out with the perps, backed by a synth-rock soundtrack.
descriptions.c64:local-40a11050bc: Starbyte's platform game about becoming king by winning challenges in six countries in any order, each with its own mini-game, from jumping a knight's horse over hurdles in England to riding a flying carpet in Arabia.
descriptions.c64:local-40a1efd4f3: Sports compilation with ten-pin bowling, air hockey, darts and ping pong. Each event offers computer opponents at several skill levels as well as two-player matches, using timing-based aim and power controls.
descriptions.c64:local-40e4e26230: Hewson maze game starring Flippo, who must turn every tile of a maze to the target colour by walking over it. Some tiles flip back or only change from certain directions, and enemies, holes and power-ups complicate each level.
descriptions.c64:local-4127667efd: Arcade conversion in which a commando dashes left and right at the foot of the screen dodging fire while steering a crosshair to gun down soldiers, tanks and helicopters and level the scenery across five stages. Two players can join in.
descriptions.c64:local-415c109f8d: Bond takes the wheel of a modified, armed speedboat in this 1988 Domark racer, loosely based on the 1973 film's river chase and adapted from an Elite game first planned as Aquablast.
descriptions.c64:local-417272213b: Domark's computer edition of the trivia board game using the Genus question set: players move around the wheel-shaped board answering questions in six categories, aiming to win a wedge in each before the final question at the hub.
descriptions.c64:local-4224fda37f: The first Speedball: a brutal future sport on a compact court with five players a side, no fouls and a goal at each end. Bribe the referee or boost your squad between matches in a knockout cup or a two-player game.
descriptions.c64:local-435091924d: Vertically scrolling shooter from Sega's arcade game. Fly the Sonic Boom jet through six stages of planes, tanks, trains and gun emplacements, picking up weapon upgrades and beating each end boss within the time limit.
descriptions.c64:local-43842b5426: A park ranger, male or female, cleans litter from a lake on foot or by dinghy while avoiding turtles and snakes, saving swimmers, chasing off food-stealing ants and log rolling for bonus points.
descriptions.c64:local-439cbc88ba: Epyx toy-car playground based on Mattel's Hot Wheels: build or pick a car, paint it and cruise around town, stopping at the car wash, gas station or oil change for small mini-games, or entering events like the demolition derby.
descriptions.c64:local-43ab334900: Level 9 adventure with pictures in which Grindleguts the orc wakes after a night's drinking strapped to a horse for a joust and sets out to get even with his friends. Other characters keep their own schedules in real time, and the story later turns to science fiction.
descriptions.c64:local-4432db7554: Datasoft illustrated adventure set in the Old West. Retired Texas Ranger Kip Starr crosses deserts, mines and ghost towns to save a friend from hanging, with commands typed or picked from an on-screen menu by joystick.
descriptions.c64:local-44594b076c: Software Projects' home take on the Dragon's Lair laserdisc game: Dirk the Daring battles through a run of deadly screens inside Singe the dragon's castle on his way to rescue Princess Daphne.
descriptions.c64:local-4552a79ad3: Stuart Smith's Greek-myth role-playing game, reissued in Electronic Arts' Age of Adventure. Players take one or more heroes on quests, each rated for strength, dexterity and speed, with training in sword, dagger and defence.
descriptions.c64:local-464bb6c50c: Domark's version of the Empire Strikes Back arcade game. Luke's snowspeeder hunts Imperial probe droids, then fights AT-AT and AT-ST walkers on Hoth, before Han Solo takes the Millennium Falcon past TIE fighters and through an asteroid field.
descriptions.c64:local-47368d523a: Scott Adams' second adventure. A secret passage in a London flat leads to Pirate's Isle, where you must build a ship, win over a pirate and his parrot, and bring Long John Silver's two treasures home using two-word commands.
descriptions.c64:local-47f0224216: Imagic shooter where you fly through Star Quadrant Jupiter dodging solar hazards, swoop down onto passing moons to pick up stranded miners, then use the accelerator rings to blast back into space once six are aboard.
descriptions.c64:local-48456bdfd4: Martech helicopter shooter in pseudo-3D. Fly a heavily armed SuperCobra over varied terrain by day and night, downing a quota of enemy aircraft on each level to advance, with smart bombs for tight spots.
descriptions.c64:local-486f309fec: Computer version of Kalah, the mancala board game: players sow seeds from their six pits around the board, aiming to gather the most in their own store, with captures and extra turns for well-placed final seeds.
descriptions.c64:local-48f550316d: Firebird action game loosely inspired by The Jewel of the Nile. Free three captured travellers and arm them with their weapons (grenades, a pistol, an umbrella), then position them on each screen before guards attack while you control one directly.
descriptions.c64:local-4aebf07db1: Magic Bytes game known in English as The Paranoia Complex. A citizen of a city run by a dictatorial computer hunts rebel terrorists, recovers disks from their bodies for cash and promotions, and must pass loyalty quizzes or become the hunted.
descriptions.c64:local-4bd43ebe71: A Tetris variant from UKY Company in which two players can stack falling blocks at the same time.
descriptions.c64:local-4c0aaec753: Based on the Choose Your Own Adventure book, Escape has you flee the totalitarian state of Dorado in 2035 through a street maze, driving and flying sections, accompanied by three companions, one of them a traitor.
descriptions.c64:local-4c6a6682f1: Synapse platform game set inside a sealed pharaoh's tomb. Explore the chambers grabbing treasure while the pharaoh and his guardian mummy roam the passages hunting intruders.
descriptions.c64:local-4cf6f256cd: Each stage hands control to a different member of the Jetson family, starting with George slipping out of Spacely's Space Sprockets unseen; between the platform levels you pilot the jet-car home, watching your speed and dodging black holes.
descriptions.c64:local-4d05a05821: CDS's 1982 Frogger clone: hop a toad safely across the road through the traffic.
descriptions.c64:local-4dad1be7c3: Two-program World Cup package. One part holds every past tournament result plus a timed multiple-choice quiz; the other is a management game where you pick a squad, follow matches as text highlights and play heading, shooting and penalty mini-games.
descriptions.c64:local-4f2805a0a1: A sailing simulation of the America's Cup races over the 24.3-mile course off Perth, sailed alone or head to head by two players.
descriptions.c64:local-4f9d9bf3cf: Scott Adams' first adventure, in its text-only form. Recover 13 treasures from an enchanted land of forests, swamps, caves and a volcano, dealing with a dragon, bees and Paul Bunyan's ox using two-word commands.
descriptions.c64:local-50c1562682: Fantasy Software shooter set inside a pyramid of 120 chambers spread over fifteen levels. Each room holds its own alien species; shoot enough to drop a crystal, catch it once it turns blue and use it to open the exit you choose.
descriptions.c64:local-50f36c963a: A fast Defender-style shooter: Leader-1 blasts waves of craft in flight, lands in robot form to pelt ground vehicles with rocks, and gathers Scooter clones to use as bombs on the enemy base's spheres. Gravity pulls him toward the nearer screen edge.
descriptions.c64:local-5153659041: A Sesame Street learning game: children lay a route of pipes, waterways and sea creatures to carry Rubber Duckie to Ernie's bathtub, with help from Bert, Grover, Oscar and Cookie Monster, practising logic, sequencing and compass directions.
descriptions.c64:local-51ac31148e: Elite's conversion of SNK's Ikari Warriors: one or two commandos fight up a vertically scrolling battlefield of jungle, rivers and ruins, picking up grenades, machine guns and rocket launchers along the way.
descriptions.c64:local-51bcdb3090: Flash Gordon first hunts through a jungle for Prince Barin's cave, then must beat Barin in a hand-to-hand bout to earn his jet-bike, and finally races the bike over a chequered landscape.
descriptions.c64:local-5269ae1c75: An overhead run-and-gun shooter in the Gauntlet mould from Elite, built for one player or two fighting side by side at once.
descriptions.c64:local-529018369c: A computer edition of the Kensington board game, played on a pattern of hexagons, squares and triangles. Forming triangles and squares lets you move enemy counters; the first to fill all six corners of a white hexagon or one of your own colour wins.
descriptions.c64:local-53ebb0b99b: Pilot a supply ship with real momentum down into the Caverns of Eriban, delivering cargo to underground mining depots. Land gently beside each tower whose light shows red, refuel at the surface and avoid touching the cave walls.
descriptions.c64:local-542816c902: Platform game from Italy's Idea Software. One of the planet's two moons holds back an evil serpent with its magic, but an eclipse by the other is about to free it, so the hero fights and jumps through the land collecting items and solving puzzles.
descriptions.c64:local-5458c8c593: Ocean beat-'em-up based on the Schwarzenegger film. As Soviet cop Ivan Danko you punch and head-butt your way through four scrolling levels after drug lord Viktor Rosta, sometimes grabbing a pistol with six shots.
descriptions.c64:local-5460fde72a: Horizontally scrolling shoot-'em-up in the vein of Delta. Fly a Hunter Killer fighter through waves of aliens to win back the Radius, a vital hyperspace route seized by invaders.
descriptions.c64:local-557e5f61cd: Mike Singleton's 1983 space shoot-'em-up for Postern, drawn in red-and-blue anaglyph 3D meant to be viewed through the matching glasses.
descriptions.c64:local-5664dd93cd: The original Speedball, a violent future sport played five-a-side on a compact court where anything goes. Bribe the referee or power up your players before matches, then play a knockout cup or a two-player game.
descriptions.c64:local-5739c71343: Aardvark text adventure: a tractor beam drags your spaceship into a space station, and you must explore it, find the right items and avoid lethal hazards to get away again.
descriptions.c64:local-58274389a2: Police management strategy set in the fictional British town of Middletown. Assign officers and units to four stations across the map, cover three shifts a day and react to crimes and events, with a traffic-light mini-game each week.
descriptions.c64:local-582e296f5c: Ocean's isometric prison-camp adventure. A captured POW follows the daily routine of roll calls, meals and exercise, slipping away to gather keys, uniforms and tools for an escape while avoiding guards and solitary confinement.
descriptions.c64:local-5963729943: Firebird's budget sample-based drum machine, expanded: build drum patterns in Bars mode, chain them into a track in Song mode or play the kit live from the keyboard, with four sample sets including Latin, disco and vocal sounds.
descriptions.c64:local-5982b4f192: Codemasters puzzle game: tilt a top-down maze to roll a ball into the hole without touching walls, opening gates with timed button presses. Energy is limited and the ball grows larger as you progress.
descriptions.c64:local-5a003018fb: System 3 shoot-'em-up that opens with a vertically scrolling stage before switching to horizontal scrolling, with speed-ups, extra cannons and other power-ups to collect and a large boss at the end of each level.
descriptions.c64:local-5baba4f95f: Sega's isometric climbing game. A safari hunter chases the ape Bongo, who set fire to his tent, across four single-screen stages, jumping past coconuts and other animal attacks with no way to fight back.
descriptions.c64:local-5bb084b81a: Magic Disk 64 version of Mastermind, the code-breaking puzzle: deduce a hidden combination of colours by reading the hints given after each guess.
descriptions.c64:local-5d5a48ab72: Isometric shooter after Sega's arcade game. Steer a shuttle through an enemy fortress, judging altitude from its shadow and an altimeter to slip through wall gaps and under force barriers while shooting fuel tanks and gun turrets.
descriptions.c64:local-5d70f948c7: Alligata shooter seen from a battleship's gun position. Swing a sight through 360 degrees and up into the sky to shoot down waves of attacking aircraft, using radar to spot raids before the damaged ship sinks.
descriptions.c64:local-5da0219188: Software Country's 1985 tribute to four pre-microcomputer classics: the Crowther and Woods Adventure, the Eliza chatbot, Conway's Life and Pong, the last offered both as a character-based version and a colour remake.
descriptions.c64:local-5f0f30daf5: Illustrated adventure blending Greek myths, in which you direct both Jason and Hercules through a three-part labyrinth full of traps and monsters to reach the Golden Fleece at its centre.
descriptions.c64:local-601c5bb379: The action game of the third Indiana Jones film. Whip and fist-fight through four levels (Colorado caves, a circus train, a Zeppelin and Castle Grunwald) to collect the Cross of Coronado, the shield and the Grail diary.
descriptions.c64:local-60471410ee: Missile Command-style shooter from the Magic Disk 64 magazine: guard your cities from incoming missiles by steering a crosshair and detonating defensive blasts in their path.
descriptions.c64:local-60757e5346: Ice hockey game with exhibition, season and playoff modes. Play is seen from the side, cuts to a close shot camera when anyone shoots on goal, and rough fouls can turn into a fistfight that decides who sits in the penalty box.
descriptions.c64:local-60c1f6e097: Artillery simulation from the War of 1812. Command a single field gun at an unfinished stockade, picking ammunition, fuse length and elevation for each shot to break advancing infantry, cavalry and enemy howitzer crews.
descriptions.c64:local-60d14d1a54: SSG's Civil War wargame puts you in the place of the commanding generals at six battles, from First Bull Run, Shiloh and Antietam through Fredericksburg to Chancellorsville.
descriptions.c64:local-6120f344fd: Five Autobots, among them Optimus Prime, Jazz and Bumblebee, search a city of platforms and ladders for the four pieces of an Energon cube while Decepticons attack. Switch robots freely and park the others in Defensa-Pods to recharge.
descriptions.c64:local-6156a86649: A 1984 puzzle game sold as separate Prelude and Finale parts; solving both qualified you for a contest for a real jewelled golden hare pendant worth £30,000. Haresoft vanished in 1985 with the contest unsolved.
descriptions.c64:local-615abda14e: County cricket management game. Pick a side from your squad, choose bowlers and field placings, and follow matches on a running scorecard; players are rated out of ten and scouts report on the opposition.
descriptions.c64:local-61750f553f: A CRL quiz program from 1984 that tests your knowledge of the rules of the road set out in the Highway Code.
descriptions.c64:local-61b4a711d5: Two wizards settle a long rivalry. As Learic you roam the countryside gathering 24 herbs to brew 12 spells, including fireballs, invisibility and teleport, then track rival Leanoric by compass and duel him.
descriptions.c64:local-61fcffe307: Plate-spinning game: keep a plate twirling on each of eight poles before the timer ends, re-spinning the ones that slow down. Plate colours score differently, and tossing a plate in the air changes its colour.
descriptions.c64:local-62332f164f: Radarsoft's sequel to Floyd the Droid finds the robot working in a big restaurant kitchen, where you teach him recipes and pick ingredients from a menu, keeping up to four of them in his built-in fridge.
descriptions.c64:local-6240ad7fa4: Maths game featuring the Wizard of Id comic characters. Spook flees the dungeon by sliding blocks to form correct sums before the jailer Turnkey catches him, with harder problems on higher floors.
descriptions.c64:local-62f975d096: Illustrated adventure in the kingdom of Balema. As a royal advisor you must steer the strong but dim champion Gorn to a dragon, buying supplies, solving riddles and managing water and money; the parser accepts multi-part commands.
descriptions.c64:local-6300b047a7: A 1986 budget take on Amidar from Players Software: move along the lines of a grid, painting around its blocks.
descriptions.c64:local-63cade0f33: The first Warrior of Ras volume sends a lone adventurer into a dungeon that is randomly built anew for every game, fighting monsters and gathering treasure on the way to its deepest level. Games in progress can be saved.
descriptions.c64:local-64aa77b90b: A text adventure adapted from Jeffrey Archer's novel, in which four men cheated out of their savings in a bogus share deal by Harvey Metcalfe scheme to win back exactly what they lost.
descriptions.c64:local-65328d4e73: A Tron-style light-cycle duel for one or two players at once, published in 1987 on the Italian Software Club tape magazine.
descriptions.c64:local-662701360d: Graphical dungeon crawl in the Rogue style. Descend randomly generated levels full of traps, treasure and monsters to recover the stolen Sword of Fargoal from the depths and escape with it.
descriptions.c64:local-6646cabae3: A Boulder Dash-style dig through a mine in search of diamonds, released on CP Verlag's Game On disk magazine in 1991.
descriptions.c64:local-66692ca886: Mirrorsoft shooter in which a star fighter navigates the narrow walkways of the Matrix of Zog hunting eight crystals, facing ramps, traps, vanishing barriers and seven kinds of alien. Brain Teaser and Zapper modes set the style of play.
descriptions.c64:local-6820d1f51c: Vertically scrolling shooter set after alien Saurans have devastated Earth. The last surviving pilot flies a VelosCraft over their territory, gunning down ships and bombing ground targets, with a huge installation closing every stage.
descriptions.c64:local-691f0555cc: One of Infocom's Infocomics, made with Tom Snyder Productions: an animated comic in which a team of alien superheroes fights a planetary tyrant. Panels play out by themselves and the reader picks which hero's thread of the story to follow.
descriptions.c64:local-6953e8dd5f: Conversion of the arcade beat-'em-up. Twin brothers Billy and Jimmy Lee fight through gang-ruled city streets with punches, kicks and grabbed weapons to rescue Marian from the Black Warriors.
descriptions.c64:local-698842104f: Pilot a star fighter through the narrow corridors of the Matrix of Zog to collect its eight crystals, avoiding traps and disappearing barriers while seven types of alien, from homers to corkscrews, attack.
descriptions.c64:local-69916eddd0: Hewson shoot-'em-up on a horizontally split screen, with two robot-controlled craft (a second player or the computer) clearing 24 side-scrolling levels of aliens and delivering collected droids to earn screen-clearing devastators.
descriptions.c64:local-6a0db094fc: Anco snooker game for one or two players viewed from above the table. Choose the target ball, set spin and power, and nominate a colour after potting a red, across three difficulty levels; an edit mode lets you arrange the balls.
descriptions.c64:local-6a8c57fa04: Bubble Bus take on Centipede: a small droid near the bottom of a field of barriers shoots upward at a segmented creature that winds down the screen, losing a segment with each hit. Barriers take several shots to clear.
descriptions.c64:local-6b103a1256: Thomas steams along the rails on errands such as carrying medical supplies to the hospital or children to the seaside, avoiding other engines and rocks on the line and slowing for bends so he does not derail.
descriptions.c64:local-6b5277ba62: Topo Soft's Pac-Man variant, issued in the UK as a Pepsi promotion. Some mazes let you turn into a hippo that flattens ghosts or a vacuum cleaner that sucks up pellets spoiled by a roaming enemy.
descriptions.c64:local-6bef1401c0: SSI strategy game of rival lords on a 6x6 field. Over 21 turns each player builds new castles or reinforces existing ones; a stronger castle captures a weaker neighbour, equal strengths lead to a siege, and whoever holds more territory at the end wins.
descriptions.c64:local-6c621e63c6: On the Delta Princess, steaming from St. Louis to New Orleans, the detective Sir Charles Foxworth and his assistant Regis question passengers, collect notes and re-interview suspects as new evidence turns up to solve a murder aboard.
descriptions.c64:local-6c98d6325f: Asleep in front of the open fridge, Garfield dreams of a winter trip: he skis downhill to a lasagna factory, hunts through a chocolate factory's pipes for the chocolate-egg-laying chicken, then skates a holed, frozen lake after it. His face shows how much energy is left.
descriptions.c64:local-6cafdf1c46: A side-scrolling brawler based on the film: switch at will between Jack Burton, Wang Chi and Egg Shen, each with his own way of fighting, through four levels before facing Lo Pan.
descriptions.c64:local-6d3e3e208f: Choplifter-style rescue game over eight horizontally scrolling levels. Find a set number of stranded men within the time limit, hover low to winch each one aboard, and shoot or dodge attackers, with smart bombs to clear the screen.
descriptions.c64:local-6d4ad3936f: Ten-pin bowling for one to four players, published by High Tech Software in 1983.
descriptions.c64:local-6d4b712da0: ShareData's Mastermind: crack a secret colour code by trial and deduction, using the clues returned after every guess to narrow down the answer.
descriptions.c64:local-6dbdb1fe67: A head-to-head tank duel for two players at once from Supernova Software, sold on its Combat Pack and 2 Player Game Pack compilations.
descriptions.c64:local-6eb16c63c0: Data East's arcade shooter: an exiled pilot is sent on a suicide mission. The ship rotates and the play area scrolls in every direction, with smart bombs on board and weapon tokens dropped by destroyed enemies.
descriptions.c64:local-6f9d13cb78: Based on Clavell's novel: as Toranaga or a rival lord you roam feudal Japan, winning characters to your cause or killing them through icon commands, and must gather twenty followers before completing a quest set by the Emperor.
descriptions.c64:local-6fc72d8b42: Konami's arcade shooter: convicts have broken out and taken the warden hostage. A cop pushes through streets, a park and a bridge to the prison, freeing hostages to gain weapons such as a tear gas gun, but loses them if a hostage is shot.
descriptions.c64:local-7023b09df1: Comic text adventure that opens with you being run over by a pink panther in a pink car. God then sends you after his lost golden eggcup, and both score and turn count track your progress.
descriptions.c64:local-7035238d39: Conversion of Sega's jet combat arcade game: fly an F-14 at speed from behind the plane, shooting down enemy fighters with cannon and a limited stock of homing missiles while dodging incoming fire.
descriptions.c64:local-70ff215ced: Mah-jongg solitaire from the German 64'er magazine: clear the stacked layout by removing matching pairs of free tiles.
descriptions.c64:local-713fd87e30: A knight on a flying horse battles dragons across six stages, first jousting dragon eggs and the hatchlings that emerge, then flying through scrolling catacombs past spiders.
descriptions.c64:local-7144a692da: Puzzle game from Genias: slide the tiles of a maze, 15-puzzle style, to open a route for a rolling ball, collecting cans and avoiding magnets, holes and stop signs before the bonus runs out. Two players can cooperate.
descriptions.c64:local-71d2274e11: MicroProse's first-person dogfighting game. Fly an F6F Hellcat through fourteen Pacific War scenarios, from Pearl Harbor and Midway to Leyte Gulf and Okinawa, against Japanese fighters and bombers by day and night.
descriptions.c64:local-7340bcab69: Electronic Arts' unusual take on Dots and Boxes. Up to four worms crawl over a grid of diagonal dots, leaving coloured trails to claim territory; each worm can be steered, trained to repeat a pattern, or left to the computer.
descriptions.c64:local-7429f5b476: Comic Viking games: pick one of four barbarians and compete in violent events such as beer drinking, cat throwing, tug of war, rock rolling and tower jumping.
descriptions.c64:local-74b02646ee: Parker Brothers' James Bond game. Drive a multi-purpose vehicle over land and sea, jumping hazards and firing at enemies through scrolling missions loosely based on four Bond films, from Diamonds Are Forever to For Your Eyes Only.
descriptions.c64:local-74b6ff8d26: Ocean shooter starring a flying professor caught between two parallel universes. Return the objects swapped between the mirror worlds to their proper places while shooting aliens, ending with a large boss creature.
descriptions.c64:local-758a467885: A chess program with 2-D and 3-D boards, a War Room screen showing clocks, move list and the computer's thinking, hint and teaching modes, blindfold play, selectable playing styles and annotated replays of classic master games.
descriptions.c64:local-78df7601fa: Codemasters' budget trials bike game, also called Moto X Simulator: steer a Super Mudbuster through five skill sections without falling off and four time trials, popping the front wheel and jumping over dunes, logs, rocks and gullies.
descriptions.c64:local-78e00f7d1e: Computer version of the Monopoly board game: roll dice around the board, buy streets and utilities, build houses and hotels, and collect rent until rivals go bankrupt.
descriptions.c64:local-78f4cc7664: Namco's Pac-Man sequel: eat keys to unlock doors around the maze and devour the food behind them while avoiding the ghosts. Super pellets make Pac-Man grow huge and immune to them for a while.
descriptions.c64:local-794ac1635e: Superman's mission mixes into-the-screen flying stages against Parademons, overhead scrolling sections and side-on brawls such as rescuing Lois Lane from terrorists, with comic-book story panels linking the parts.
descriptions.c64:local-79773d1953: Single-screen shooter where your ship can travel around all four edges of the screen, firing inward at swarms of abstract shapes circling the middle. There are 24 levels before it loops.
descriptions.c64:local-797ee5412e: Activision cycling game for up to eight players taking turns to ride stages of the Tour de France against the clock, with practice and competition modes covering the whole race, selected stages or a single stage.
descriptions.c64:local-79b3b03633: The first Magic Knight game. Sent by a king to find a gift for his daughter, the knight explores the castle of Spriteland and its scrolling mazes, combining items and trading them for more valuable ones.
descriptions.c64:local-79ec3f0c5e: Ocean shoot-'em-up with multi-directional scrolling over a layered landscape. Hunt down scientists, sedate them and deliver them to the master computer to unlock its code, buying better weapons and shields along the way.
descriptions.c64:local-7a637cb785: Tynesoft circus events: train tigers, swing through trapeze stunts, walk the tightrope with handstands and flips, and ride a horse doing tricks, either separately or in an international competition.
descriptions.c64:local-7a8ee86f4f: Arcade adventure in which you search seven levels of the Ice Queen's palace of hexagonal rooms for the pieces of your dead father's crown, using objects to solve puzzles, to end her eternal darkness.
descriptions.c64:local-7acb2560d2: Coleco's game of the 1983 film WarGames. Defend six regions of the United States from missiles, bombers and submarines by assigning missiles, planes, subs and occasional satellites, each with its own range and speed.
descriptions.c64:local-7c1f6f2fa9: A Space Invaders-style shooter for one or two players at once, released on CP Verlag's Game On disk magazine in 1991.
descriptions.c64:local-7c2a83791a: Learning Company educational game that teaches children aged about 8 to 12 to plot points on a grid through geometry problems presented with playful graphics.
descriptions.c64:local-7ca5b9a34b: A Galaxian-style shooter from Micro Power whose invaders are wing-flapping Birdmen; any that reach the bottom lay explosive eggs that hem in your laser base until they fade. Eight phases grow steadily harder.
descriptions.c64:local-7cd401bf92: Geoff Crammond's expanded Formula 3 simulation. Besides Brands Hatch and Silverstone it adds four more tracks, among them Donington Park and the Nurburgring, plus computer-driven rivals, adjustable wings and an assisted mode for digital joysticks.
descriptions.c64:local-7d219ed4a1: Centipede-style shooter: a craft at the foot of the screen fires up at a centipede snaking down through a field of mushrooms, splitting it in two with every hit until it is wiped out.
descriptions.c64:local-7d96f60101: Origin's adaptation of the Steve Jackson Games tabletop wargame. On a hex map, one side commands infantry, tanks and howitzers against a single giant cybernetic supertank, the Ogre, in turn-based play.
descriptions.c64:local-7e069c230b: Konami's shooter, known in Europe as Salamander. The planet-eating alien Zelos threatens your world; fly through stages that alternate between horizontal and vertical scrolling, powering up your ship and beating a guardian at the end of each.
descriptions.c64:local-7e11ccdffb: Leisure Genius version of Mastermind, the code-breaking game in which you work out a concealed sequence of colours from the scoring clues given for each attempt.
descriptions.c64:local-7e4b89849d: Hewson maze puzzler in which Flippo walks over tiles to turn every one to the required colour, coping with tiles that flip back or only change from one direction, plus enemies, holes and power-ups.
descriptions.c64:local-7ee52e7673: After a night of drinking, the orc Grindleguts wakes strapped to a horse facing a human knight in a joust, deserted by his friends. Level 9's text adventure has him survive and seek revenge in a world whose characters follow their own routines. This edition has no pictures.
descriptions.c64:local-7ef04bcda8: Version of the TV game show. Two families try to guess the most popular survey answers to questions put to 100 people, scoring points for each matching answer over several rounds.
descriptions.c64:local-7f76566fbb: Geoff Crammond's racer on elevated, roller-coaster circuits: duel a rival car over jumps and humps, ration your turbo boost, and avoid heavy landings that widen a crack in the chassis, while climbing a league of divisions.
descriptions.c64:local-7fea3c950e: Epyx flight and strategy game set in World War II. Crew a torpedo bomber, switching between pilot, navigator, engineer and gunner stations, and search the sea for the battleship Bismarck to sink it.
descriptions.c64:local-818966e540: One or two rebel commandos fight across a Caribbean island to topple its tyrannical dictator, rescuing hostages without shooting them in the crossfire, grabbing weapons dropped by soldiers and taking over tanks. A conversion of the SNK coin-op.
descriptions.c64:local-81e98b4d1a: Vertically scrolling helicopter shooter: fly a Soviet Mi-28 Havoc or an AH-64 Apache through seven war zones, each ending in a huge enemy gunship. Shooting friendly aircraft turns them hostile.
descriptions.c64:local-827623d2bc: Platform game about Tommy the tomcat, who used a wizard's magic book and crystal ball to leave the Dream Islands. The ball shattered, so he must gather its pieces and magic potions across several worlds to get home.
descriptions.c64:local-82d2cb4a8e: Interceptor Micros underwater shooter. Serving with the Aquanaut Patrol, you steer an armed craft through the Caves of Shallic, scrolling in all directions as you destroy enemy vessels and weapons and slip past rockets and gates that switch on and off.
descriptions.c64:local-83b934f43f: SSG wargame recreating six late Civil War battles, from the Wilderness and Cold Harbor to Atlanta and Nashville. Turn-based hex play stresses limited command and fog of war, and an editor allows new scenarios.
descriptions.c64:local-8425040371: Martech arcade adventure. Jane has been kidnapped by Usanga, chief of the Wamabo, and Tarzan must roam the jungle fighting enemies to recover the seven gemstones stolen from the tribe's shrine.
descriptions.c64:local-84a33ce03f: Wicked Software's computer draughts: pieces move diagonally across the 8x8 board, captures are made by jumping, and a piece reaching the far row is crowned a king.
descriptions.c64:local-84f1e652bb: A Bird in the Hand, the Penguin half of Batman: The Caped Crusader. Each location appears as a comic-book panel laid over the previous ones while Batman punches, kicks and throws batarangs at henchmen and solves puzzles to foil the Penguin.
descriptions.c64:local-85d3eb1ca8: Gravity-based exploration game. Solar Jetman pilots a jetpod down from the mothership on twelve worlds, towing parts of the lost golden warpship and other useful items back against strong gravitational pull.
descriptions.c64:local-86c060e1cb: A Pac-Man-style maze chase, one of the fifty games on Cascade's 1984 Cassette 50 compilation.
descriptions.c64:local-8799a15cac: First-person dogfighting in a Grumman F6F Hellcat across fourteen Pacific War scenarios, from Pearl Harbor and Midway to Okinawa, against bombers, scouts and agile Zeros. Five kills earn ace status, and the cockpit offers a rear-view mirror for spotting pursuers.
descriptions.c64:local-887ff48b8d: Infocom's sequel to Enchanter: Belboz, head of the Circle of Enchanters, has fallen under an evil influence and vanished, and the newly promoted apprentice must find him. A text adventure built on spellcasting, now with magic potions to drink as part of the puzzles.
descriptions.c64:local-88ec69b4cc: Movie tie-in where terrorists have seized a high-rise to steal $600 million and John McClane must free his trapped wife. Unlike the PC original this C64 version is a side-scroller; explore the tower for useful gear and fight gunmen, who chase you off-screen.
descriptions.c64:local-88f40e6fa0: Obygurgle wants to get home to his father Glug, who first sets him a test: fetch the pieces of a teleportation spell from fantasy zones one at a time and return each to the teleport pod, then ride a time-warp highway full of bonuses. Music by David Whittaker.
descriptions.c64:local-89bbee1084: Expanded edition of Geoff Crammond's Formula 3 simulator Revs. Four extra tracks, Donington Park, Oulton Park, Snetterton and the Nurburgring, join Brands Hatch and Silverstone, front and rear wings can be tuned per circuit, and an assisted mode helps players without an analog joystick.
descriptions.c64:local-89df5340ca: A Pac-Man-like maze chase in which you drive a garbage truck, picking up every scrap of trash and hauling it to the city dump while dodging bird-like pests. Six trash-can power-ups per maze let you turn the tables, and the maze wraps around on all sides.
descriptions.c64:local-8a7b74062f: Single-screen maze in a lost valley: find the hidden axe and use it to smash the blue door on the far side while a dinosaur hunts you. Carrying the axe slows you down, so you may need to drop it when the beast closes in; higher skill levels add more dinosaurs.
descriptions.c64:local-8b00de6f08: The long-lost space station Discovery has turned up with its defenses switched on. Fly over it in a top-down shooter, and enter its twelve hatches to win mini-games, variants of Breakout, Centipede, Amidar, solitaire and a sliding puzzle, that build the circuit board to shut the defenses down.
descriptions.c64:local-8c0b05568c: An unofficial edit of International Karate +, the three-fighter karate contest with a ball-deflecting bonus round, changed so a third person can control the extra fighter with a joystick.
descriptions.c64:local-8c2682fa61: Single-screen shooter spanning 256 waves of bomb-dropping aliens. Your weapon overheats if fired too long and fuel drains as you move, so you grab fireballs during asteroid storms and dock with the mothership for refuelling; up to four players take turns.
descriptions.c64:local-8ce3024e9b: Scott Adams text adventure set in an abandoned Old West mining town. Hunt down thirteen treasures for the dry-goods store by exploring the saloon, jail, mine and Boot Hill, cracking a safe, making gunpowder and heeding ghostly voices, all through two-word commands.
descriptions.c64:local-8d584bff2a: The second load of Dinamic's Army Moves, entered with the code earned in part one: the soldier hops from rock to rock across a jungle full of toucans, then storms the enemy general's headquarters, gunning down guards and searching for secret documents.
descriptions.c64:local-8e57cd276d: An SSI aid for AD&D referees rather than a game: it generates random encounters from a database of over 1,300 monsters and characters drawn from the Monster Manual books, listing their numbers, arms, armor and spells.
descriptions.c64:local-8f102bdc73: Detective Alan Chance watches the mourners leave his own funeral: betrayed while working undercover against a drug gang, he returns as a ghost with three nights to expose the traitor, clear his name and rescue his missing partner Sarah. A Level 9 text adventure.
descriptions.c64:local-8f5955457e: Typing tutor starring characters from Brant Parker and Johnny Hart's Wizard of Id. As the Wiz you type words fast enough to shrink the Evil Spirit in your vat before it turns into a dragon, then keep pace with Bung the Jester as he hops across a paragraph on a pogo stick.
descriptions.c64:local-8f93453c05: A rogue computer has cut Earth's power, sending nuclear-powered Flexible Robot Caterpillars on the rampage. From an overhead scrolling view you pilot a tank through three levels, blasting off each caterpillar's tail to recover the fuel rod in its head and feed all eight into the reactor.
descriptions.c64:local-8fbed758a8: SSI role-playing game set on the island of Ymros, where the sorceress Siriadne has stolen the crystal that keeps the land in eternal spring. Build a party from five races, including elves, dwarves and trolls, as warriors or wizards, shop in menu-driven towns and fight turn-based dungeon battles.
descriptions.c64:local-905baeec60: Computer version of the board game: drop counters into a seven-column upright grid, trying to line up four of your colour in any direction. Play another person or the computer at one of four skill levels.
descriptions.c64:local-9110939371: Top Cat reports that toys have gone missing, and while investigating, Yogi's friends are captured by the Greed Monster. Yogi must recover the toys and free them, eating picnic baskets for energy and pelting enemies with sweets.
descriptions.c64:local-9264427d3b: Level 9's sequel to Gnome Ranger: the gnome Ingrid Bottomlow returns home to find the greedy developer Jasper Quickbuck threatening her village of Little Moaning, and sets out to stop him, gathering villagers' support for her petition. This edition is text only.
